baldwin-spencer.s: Baldwin Spencer is an Antiguan politician and former trade unionist who led the United Progressive Party and was prime minister of Antigua and Barbuda from 2004 to 2014. His victory in 2004 ended nearly three decades of rule by the Bird family's Antigua Labour Party.

bajaur.s: Bajaur is a district in the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province of Pakistan, on the Afghan border north of Peshawar. Alexander the Great campaigned in the area in 327 BCE, and in the following centuries it was a Buddhist borderland of Gandhara, home of the Apracharaja rulers, whose…

battle-of-otlukbeli.s: The Battle of Otlukbeli was fought on 11 August 1473 near Erzincan in eastern Anatolia between the Ottoman sultan Mehmed II and Uzun Hasan of the Aq Qoyunlu. Ottoman artillery and firearms decided the day, ending Uzun Hasan's challenge to the Ottomans in Anatolia and his hopes…

battle-of-maysalun.s: The Battle of Maysalun was fought on 24 July 1920 at the Maysalun pass west of Damascus between French forces under General Mariano Goybet and a small Syrian army led by the war minister Yusuf al-Azma. The French victory, in which al-Azma was killed, ended King Faisal's Arab…

ben-hadad-i.s: Ben-Hadad I was a king of Aram-Damascus in the early 9th century BCE. According to the Bible, King Asa of Judah paid him to break his alliance with Baasha of Israel, and he then invaded northern Israel, taking towns such as Abel-beth-maacah.

battle-of-mantinea-362-bce.s: The Battle of Mantinea was fought in Arcadia in 362 BCE between Thebes under Epaminondas, with its Arcadian and other allies, and a coalition of Sparta, Athens, Mantinea and Elis. The Thebans won, but Epaminondas was mortally wounded, and the battle left no Greek state supreme.

battle-of-caseros.s: The Battle of Caseros was fought on 3 February 1852 near Buenos Aires between the army of Juan Manuel de Rosas and a coalition led by Justo José de Urquiza, governor of Entre Ríos, backed by Brazil and Uruguay. Urquiza's victory ended Rosas's long rule and sent him into exile…

battle-of-pavon.s: The Battle of Pavón was fought on 17 September 1861 in Santa Fe province between the forces of the State of Buenos Aires under Bartolomé Mitre and those of the Argentine Confederation under Justo José de Urquiza. Urquiza withdrew from the field despite an uncertain outcome,…

bukkur.s: Bukkur is a limestone island in the Indus river between the cities of Sukkur and Rohri in Sindh, Pakistan, crowned by an old fortress. Called Bhakkar in Persian chronicles, it commanded the river crossing and was a key stronghold of the Arghun dynasty and later of Mughal…

battle-of-sepeia.s: The Battle of Sepeia was fought around 494 BCE near Tiryns in the Argolid between Sparta, led by King Cleomenes I, and Argos. The Spartans surprised and routed the Argive army, then burned many survivors who had taken refuge in a sacred grove.

brandenburg-african-company.s: The Brandenburg African Company was a trading company founded in 1682 by Frederick William, Elector of Brandenburg, to trade with West Africa. It built the fort of Gross Friedrichsburg on the Gold Coast and held Arguin off Mauritania from 1685, dealing in gold, ivory, gum and…

banc-darguin-national-park.s: Banc d'Arguin National Park is a protected area on the Atlantic coast of Mauritania, between Nouakchott and Nouadhibou. Created in 1976, it covers sand dunes, coastal swamps, islands and shallow waters that host millions of migratory birds, and its Imraguen fishermen still use…

book-of-knowledge-of-ingenious-mechanica.n: Book of Knowledge of Ingenious Mechanical Devices
book-of-knowledge-of-ingenious-mechanica.s: The Book of Knowledge of Ingenious Mechanical Devices is an Arabic treatise completed around 1206 by Ismail al-Jazari, engineer to the Artuqid rulers of Diyarbakır. It describes and illustrates about fifty devices, including water clocks, automata, fountains and water-raising…

betico-croes.s: Betico Croes, born Gilberto François Croes, was an Aruban politician who led the movement for Aruba's separation from the Netherlands Antilles. He founded the People's Electoral Movement in 1971 and won a referendum for separation in 1977, securing status aparte for Aruba…

bituitus.s: Bituitus was a king of the Arverni in Gaul in the late 2nd century BCE, son of Luernios. In 121 BCE he led a huge army of Arverni and Allobroges against the Romans but was defeated near the junction of the Rhône and Isère by Quintus Fabius Maximus.

battle-of-qarqar.s: The Battle of Qarqar was fought in 853 BCE near the Orontes river in Syria between the Assyrian king Shalmaneser III and a coalition of twelve kings led by Hadadezer of Damascus, Irhuleni of Hamath and Ahab of Israel. Shalmaneser claimed victory on the Kurkh Monolith, but his…

batak.s: The Batak are a group of related peoples of the highlands of North Sumatra in Indonesia, centred on Lake Toba. They include the Toba, Karo, Simalungun, Pakpak, Angkola and Mandailing, each with its own language and customs.

battle-of-anegawa.s: The Battle of Anegawa was fought in the summer of 1570 by the Ane river in northern Ōmi province, Japan. Oda Nobunaga and his ally Tokugawa Ieyasu defeated the combined armies of Azai Nagamasa and the Asakura clan.

battle-of-the-eurymedon.s: The Battle of the Eurymedon was a double victory won around 466 BCE by the Delian League under Cimon over the Persian Empire at the mouth of the Eurymedon river in Pamphylia. Cimon destroyed a Phoenician fleet and then defeated the Persian army on land the same day.

bodhan.s: Bodhan is a town in the Nizamabad district of Telangana in southern India. It is often identified with Potali or Potana, capital of the ancient kingdom of Assaka, and it was an early seat of the Chalukyas of Vemulavada.

battle-of-chaeronea-338-bce.s: The Battle of Chaeronea was fought in Boeotia in August 338 BCE between Philip II of Macedon and an alliance led by Athens and Thebes. The Macedonian phalanx and cavalry, the latter commanded by the young Alexander, destroyed the allied army and the Theban Sacred Band.

battle-of-the-sabis.s: The Battle of the Sabis was fought in 57 BCE on the river Sabis, usually identified with the Sambre, in northern Gaul. The Nervii, with the Atrebates and Viromandui, surprised Julius Caesar's legions while they were making camp.

brescia.s: Brescia is a city in Lombardy, northern Italy, at the foot of the Alps. Founded as Brixia, it was the chief town of the Cenomani Gauls before becoming a Roman town, whose forum and Capitolium temple survive.

bavaria.s: Bavaria is a region of southern Germany and the country's largest state, with its capital at Munich. Named after the Bavarii, a people first recorded in the 6th century, it was a stem duchy under the Agilolfings and from 1180 was ruled by the Wittelsbach family, who became…

brunhilda-of-austrasia.s: Brunhilda was a Visigothic princess who married the Frankish king Sigebert I of Austrasia in 567 and dominated Merovingian politics for half a century. The murder of her sister, blamed on Fredegund, began a long feud between Austrasia and Neustria.

battle-of-tertry.s: The Battle of Tertry was fought in 687 near Péronne in northern France between Pippin of Herstal, mayor of the palace of Austrasia, and the Neustrian mayor Berchar with King Theuderic III. Pippin's victory made him master of all the Frankish kingdoms and secured his family's…

battle-of-koniggratz.s: The Battle of Königgrätz, or Sadowa, was fought on 3 July 1866 near Hradec Králové in Bohemia and was the decisive battle of the Austro-Prussian War. Prussian armies under Helmuth von Moltke, using railways and breech-loading needle guns, defeated the Austrian and Saxon army…

battle-of-solferino.s: The Battle of Solferino was fought on 24 June 1859 in Lombardy between the French and Sardinian armies under Napoleon III and Victor Emmanuel II and the Austrian army under Emperor Franz Joseph. The Austrian defeat led to the loss of Lombardy and advanced Italian unification.

barrier-treaty-1715.s: The Barrier Treaty of 15 November 1715, signed at Antwerp by Austria and the Dutch Republic with British mediation, settled the status of the Southern Netherlands after the War of the Spanish Succession. Austria took over the former Spanish provinces but allowed the Dutch to…

battle-of-fleurus-1794.s: The Battle of Fleurus was fought on 26 June 1794 near Charleroi in the Austrian Netherlands between the French Army of the Sambre-et-Meuse under Jean-Baptiste Jourdan and the Coalition army of the Prince of Coburg. The French victory, in which a reconnaissance balloon was used…

bosnia.s: Bosnia is a historical region of the western Balkans, named after the river Bosna, which forms the larger, northern part of modern Bosnia and Herzegovina. In the Middle Ages it was a banate and from 1377 a kingdom, home to the Bosnian Church.

briviesca.s: Briviesca is a town in the province of Burgos, in northern Spain, on the road from Burgos to Miranda de Ebro. It descends from Virovesca, a town of the Autrigones named by Pliny and Ptolemy that became a Roman stopping place on the road through the upper Ebro region.

bara-imambara.s: The Bara Imambara is a large Shia congregation hall in Lucknow, India, built by Nawab Asaf-ud-Daula from 1784, partly to provide work during a famine. Its central hall, roofed without supporting beams, is among the largest vaulted chambers of its kind, and the complex includes…

begum-hazrat-mahal.s: Begum Hazrat Mahal was a wife of Wajid Ali Shah, the last Nawab of Awadh, and a leader of the Indian Rebellion of 1857. After the British exiled her husband, she proclaimed her young son Birjis Qadr ruler and directed resistance at Lucknow.

battle-of-buxar.s: The Battle of Buxar was fought in October 1764 in Bihar between the East India Company army under Hector Munro and the combined forces of Mir Qasim of Bengal, Shuja-ud-Daula of Awadh and the Mughal emperor Shah Alam II. The British victory led to the Treaty of Allahabad of…

bambara-people.s: The Bambara, or Bamana, are a Mande people of the upper Niger valley in Mali and the country's largest ethnic group. In the 18th century they founded the kingdoms of Ségou and Kaarta, warrior states that long resisted Islam until Umar Tall conquered them in 1861 and 1854.

birgi.s: Birgi is a small town in İzmir province, western Turkey, on the slopes of the Bozdağ mountains. Known in Byzantine times as Pyrgion, it became the first capital of the Aydinid beylik in the early 14th century, and its Great Mosque, built in 1312 for Mehmed Bey, survives.

borommatrailokkanat.s: Borommatrailokkanat was king of Ayutthaya from 1448 to 1488. He reorganised government into civil and military divisions, with ministries for the capital, the palace, the treasury and the lands, and codified the sakdina system that ranked every subject by notional landholding.

baalbek.s: Baalbek is a town in the Beqaa valley of Lebanon, known in antiquity as Heliopolis. Its Roman temple complex, with the temples of Jupiter, Bacchus and Venus built between the 1st and 3rd centuries, is one of the largest in the Roman world.

battle-of-la-forbie.s: The Battle of La Forbie was fought on 17–18 October 1244 near Gaza between the army of the Ayyubid sultan of Egypt, as-Salih Ayyub, with Khwarazmian allies under Baybars, and an alliance of the Crusader states with the Ayyubid rulers of Damascus and Homs. The Egyptian victory…

battle-of-imphal.s: The Battle of Imphal was fought from March to July 1944 around the town of Imphal in north-eastern India, when the Japanese Fifteenth Army attempted to invade India from Burma. Supplied by air, British and Indian forces under William Slim held the Imphal plain, and the…

battle-of-kohima.s: The Battle of Kohima was fought from April to June 1944 at Kohima in the Naga Hills of north-eastern India, as part of the Japanese offensive against India. The small British and Indian garrison held out, fighting at close quarters across the deputy commissioner's tennis…

baku-tbilisi-ceyhan-pipeline.s: The Baku–Tbilisi–Ceyhan pipeline carries crude oil about 1,768 km from the Caspian oilfields near Baku in Azerbaijan through Georgia to the Turkish Mediterranean port of Ceyhan. Built by a BP-led consortium and opened in 2005, it was designed to bring Caspian oil to Western…

battle-of-baekgang.s: The Battle of Baekgang was fought in 663 near the mouth of the Geum river in south-western Korea between Tang Chinese and Silla forces and the fleet of Yamato Japan, sent to support the Baekje restoration movement. The Tang navy destroyed the Japanese fleet, ending hopes of…

bahawal-khan-i.s: Bahawal Khan I was a nawab of the Abbasi Daudpota family, which claimed descent from the Abbasid caliphs and had moved from Sindh to the Sutlej valley earlier in the 18th century. Around 1748 he founded the town of Bahawalpur, which took his name and became the capital of the…

baha-al-dawla.s: Baha al-Dawla was a Buyid ruler, a son of Adud al-Dawla, who held Baghdad and Iraq from 989 and later reunited Fars, ruling until his death in 1012. He took power after the death of his brother Sharaf al-Dawla and fought long wars with rival members of his family.

bidar.s: Bidar is a city on a plateau in the north-east of Karnataka, India. Ahmad Shah I made it the capital of the Bahmani Sultanate in the 1420s, and it was later the seat of the Barid Shahi rulers of the Bidar Sultanate until Bijapur annexed it in 1619.

bahurutshe.s: The Bahurutshe are a Tswana people regarded in tradition as the senior line from which the Bakwena and other Tswana groups branched. By the 16th century they lived in the Marico area of the western highveld, where their stone-walled capital Kaditshwene was one of the largest…

bakwena.s: The Bakwena are a Tswana people who trace their origin to a split from the Bahurutshe and who in turn gave rise to the Bangwato and Bangwaketse. Settled in what is now south-eastern Botswana, they were rebuilt in the 19th century by Sechele I, who made Molepolole their capital.

botswana.s: Botswana is a landlocked country in southern Africa, much of it covered by the Kalahari Desert, with the Okavango Delta in the north-west. Its Tswana chiefdoms came under British protection as the Bechuanaland Protectorate in 1885, and it became independent in 1966 under…

battle-of-jersey.s: The Battle of Jersey was fought on 6 January 1781, when a French force under Baron Philippe de Rullecourt landed at night and seized Saint Helier in an attempt to take the island during the American War of Independence. British regulars and the island militia under Major…

bayeux.s: Bayeux is a town in the Calvados department of Normandy, France, near the English Channel coast. As Augustodurum it was the Roman chief town of the Gallic Baiocasses, whose name it later took, and it became a bishop's seat.

bangwaketse.s: The Bangwaketse are a Tswana people who separated from the Bakwena in the 18th century and settled in south-eastern Botswana. Under Makaba II they became one of the strongest Tswana states until his death in 1824, and in the 19th century they rebuilt their chiefdom around the…

bavarians.s: The Bavarians, or Baiuvarii, are a people who first appear in written sources in the mid-6th century, settled between the Danube, the Lech and the Alps. They formed from Germanic groups and the Romanised population of the old provinces of Raetia and Noricum, under dukes of the…

battle-of-tianmenling.s: The Battle of Tianmenling was fought in 698 between the Goguryeo and Mohe followers of Dae Joyeong and a pursuing Tang army under Li Kaigu. Dae Joyeong's forces won a decisive victory at the pass, in the region of modern Jilin province in China, and soon afterwards he founded…

biton-coulibaly.s: Bitòn Coulibaly, also called Mamari Kulibali, was the founder of the Bambara Empire of Ségou in present-day Mali, ruling from about 1712 until his death in 1755. He turned a youth association, the ton, into a standing army bound to him and used captives as soldiers to conquer…

ban-boric.s: Ban Borić was the first ruler of Bosnia known by name, recorded as ban in 1154 as a vassal of the Kingdom of Hungary. He fought on the Hungarian side against the Byzantine Empire and was drawn into the Hungarian succession disputes of the early 1160s, after which he disappears…

ban-kulin.s: Ban Kulin ruled Bosnia from about 1180 to 1204, nominally under Hungarian and Byzantine overlordship but in practice independently, and his reign was later remembered as a golden age. His charter of 1189 granting free trade to the merchants of Ragusa is one of the oldest state…

burgenland.s: Burgenland is the easternmost and least populous state of Austria, a narrow strip of land along the Hungarian border with its capital at Eisenstadt. For centuries part of the Kingdom of Hungary, the largely German-speaking region was assigned to Austria by the treaties of…

bega-canal.s: The Bega Canal is a navigable canal in the Banat region of Romania and Serbia, which follows and regulates the course of the Bega river. It was dug from 1728 under the Habsburg governor Claudius Florimund Mercy to drain marshes and link Temeswar, now Timișoara, with the Tisza,…

bathoen-i.s: Bathoen I was chief of the Bangwaketse, a Tswana people of southern Botswana, from 1889 until his death in 1910, ruling from Kanye. In 1895 he travelled to Britain with Khama III and Sebele I to oppose the planned transfer of the Bechuanaland Protectorate to Cecil Rhodes's…

banjarmasin-war.s: The Banjarmasin War was a conflict in southern Borneo between the Dutch colonial government and supporters of the Banjar Sultanate, beginning in 1859 after the Dutch imposed their own candidate in a succession dispute following Sultan Adam's death. Led by Pangeran Antasari,…

barito-river.s: The Barito is the largest river of southern Borneo, flowing some 900 kilometres from the Müller Mountains to the Java Sea through Indonesia's Central and South Kalimantan provinces. Banjarmasin, the capital of the Banjar Sultanate and later of the Dutch residency, grew near…

banu-sulaym.s: The Banu Sulaym were an Arab tribe of the Hejaz who, together with the Banu Hilal, migrated from Upper Egypt into North Africa in the 11th century, encouraged by the Fatimids to punish the rebellious Zirids. Settling mainly in Cyrenaica, Tripolitania and southern Ifriqiya,…

banu-ifran.s: The Banu Ifran were a Zenata Berber tribe of the central and western Maghreb. In the Berber revolt against the Umayyads from 740 they embraced Sufri Kharijism, and their leader Abu Qurra founded a state at Tlemcen.

battle-of-albelda.s: The Battle of Albelda was fought in 859 near Albelda in La Rioja, northern Spain, where King Ordoño I of Asturias defeated Musa ibn Musa of the Banu Qasi, the dominant lord of the Upper March of al-Andalus. According to the Asturian chronicles Ordoño stormed the fortress Musa…

barbados-labour-party.s: The Barbados Labour Party is one of the two main political parties of Barbados, founded in 1938 by Grantley Adams and others after the labour riots of 1937. It led the island towards universal suffrage and self-government, and later governed under Tom Adams, Owen Arthur and,…

bridgetown-initiative.s: The Bridgetown Initiative is a set of proposals for reforming international development and climate finance, launched in 2022 by Mia Mottley, the prime minister of Barbados. It calls for emergency liquidity for vulnerable countries, clauses suspending debt payments after…

betar.s: Betar was an ancient fortified town in the Judaean hills south-west of Jerusalem, at Khirbet al-Yahud near the village of Battir. It was the last stronghold of Simon bar Kokhba in the revolt against Rome, and its fall in 135 CE ended the rising.

barolong.s: The Barolong are a Tswana-speaking people of southern Africa, among the oldest Tswana groups, traditionally settled in the southern Kalahari margins and the Molopo valley. After the death of the 18th-century chief Tau they split into branches, including the Ratlou, Tshidi,…

barotseland-agreement-1964.s: The Barotseland Agreement 1964 was signed in May 1964 by Kenneth Kaunda for Northern Rhodesia, the Litunga Mwanawina III and the British government. It made Barotseland part of independent Zambia while promising the Lozi kingdom its own institutions and a degree of…

bartoszyce.s: Bartoszyce, German Bartenstein, is a town in the Warmian-Masurian Voivodeship of north-eastern Poland, on the Łyna river near the Russian border. It grew around a castle built by the Teutonic Order around 1240 in the Prussian territory of Barta, which the Prussians besieged…

bashkirs.s: The Bashkirs are a Turkic people of the southern Ural Mountains and adjacent plains in Russia, most of whom live in the Republic of Bashkortostan. Traditionally semi-nomadic herders and Sunni Muslims, they came under Russian rule in the 1550s and rose repeatedly against…

bashkir-autonomous-soviet-socialist-repu.s: The Bashkir Autonomous Soviet Socialist Republic was an autonomous republic of Soviet Russia in the southern Urals, recognised in March 1919 as the first autonomous republic in the RSFSR. Its capital was Ufa from 1922.

bashkortostan.s: Bashkortostan is a republic of the Russian Federation in the southern Urals and the plains to their west, with its capital at Ufa. It is the homeland of the Bashkirs, though Russians and Tatars also form large parts of its population.

butha-buthe.s: Butha-Buthe is a town in northern Lesotho, capital of the district of the same name, below the mountain of Butha-Buthe. In the early 1820s the young chief Moshoeshoe gathered his followers there, before the attacks of the Lifaqane drove him to move in 1824 to the stronger…

bastar-dussehra.s: Bastar Dussehra is a festival held each year in Jagdalpur and across the Bastar region of Chhattisgarh, India, lasting about 75 days. Unlike Dussehra elsewhere, it is devoted to the goddess Danteshwari and the local deities of Bastar's villages rather than to Rama.

bhumkal-rebellion.s: The Bhumkal rebellion was an uprising of Adivasi communities in the princely state of Bastar, central India, in 1910. Led by Gunda Dhur, it was a reaction to forest reservation, restrictions on shifting cultivation and the power of outside officials.

basti-iberia.s: Basti was the chief town of the Bastetani, an Iberian people of south-eastern Spain, on the hill of Cerro Cepero near modern Baza in the province of Granada. It continued as a Roman town.

baza.s: Baza is a town in the province of Granada, Andalusia, Spain, on a high plateau in the north-east of the province, near the site of the Iberian town of Basti. Under Muslim rule it was an important town of the Nasrid Emirate of Granada until the Catholic Monarchs took it after a…

basotho-congress-party.s: The Basotho Congress Party is a political party in Lesotho, founded in 1952 as the Basutoland African Congress by Ntsu Mokhehle and renamed the Basutoland Congress Party. It led the campaign for independence but lost the 1965 election.

basutoland-national-council.s: The Basutoland National Council was a body of chiefs and nominated members created in 1903 to advise the British administration of Basutoland, presided over by the Paramount Chief. It gave chiefs a formal voice in colonial government.

batavodurum.s: Batavodurum was the chief settlement of the Batavi on the site of modern Nijmegen in the Netherlands, mentioned by Tacitus and Ptolemy. It was burned during the Batavian revolt of 69–70 CE.

betuwe.s: The Betuwe is a region of the province of Gelderland in the Netherlands, lying between the Nederrijn and Lek to the north and the Waal to the south. Its name derives from that of the Batavi, who settled there in Roman times.

battle-of-camperdown.s: The Battle of Camperdown was fought on 11 October 1797 off the Dutch coast near Camperduin between the British North Sea Fleet under Admiral Adam Duncan and the fleet of the Batavian Republic under Vice-Admiral Jan de Winter. The British captured eleven Dutch ships, including…

battle-of-dithakong.s: The Battle of Dithakong was fought in June 1823 near the Batlhaping town of Dithakong, in the north of present-day South Africa. Mounted Griqua gunmen, allied with the Batlhaping and called in through the missionary Robert Moffat, defeated a large force of displaced…

bauchi.s: Bauchi is a city in north-eastern Nigeria and the capital of Bauchi State. It was founded around 1809 by Yakubu, a scholar and flag-bearer of Usman dan Fodio, as the capital of the Bauchi Emirate within the Sokoto Caliphate.

bauchi-state.s: Bauchi State is a state in north-eastern Nigeria, created in 1976, with its capital at Bauchi. Gombe State was split from it in 1996.

botswana-democratic-party.s: The Botswana Democratic Party was founded as the Bechuanaland Democratic Party in 1962 by Seretse Khama and others. It won the pre-independence election of 1965 and governed Botswana without interruption from independence in 1966, under Seretse Khama and his successors, until…

bedulu.s: Bedulu is a village in Gianyar regency, Bali, Indonesia, near Ubud and Pejeng, in the fertile area between the Petanu and Pakerisan rivers. It was a royal centre of the early Balinese kings before the Majapahit conquest of 1343, and the area holds many ancient sites, including…

belanjong-pillar.s: The Belanjong pillar is an inscribed stone pillar at Sanur, Bali, dated to 914 CE. Its text, in Sanskrit and Old Balinese written in two scripts, records a campaign of King Sri Kesari Warmadewa.

beiyang-army.s: The Beiyang Army was the Western-style army created by the Qing dynasty from 1895 under Yuan Shikai, based in the northern region of Zhili. It became the most modern force in China and the basis of Yuan's power, allowing him to negotiate the abdication of the last emperor in…

bath.s: Bath is a city in Somerset, south-west England, built around natural hot springs. As Roman Aquae Sulis it had a great bathing complex and a temple of Sulis Minerva.

battle-of-st-georges-caye.s: The Battle of St George's Caye was a series of engagements on 3–10 September 1798 off the coast of Belize, in which British settlers, freed and enslaved people and the sloop HMS Merlin repelled a Spanish flotilla from Yucatán. The victory secured the British settlement, and 10…

baymen.s: The Baymen were the British settlers of the Bay of Honduras, mainly in present-day Belize, who cut logwood and later mahogany from the mid-17th century, using enslaved African labour. Spain contested their presence, but treaties of 1763, 1783 and 1786 allowed them to cut timber.

beauvais.s: Beauvais is a city in northern France, capital of the Oise department in Hauts-de-France. It grew from Caesaromagus, the Roman chief town of the Bellovaci, and became a bishopric.

bratuspantium.s: Bratuspantium was a fortified town (oppidum) of the Bellovaci in northern Gaul. In 57 BCE, during Julius Caesar's campaign against the Belgae, the Bellovaci gathered there and surrendered after the Aeduan leader Diviciacus pleaded on their behalf.

bhadohi.s: Bhadohi is a town in Uttar Pradesh, northern India, west of Varanasi, and the headquarters of a district of the same name. It is the centre of India's largest hand-knotted carpet-weaving industry.

bhumihar.s: The Bhumihars are a Hindu landholding caste of Bihar and eastern Uttar Pradesh in northern India, who claim Brahmin status. Many held large zamindari estates under the Mughals, the Nawabs of Awadh and the British.

bengkulu.s: Bengkulu, formerly Bencoolen, is a city on the south-west coast of Sumatra in Indonesia and the capital of Bengkulu province. The English East India Company founded a pepper-trading post there in 1685 and built Fort Marlborough from 1714.

bagerhat.s: Bagerhat is a town in south-western Bangladesh, in the Sundarbans region. In the 15th century the frontier magnate Khan Jahan Ali founded a settlement there, called Khalifatabad, with mosques, tombs, roads and water tanks.

berar.s: Berar is a historical region of central India, now the western part of the Vidarbha division of Maharashtra, around Amravati and Akola. A fertile cotton-growing plain, it was a province of the Bahmani Sultanate, an independent sultanate from about 1490 to 1574, a Mughal…

berga.s: Berga is a town in the province of Barcelona in Catalonia, north-eastern Spain, and the capital of the Berguedà comarca in the upper Llobregat valley. In the Middle Ages it was the seat of a lordship and later part of the County of Cerdanya.

bergium.s: Bergium was a hill fortress of the Bergistani, an Iberian people of north-eastern Spain, known from Livy's account of the campaign of Cato the Elder in 195 BCE. After the Bergistani revolted twice, Cato took their strongholds, and Bergium fell when its chief helped the Romans…

bergueda.s: The Berguedà is a comarca, or county, in the province of Barcelona in Catalonia, Spain, covering the upper valley of the Llobregat with Berga as its capital. Its name is traced to the ancient Bergistani.

bitola.s: Bitola is a city in the Pelagonia plain of southern North Macedonia, near the Greek border and the ruins of the ancient city of Heraclea Lyncestis. Under Ottoman rule, as Monastir, it was a major administrative and military centre of the Balkans.

boris-i-of-bulgaria.s: Boris I was ruler of the First Bulgarian Empire from 852 to 889. He accepted Christian baptism around 864, taking the name Michael, and secured an autonomous Bulgarian church under Constantinople.

battle-of-levounion.s: The Battle of Levounion was fought on 29 April 1091 in Thrace, near the mouth of the Maritsa, between the Byzantine Empire and the Pechenegs. Emperor Alexios I Komnenos, aided by Cuman allies, destroyed a Pecheneg horde that had threatened Constantinople, killing most of its…

bhadarwah.s: Bhadarwah is a town in an upland valley of the Doda district in the Jammu division of Jammu and Kashmir, India. Ruled by local Rajput chiefs, it was for long periods a dependency of Chamba State and later came under the Dogra rulers of Jammu and Kashmir.

balwant-singh-of-bharatpur.s: Balwant Singh was the Jat Maharaja of Bharatpur from 1826 to 1853. As a child he was displaced by his cousin Durjan Sal in a succession dispute, and the British, under Lord Combermere, besieged and stormed the fortress of Bharatpur in January 1826 and restored him to the throne.

bhavsinhji-i.s: Bhavsinhji I was a Gohil Rajput ruler in southern Saurashtra, Gujarat. In 1723 he founded the port of Bhavnagar on the Gulf of Khambhat and moved his capital there from Sihor, giving the state his name.

berkshire.s: Berkshire is a county in southern England, west of London, with Reading as its largest town. The River Thames formed its historic northern boundary, and it contains Windsor Castle, a royal residence since the time of William the Conqueror.

barid-shahi-dynasty.s: The Barid Shahi dynasty ruled the Bidar Sultanate in the Deccan after the break-up of the Bahmani Sultanate. Its founder, Qasim Barid, and his son Amir Barid controlled the last Bahmani sultans as ministers, and Ali Barid took the royal title in 1542.

bijapur.s: Bijapur, officially Vijayapura since 2014, is a city in northern Karnataka, India. From about 1490 to 1686 it was the capital of the Adil Shahi sultans of Bijapur, one of the Deccan sultanates, who filled it with mosques, palaces and tombs, including the Ibrahim Rauza and the…

battle-of-talikota.s: The Battle of Talikota was fought in January 1565 in the northern Deccan between the Vijayanagara Empire and an alliance of the Deccan sultanates of Bijapur, Ahmadnagar, Golconda and Bidar. Vijayanagara's regent, Aliya Rama Raya, was captured and killed, his army collapsed,…

bhakra-dam.s: The Bhakra Dam is a concrete gravity dam on the Sutlej in the Bilaspur district of Himachal Pradesh, India, completed in 1963. Over 220 metres high, it holds back the Gobind Sagar reservoir and supplies irrigation and hydroelectric power to Punjab, Haryana and Rajasthan.

bhim-chand-of-kahlur.s: Bhim Chand was Raja of Kahlur, later known as Bilaspur, in the lower Himalaya in the late 17th century. He came into conflict with the Sikh Guru Gobind Singh, whose base at Anandpur lay in his territory, and joined other hill rajas in several campaigns against the Guru in the…

bilaspur-himachal-pradesh.s: Bilaspur is a town on the Sutlej in Himachal Pradesh, India, and the headquarters of Bilaspur district. Founded in the mid-17th century as the capital of the hill state of Kahlur, it gave the state its later name.

bo-sangaji-kai.s: The Bo Sangaji Kai is the court chronicle of the Bima Sultanate on the island of Sumbawa in eastern Indonesia. Kept by the sultans' scribes from the 17th to the 19th century, mostly in Malay, it records royal decrees, genealogies, treaties and events such as the arrival of…

bima-people.s: The Bima people, who call themselves Mbojo, are an ethnic group of eastern Sumbawa in Indonesia, speaking the Bima language. Their homeland was the Hindu-Buddhist kingdom and later the Bima Sultanate, which accepted Islam in the early 17th century under the influence of the…

berlin.s: Berlin is the capital and largest city of Germany. It grew from medieval trading towns on the Spree into the capital of Brandenburg-Prussia and, from 1871, of the German Empire.

borsippa.s: Borsippa was an ancient city of Babylonia, about 20 km south-west of Babylon in modern Iraq. It was the cult centre of the god Nabu, whose temple, Ezida, was rebuilt by Nebuchadnezzar II.

bellovesus.s: Bellovesus was a legendary Gallic leader, nephew of King Ambigatus of the Bituriges, who according to Livy led a great migration of Celts across the Alps into northern Italy around 600 BCE. Livy says his followers defeated the Etruscans near the Ticino and founded Mediolanum,…

berry-province.s: Berry is a former province of central France, with Bourges as its capital, roughly the modern departments of Cher and Indre. It took its name from the Bituriges, the Gallic people of the area.

bordeaux.s: Bordeaux is a city on the Garonne in south-western France. As Burdigala it was founded by the Bituriges Vivisci and became the capital of Roman Aquitania.

bourges.s: Bourges is a city in central France, capital of the Cher department and of the old province of Berry. As Avaricum it was the chief town of the Bituriges, taken by Caesar in 52 BCE.

blackfeet-reservation.s: The Blackfeet Reservation is the home of the Blackfeet Nation, the Piikani or Amskapi Pikuni, in north-western Montana, United States, east of Glacier National Park, with its headquarters at Browning. Its lands are the remnant of the large territory recognised to the Blackfoot…

banyuwangi.s: Banyuwangi is a regency and town at the eastern tip of Java in Indonesia, facing Bali across the Bali Strait. It covers much of the territory of the former Hindu kingdom of Blambangan, which the Dutch East India Company conquered in the 1760s and 1770s.

berke.s: Berke was khan of the Golden Horde from 1257 to 1266, a grandson of Genghis Khan through Jochi. He was the first Mongol ruler of the Horde to adopt Islam, and he fought his cousin Hülegü of the Ilkhanate over the Caucasus, allying with the Mamluk sultanate of Egypt against him.

biatec.s: Biatec is a name, probably that of a Celtic ruler, inscribed on large silver coins minted in the 1st century BCE at the oppidum on the site of modern Bratislava, in the lands of the Boii. The coins are among the most important Celtic finds in central Europe, and the Biatec…

boiohaemum.s: Boiohaemum was the Latin name, recorded by Roman writers such as Tacitus, for the land of the Boii, the Celtic people who lived in what is now the Czech Republic. After the Germanic Marcomanni settled there around the turn of the era the name remained in use, and it is the…

bratislava.s: Bratislava is the capital of Slovakia, on the Danube near the borders with Austria and Hungary. A Celtic oppidum of the Boii stood there in the 1st century BCE.

baghdadi-jews.s: The Baghdadi Jews were communities of Arabic-speaking Jews from Iraq and neighbouring lands who settled in the trading ports of India and East Asia from the late 18th century. Their main centres were Bombay, Calcutta, Rangoon, Singapore and Shanghai, and leading families such…

bone-regency.s: Bone Regency is a regency in South Sulawesi province, Indonesia, on the western shore of the Gulf of Bone. It covers the heartland of the former Bugis sultanate of Bone, one of the most powerful states of Sulawesi, and its capital is Watampone.

begho.s: Begho was a trading town in what is now the Bono Region of Ghana, near the edge of the forest. From about the 11th century to the early 18th century it linked the gold and kola producing forest with the Mande traders of the Niger, and had separate quarters for Muslim merchants…

brahmanabad.s: Brahmanabad was an ancient city in lower Sindh, in present-day Pakistan, whose ruins lie near Shahdadpur in Sanghar District. It was a provincial centre of the Brahman dynasty of Chach and Dahir, and was taken by Muhammad ibn Qasim during the Arab conquest of Sindh in 712.

brazilian-democratic-movement.s: The Brazilian Democratic Movement, or MDB, was created in 1965–1966 as the only legal opposition party under the military dictatorship, alongside the government party ARENA. It grew into the main channel of opposition to the regime, and after the return to a multi-party system…

bato-the-daesitiate.s: Bato the Daesitiate was a leader of the Daesitiates of central Bosnia and the principal commander of the Great Illyrian Revolt against Rome in 6–9 CE. He fought alongside Bato the Breucian, but had him executed in 8 CE for betraying the rising.

brigantia.s: Brigantia was a Celtic goddess worshipped in northern Britain in the Roman period, known from inscriptions and a relief found at Birrens in Scotland. Her name, meaning 'the high one', is linked to that of the Brigantes, whose patron deity she probably was, and Roman…

brigid-goddess.s: Brigid is a goddess of early Irish mythology, a daughter of the Dagda associated with poetry, healing and smithcraft. Her feast fell at Imbolc, the start of spring.

blantyre.s: Blantyre is the main commercial city of Malawi, in the Shire Highlands of the south. It was founded in 1876 as a Church of Scotland mission and named after the Scottish birthplace of David Livingstone.

belmopan.s: Belmopan is the capital of Belize, a planned city built in the interior of the country in the 1960s. The government decided to move the capital from coastal Belize City after Hurricane Hattie devastated it in 1961, and Belmopan became the seat of government in 1970.

belize-estate-and-produce-company.s: The Belize Estate and Produce Company was a British firm founded in 1875 that became the largest landowner in British Honduras. Exporting mahogany and other timber, it controlled a large share of the colony's land and economy for most of the colonial period, and its power was…

bevin-sforza-plan.s: The Bevin–Sforza plan was a proposal agreed in May 1949 by the British foreign secretary Ernest Bevin and the Italian foreign minister Carlo Sforza for the future of Italy's former colony of Libya. It would have placed Tripolitania under Italian, Cyrenaica under British and…

bacolor.s: Bacolor is a town in the province of Pampanga on Luzon in the Philippines. During the British occupation of Manila in 1762–1764 Simón de Anda y Salazar made it the seat of the Spanish resistance and temporary capital of the colony.

bridgetown.s: Bridgetown is the capital and main port of Barbados, on Carlisle Bay on the island's south-west coast. Founded by English settlers in 1628, it became a centre of the Atlantic sugar and slave trade and the seat of British governors in the eastern Caribbean.

bretons.s: The Bretons are a Celtic people of Brittany in north-western France. Their ancestors include Britons who migrated from Britain to Armorica between the 4th and 7th centuries and gave the region its name and the Breton language.

bolkiah.s: Bolkiah was the fifth sultan of Brunei, who reigned from about 1485 to 1524. Remembered in legend as Nakhoda Ragam, the singing captain, he led naval expeditions that extended Brunei's power over much of the coast of Borneo and into the Philippines, including Manila.

bangsamoro.s: Bangsamoro, officially the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao, is an autonomous region of the southern Philippines created in 2019. It replaced the earlier Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao after the peace agreement between the government and the Moro Islamic…

bukey-khan.s: Bukey Khan was a Kazakh sultan of the Junior Juz, a son of Nurali Khan, who founded the Inner or Bukey Horde. In 1801 the Russian emperor Paul I allowed him to lead some 5,000 families across the Ural River into the steppe between the Ural and the Volga, left empty by the…

berau-sultanate.s: The Berau Sultanate was a Malay Muslim state on the Berau River in north-eastern Borneo, in what is now East Kalimantan, Indonesia. It held influence over neighbouring Bulungan and stood between the spheres of the Sulu Sultanate and Kutai.

battle-of-samugarh.s: The Battle of Samugarh was fought on 29 May 1658 near Agra between Dara Shikoh, heir of the ailing Mughal emperor Shah Jahan, and his brothers Aurangzeb and Murad Bakhsh. Aurangzeb's victory, in which Rao Chhatrasal of Bundi and many other Rajput allies of Dara were killed,…

bayreuth.s: Bayreuth is a town in Upper Franconia, northern Bavaria, Germany. Under the Franconian Hohenzollerns it became in the early 17th century the residence of the margraves of Brandenburg-Kulmbach, thereafter called Brandenburg-Bayreuth, whose court built the Margravial Opera…

brandenburg-ansbach.s: Brandenburg-Ansbach was a principality of the Holy Roman Empire in Franconia, ruled by a branch of the Hohenzollerns from its capital at Ansbach. It emerged from the Franconian lands of the burgraves of Nuremberg, divided in 1398, and was held as a margraviate by princes of…

buton-island.s: Buton is an island off the south-eastern peninsula of Sulawesi, Indonesia, in the province of Southeast Sulawesi. Its main town, Baubau, was the seat of the Sultanate of Buton, which adopted Islam in the 16th century and controlled sea routes between Makassar and the Moluccas.

band-e-amir-dam.s: Band-e Amir is a dam on the Kur River in Fars, Iran, north-east of Shiraz, built in the 10th century for the Buyid ruler Adud al-Dawla. Its masonry weir raised the river to irrigate the surrounding plain and drove water-mills.

baalat-gebal.s: Baalat Gebal, 'the Lady of Byblos', was the chief goddess of the Phoenician city of Byblos. Her temple received offerings from Egyptian kings from the Old Kingdom onwards, and the Egyptians identified her with Hathor.

byzas.s: Byzas was the legendary founder of Byzantium, the Greek city on the Bosporus that later became Constantinople and Istanbul. According to tradition he led settlers from Megara in the 7th century BCE, after the Delphic oracle told them to settle opposite the 'land of the blind',…

bohechio.s: Bohechío was the paramount cacique of Jaragua in south-western Hispaniola when Columbus arrived, ruling from a town near modern Léogâne and receiving tribute from many lesser chiefs. He received Bartholomew Columbus in 1497 and agreed to pay tribute in cotton and cassava bread…

broch.s: A broch is a type of Iron Age drystone tower found in northern and western Scotland, especially in Caithness, Orkney and Shetland. Built mostly between about 400 BCE and 100 CE, brochs have hollow double walls containing stairs and galleries.

battle-of-marj-rahit-684.s: The Battle of Marj Rahit was fought in August 684 north of Damascus between the Umayyad Marwan I, backed by the Kalb tribes, and the Qays tribes under al-Dahhak ibn Qays, who supported the caliph Ibn al-Zubayr. Marwan's victory secured Syria for the Umayyads during the Second…

bandua.s: Bandua was a god of the pre-Roman peoples of western Iberia, worshipped in what is now northern and central Portugal, Galicia and western Spain. He is known from dozens of Latin altar inscriptions of the Roman period, where his name often carries an epithet linking him to a…

brinno.s: Brinno was a chieftain of the Cananefates, a Germanic people of the western Rhine delta. According to Tacitus, in 69 CE his people raised him on a shield to proclaim him leader, the earliest record of that custom, and he opened the Batavian revolt of Julius Civilis by…

bigbury-camp.s: Bigbury Camp is an Iron Age hillfort near Canterbury in Kent, England, covering about 10 hectares. It is probably the stronghold that Julius Caesar's Seventh Legion stormed in 54 BCE, and finds from it include iron tools, slave chains and horse gear.

britons-celtic-people.s: The Britons were the Celtic-speaking inhabitants of Great Britain from the Iron Age through the Roman period and the early Middle Ages. They spoke Brittonic languages, the ancestors of Welsh, Cornish and Breton, and were organised in peoples such as the Catuvellauni and Iceni.

battle-of-vogelinsegg.s: The Battle of Vögelinsegg was fought on 15 May 1403 near Speicher in Appenzell, Switzerland, in the Appenzell Wars. Appenzell peasants, aided by men from Schwyz and Glarus, ambushed and defeated the forces of the abbot of St Gall and the allied Swabian imperial cities.

battle-of-stoss.s: The Battle of Stoss was fought on 17 June 1405 at the Stoss pass between Altstätten and Gais, Switzerland, in the Appenzell Wars. The Appenzellers, fighting downhill in heavy rain, defeated an army of Duke Frederick IV of Austria.

basel-landschaft.s: Basel-Landschaft is a canton of north-western Switzerland, with its capital at Liestal. It was formed in 1833 when the rural districts, after armed conflict with the city of Basel over political rights, broke away from the canton of Basel.

basel-stadt.s: Basel-Stadt is a canton of north-western Switzerland made up of the city of Basel and the two small communes of Riehen and Bettingen, on the Rhine where Switzerland meets France and Germany. It was created in 1833 when the rural districts split off as Basel-Landschaft.

berthold-v-duke-of-zahringen.s: Berthold V was the last duke of Zähringen, a powerful dynasty of south-western Germany and western Switzerland, ruling from 1186 to 1218. He founded the city of Bern in 1191 to strengthen his hold on the lands between the Jura and the Alps, and declined the German crown…

battle-of-grauholz.s: The Battle of Grauholz was fought on 5 March 1798 north-east of Bern, during the French invasion of Switzerland. A French army under General Schauenburg defeated the Bernese forces, and the city of Bern surrendered the same day.

battle-of-laupen.s: The Battle of Laupen was fought on 21 June 1339 near Laupen, west of Bern, between Bern, supported by troops from the Forest Cantons, and a coalition of regional nobles allied with the city of Fribourg. Bern's victory secured its expansion and drew it closer to the Swiss…

battle-of-morat.s: The Battle of Morat was fought on 22 June 1476 at Murten, west of Bern, during the Burgundian Wars. The Swiss Confederates relieved the town, held by Adrian von Bubenberg against a siege by Charles the Bold, duke of Burgundy, and routed his army with heavy losses.

berthold-iv-of-zahringen.s: Berthold IV of Zähringen was Duke of Zähringen from 1152 until his death in 1186 and rector of Burgundy, the imperial office that gave his family authority west of the Rhine. He strengthened Zähringen power in the Swiss plateau by founding towns, above all Fribourg in 1157 on…

battle-of-kappel.s: The Battle of Kappel was fought on 11 October 1531 near Kappel am Albis, between the Catholic cantons of central Switzerland and Protestant Zürich. The Catholic forces won, and the reformer Huldrych Zwingli, who accompanied the Zürich army as chaplain, was killed.

battle-of-guandu.s: The Battle of Guandu was fought in 200 CE near the Yellow River in northern China between the warlords Cao Cao and Yuan Shao. Though heavily outnumbered, Cao Cao won by raiding and burning Yuan Shao's supply depot at Wuchao.

biobio-river.s: The Biobío is one of the longest rivers of Chile, rising in the Andes and flowing north-west to the Pacific at Concepción. For three centuries after the Mapuche victory at Curalaba in 1598 it marked the frontier between the Spanish colony and the independent Mapuche lands to…

battle-of-chacabuco.s: The Battle of Chacabuco was fought on 12 February 1817 north of Santiago, Chile. The Army of the Andes under José de San Martín and Bernardo O'Higgins, having crossed the Andes from Argentina, defeated the royalist army.

battle-of-curalaba.s: The Battle of Curalaba was fought on 23 December 1598 in southern Chile, when Mapuche warriors under Pelantaro ambushed and killed the Spanish governor Martín García Óñez de Loyola and his escort. The victory set off a general uprising that destroyed the Spanish towns south of…

battle-of-maipu.s: The Battle of Maipú was fought on 5 April 1818 near Santiago, Chile. The patriot army under José de San Martín decisively defeated the royalist forces of Mariano Osorio, a few weeks after Chile had proclaimed its independence.

battle-of-tucapel.s: The Battle of Tucapel was fought in December 1553 in southern Chile, when Mapuche forces led by Lautaro destroyed a small Spanish column under Pedro de Valdivia, the conqueror and governor of Chile. Valdivia was captured and killed.

baracoa.s: Baracoa is a town on the north-eastern coast of Cuba, founded in 1511 by Diego Velázquez de Cuéllar as the first Spanish settlement on the island. It served briefly as the colony's capital before Santiago de Cuba replaced it.

battle-of-carabobo.s: The Battle of Carabobo was fought on 24 June 1821 south-west of Valencia, Venezuela. Simón Bolívar's patriot army defeated the royalist forces of Miguel de la Torre, with the British Legion playing a notable part.

brasilia.s: Brasília is the capital of Brazil, built on the central plateau and inaugurated on 21 April 1960 under President Juscelino Kubitschek. It was planned by Lúcio Costa, with major buildings by Oscar Niemeyer, to move government away from the coast and open up the interior.

battle-of-pichincha.s: The Battle of Pichincha was fought on 24 May 1822 on the slopes of the Pichincha volcano above Quito. Patriot forces under Antonio José de Sucre, including troops sent by Bolívar and from Peru, defeated the royalist army of Melchor Aymerich.

borut.s: Borut was a Slavic prince of Carantania, in what is now Carinthia and Slovenia, in the mid-8th century. Around 743, threatened by the Avars, he sought help from the Bavarians, who defeated the Avars but made Carantania subject to Bavaria.

bobbio-abbey.s: Bobbio Abbey was a monastery in the Trebbia valley of northern Italy, founded in 614 by the Irish missionary Columbanus on land granted by the Lombard king Agilulf. It became one of the great centres of learning of early medieval Europe, with a library of rare classical and…

brougham.s: Brougham is a village near Penrith in Cumbria, England, at the crossing of the River Eamont. It was the site of the Roman fort of Brocavum, whose cemetery and inscriptions, including a milestone naming the civitas of the Carvetii, have been found nearby.

battle-of-montjuic-1641.s: The Battle of Montjuïc was fought on 26 January 1641 on the hill of Montjuïc above Barcelona. Catalan militia and French troops repulsed the royal army of Philip IV under the Marquis of Los Vélez, which had advanced on the city.

barda.s: Barda is a town in central Azerbaijan near the Kura river, the ancient Partav, which replaced Kabala as the capital of Caucasian Albania in the 5th century. Under the Arabs, as Bardha'a, it was one of the largest cities of the Caucasus and the seat of governors of Arran.

battle-of-dargo.s: The Battle of Dargo was a Russian expedition in 1845 under Prince Mikhail Vorontsov against Imam Shamil's capital at Dargo in Chechnya. The Russians took and burned the village, but on their retreat through the forests they suffered heavy losses to Shamil's fighters.

battle-of-dekhele.s: The Battle of Dékhelé was fought on 26 October 1886 in Cayor, in present-day Senegal, between French colonial troops and the followers of Lat Dior Diop, the former Damel of Cayor. Lat Dior, who had long opposed the building of the Dakar–Saint-Louis railway across his country,…

buffalo-creek-reservation.s: The Buffalo Creek Reservation was a Seneca reservation in western New York, along Buffalo Creek near present-day Buffalo, created after the American Revolutionary War. Displaced Iroquois, including many Cayuga and Onondaga, gathered there, and it became a centre of…

bennachie.s: Bennachie is a range of hills in Aberdeenshire, north-east Scotland, whose best-known summit, the Mither Tap (518 m), is crowned by the ruins of a hillfort, probably of the Pictish period. Some historians have proposed it as the site of the Battle of Mons Graupius of 83 CE,…

botorrita.s: Botorrita is a village in the province of Zaragoza, Spain, on the site of the Celtiberian town of Contrebia Belaisca. Excavations there found four inscribed bronze plaques of the 2nd and 1st centuries BCE, three in the Celtiberian language and one in Latin recording a…

beturia.s: Beturia was the ancient name of the region between the Guadiana and Guadalquivir rivers in south-western Iberia, roughly northern Huelva, southern Badajoz and part of the province of Seville. Pliny the Elder divided it into a Celtic part, whose people were linked to the…

battle-of-degsastan.s: The Battle of Degsastan was fought in 603 between Æthelfrith of Bernicia and Áedán mac Gabráin, king of Dál Riata, who led a large army including Irish allies. Æthelfrith won decisively despite heavy losses, including his brother Theodbald, and Bede wrote that no king of the…

bases-organicas.s: The Bases Orgánicas were a centralist constitution of Mexico, drafted by a junta of notables under Antonio López de Santa Anna and promulgated on 12 June 1843. They replaced the Siete Leyes of 1836, kept the departments under central control and strengthened the presidency.

battle-of-cissa.s: The Battle of Cissa was fought in 218 BCE near the town of Cissa, north of Tarraco in north-eastern Spain, early in the Second Punic War. Gnaeus Cornelius Scipio Calvus, who had landed at Emporion, defeated the Carthaginian commander Hanno, left to hold the region north of the…

bharmour.s: Bharmour is a town in Chamba district of Himachal Pradesh, India, in the upper Ravi valley. As Brahmapura it was by tradition the first capital of the Chamba state, founded around the 6th century, until the capital moved to Chamba in the 10th century.

bhuri-singh.s: Bhuri Singh was Raja of the princely state of Chamba in the western Himalayas from 1904 to 1919. A reforming ruler, he donated his family's collection of Pahari paintings and other objects to found the Bhuri Singh Museum in Chamba, opened in 1908, which preserves much of the…

ballarpur.s: Ballarpur is a town on the Wardha river in Chandrapur district of Maharashtra, India. It served as a capital of the Gond kingdom of Chanda before the court moved to Chanda (Chandrapur) in the 15th or 16th century, and its fort survives on the riverbank.

bhima-i-chaulukya-dynasty.s: Bhima I was king of the Chaulukya dynasty of Gujarat from about 1022 to 1064. Early in his reign Mahmud of Ghazni sacked the Somnath temple in 1025, but the kingdom recovered, and Bhima fought the Paramaras of Malwa.

baidicheng.s: Baidicheng, the "White Emperor City", is a historic fortress and temple site on a hill above the Yangtze at the entrance to the Qutang Gorge, the first of the Three Gorges, near Fengjie in Chongqing, China. Tradition links its name to Gongsun Shu, who styled himself the White…

battle-of-lake-poyang.s: The Battle of Lake Poyang was a naval battle fought on Lake Poyang in Jiangxi from August to October 1363 between the fleets of Zhu Yuanzhang and Chen Youliang, rival leaders of the rebellions against the Yuan dynasty. Chen's larger fleet of tower ships had been besieging…

bhavavarman-i.s: Bhavavarman I was a king of Chenla in present-day Cambodia in the second half of the 6th century. With his relative Chitrasena, the future Mahendravarman, he attacked Funan, the older kingdom of the Mekong delta, and Chenla displaced it as the main power of the region.

bundela.s: The Bundelas are a Rajput clan of central India who gave their name to Bundelkhand, the region between the Yamuna and the Vindhya hills. Rising to power in the 16th century, they ruled from Orchha, where the Mughal ally Bir Singh Deo built palaces and temples.

battle-of-ackia.s: The Battle of Ackia was fought on 26 May 1736 near modern Tupelo, Mississippi, when a French army under Jean-Baptiste Le Moyne de Bienville, governor of Louisiana, with Choctaw allies, attacked the fortified Chickasaw village of Ackia. The Chickasaw, supplied by British…

battle-of-mokuohai.s: The Battle of Mokuʻōhai was fought in July 1782 near Keʻei in South Kona on the island of Hawaiʻi, between the forces of Kiwalaʻō, heir of Kalaniʻōpuʻu, and his cousin Kamehameha. Kiwalaʻō was killed, and the island was divided among Kamehameha, Keōua and other chiefs.

balowoka.s: Balowoka, "those who crossed", is the name given in Tumbuka tradition to traders and ivory hunters who crossed Lake Malawi from the east in the late 18th century. Their leader, remembered as Gonapamuhanya, settled in the north of present-day Malawi, and his descendants founded…

brihadishvara-temple.s: The Brihadishvara Temple at Thanjavur in Tamil Nadu, India, is a Hindu temple dedicated to Shiva, built by the Chola king Rajaraja I and completed in 1010. Its granite tower, about 66 metres high, was among the tallest buildings of its time, and its walls carry Chola…

bunei.s: Bunei was king of Chūzan on Okinawa from 1396 to 1405, a son of Satto. He maintained tribute relations with Ming China and was formally invested as king by the Ming court.

brendan-the-navigator.s: Brendan the Navigator (c. 484–c. 577) was an Irish monk and saint, born according to tradition near Tralee in County Kerry. He founded several monasteries, most famously Clonfert in County Galway around 557.

battle-of-ituzaingo.s: The Battle of Ituzaingó, called Passo do Rosário in Brazil, was fought on 20 February 1827 in Rio Grande do Sul between the army of the United Provinces of the Río de la Plata under Carlos María de Alvear and the Brazilian imperial army under the Marquis of Barbacena. The…

bodo-kachari-peoples.s: The Bodo-Kachari peoples are a group of Tibeto-Burman-speaking communities of north-eastern India, among them the Bodo, Dimasa, Tiwa, Garo, Rabha and Chutia, whose languages belong to the Boro-Garo branch. Living in the Brahmaputra valley and the surrounding hills, they…

banavasi.s: Banavasi is an ancient temple town in Uttara Kannada district, Karnataka, India, on the Varada river. Mentioned in early Buddhist sources, it was a centre of the Chutu rulers and then, from the mid-4th century, the capital of the Kadamba dynasty, the first native dynasty to…

battle-of-knockdoe.s: The Battle of Knockdoe was fought on 19 August 1504 near Lackagh in County Galway, Ireland. The Lord Deputy, Gerald FitzGerald, 8th Earl of Kildare, with allies from the Pale, Ulster and Connacht, defeated Ulick Fionn Burke of Clanricarde and his ally Turlough O'Brien of Thomond.

battle-of-sentinum.s: The Battle of Sentinum was fought in 295 BCE near Sentinum in Umbria, close to modern Sassoferrato, between Rome and a coalition of Samnites and Senone Gauls, with Etruscan and Umbrian backing. The consuls Quintus Fabius Maximus Rullianus and Publius Decius Mus won a…

barbuda.s: Barbuda is a flat coral island in the Leeward Islands of the Caribbean, about 45 kilometres north of Antigua. From 1685 it was leased to the Codrington family, who used it to raise food and livestock for their Antigua plantations, and it was annexed to Antigua in 1860.

barbados-slave-code.s: The Barbados Slave Code of 1661, formally An Act for the better ordering and governing of Negroes, was a law passed by the colonial assembly of Barbados to regulate enslaved Africans. It treated the enslaved as property, imposed harsh punishments and gave masters broad powers…

bonaire.s: Bonaire is an island in the Leeward Antilles of the southern Caribbean, east of Curaçao and off the coast of Venezuela. Spain claimed it from 1499, and the Dutch West India Company took it in 1636, using it for salt production and cattle raising worked by enslaved Africans.

baptist-war.s: The Baptist War, or Christmas Rebellion, was a rising of up to 60,000 enslaved people in western Jamaica that began on 25 December 1831. Led by the Baptist deacon Samuel Sharpe, it started as a strike for wages and turned into an armed revolt in which many plantations were…

birchtown.s: Birchtown is a community near Shelburne in Nova Scotia, Canada, founded in 1783 by about 1,500 Black Loyalists who had escaped slavery to support the British in the American Revolutionary War. It was then the largest free Black settlement in North America.

brisbane.s: Brisbane is the capital of Queensland, Australia, on the Brisbane River near Moreton Bay. It began in 1825 as a penal settlement for convicts who had reoffended in New South Wales, moved from Redcliffe, and was opened to free settlers in 1842.

baptists.s: Baptists are Protestant Christians who practise the baptism of believers, usually by immersion, rather than of infants, and stress the independence of each congregation. The movement arose among English Separatists in the early 17th century, led by John Smyth and Thomas Helwys.

brimstone-hill-fortress.s: Brimstone Hill Fortress is a British fortress on a steep volcanic hill on the west coast of Saint Kitts, built mainly between 1690 and 1790 by enslaved African labourers. Known as the 'Gibraltar of the West Indies', it fell to a French siege in 1782 but was returned under the…

black-war.s: The Black War was a period of violent conflict between British colonists and Aboriginal Tasmanians in Van Diemen's Land from the mid-1820s to about 1832. As settlement spread across the island, Aboriginal attacks on settlers were met by killings and the declaration of martial…

bay-street-boys.s: The Bay Street Boys were the white merchant elite of Nassau, named after the city's main commercial street, who dominated the politics and economy of the Bahamas in the late 19th and 20th centuries. Through the United Bahamian Party, led by Roland Symonette, they controlled…

bermuda.s: Bermuda is a British Overseas Territory consisting of a group of small islands in the North Atlantic, about 1,000 kilometres east of North Carolina. It was settled by the English after the wreck of the Sea Venture in 1609 and became one of England's oldest colonies, run by the…

belmanna-riots.s: The Belmanna riots were an uprising of labourers at Roxborough in Tobago in May 1876, named after Corporal Belmanna, a police officer who had shot a woman during unrest on an estate. The crowd killed Belmanna and burned buildings before troops restored order.

ballarat.s: Ballarat is a city in central Victoria, Australia, founded after gold was discovered there in August 1851. It became one of the richest goldfields of the Victorian gold rush, and in 1854 its miners rose against licence fees at the Eureka Stockade.

bendigo.s: Bendigo is a city in central Victoria, Australia, which grew after gold was discovered there in 1851. It became one of the richest goldfields in the world, later mined from deep quartz reefs, and attracted a large Chinese community.

battle-of-bataan.s: The Battle of Bataan was fought from January to April 1942 on the Bataan Peninsula of Luzon, where American and Filipino forces under Douglas MacArthur withdrew after the Japanese invasion of the Philippines. Short of food and medicine, about 75,000 defenders surrendered on 9…

battle-of-corregidor-1942.s: The Battle of Corregidor was the last stand of American and Filipino forces in the Philippines in 1942, on the fortified island at the mouth of Manila Bay. After months of bombardment, Japanese troops landed on 5 May, and General Jonathan Wainwright surrendered the next day.

battle-of-leyte.s: The Battle of Leyte began with the American landing on the island of Leyte in the central Philippines on 20 October 1944, when Douglas MacArthur returned accompanied by President Sergio Osmeña. The nearby naval Battle of Leyte Gulf destroyed much of the Japanese fleet, and by…

bormida.s: The Bormida is a river of north-western Italy that rises in the Ligurian Apennines and flows north through southern Piedmont. It joins the Tanaro just east of Alessandria, a city founded in 1168 at the meeting of the two rivers.

battle-of-campaldino.s: The Battle of Campaldino was fought on 11 June 1289 in the upper Arno valley between the Guelphs of Florence and their allies and the Ghibellines of Arezzo. The Florentine victory, in which the Ghibelline bishop of Arezzo Guglielmino degli Ubertini was killed, confirmed Guelph…

brenta.s: The Brenta is a river of north-eastern Italy, about 174 km long, rising in the lakes of Caldonazzo and Levico in Trentino. It flows through the Valsugana and past Bassano and Padua to the Adriatic south of the Venetian lagoon.

benedetto-antelami.s: Benedetto Antelami was an Italian sculptor and architect active in Parma and the Po valley. His relief of the Deposition in Parma Cathedral is dated 1178, and in 1196 he began the octagonal baptistery of Parma, designing both its architecture and its sculpture, including…

black-and-white-guelphs.s: The Black and White Guelphs were rival factions into which the Guelph party of Tuscany split around 1300, beginning in a feud within the Cancellieri family of Pistoia. In Florence the Blacks, led by Corso Donati and backed by Pope Boniface VIII, took power in 1301 with the…

bisenzio.s: The Bisenzio is a river of Tuscany that flows from the Apennines south through Prato into the Arno near Florence. Its water powered fulling mills and dye works that sustained Prato's woollen cloth industry from the Middle Ages, a canal system still known as the gore.

basilica-of-santandrea-vercelli.s: The Basilica of Sant'Andrea in Vercelli, Piedmont, was built from 1219 to 1227 for an abbey founded by Cardinal Guala Bicchieri, endowed with English revenues from his legation. It is one of the earliest Gothic buildings in Italy, combining Romanesque Lombard façade and towers…

basilica-of-san-zeno.s: The Basilica of San Zeno in Verona is a Romanesque church built mainly in the 12th century over the tomb of Verona's patron saint, Bishop Zeno. Its façade has a large rose window and bronze doors with biblical reliefs, and its high altar holds a triptych by Andrea Mantegna.

bopolu.s: Bopolu is a town in north-western Liberia, now the capital of Gbarpolu County. In the early 19th century it was the centre of the Condo Confederation of Sao Boso, a market town where caravans from the interior exchanged goods with traders from the coast.

battle-of-benburb.s: The Battle of Benburb was fought on 5 June 1646 in County Tyrone, where the Ulster army of Confederate Ireland under Owen Roe O'Neill routed a Scottish Covenanter army led by Robert Monro. It was the greatest Irish victory of the Confederate Wars, but divisions among the…

battle-of-appomattox-court-house.s: The Battle of Appomattox Court House, fought in Virginia on 9 April 1865, was the last engagement of Robert E. Lee's Army of Northern Virginia. Cut off by Union forces under Ulysses S. Grant after the fall of Richmond, Lee surrendered that day on generous terms.

battle-of-fort-sumter.s: The Battle of Fort Sumter, on 12–13 April 1861, opened the American Civil War, when Confederate batteries bombarded the federal fort in the harbour of Charleston, South Carolina. Its garrison under Major Robert Anderson surrendered after a day and a half.

battle-of-gettysburg.s: The Battle of Gettysburg, fought in Pennsylvania on 1–3 July 1863, was the largest battle of the American Civil War. The Union Army of the Potomac under George Meade defeated Robert E. Lee's invasion of the North, ending with the failed Confederate assault known as Pickett's…

bhamo.s: Bhamo is a town in Kachin State in northern Myanmar, on the Irrawaddy River near the Chinese border. For centuries it was the river port for the caravan trade between Burma and Yunnan.

boma.s: Boma is a port town on the Congo River estuary in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Long a trading post for European merchants, including slave traders, it became the capital of King Leopold II's Congo Free State in 1886 and of the Belgian Congo until the capital moved to…

baltimore-county-cork.s: Baltimore is a coastal village in the far south-west of County Cork, Ireland, overlooking Roaringwater Bay and the islands of Sherkin and Cape Clear. It was a stronghold of the O'Driscoll lords, whose castle of Dún na Séad stands there.

battle-of-leucimme.s: The Battle of Leucimme was a naval battle fought in 435 BCE off the promontory of Leucimme on Corfu, in which the fleet of Corcyra defeated a Corinthian fleet. The two cities were quarrelling over their joint colony of Epidamnus.

battle-of-sybota.s: The Battle of Sybota was a naval battle fought in 433 BCE near the Sybota islands, off the coast of Epirus, between Corinth and its allies and Corcyra, supported by an Athenian squadron. It was among the largest sea battles between Greek states up to that time.

bacchiadae.s: The Bacchiadae were a Dorian aristocratic clan that ruled Corinth as a closed oligarchy from about the mid-8th century BCE, marrying only among themselves. Under their rule Corinth founded colonies at Corcyra and Syracuse and grew rich from trade across the Isthmus.

breiddin.s: The Breiddin is a steep volcanic hill above the River Severn in Powys, Wales, close to the English border. Its summit carries a large hillfort first fortified in the late Bronze Age, occupied through much of the Iron Age and used again in the late Roman period.

battle-of-ponte-novu.s: The Battle of Ponte Novu was fought on 8–9 May 1769 at a bridge over the Golo river in northern Corsica, between the forces of Pasquale Paoli's Corsican Republic and a French army under the Comte de Vaux. The French victory ended effective Corsican resistance, and Paoli went…

battle-of-zhovti-vody.s: The Battle of Zhovti Vody was fought in April and May 1648 in central Ukraine, the first major battle of the Khmelnytsky Uprising. Cossacks under Bohdan Khmelnytsky, allied with Crimean Tatars under Tugay Bey, destroyed an advance force of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth…

bernard-vii-count-of-armagnac.s: Bernard VII was count of Armagnac from 1391 and the leader of the Armagnac faction in the French civil war against the Burgundians. His daughter married Charles, Duke of Orléans, whose father had been murdered on the orders of John the Fearless, and Bernard became constable of…

battle-of-al-mansurah.s: The Battle of al-Mansurah was fought in February 1250 in the Nile Delta of Egypt during the Seventh Crusade led by Louis IX of France. Crusaders under the king's brother Robert of Artois charged into the town of al-Mansurah, where they were trapped and killed by Ayyubid and…

bera-count-of-barcelona.s: Bera was the first count of Barcelona after the Franks captured the city in 801, a Goth probably descended from William of Gellone. Accused of treason and of dealings with al-Andalus, he lost a judicial duel at Aachen in 820 and was deposed and exiled to Rouen, where he died.

bentheim-castle.s: Bentheim Castle is a hilltop castle in Bad Bentheim, Lower Saxony, Germany, built on a sandstone ridge near the Dutch border. First recorded in the late 11th or early 12th century, it was the seat of the counts of Bentheim and is one of the largest castles in north-west Germany.

bernat-i-count-of-besalu.s: Bernat I, called Tallaferro ('iron-cutter'), was count of Besalú from 988 to 1020 and a brother of Abbot Oliba. He took part in the Catalan expedition to Córdoba in 1010 and in 1017 obtained from the pope a bishopric for Besalú, which did not outlast him.

bernat-iii-of-besalu.s: Bernat III was the last count of Besalú, in north-eastern Catalonia. He married Ximena, a daughter of Ramon Berenguer III of Barcelona, and when he died without children in 1111 the county passed to Barcelona under an agreement with his father-in-law.

besalu.s: Besalú is a medieval town in the Garrotxa district of Catalonia, Spain, on the Fluvià river. From the 9th century until 1111 it was the seat of the counts of Besalú, after which it passed to the counts of Barcelona.

beauce.s: The Beauce is a flat, fertile plain of north-central France, between Chartres and Orléans, long known as the granary of France for its wheat. In the Middle Ages much of it lay within the lands of the counts of Blois and Chartres.

baldwin-ii-margrave-of-flanders.s: Baldwin II, called the Bald, was count of Flanders from 879 to 918, son of Baldwin I Iron Arm and Judith, daughter of Charles the Bald. Using the disorder of the Viking raids, he built fortresses and gathered counties, abbeys and royal lands into a single principality.

battle-of-bouvines.s: The Battle of Bouvines was fought on 27 July 1214 near Lille in Flanders, where Philip II of France defeated the army of Emperor Otto IV, Count Ferrand of Flanders and Renaud de Dammartin, allies of King John of England. The victory secured French control of Normandy and…

bernat-guillem-of-cerdanya.s: Bernat Guillem was count of Cerdanya from 1109 to 1117, succeeding his brother William Jordan, who had gone on crusade and become count of Tripoli. He was the last of the line of counts of Cerdanya descended from Wilfred the Hairy, and on his death without heirs the county…

bar-sur-aube.s: Bar-sur-Aube is a small town on the Aube in the Champagne region of north-eastern France. In the 12th and 13th centuries it hosted one of the six Champagne fairs, held each spring, where merchants from Italy, Flanders and across Europe traded under the protection of the counts…

bernard-iv-of-comminges.s: Bernard IV was count of Comminges from about 1176 to 1225. During the Albigensian Crusade he sided with his overlord Raymond VI of Toulouse and with Peter II of Aragon against Simon de Montfort, and he was present at the Battle of Muret in 1213.

beatrice-of-provence.s: Beatrice of Provence was countess of Provence and Forcalquier from 1245, the youngest daughter of Count Ramon Berenguer IV; her three sisters married the kings of France and England and Richard of Cornwall. Her marriage in 1246 to Charles of Anjou, brother of Louis IX, brought…

beatrice-i-countess-of-burgundy.s: Beatrice I was countess of the Free County of Burgundy from 1148, the only child of Count Renaud III. Her marriage in 1156 to Emperor Frederick Barbarossa tied Burgundy to the Hohenstaufen, and she was crowned empress in 1167 and queen of Burgundy in 1178.

beatrice-of-bourbon.s: Beatrice of Bourbon was the heiress of the lordship of Bourbon through her mother Agnes. In 1272 she married Robert, Count of Clermont, the youngest son of Louis IX, and their son Louis I became the first duke of Bourbon in 1327.

battle-of-the-golden-spurs.s: The Battle of the Golden Spurs was fought on 11 July 1302 at Courtrai (Kortrijk) in Flanders, where an army of Flemish town militias fighting on foot destroyed a French cavalry army under Robert II of Artois. Hundreds of golden spurs taken from the dead knights were hung in a…

bruges.s: Bruges is a city in West Flanders, Belgium, linked to the North Sea by canals. From the 12th to the 15th century it was the commercial capital of north-western Europe, home of a Hanseatic office and Italian banking houses, a leading centre of the Flemish cloth trade and of…

bernard-roger-of-foix.s: Bernard-Roger was a son of Count Roger I of Carcassonne who, on the division of his father's lands around 1012, received the region around Foix together with the Couserans. His son Roger took the title of count of Foix, founding the line of counts that later inherited Béarn…

brugg.s: Brugg is a small town in the Swiss canton of Aargau, at a crossing of the Aare close to its confluence with the Reuss and the Limmat. Habsburg Castle, the ancestral seat of the Habsburg dynasty, stands on a hill nearby, and the Roman legionary camp of Vindonissa lay at…

battle-of-morgarten.s: The Battle of Morgarten was fought on 15 November 1315 near Lake Ägeri, where men of Schwyz and Uri ambushed a Habsburg army under Duke Leopold I of Austria on a narrow path between a steep slope and marshland. The heavily armed knights were routed.

battle-of-sempach.s: The Battle of Sempach was fought on 9 July 1386 near Sempach in the canton of Lucerne, where the Swiss Confederates defeated the army of Duke Leopold III of Austria, who was killed with many of his nobles. Legend credits Arnold von Winkelried with breaking the Habsburg line.

baldwin-vi-count-of-flanders.s: Baldwin VI (c. 1030–1070) was Count of Flanders from 1067 and, as Baldwin I, Count of Hainaut through his marriage in 1051 to Countess Richilde. The marriage joined Hainaut to the Flemish comital house.

bouxwiller.s: Bouxwiller, in German Buchsweiler, is a small town in northern Alsace, in the Bas-Rhin department of France. From the late 15th century it was the capital of the County of Hanau-Lichtenberg, governed from its castle, and from 1736 it passed with the county to the landgraves of…

brothers-grimm.s: The Brothers Grimm, Jacob (1785–1863) and Wilhelm (1786–1859), were German scholars born in Hanau who collected folk tales and founded the study of German language and literature. Their Children's and Household Tales, first published in 1812–1815, includes Snow White, Hansel…

berthold-vii-count-of-henneberg-schleusi.s: Berthold VII (1272–1340), called the Wise, was Count of Henneberg-Schleusingen, raised to the rank of princely count in 1310. He became one of the closest advisers of Emperor Louis IV the Bavarian, serving him as diplomat and as regent in Brandenburg for the emperor's young…

binnenhof.s: The Binnenhof is a complex of buildings in the centre of The Hague, Netherlands, that grew from the residence of the counts of Holland, begun by Count William II around 1250, with the great Hall of Knights (Ridderzaal) built under Floris V. Since the late 16th century it has…

battle-of-vlaardingen.s: The Battle of Vlaardingen was fought on 29 July 1018, when Count Dirk III of Holland defeated an imperial army under Duke Godfrey II of Lower Lorraine near his stronghold at Vlaardingen in the Maas delta. Emperor Henry II had sent the army to stop Dirk from levying tolls on…

budingen.s: Büdingen is a town in the Wetterau district of Hesse, Germany, known for its well-preserved medieval walls and old town. Its moated castle was the seat of the counts of Isenburg-Büdingen, who in the 18th century allowed religious dissenters, among them the Inspirationists and…

baldwin-iii-of-jerusalem.s: Baldwin III (1130–1163) was King of Jerusalem from 1143, at first under the regency of his mother Melisende, whom he pushed aside in 1152. He took part in the failed siege of Damascus during the Second Crusade in 1148 and captured Ascalon from the Fatimids in 1153, his…

burg-katz.s: Burg Katz (Katz Castle) is a castle above St. Goarshausen on the right bank of the Middle Rhine in Germany, built around 1371 by Count William II of Katzenelnbogen. Facing Rheinfels Castle across the river, it helped the counts control the Rhine tolls, and its popular name…
