burgdorf.s: Burgdorf is a town in the Swiss canton of Bern, on the Emme at the entrance to the Emmental. It grew below a castle of the dukes of Zähringen, passed to the counts of Kyburg in 1218 and was bought by Bern in 1384.

borgloon.s: Borgloon is a small town in the province of Limburg, Belgium, in the fruit-growing Haspengouw (Hesbaye) region. It was the original seat of the counts of Loon, whose county was annexed by the prince-bishopric of Liège in 1366, and it remained one of the 'good towns' of Liège.

brussels.s: Brussels is the capital of Belgium and the seat of the main institutions of the European Union and of NATO's headquarters. It grew from a settlement on the Senne, fortified by the counts of Louvain in the 11th century, into a residence of the dukes of Brabant and the…

battle-of-crecy.s: The Battle of Crécy was fought on 26 August 1346 near Crécy-en-Ponthieu in northern France, during the Hundred Years' War. Edward III of England, in a defensive position, defeated a much larger French army under Philip VI, as English and Welsh longbowmen broke repeated French…

belfort-gap.s: The Belfort Gap, or Burgundian Gate, is a lowland pass in eastern France between the Vosges to the north and the Jura to the south, linking the Rhine valley with the basins of the Saône and Rhône. Guarded by Montbéliard and later by the fortress of Belfort, it has been a major…

bregenz.s: Bregenz is the capital of the Austrian state of Vorarlberg, on the eastern shore of Lake Constance. On the site of the Roman town of Brigantium, it was ruled by the counts of Bregenz and then of Montfort, who sold it in stages to the Habsburgs in 1451 and 1523.

bagnolo-in-piano.s: Bagnolo in Piano is a small town in the province of Reggio Emilia, in the plain north of Reggio. From the 14th century it belonged, with Novellara, to a branch of the Gonzaga family, who held both as imperial fiefs until their line died out in 1728.

battle-of-sao-mamede.s: The Battle of São Mamede was fought on 24 June 1128 near Guimarães between Afonso Henriques and the forces of his mother, Countess Teresa, and her Galician ally Fernão Peres de Trava. Afonso's victory gave him control of the County of Portugal, and it is traditionally seen as…

bad-pyrmont.s: Bad Pyrmont is a spa town in Lower Saxony, in the Weser hills south-west of Hamelin. Its mineral springs made it one of Europe's fashionable spas from the 17th century, visited by Peter the Great and Goethe.

barmstedt.s: Barmstedt is a small town in the Pinneberg district of Schleswig-Holstein, north-west of Hamburg. In 1649 Christian Rantzau bought the district from the Duke of Holstein-Gottorp, and in 1650 it became the imperial County of Rantzau, governed from a castle on an island in the…

bielefeld.s: Bielefeld is a city in North Rhine-Westphalia, on a pass through the Teutoburg Forest. It was founded around 1214 by Count Hermann IV of Ravensberg below the Sparrenburg castle and became the main town of the county.

borgholzhausen.s: Borgholzhausen is a small town in the Gütersloh district of North Rhine-Westphalia, on the southern slope of the Teutoburg Forest. Above it stands the castle of Ravensberg, from which the counts of Ravensberg took their name in the 12th century.

battle-of-halmyros.s: The Battle of Halmyros was fought on 15 March 1311, probably near the Cephissus in Boeotia, between the Catalan Company and the army of Walter V of Brienne, Duke of Athens. The Catalans flooded the marshy ground in front of their lines, trapping the Frankish heavy cavalry, and…

bendorf.s: Bendorf is a town on the right bank of the Rhine just north of Koblenz, in Rhineland-Palatinate. The castle of the counts of Sayn, recorded from the 12th century, stands in the Sayn district of the town, beside Sayn Abbey and the 19th-century palace of the princes of…

bad-berleburg.s: Bad Berleburg is a town in the Siegen-Wittgenstein district of North Rhine-Westphalia, in the Rothaar hills. It was the residence of the counts, later princes, of Sayn-Wittgenstein-Berleburg, whose castle still dominates the town.

berleburg-bible.s: The Berleburg Bible is an eight-volume German Bible translation with a mystical and allegorical commentary, published at Berleburg from 1726 to 1742. Produced by radical Pietists under the protection of Count Casimir of Sayn-Wittgenstein-Berleburg, chiefly under Johann…

buckeburg.s: Bückeburg is a town in Lower Saxony, between the Weser and the Steinhuder Meer. Count Ernst of Holstein-Schaumburg made it his residence in the early 17th century and rebuilt its palace and church, and from 1647 to 1946 it was the capital of Schaumburg-Lippe.

boizenburg.s: Boizenburg is a town on the Elbe in the west of Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, near the border with Lower Saxony. In the Middle Ages it belonged to the counts of Schwerin, one of whose lines was based there, and later to the dukes of Mecklenburg.

barbastro.s: Barbastro is a city in the province of Huesca, Aragon, on the Vero river. Under Muslim rule it was a frontier stronghold of the Upper March, and in 1064 it was captured by an army of Norman, French and Aragonese knights in a campaign often seen as a forerunner of the Crusades,…

braunfels.s: Braunfels is a small town in Hesse on a hill above the Lahn near Wetzlar. Its castle, recorded from the 13th century, became the main seat of the counts, later princes, of Solms-Braunfels and was rebuilt in neo-Gothic style in the 19th century.

bad-kreuznach.s: Bad Kreuznach is a spa town on the Nahe in Rhineland-Palatinate, south-west of Mainz. It was the centre of the Front County of Sponheim and was later shared between the Electoral Palatinate and Baden.

brocken.s: The Brocken is the highest mountain of the Harz range in Saxony-Anhalt, rising to 1,141 metres. Wrapped in fog for much of the year, it is famed in German folklore as the gathering place of witches on Walpurgis Night, a scene used by Goethe in Faust.

battle-of-muret.s: The Battle of Muret was fought on 12 September 1213 south of Toulouse, during the Albigensian Crusade. A small crusader army under Simon de Montfort routed the much larger forces of Peter II of Aragon and Raymond VI of Toulouse, killing King Peter.

bertrand-of-toulouse.s: Bertrand was a son of Raymond IV of Toulouse who governed the county of Toulouse and in 1108 sailed to the East to claim his father's conquests in the Levant. He captured Tripoli in July 1109, becoming the first Count of Tripoli as a vassal of the Kingdom of Jerusalem, and…

byblos.s: Byblos is an ancient port city on the coast of Lebanon, north of Beirut, known in Arabic as Jbeil or Jubail. Inhabited for some 7,000 years, it was a leading Phoenician city that traded timber and papyrus with Egypt, and the Greek word for book derives from its name.

battle-of-monte-porzio.s: The Battle of Monte Porzio was fought on 29 May 1167 near Tusculum, south-east of Rome, between the army of the Roman commune and imperial forces of Frederick Barbarossa under Archbishops Christian of Mainz and Rainald of Dassel, joined by Tusculan troops. The much larger…

balaguer.s: Balaguer is a town on the Segre in the province of Lleida, Catalonia. Taken from the Muslims by Count Ermengol VI of Urgell in 1105, it became the capital of the county of Urgell.

battle-of-bulgneville.s: The Battle of Bulgnéville was fought on 2 July 1431 in Lorraine between René of Anjou and Antoine of Vaudémont, rival claimants to the Duchy of Lorraine. Supported by Burgundian troops and English archers, Antoine routed René's larger army and took him prisoner, handing him to…

bernkastel-kues.s: Bernkastel-Kues is a wine town on the Moselle in Rhineland-Palatinate, formed in 1905 from Bernkastel and Kues on opposite banks. Above it stands Landshut castle, built by the archbishops of Trier, and Kues was the birthplace of the philosopher Nicholas of Cusa.

bad-waldsee.s: Bad Waldsee is a spa town in Upper Swabia, in the Ravensburg district of Baden-Württemberg, Germany. Its old town lies between two lakes.

beeston-castle.s: Beeston Castle is a ruined castle on a high sandstone crag in Cheshire, England. Ranulf de Blondeville, Earl of Chester, began it in the 1220s after returning from crusade, and it passed to the crown with the earldom in 1237.

bakhchysarai.s: Bakhchysarai is a town in the south-west of the Crimean peninsula. It was the capital of the Crimean Khanate from the 16th century until the Russian annexation of 1783, and its Khan's Palace, mosques and Zincirli Medrese date from that era.

bakhchysarai-palace.s: The Bakhchysarai Palace, or Khan's Palace, is the residence of the Crimean khans at Bakhchysarai, begun in the 16th century. Its courtyards, mosques, harem, cemetery and the Fountain of Tears, which inspired a poem by Pushkin, reflect Ottoman and Persian influence.

battle-of-the-sagra.s: The Battle of the Sagra was fought in the 6th century BCE beside the river Sagras in Calabria, where the small army of Locri Epizephyrii defeated a much larger force from Croton. Ancient writers told of divine help for the Locrians from the Dioscuri.

battle-of-the-alta-river-1068.s: The Battle of the Alta River was fought in 1068 near Pereyaslavl, where the Cumans (Polovtsians) defeated the combined forces of three sons of Yaroslav the Wise: Iziaslav of Kyiv, Sviatoslav of Chernigov and Vsevolod of Pereyaslavl. It was the first major Cuman victory over…

boniak.s: Boniak was a Cuman khan of the late 11th and early 12th centuries, notorious in the Rus' chronicles for his raids on Kyiv and the surrounding lands, including the sack of the Kyiv Caves Monastery in 1096. In 1099 he helped a Rus' prince defeat a Hungarian army in Galicia.

battle-of-the-kalka-river.s: The Battle of the Kalka River was fought in 1223 near the Sea of Azov, where a Mongol force under Jebe and Subutai, raiding west of the Caspian, routed an army of Rus' princes and Cumans. Several princes, including Mstislav of Kyiv, were killed.

bhuj.s: Bhuj is a city in the Kutch district of Gujarat, India, at the foot of Bhujia hill. It became the capital of the Jadeja rulers of Cutch in the 16th century and is known for its palaces, among them the Aina Mahal and the Prag Mahal, and for its craft traditions.

berengaria-of-navarre.s: Berengaria of Navarre was queen of England as the wife of Richard I. A daughter of King Sancho VI of Navarre, she sailed east with Richard's crusading fleet; storms drove her ship to Cyprus, and after Richard conquered the island they married at Limassol in May 1191.

bangor-abbey.s: Bangor Abbey was a monastery on the southern shore of Belfast Lough in County Down, Northern Ireland, founded by Saint Comgall around 558. It became one of the great schools of early Irish Christianity, sending out missionaries such as Columbanus and producing the Antiphonary…

bartholomaus-ziegenbalg.s: Bartholomäus Ziegenbalg was a German Lutheran missionary, one of the first Protestant missionaries in India. Sent by King Frederick IV of Denmark, he arrived at Tranquebar in 1706 with Heinrich Plütschau, learned Tamil, founded schools and set up a printing press.

bohemond-i-of-antioch.s: Bohemond I of Antioch was a Norman leader of the First Crusade, eldest son of Robert Guiscard. Given Taranto in 1088, he joined the crusade and in 1098 secured Antioch for himself, founding the Principality of Antioch.

banaskantha-district.s: Banaskantha district is a district in the north of Gujarat, India, bordering Rajasthan, with its headquarters at Palanpur. It takes its name from the Banas river.

bato-of-dardania.s: Bato was a king of the Dardani, son of King Longarus, who ruled in the late 3rd century BCE. In 200 BCE, at the start of the Second Macedonian War, he offered help to the Roman consul Publius Sulpicius Galba against Philip V of Macedon, as Livy records.

battle-of-kosovo.s: The Battle of Kosovo was fought on 15 June 1389 on the Kosovo field near Pristina between a Serbian-led coalition under Prince Lazar and the Ottoman army of Sultan Murad I. Both rulers were killed, and although the outcome was not immediately decisive, Serbia soon became an…

battle-of-dorothe.s: The Battle of Dorothé was fought on 9 November 1910 in Dar Masalit, on the border of Darfur and Chad, between Masalit forces of Sultan Taj al-Din and a French colonial column. The Masalit defeated the French, and the French commander, Lieutenant-Colonel Maillard, was killed,…

bist-doab.s: The Jalandhar Doab, also called the Bist Doab, is the land between the Beas and the Sutlej in Punjab, India, including the districts of Jalandhar, Hoshiarpur, Kapurthala and Nawanshahr. A fertile plain backed by the Shivalik hills, it was ceded by the Sikh Empire to the East…

battle-of-suriagehara.s: The Battle of Suriagehara was fought in 1589 near Mount Bandai in northern Japan between Date Masamune and Ashina Yoshihiro. Masamune's victory destroyed the power of the Ashina and gave him their castle and the Aizu region, making the Date the dominant clan of southern Tohoku.

brianconnais.s: The Briançonnais is the mountain district around Briançon in the French Alps, in the upper Durance valley close to the Italian border. It controlled the route over the Montgenèvre pass and became part of the lands of the Dauphins of Viennois.

black-isle.s: The Black Isle is a peninsula in Easter Ross in the Scottish Highlands, bounded by the Cromarty Firth, the Beauly Firth and the Moray Firth. Despite its name it is not an island.

beit-shean.s: Beit She'an is a town in northern Israel at the junction of the Jordan and Jezreel valleys. An Egyptian stronghold in the Late Bronze Age, it became the Greek city of Scythopolis, the only member of the Decapolis west of the Jordan, and a major Roman and Byzantine city.

battle-of-chester.s: The Battle of Chester was fought around 615 near Chester, where Æthelfrith of Northumbria defeated the Britons of Powys and their allies. According to Bede, Æthelfrith slaughtered many monks of Bangor-on-Dee who had come to pray for the British army.

ba-dinh-square.s: Ba Dinh Square is the largest public square in Hanoi, Vietnam. There, on 2 September 1945, Ho Chi Minh read the declaration of independence of the Democratic Republic of Vietnam.

boa-amponsem.s: Boa Amponsem was a king of Denkyira, in what is now southern Ghana, who reigned in the second half of the 17th century. Under him Denkyira became the leading Akan state, taking tribute from many neighbours, including the early Asante chiefdoms, and controlling trade with the…

badra-iraq.s: Badra is a town in Wasit Governorate in eastern Iraq, close to the Iranian border at the foot of the Zagros mountains. Near it lies Tell Aqar, the site of the ancient city of Der, which guarded the route from Mesopotamia to Elam and Susa.

battle-of-dul-madoba.s: The Battle of Dul Madoba was fought on 9 August 1913 in British Somaliland, when Dervish forces of Mohammed Abdullah Hassan ambushed the newly formed Somaliland Camel Constabulary. The British commander, Richard Corfield, was killed along with many of his men.

battle-of-lepanto.s: The Battle of Lepanto was a naval battle fought on 7 October 1571 in the Gulf of Patras, off western Greece, between the fleet of the Holy League, led by Don John of Austria, and the Ottoman fleet. The League, whose ships came chiefly from Spain, Venice and the Papal States,…

balik.s: Balik was a Bulgarian noble who ruled the coastal region of Karvuna, the later Dobruja, in the 1340s, the first known ruler of the Dobrujan principality. In 1346 he sent troops under his brothers Theodore and Dobrotitsa to help the Byzantine empress Anna of Savoy in the civil…

boril-of-bulgaria.s: Boril was tsar of Bulgaria from 1207 to 1218, a nephew of Tsar Kaloyan, whose throne he took after Kaloyan's death. He fought the Latin Empire of Constantinople and rebel relatives such as Alexius Slav, and in 1211 he called a church council against the Bogomil heresy.

bhojshala.s: The Bhojshala is a monument in Dhar, Madhya Pradesh, India, associated by tradition with the 11th-century Paramara king Bhoja, a famous patron of learning, and held by Hindus to have been a temple of the goddess Saraswati and a centre of Sanskrit study. Muslims regard it as…

baji-rout.s: Baji Rout was a 12-year-old boatman from Dhenkanal in Odisha, India, who was shot dead by state police on 11 October 1938 for refusing to ferry them across the Brahmani river at Bhuban. The police were pursuing protesters of the Praja Mandal movement against the ruler of…

brahmani-river.s: The Brahmani is a major river of Odisha, India, formed by the joining of the Sankh and South Koel rivers near Rourkela. It flows south-east through Talcher and Dhenkanal to a delta shared with the Mahanadi and Baitarani, reaching the Bay of Bengal near Dhamra.

battle-of-madagascar.s: The Battle of Madagascar was the Allied campaign of 1942 to take Vichy French Madagascar and deny its harbours to Japan. British forces landed near Diego Suarez on 5 May 1942 and captured the naval base, then advanced on the rest of the island from September.

borno-state.s: Borno State is a state in north-eastern Nigeria, bordering Niger, Chad and Cameroon, with its capital at Maiduguri. Created in 1976, it covers much of the heartland of the old Kanem–Bornu realm, and the Shehu of Borno and the Emir of Dikwa remain traditional rulers there.

bitlis.s: Bitlis is a city in eastern Turkey, south-west of Lake Van, in a narrow valley on the route between the Armenian highlands and Upper Mesopotamia. In the Middle Ages it was held by Arab, Kurdish and Turkish rulers, among them the Dilmaçoğulları, and from the 14th century it was…

barbar-temple.s: Barbar Temple is an archaeological site in northern Bahrain with a series of temples built one above another in the late 3rd and early 2nd millennia BCE. Excavated by a Danish expedition from 1954, it included a sacred pool fed by a freshwater spring, probably linked to the…

bagendon.s: Bagendon is a village in Gloucestershire, England, near Cirencester, beside which lie the earthworks of a large late Iron Age oppidum. Probably a centre of the Dobunni, the site has produced evidence of coin minting and of Roman goods imported in the decades before the Roman…

battle-of-rozgony.s: The Battle of Rozgony was fought on 15 June 1312 near Rozgony, now Rozhanovce in eastern Slovakia, between King Charles I of Hungary and the Aba family, who were supported by troops of Matthew Csák. Charles's victory, won with the help of the Saxons of Spiš, strengthened his…

b-r-ambedkar.s: B. R. Ambedkar was an Indian jurist, economist and social reformer who chaired the drafting committee of the Constitution of India. Born into the Mahar caste, then treated as untouchable, he studied at Columbia University and the London School of Economics with a scholarship…

beaumont-hamel.s: Beaumont-Hamel is a village in the Somme department of northern France. On 1 July 1916, the first day of the Battle of the Somme, the Newfoundland Regiment attacked near the village and was almost wiped out in half an hour: of some 800 men who went forward, only 68 answered…

belarus.s: Belarus is a landlocked country in Eastern Europe, with its capital at Minsk, bordered by Russia, Ukraine, Poland, Lithuania and Latvia. Its lands belonged to Kievan Rus' and then for centuries to the Grand Duchy of Lithuania and the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, before…

battle-of-pelagonia.s: The Battle of Pelagonia was fought in 1259 in the Pelagonia plain of Macedonia between the Empire of Nicaea and an alliance of the Despotate of Epirus, the Principality of Achaea and the Kingdom of Sicily. The alliance broke apart before the fighting, and Nicaean forces under…

baden-wurttemberg.s: Baden-Württemberg is a state in south-western Germany, with its capital at Stuttgart, bordering France and Switzerland along the Rhine and Lake Constance. It was created in 1952 by merging Württemberg-Baden, Württemberg-Hohenzollern and South Baden, uniting the historical…

blood-court-at-cannstatt.s: The blood court at Cannstatt was the killing of Alemannic nobles in 746 by the Frankish mayor of the palace Carloman. Having summoned the Alemannic leaders to an assembly at Cannstatt, now part of Stuttgart, he had many of them executed for supporting revolts against Frankish…

battle-of-castillon.s: The Battle of Castillon was fought on 17 July 1453 near Castillon on the Dordogne in Gascony, and is regarded as the last battle of the Hundred Years' War. An English army under John Talbot, Earl of Shrewsbury, attacked a fortified French camp and was destroyed by French…

battle-on-the-marchfeld.s: The Battle on the Marchfeld, also called the Battle of Dürnkrut and Jedenspeigen, was fought on 26 August 1278 on the plain north-east of Vienna. King Rudolf I of Germany, allied with King Ladislaus IV of Hungary, defeated and killed King Ottokar II of Bohemia.

bar-le-duc.s: Bar-le-Duc is a town in the Meuse department of north-eastern France, on the Ornain river. It grew around a castle built in the 10th century by Frederick, Duke of Upper Lorraine, and was the capital of the County and later Duchy of Bar.

burghausen.s: Burghausen is a town in Upper Bavaria on the Salzach river, which forms the border with Austria. Its castle, stretching for over a kilometre along a ridge above the old town, is regarded as the longest castle complex in the world.

boleslaus-i-of-bohemia.s: Boleslaus I, called the Cruel, was Duke of Bohemia from 935, after he murdered his brother Wenceslas. He resisted Otto I for fourteen years before accepting his overlordship in 950, and his forces helped defeat the Magyars at the Battle of Lechfeld in 955.

boleslaus-ii-of-bohemia.s: Boleslaus II, called the Pious, was Duke of Bohemia from 967 or 972 until 999. He founded the bishopric of Prague in 973 and in 995 massacred the rival Slavník family, completing Přemyslid control of Bohemia.

borivoj-i-duke-of-bohemia.s: Bořivoj I is the first historically attested Duke of Bohemia of the Přemyslid dynasty. He was baptised around 870, traditionally by Saint Methodius at the court of Great Moravia, whose overlordship he accepted.

battle-of-auray.s: The Battle of Auray, fought on 29 September 1364 in southern Brittany, was the decisive battle of the War of the Breton Succession. An Anglo-Breton army under John of Montfort and Sir John Chandos defeated the Franco-Breton forces of Charles of Blois, who was killed, while…

battle-of-saint-aubin-du-cormier.s: The Battle of Saint-Aubin-du-Cormier was fought on 28 July 1488 in Brittany and was the decisive battle of the Mad War. A French royal army under Louis de La Trémoille routed the forces of Duke Francis II of Brittany and his allies, capturing Louis of Orléans, the future Louis…

battle-of-trans.s: The Battle of Trans was fought in 939 at Trans, near Dol in north-eastern Brittany, traditionally on 1 August. Alan Twisted Beard, who had returned from exile in England, defeated the last Viking army in Brittany.

bretislaus-i-duke-of-bohemia.s: Bretislaus I was Duke of Bohemia from 1035 to 1055. Before his accession he secured Moravia for Bohemia, and in 1039 he raided Poland and carried off the relics of Saint Adalbert from Gniezno, but he had to submit to Emperor Henry III in 1041.

brno.s: Brno is the second-largest city of the Czech Republic and the historic capital of Moravia. A Přemyslid castle stood there by the 11th century, when it became the seat of an appanage duchy, and the town received its privileges in 1243.

black-brunswickers.s: The Black Brunswickers were a volunteer corps raised in 1809 by Frederick William, Duke of Brunswick, to fight Napoleon after his duchy had been absorbed into the Kingdom of Westphalia. Dressed in black with a skull badge, they fought their way across northern Germany to the…

brunswick.s: Brunswick, in German Braunschweig, is a city in Lower Saxony, Germany, on the Oker river. Henry the Lion made it his residence in the 12th century, building Dankwarderode Castle and setting up the bronze lion.

brzeg.s: Brzeg is a town on the Oder in the Opole Voivodeship of southern Poland. From 1311 it was the capital of the Duchy of Brzeg, ruled by Silesian Piasts who rebuilt its castle in Renaissance style, earning it the name of the Silesian Wawel.

bukovina.s: Bukovina is a historical region on the north-eastern slopes of the Carpathians, divided today between Romania and Ukraine. Part of the Principality of Moldavia, it was annexed by the Habsburg monarchy in 1775 and became a separate crown land in 1849, with its capital at…

battle-of-nancy.s: The Battle of Nancy, fought on 5 January 1477 outside Nancy in Lorraine, was the final battle of the Burgundian Wars. Duke René II of Lorraine and his Swiss allies defeated the army of Charles the Bold, Duke of Burgundy, who was killed.

borna-duke-of-croatia.s: Borna was duke of the Dalmatian Croats in the early 9th century and the first Croatian ruler recorded in contemporary sources, the Frankish royal annals. A vassal of the Franks, he fought for Emperor Louis the Pious against Ljudevit Posavski, the rebel duke of Pannonian…

branimir-of-croatia.s: Branimir was Duke of Croatia from 879 to about 892. He came to power by overthrowing Duke Zdeslav, a Byzantine client, and in June 879 received the blessing of Pope John VIII, which is often regarded as papal recognition of Croatia as an independent state.

battle-of-montemurlo.s: The Battle of Montemurlo was fought on 1 August 1537 near Prato, where the forces of the new Duke of Florence, Cosimo I de' Medici, defeated republican exiles led by Filippo Strozzi. Strozzi was captured and died in prison the following year.

bamberg.s: Bamberg is a city in Upper Franconia, Bavaria, on the Regnitz near the Main. Emperor Henry II founded its bishopric in 1007, and the cathedral holds his tomb and the statue of the Bamberg Horseman.

battle-of-andernach.s: The Battle of Andernach was fought on 2 October 939 on the Rhine near Andernach. Forces loyal to King Otto I defeated the rebel dukes Eberhard of Franconia and Gilbert of Lotharingia; Eberhard was killed and Gilbert drowned in the Rhine.

bolkow-castle.s: Bolków Castle stands above the town of Bolków in Lower Silesia, Poland. It was built in the late 13th century by Duke Bolko I the Strict of Świdnica and Jawor to guard the routes to Bohemia.

bochnia.s: Bochnia is a town in Lesser Poland, east of Kraków, known for its salt mine, one of the oldest in Europe, where rock salt was mined from the mid-13th century until 1990. Together with the mine at Wieliczka it formed the royal salt works of Kraków, a major source of crown…

boleslaw-iv-the-curly.s: Bolesław IV the Curly was Duke of Masovia and from 1146 High Duke of Poland, holding Kraków after he and his younger brothers drove out their eldest brother, Władysław II the Exile. He had to submit to Emperor Frederick Barbarossa after the imperial invasion of 1157.

bidzina-cholokashvili.s: Bidzina Cholokashvili was a Georgian nobleman of Kakheti who, with the brothers Shalva and Elizbar, dukes of Ksani, led the Bakhtrioni uprising of 1659 against Safavid Persian rule and the settlement of Turkmen nomads in Kakheti. The rebels destroyed the Persian strongholds at…

bruno-the-great.s: Bruno the Great (925–965) was Archbishop of Cologne from 953 and a younger brother of Otto I. Otto also made him Duke of Lotharingia, and around 959 he divided the duchy into Upper and Lower Lorraine, each under a subordinate duke.

bavaria-landshut.s: Bavaria-Landshut was a duchy of the Wittelsbach dynasty created in the partition of Bavaria in 1392, with its seat at Landshut in Lower Bavaria. Under the 'rich dukes' Henry XVI, Louis IX and George it became the wealthiest of the Bavarian duchies.

battle-of-gammelsdorf.s: The Battle of Gammelsdorf was fought on 9 November 1313 near Gammelsdorf in Bavaria between Duke Louis of Upper Bavaria, later Emperor Louis IV, and the Habsburg duke Frederick the Fair of Austria, who disputed the guardianship of the young dukes of Lower Bavaria. Louis's…

bihar.s: Bihar is a state of eastern India in the middle Ganges plain, with its capital at Patna. In antiquity it was the land of Videha, the Vajji confederacy and Magadha, whose capital Pataliputra served the Maurya and Gupta empires, and the Buddha attained enlightenment at Bodh Gaya.

biharea.s: Biharea (Hungarian: Bihar) is a village in Bihor County, north-western Romania, near Oradea, the site of an early medieval earthwork fortress. The Gesta Hungarorum names it as the seat of Menumorut, a ruler said to have resisted the Hungarians around 900, and it later gave its…

berthold-iv-duke-of-merania.s: Berthold IV (d. 1204), of the Bavarian counts of Andechs, was Duke of Merania from 1188, a title linked to lands on the Adriatic coast, and Margrave of Istria. He held wide lands in Bavaria, Franconia, Tyrol and Burgundy.

biblioteca-estense.s: The Biblioteca Estense is the library of the Este family, moved from Ferrara to Modena in 1598 when the dukes lost Ferrara to the Papal States. The historian Ludovico Antonio Muratori served as its librarian.

battle-of-rignano.s: The Battle of Rignano was fought on 30 October 1137 near Rignano Garganico in Apulia between King Roger II of Sicily and the rebel Ranulf of Alife, supported by troops left behind by Emperor Lothair III. Roger was defeated, and Duke Sergius VII of Naples, who had submitted to…

bad-ems.s: Bad Ems is a spa town in Rhineland-Palatinate, Germany, on the river Lahn. Its warm springs made it one of the most fashionable resorts of 19th-century Europe, visited by royalty.

bec-abbey.s: Bec Abbey, at Le Bec-Hellouin in Normandy, is a Benedictine monastery founded around 1034 by the knight Herluin. Under the teachers Lanfranc and Anselm, both later archbishops of Canterbury, its school became one of the leading centres of learning in 11th-century Europe.

black-madonna-of-czestochowa.s: The Black Madonna of Częstochowa is an icon of the Virgin Mary and Child kept at the Jasna Góra Monastery in Częstochowa, Poland. Brought there in 1382 by Duke Władysław II of Opole, it bears two scars on the Virgin's cheek, traditionally attributed to Hussite raiders in 1430.

bytom.s: Bytom is a city in the Silesian Voivodeship of southern Poland and one of the oldest towns in Upper Silesia. It grew around an early medieval stronghold, received town rights in 1254 and from 1281 was the seat of the Piast Duchy of Bytom.

braslav-duke-of-lower-pannonia.s: Braslav (fl. 884–896) was the last known duke of Lower Pannonia, the Slavic principality between the Drava and Sava rivers under Frankish overlordship. A loyal vassal of the East Frankish king Arnulf of Carinthia, he fought alongside him against Great Moravia, and in 896…

battle-of-blue-waters.s: The Battle of Blue Waters was fought around 1362 or 1363 near the Syniukha river, a tributary of the Southern Bug in present-day Ukraine, between the Grand Duchy of Lithuania under Algirdas and the forces of three Tatar lords of the Golden Horde. The Lithuanian victory ended…

brandenburg-prussia.s: Brandenburg-Prussia is the historians' name for the lands of the Hohenzollern electors of Brandenburg after they inherited the Duchy of Prussia in 1618. Ruled in personal union, the scattered territories were turned into a centralised state by Frederick William, the Great…

bresse.s: Bresse is a historical region of eastern France, lying mostly in the Ain department between the Saône and the Jura, with Bourg-en-Bresse as its main town. It passed to the House of Savoy in 1272 through marriage and remained Savoyard until the Treaty of Lyon of 1601 ceded it…

bergedorf.s: Bergedorf is a borough in the south-east of Hamburg, Germany. In 1420 Hamburg and Lübeck took the town and its castle from the dukes of Saxe-Lauenburg and ruled it jointly, together with the Vierlande, for more than four centuries.

bernhard-of-saxe-weimar.s: Bernhard of Saxe-Weimar was a German prince and one of the leading Protestant generals of the Thirty Years' War. Serving Sweden, he took command at the Battle of Lützen in 1632 after Gustavus Adolphus was killed, but was heavily defeated at Nördlingen in 1634.

bernhard-duke-of-saxony.s: Bernhard, a younger son of Albert the Bear of the Ascanian house, was Count of Anhalt and from 1180 Duke of Saxony. He received the ducal title after the fall of Henry the Lion, but only with the eastern remnants of the old duchy, while Westphalia went to the Archbishop of…

battle-of-legnica.s: The Battle of Legnica was fought on 9 April 1241 near Legnica in Silesia, where a Mongol army defeated the forces of Duke Henry II the Pious of Silesia, who was killed. It was part of the Mongol invasion of Europe.

banjarmasin.s: Banjarmasin is a city in South Kalimantan, Indonesia, on the Martapura and Barito rivers near the south coast of Borneo. It was the capital of the Banjar Sultanate, founded in the early sixteenth century, and a port for pepper and forest products.

battle-of-vincy.s: The Battle of Vincy was fought on 21 March 717 near Cambrai, in northern France, during the civil war that followed the death of Pepin of Herstal. Charles Martel, leader of the Austrasians, defeated the Neustrian king Chilperic II and his mayor of the palace Ragenfrid.

battle-of-coronate.s: The Battle of Coronate was fought in 689 on the Adda river, near present-day Cornate d'Adda in Lombardy, between the Lombard king Cunipert and the rebel duke Alahis of Trent and Brescia. Cunipert won and Alahis was killed, ending a revolt that had driven the king from Pavia.

battle-of-muhldorf.s: The Battle of Mühldorf was fought on 28 September 1322 near Mühldorf am Inn in Bavaria between the rival German kings Louis IV of Bavaria and Frederick the Fair of Austria. Louis won decisively and captured Frederick, securing his position in the empire.

bar-montenegro.s: Bar is a port town on the Adriatic coast of southern Montenegro. Its medieval predecessor, Stari Bar, was an important town of Duklja and became the seat of an archbishopric in 1089.

banu-ijl.s: The Banu Ijl were an Arab tribe of the Bakr ibn Wa'il confederation, living in eastern Arabia and on the edges of Iraq before Islam. Clans of the tribe took part in the victory over the Sasanians at Dhi Qar.

battles-of-guararapes.s: The Battles of Guararapes were two battles fought in April 1648 and February 1649 on the Guararapes hills south of Recife in north-eastern Brazil. Portuguese, Brazilian, Indigenous and African forces of the Pernambuco insurrection defeated the army of the Dutch West India…

batticaloa.s: Batticaloa is a city on the east coast of Sri Lanka, built around a large lagoon in the Eastern Province. The Portuguese built a fort there in the 1620s, which the Dutch captured in 1638 with the help of the king of Kandy, opening their conquest of the island's coasts.

bheemunipatnam.s: Bheemunipatnam, also known as Bimlipatnam, is a coastal town north of Visakhapatnam in Andhra Pradesh, India. In the 17th century the Dutch East India Company established a trading post there, part of its Coromandel governorate, dealing in cotton cloth and other goods.

battle-of-colachel.s: The Battle of Colachel was fought in August 1741 at the port of Colachel on the south-western coast of India, where the army of Marthanda Varma of Travancore defeated a force of the Dutch East India Company. It was one of the first defeats of a European power by an Indian state.

baruch-spinoza.s: Baruch Spinoza was a Dutch philosopher from Amsterdam's Portuguese Jewish community, which expelled him in 1656. His Theological-Political Treatise of 1670 argued for freedom of thought and a historical reading of the Bible, and his Ethics, published after his death, set out a…

battle-of-svolder.s: The Battle of Svolder was a naval battle fought in September 1000 in the western Baltic. King Olaf Tryggvason of Norway was defeated and killed by an alliance of Sweyn Forkbeard of Denmark, Olof Skötkonung of Sweden and Eric Haakonsson, Earl of Lade.

birsay.s: Birsay is a parish and village in the north-west of Mainland Orkney, Scotland. The tidal island of the Brough of Birsay has remains of Pictish and Norse settlement, and in the 11th century Earl Thorfinn the Mighty made Birsay his seat and built a minster there, the first seat…

butler-dynasty.s: The Butler dynasty was an Anglo-Norman family in Ireland descended from Theobald Walter, who held the hereditary office of butler of Ireland from 1185. As earls, later marquesses and dukes, of Ormond they dominated Kilkenny and Tipperary and were the great rivals of the…

belfast.s: Belfast is the capital of Northern Ireland, at the mouth of the River Lagan on Belfast Lough. It grew from a small settlement in the 17th century into a major industrial city of linen, rope and shipbuilding; the Harland and Wolff yard built the Titanic.

battle-of-venni.s: The Battle of Venni was fought near Thanjavur in southern India in the Sangam age, when the Chola king Karikala defeated a coalition of the Chera and Pandya kings and eleven chieftains. Sangam poets celebrated it as a great victory that established Chola supremacy among the…

battle-of-talaiyalanganam.s: The Battle of Talaiyalanganam was fought in the Sangam age in southern India, when the young Pandya king Nedunjeliyan II defeated an alliance of the Chera and Chola kings and five chieftains. Sangam poems celebrate the victory, which secured Pandya power in Tamilakam.

bhimavaram.s: Bhimavaram is a town in the Godavari delta of Andhra Pradesh, India. It is known for the Somarama temple, one of the five Pancharama shrines of Shiva, built under the Eastern Chalukya kings.

buda.s: Buda is the historic town on the western, hilly bank of the Danube that in 1873 merged with Pest and Óbuda to form Budapest. Its castle hill became the main royal residence of medieval Hungary from the 14th century and the seat of King Matthias Corvinus's Renaissance court.

battle-of-shayuan.s: The Battle of Shayuan was fought in 537 between the Eastern Wei under Gao Huan and the Western Wei under Yuwen Tai, near the Wei River in modern Shaanxi. Though heavily outnumbered, Yuwen Tai ambushed Gao Huan's army among reed marshes and routed it, capturing tens of…

battle-of-yubi.s: The Battle of Yubi was Gao Huan's siege of the Western Wei fortress of Yubi, in modern Jishan county, Shanxi, in 546. For some fifty days the Eastern Wei army used tunnels, siege engines and earthworks against the defenders led by Wei Xiaokuan, who countered every attempt.

board-of-proprietors-of-east-jersey.n: Board of Proprietors of East Jersey
board-of-proprietors-of-east-jersey.s: The Board of Proprietors of East Jersey was the body through which the proprietors who bought East Jersey in 1682 managed their land rights. Organised in the 1680s and based at Perth Amboy, it kept control of unallocated land after the proprietors surrendered government to the…

bes.s: Bes was an ancient Egyptian protective deity, shown as a bearded dwarf with a lion-like face, who guarded households, women in childbirth and children against evil. His cult spread across the Mediterranean through Phoenician trade.

bozrah.s: Bozrah was the capital of the Iron Age kingdom of Edom, identified with the site of Busayra in southern Jordan, south of Tafilah. Excavations by Crystal-M. Bennett in the 1970s uncovered a fortified town with a large palace or temple complex, mainly of the 8th to 6th centuries…

battle-of-shamkor.s: The Battle of Shamkor was fought in 1195 near the town of Shamkor, in modern Azerbaijan, between the army of the Kingdom of Georgia and the forces of the Eldiguzid atabeg Abu Bakr. Georgian troops under the brothers Zakare and Ivane Mkhargrdzeli, sent by Queen Tamar, won a…

battle-of-blenheim.s: The Battle of Blenheim was fought on 13 August 1704 near the village of Blindheim on the Danube in Bavaria, during the War of the Spanish Succession. An allied army under the Duke of Marlborough and Prince Eugene of Savoy crushed a Franco-Bavarian army under Marshal Tallard…

bonn.s: Bonn is a city on the Rhine in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany, south of Cologne. Founded as a Roman legionary fortress, it became the residence of the archbishop-electors of Cologne from the late 13th century, and Beethoven was born there in 1770.

bruhl-rhineland.s: Brühl is a town in the Rhineland between Cologne and Bonn, in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany. The archbishop-elector Clemens August of Cologne, of the Wittelsbach family, built Augustusburg Palace and the hunting lodge of Falkenlust there from 1725.

battle-of-austerlitz.s: The Battle of Austerlitz was fought on 2 December 1805 near Austerlitz (Slavkov u Brna) in Moravia, during the War of the Third Coalition. Napoleon's French army decisively defeated the Russian and Austrian armies of Tsar Alexander I and Emperor Francis II.

balakan.s: Balakan is a town in north-western Azerbaijan, near the borders with Georgia and Russia, at the foot of the Greater Caucasus. In the 17th and 18th centuries it was a centre of the Jar-Belokan free communities of Avar and Tsakhur highlanders, which resisted Persian governors,…

bari.s: Bari is a port city on the Adriatic coast of southern Italy and the capital of Apulia. The seat of an Arab emirate from about 847 to 871 and later of the Byzantine catepan of Italy, it fell to the Normans in 1071.

battle-of-lalakaon.s: The Battle of Lalakaon was fought on 3 September 863 in Paphlagonia, in northern Asia Minor, between a Byzantine army under Petronas and the forces of Umar al-Aqta, emir of Melitene, who had sacked Amisos on the Black Sea. The Byzantines encircled the Arab army and destroyed…

banu-munabbih.s: The Banu Munabbih were an Arab family claiming Qurayshi descent who ruled Multan, in present-day Pakistan, as an autonomous emirate from the mid-9th century, while recognising the Abbasid caliph. Arab geographers such as al-Mas'udi describe their city and its famous Sun…

battle-of-mulayda.s: The Battle of Mulayda was fought in January 1891 in the Qassim region of central Arabia. Muhammad ibn Rashid, emir of Jabal Shammar, defeated an alliance of the towns of Qassim and supporters of the Al Saud.

battle-of-rawdat-muhanna.s: The Battle of Rawdat Muhanna was fought in April 1906 in the Qassim region of central Arabia between Abd al-Aziz ibn Saud and Abd al-Aziz ibn Mutib, emir of Jabal Shammar. The Rashidi emir was killed, and the Ottoman troops who had supported him soon withdrew from Qassim.

bakar-ould-soueid-ahmed.s: Bakar ould Soueid Ahmed was emir of Tagant in central Mauritania, of the Idaw Aish, whose long reign covered much of the 19th century. He made Tagant one of the strongest emirates of the region, fighting rival emirates and controlling caravan routes.

bugha-the-elder.s: Bugha the Elder was a Turkish general in the service of the Abbasid caliphs at Samarra. In 852–855 he led a harsh campaign to restore caliphal authority in Armenia and the Caucasus, deporting Armenian princes to Samarra.

babiito-dynasty.s: The Babiito are the ruling dynasty of the Kingdom of Bunyoro-Kitara in western Uganda. According to tradition they were Luo-speaking newcomers from the north who succeeded the legendary Chwezi around 1500.

bigo-bya-mugenyi.s: Bigo bya Mugenyi is an archaeological site on the Katonga River in western Uganda, consisting of kilometres of deep ditches enclosing large areas of grassland. Dated to around the 14th and 15th centuries, it is thought to have protected cattle and settlements, and oral…

bessarion.s: Bessarion was a Byzantine scholar and churchman born in Trebizond. As metropolitan of Nicaea he supported the union of the Orthodox and Catholic churches at the Council of Florence in 1439 and was made a cardinal of the Roman church.

battle-of-guaxenduba.s: The Battle of Guaxenduba was fought on 19 November 1614 on the coast of Maranhão in northern Brazil. A Portuguese force under Jerónimo de Albuquerque defeated the French colonists of Equinoctial France and their Tupinambá allies, although it was outnumbered.

battle-of-karanbuk.s: The Battle of Karanbük was fought in 1343 in central Anatolia between Eretna, the former Ilkhanid governor who had made himself independent ruler, and a Chobanid army sent against him. Eretna's victory secured his rule over the former Ilkhanid province of Anatolia and…

beysehir.s: Beyşehir is a town in Konya Province in central Turkey, on the shore of Lake Beyşehir, the country's largest freshwater lake. In the late 13th and early 14th centuries it was the capital of the Eshrefid beylik, whose ruler Süleyman Bey built the wooden-columned Eşrefoğlu…

basque-nationalist-party.s: The Basque Nationalist Party is a Christian democratic party founded in 1895 by Sabino Arana to defend Basque identity and self-government. In the Spanish Civil War it sided with the Republic in return for autonomy, and its leader José Antonio Aguirre headed the Basque…

baba-farid.s: Baba Farid, Fariduddin Masud Ganjshakar, was a Sufi master of the Chishti order in the Punjab, who lived and taught at Ajodhan, now Pakpattan in Pakistan, where his shrine remains a major place of pilgrimage. He was one of the first poets to write in Punjabi, and verses…

brar-clan.s: The Brar are a Jat clan of the Punjab, concentrated in the Malwa region south of the Sutlej. Brar chiefs rose to power in the 18th century as Mughal and Durrani authority collapsed, and Brar families ruled the princely state of Faridkot, while the related Sidhu-Brar Phulkian…

battle-of-tacuarembo.s: The Battle of Tacuarembó was fought on 22 January 1820 in the north of the Eastern Province, now Uruguay, when Portuguese forces under the Count of Figueira routed the troops of José Gervasio Artigas under Andrés Latorre. The defeat ended organised resistance to the Portuguese…

briggs-plan.s: The Briggs Plan was the British strategy against the communist insurgency in Malaya devised in 1950 by Lieutenant-General Sir Harold Briggs, the director of operations during the Malayan Emergency. It resettled about half a million rural Chinese squatters into guarded new…

battle-of-tampere.s: The Battle of Tampere was the decisive battle of the Finnish Civil War, fought in March and April 1918. The White army under Carl Gustaf Emil Mannerheim besieged the Red-held industrial city of Tampere and took it after heavy street fighting on 6 April 1918, capturing about…

battle-of-kleidion.s: The Battle of Kleidion was fought on 29 July 1014 in the Belasitsa mountains, where the Byzantine emperor Basil II outflanked and destroyed the army of Tsar Samuel of Bulgaria. According to Byzantine chroniclers, Basil had some 15,000 prisoners blinded, leaving one man in…

battle-of-santome.s: The Battle of Santomé was fought on 22 December 1855 near San Juan de la Maguana in the west of the Dominican Republic, when Dominican troops defeated an invading army of the Haitian emperor Faustin Soulouque. Together with the battle of Sabana Larga in January 1856, it ended…

battle-of-vertieres.s: The Battle of Vertières was fought on 18 November 1803 outside Cap-Français, when the Haitian revolutionary army under Jean-Jacques Dessalines, with François Capois prominent in the assault, defeated the French forces of General Rochambeau. It was the last major battle of the…

battle-of-sripurambiyam.s: The Battle of Sripurambiyam was fought around 885 near Kumbakonam in the Kaveri delta, when the Pallava king Aparajita and his ally Prithvipati I of the Western Gangas, with Chola support, defeated the Pandya king Varaguna II. Prithvipati was killed in the battle.

battle-of-la-lys-1918.s: The Battle of La Lys was the opening of the German spring offensive in Flanders known as Operation Georgette, launched on 9 April 1918. The attack fell on the 2nd Portuguese Division holding the line near the Lys river, which was overwhelmed with the loss of over 7,000 men…

battle-of-sardarabad.s: The Battle of Sardarabad was fought from 21 to 29 May 1918 west of Erivan, when Armenian forces under generals Movses Silikyan and Daniel Bek-Pirumyan stopped an Ottoman offensive into the Ararat plain. Together with the battles of Bash Abaran and Karakilisa, it saved the…

battle-of-fangtou.s: The Battle of Fangtou was fought in 369 in northern China, when the Former Yan general Murong Chui defeated the northern expedition of the Eastern Jin commander Huan Wen near Fangtou, in modern Henan. Huan Wen's army, short of supplies, retreated and lost many thousands of men.

blue-division.s: The Blue Division was a unit of Spanish volunteers, mostly Falangists and army men, that fought for Nazi Germany on the Eastern Front as the 250th Infantry Division of the Wehrmacht. Sent by Franco in 1941 after the German invasion of the Soviet Union, some 45,000 men served…

bauto.s: Bauto was a Frankish general who served the Roman Empire as commander of the western army under Gratian and Valentinian II and was consul in 385. His daughter Aelia Eudoxia married the eastern emperor Arcadius, making Bauto the grandfather of Theodosius II.

bbc.s: The BBC, the British Broadcasting Corporation, is the United Kingdom's public broadcaster, founded as a company in 1922 and established by royal charter in 1927. Funded mainly by a licence fee, it became a model of public-service broadcasting.

battle-of-bir-hakeim.s: The Battle of Bir Hakeim was fought in the Libyan desert from 26 May to 11 June 1942, as part of the Battle of Gazala. A Free French brigade under General Marie-Pierre Koenig held the desert fort against German and Italian forces under Erwin Rommel for over two weeks before…

bremerhaven.s: Bremerhaven is a port city at the mouth of the Weser on the North Sea, an exclave of the German state of Bremen. It was founded in 1827 by Bremen's mayor Johann Smidt on land bought from Hanover, because silting of the Weser kept large ships from reaching Bremen.

biberach-an-der-riss.s: Biberach an der Riss is a town in Upper Swabia, Baden-Württemberg, on the river Riss. A market town under the Hohenstaufen, it was a free imperial city from the late 13th century until 1803 and prospered from fustian weaving.

bad-buchau.s: Bad Buchau is a small spa town in Upper Swabia, Baden-Württemberg, on the Federsee. It grew beside an abbey of noble canonesses founded in the 8th century and was a free imperial city until 1803.

brenz-river.s: The Brenz is a river in eastern Baden-Württemberg and Bavaria that rises in the Brenztopf spring at Königsbronn on the Swabian Jura and flows south past Heidenheim and Giengen to join the Danube near Lauingen. Its valley has been an industrial area since early modern ironworking.

battle-of-frankenhausen.s: The Battle of Frankenhausen, fought on 15 May 1525 in Thuringia, was one of the decisive defeats of the German Peasants' War. An army of princes led by Philip of Hesse and Duke George of Saxony routed a peasant force inspired by Thomas Müntzer, killing thousands.

battle-of-nordlingen-1634.s: The Battle of Nördlingen, fought on 6 September 1634 in Swabia, was a crushing victory of the imperial and Spanish armies under the future Emperor Ferdinand III and the Cardinal-Infante Ferdinand over the Swedes and their German allies under Gustav Horn and Bernhard of…

battle-of-reutlingen.s: The Battle of Reutlingen was fought on 14 May 1377 outside the imperial city of Reutlingen, where its citizens defeated a force of Count Eberhard II of Württemberg led by his son Ulrich. The victory over Württemberg was a high point of the Swabian League of Cities, founded the…

bas-rhin.s: Bas-Rhin is a department of eastern France covering northern Alsace, with Strasbourg as its prefecture. Created in 1790, it was annexed by Germany from 1871 to 1918 and again in practice during the Second World War.

beatus-rhenanus.s: Beatus Rhenanus was an Alsatian humanist from Sélestat who edited classical texts, including Tacitus and Velleius Paterculus, and wrote a history of ancient Germany. A friend and biographer of Erasmus, he worked with the printers of Basel.

battle-of-sainte-foy.s: The Battle of Sainte-Foy was fought on 28 April 1760 just outside Quebec City, when French forces under the Chevalier de Lévis defeated the British garrison under James Murray. It was the last French victory of the war in North America, but Lévis could not retake Quebec once…

battle-of-turckheim.s: The Battle of Turckheim was fought on 5 January 1675 near Colmar in Alsace, when the French army under Marshal Turenne, after a surprise winter march through the Vosges, defeated the imperial and Brandenburg forces. The victory drove the Germans back across the Rhine and…

blau-river.s: The Blau is a short river in Baden-Württemberg that rises at the Blautopf, a deep blue karst spring in Blaubeuren, and flows east to join the Danube at Ulm. Its spring, the Blautopf, is the second-largest karst spring in Germany, and the town of Blaubeuren grew around a…

biriciana.s: Biriciana was a Roman cavalry fort on the Raetian Limes on the site of present-day Weißenburg in Bavaria, built around 90 CE. It held a cavalry unit of about 500 men, and its rebuilt north gate, the nearby Roman baths and the Weißenburg Roman treasure, found in 1979, are now…

battle-of-wimpfen.s: The Battle of Wimpfen was fought on 6 May 1622 near Bad Wimpfen on the Neckar, when the army of the Catholic League under Tilly, with Spanish troops under Gonzalo Fernández de Córdoba, defeated Margrave George Frederick of Baden-Durlach. It was part of the campaign in which…

bad-wimpfen.s: Bad Wimpfen is a small town on the Neckar in Baden-Württemberg, with an upper town on a hill around the remains of one of the largest Hohenstaufen imperial palaces and a lower town, Wimpfen im Tal, around the collegiate church of St. Peter. It was a free imperial city until…

bad-windsheim.s: Bad Windsheim is a town in Middle Franconia, Bavaria, which grew from a Frankish royal estate and was a free imperial city from the late 13th century until 1802. It adopted the Reformation and subscribed to the Augsburg Confession in 1530.

bitterfeld.s: Bitterfeld is a town in Saxony-Anhalt, Germany, which grew from the late 19th century into a centre of the chemical industry, based on local brown coal. In East Germany its chemical works made it one of the most polluted places in Europe.

beer-hall-putsch.s: The Beer Hall Putsch was a failed coup attempt by Adolf Hitler, the Nazi Party and General Erich Ludendorff in Munich on 8 and 9 November 1923. Launched in the Bürgerbräukeller beer hall, it was crushed by the Bavarian police at the Feldherrnhalle, where 16 putschists and four…

bussing.s: Büssing was a German maker of buses and lorries founded by Heinrich Büssing in Braunschweig in 1903. It became one of Germany's leading commercial-vehicle makers, known for its lion emblem taken from the city's arms, and was taken over by MAN in 1971.

buckeburg-palace.s: Bückeburg Palace is the residence of the princes of Schaumburg-Lippe in Bückeburg, Lower Saxony, developed from a 14th-century moated castle and rebuilt in Renaissance style around 1600 by Count Ernest of Holstein-Schaumburg. Its chapel and golden hall are notable works of the…

buchenwald-concentration-camp.s: Buchenwald was a Nazi concentration camp on the Ettersberg hill near Weimar, opened in 1937. About 280,000 people were imprisoned there and in its subcamps, and some 56,000 died from hunger, disease, medical experiments and executions.

battle-of-peregonovka.s: The Battle of Peregonovka was fought in September 1919 near the village of Peregonovka (Perehonivka), near Uman in central Ukraine, during the Russian Civil War. Nestor Makhno's Revolutionary Insurrectionary Army, cornered by White forces of Anton Denikin's Armed Forces of…

bingerville.s: Bingerville is a town on the Ébrié Lagoon east of Abidjan in Ivory Coast, named after the explorer and first governor Louis-Gustave Binger. It replaced yellow-fever-stricken Grand-Bassam as capital of the French colony in 1900 and remained the capital until it moved to Abidjan…

biloxi.s: Biloxi is a city on the Gulf Coast of Mississippi, United States. In 1699 Pierre Le Moyne d'Iberville built Fort Maurepas across Biloxi Bay, the first French settlement in Louisiana, and a later settlement on the present site served as the colony's capital from 1720 to 1722.

battle-of-the-nile.s: The Battle of the Nile was a naval battle fought on 1–3 August 1798 in Aboukir Bay, near Alexandria in Egypt. A British fleet under Horatio Nelson attacked the French fleet that had carried Napoleon Bonaparte's army to Egypt, destroying or capturing eleven of its thirteen…

battle-of-the-pyramids.s: The Battle of the Pyramids was fought on 21 July 1798 at Embabeh on the west bank of the Nile, near Cairo, during the French campaign in Egypt. Napoleon Bonaparte's army, formed in infantry squares, repelled the charges of the Mamluk cavalry of Murad Bey and inflicted heavy…

berber-dahir.s: The Berber Dahir was a decree issued on 16 May 1930 in the name of Sultan Muhammad V under the French protectorate in Morocco. It placed Berber-speaking areas under customary law administered by local councils and French criminal courts rather than Islamic sharia courts.

battambang.s: Battambang is the second-largest city of Cambodia, on the Sangkae River in the north-west, and capital of Battambang Province. Ruled by Siam from 1795, the province was ceded with Siem Reap to French-protected Cambodia by the Franco-Siamese treaty of 1907.

black-flag-army.s: The Black Flag Army was a band of Chinese irregulars led by Liu Yongfu, formed from rebel remnants who crossed into northern Vietnam in the 1860s. Taken into the service of the Vietnamese court, it controlled trade on the Red River and fought the French in Tonkin, killing…

basseterre.s: Basseterre is the capital of Saint Kitts and Nevis, on the south-west coast of the island of Saint Kitts. Founded by the French in 1627 after they and the English partitioned the island, it was the capital of the French part until the island was ceded to Britain by the Treaty…

battle-of-palo-hincado.s: The Battle of Palo Hincado was fought on 7 November 1808 near El Seibo in the east of the colony of Santo Domingo. Dominican creole forces led by Juan Sánchez Ramírez, with support from Puerto Rico, defeated the French troops of General Jean-Louis Ferrand, who killed himself…

blaise-diagne.s: Blaise Diagne was a Senegalese politician, elected in 1914 as deputy for the Four Communes of Senegal, the first black African in the French Chamber of Deputies. His laws of 1915 and 1916 confirmed the French citizenship of the communes' inhabitants.

bamako.s: Bamako is the capital and largest city of Mali, on the Niger River in the south-west of the country. A small trading town when French troops built a fort there in 1883, it became the capital of the colony of Upper Senegal and Niger in 1908 and later of French Sudan, linked to…

battle-of-the-boarn.s: The Battle of the Boarn was fought in 734 on the river Boarn (Boorne) in present-day Friesland, Netherlands. The Frankish mayor of the palace Charles Martel led a fleet and army against the Frisians and defeated and killed their king Poppo.

battle-of-baduhenna-wood.s: The Battle of Baduhenna Wood was fought in 28 CE in Frisia, in the present-day Netherlands, between the rebellious Frisii and Roman troops. The Frisii had risen after a Roman official demanded tribute in oxhides of impossible size and quality, and they hanged the soldiers…

battle-of-ilipa.s: The Battle of Ilipa was fought in 206 BCE near Ilipa, north of Seville in southern Spain, during the Second Punic War. The Roman general Publius Cornelius Scipio, later called Africanus, outmanoeuvred a larger Carthaginian army under Hasdrubal Gisco and Mago by reversing his…

battle-of-chandawar.s: The Battle of Chandawar was fought in 1194 near the Yamuna, in the area of modern Firozabad in Uttar Pradesh, between the army of Muhammad of Ghor and the Gahadavala king Jayachandra of Kannauj. Jayachandra was killed, reportedly struck by an arrow, and his forces broke.

bay-of-biscay.s: The Bay of Biscay is the gulf of the Atlantic Ocean bounded by the west coast of France and the north coast of Spain, from Brittany to Galicia. Known for storms and heavy swells, it was an important fishing and whaling ground for Basque and Breton sailors.

banjul.s: Banjul is the capital of The Gambia, on St Mary's Island at the mouth of the Gambia river. It was founded as Bathurst in 1816 by the British, who wanted a base to suppress the slave trade, and became the capital of the Gambia colony and protectorate.

battle-of-ulai.s: The Battle of the Ulai, also called the Battle of Til-Tuba, was fought around 653 BCE on the Ulai river in Elam between the army of the Assyrian king Ashurbanipal and the Elamite king Teumman. Teumman was defeated and beheaded, and Ashurbanipal installed his own candidates on…

beruas.s: Beruas is a small town in the Manjung district of Perak, Malaysia. Archaeological finds there, including Hindu-Buddhist statues, beads and Chinese ceramics, are linked with the half-legendary kingdom of Gangga Negara.

badrinath.s: Badrinath is a Hindu pilgrimage town in Chamoli district, Uttarakhand, India, high in the Garhwal Himalaya on the Alaknanda river. Its temple of Vishnu as Badrinarayan is one of the four Char Dham sites and is traditionally linked with Adi Shankara.

battle-of-bhangani.s: The Battle of Bhangani was fought in 1688 near Paonta Sahib in the Himalayan foothills between Guru Gobind Singh and the forces of Raja Fateh Shah of Garhwal and his allies among the hill rajas. It was the Guru's first battle, and his own account of it in the Bachittar Natak…

balliceaux.s: Balliceaux is a small, uninhabited island in the Grenadines of Saint Vincent. In 1796 and 1797 the British held several thousand Garifuna, defeated in the Second Carib War, on the island, where about half died of disease and hunger.

bodh-gaya.s: Bodh Gaya is a town in Bihar, India, where according to Buddhist tradition Siddhartha Gautama attained enlightenment under the Bodhi tree. It is the most sacred site of Buddhism, visited by pilgrims from across Asia.

batis.s: Batis was the commander of Gaza for the Achaemenid Persian Empire in 332 BCE. He refused to surrender to Alexander the Great and held the fortified city for about two months, during which Alexander was wounded.

bank-of-saint-george.s: The Bank of Saint George, or Casa di San Giorgio, was a financial institution of the Republic of Genoa, founded in 1407 to consolidate and manage the state's public debt. It collected the taxes assigned to its creditors and in the 15th century took over the administration of…

balaklava.s: Balaklava is a former town, now part of Sevastopol, on a narrow sheltered bay in the south-west of the Crimea. The Genoese held it as Cembalo from the 14th century until the Ottoman conquest in 1475, and the ruins of their fortress overlook the harbour.

bidzina-ivanishvili.s: Bidzina Ivanishvili is a Georgian billionaire and politician who made his fortune in Russia in the 1990s. He founded the Georgian Dream coalition, which defeated Mikheil Saakashvili's party in the 2012 elections, and served as prime minister from 2012 to 2013.

battle-of-bita-paka.s: The Battle of Bita Paka was fought on 11 September 1914 on the island of New Britain, then part of German New Guinea. An Australian naval and military expedition landed to seize the German radio station at Bita Paka, defended by German reservists and Melanesian police.

bethsaida.s: Bethsaida is an ancient town near the northern shore of the Sea of Galilee, associated in the New Testament with the apostles Peter, Andrew and Philip. Philip the Tetrarch raised it to the rank of a city named Julias.

beopheung-of-silla.s: Beopheung was the 23rd king of Silla in Korea, ruling from 514 to 540. He issued a code of administrative law in 520, recognised Buddhism after the martyrdom of Ichadon in 527, and adopted the first Silla era name.

brexit.s: Brexit was the withdrawal of the United Kingdom from the European Union, decided by a referendum on 23 June 2016 in which 51.9 per cent voted to leave. After years of negotiation the UK left on 31 January 2020, and a transition period ended on 31 December 2020.

banaba.s: Banaba, also called Ocean Island, is a raised coral island in the central Pacific, now part of Kiribati. Rich phosphate deposits found in 1900 led Britain to annex it, and mining by the Pacific Phosphate Company and later the British Phosphate Commissioners stripped most of…

banabans.s: The Banabans are the indigenous people of Banaba in the central Pacific. Phosphate mining from 1900 destroyed much of their land, and after the Japanese occupation of the Second World War most of them were resettled in 1945 on Rabi Island in Fiji, bought with mining royalties.

battle-of-tarawa.s: The Battle of Tarawa was fought from 20 to 23 November 1943 on Betio, an islet of Tarawa atoll in the Gilbert Islands, when United States Marines stormed a strongly fortified Japanese garrison. Nearly all of the roughly 4,500 Japanese defenders and Korean labourers were…

battle-of-salsu.s: The Battle of Salsu was fought in 612 when Goguryeo forces under Eulji Mundeok destroyed a large Sui army as it retreated across the Salsu river, usually identified with the Chongchon in north-western Korea. Only a few thousand of the Sui soldiers are said to have returned.

bianca-maria-visconti.s: Bianca Maria Visconti was the only child of Filippo Maria Visconti, Duke of Milan, born to his mistress. Her marriage to the condottiere Francesco Sforza in 1441 gave him a claim to Milan, which he took as duke in 1450.

battle-of-caravaggio.s: The Battle of Caravaggio was fought on 15 September 1448 near the town of Caravaggio in Lombardy, when Francesco Sforza, commanding the army of the Golden Ambrosian Republic of Milan, routed the Venetian army. Soon afterwards Sforza made peace with Venice and turned against…

bhagavadgomandal.s: The Bhagavadgomandal is a Gujarati encyclopedia and dictionary compiled under the patronage of Maharaja Bhagvatsinhji of Gondal. Work began in 1928, and it was published in nine volumes between 1944 and 1955.

bhagvatsinhji.s: Bhagvatsinhji was Maharaja of Gondal, a princely state in Kathiawar, until his death in 1944. Trained as a doctor at Edinburgh, he was among the most progressive Indian princes: he built railways, roads and schools, made education compulsory for girls, abolished many taxes and…

battle-of-gwiju.s: The Battle of Gwiju was fought in 1019 near Gwiju, in modern North Pyongan province, when Goryeo forces under Gang Gam-chan destroyed a retreating Khitan army of the Liao dynasty, of which only a few thousand men are said to have survived. The victory ended the wars between…

bruno-mauricio-de-zabala.s: Bruno Mauricio de Zabala was a Spanish soldier from the Basque Country who served as governor of Buenos Aires from 1717 to 1734. To halt Portuguese expansion from Colonia del Sacramento, he founded Montevideo on the eastern bank of the Río de la Plata in 1724–1726.

battle-of-las-salinas.s: The Battle of Las Salinas was fought in April 1538 near Cusco between the forces of Francisco Pizarro, led by his brother Hernando, and those of Diego de Almagro, in the first of the civil wars among the conquistadors of Peru. Almagro's army was routed, and he was captured,…

battle-of-chupas.s: The Battle of Chupas was fought on 16 September 1542 near Huamanga (Ayacucho) in Peru, when the royal governor Cristóbal Vaca de Castro defeated Diego de Almagro the Younger, whose followers had murdered Francisco Pizarro in 1541. Almagro was captured and beheaded at Cusco,…

breisgau.s: The Breisgau is a region in south-western Germany between the Rhine and the Black Forest, centred on Freiburg. For most of the period from the fourteenth century to 1805 it belonged to the Habsburgs as part of Further Austria, before passing to Baden under Napoleon.

barmen.s: Barmen is a former industrial town in the Wupper valley of western Germany, since 1929 part of the city of Wuppertal. With neighbouring Elberfeld it was one of Germany's earliest centres of textile manufacture, especially yarn bleaching, ribbons and lace, and it was the…

battle-of-saule.s: The Battle of Saule was fought on 22 September 1236 in northern Lithuania, near modern Šiauliai, when Samogitian and Semigallian forces destroyed an army of the Livonian Brothers of the Sword returning from a raid, killing the order's master Volkwin. The broken order was…

benelux.s: Benelux is the union of Belgium, the Netherlands and Luxembourg. It began as a customs union agreed by their governments in exile in London in 1944 and in force from 1948, and became an economic union by a treaty of 1958 that took effect in 1960.

belgian-revolution.s: The Belgian Revolution was the uprising of 1830–1831 in which the southern provinces of the United Kingdom of the Netherlands broke away from King William I. It began with riots in Brussels after a performance of the opera La muette de Portici in August 1830, and a provisional…

bazar-poznan.s: The Bazar is a hotel and commercial building in Poznań, Poland, opened in 1841 on the initiative of the physician and social activist Karol Marcinkowski as a centre of Polish economic and cultural life in Prussian Posen. It housed shops, a hotel and Polish societies, and in…

battle-of-kulikovo.s: The Battle of Kulikovo was fought on 8 September 1380 on Kulikovo Field near the upper Don, when an army of Russian principalities led by Grand Prince Dmitry of Moscow defeated the forces of Mamai, the warlord of the western Golden Horde. Although Tokhtamysh sacked Moscow two…

blaj.s: Blaj is a small town in Alba County, Romania, in central Transylvania. It became the seat of the Romanian Greek Catholic Church after the union of many Orthodox Romanians with Rome around 1700, and its schools, opened in 1754, made it a cradle of the Romanian national movement.

boris-of-tver.s: Boris Alexandrovich was Grand Prince of Tver from 1425 to 1461. He restored Tver's strength as an independent power between Moscow and Lithuania, allying first with Vytautas of Lithuania and later with Vasily II of Moscow during the Muscovite civil war, and his court produced…

battle-of-pressburg.s: The Battle of Pressburg was fought on 4 July 907 near Pressburg, modern Bratislava, when a Hungarian army destroyed a large Bavarian force under Margrave Luitpold, who was killed with many nobles and bishops. The victory secured the Hungarians' hold on the Carpathian Basin,…

battle-of-the-little-bighorn.s: The Battle of the Little Bighorn was fought on 25–26 June 1876 near the Little Bighorn River in Montana. Lakota, Northern Cheyenne and Arapaho warriors led by Sitting Bull, Crazy Horse and others destroyed five companies of the US 7th Cavalry under George Armstrong Custer, who…

balkh.s: Balkh, known to the Greeks as Bactra, is an ancient city in northern Afghanistan, near Mazar-i-Sharif, once the capital of Bactria. It was a centre of Achaemenid, Greco-Bactrian, Kushan and early Islamic rule and a hub of Buddhist and Zoroastrian learning, later called the…

bernard-coard.s: Bernard Coard is a Grenadian politician who was deputy prime minister in Maurice Bishop's People's Revolutionary Government. In October 1983 his faction in the New Jewel Movement placed Bishop under house arrest, and Bishop and several ministers were shot on 19 October, events…

big-hole.s: The Big Hole is a vast open pit at Kimberley in South Africa, dug largely by hand from 1871 to 1914 on the site of the Kimberley diamond mine. Tens of thousands of miners removed some 22 million tonnes of earth and recovered about 2,700 kilograms of diamonds.

black-flag-rebellion.s: The Black Flag Rebellion was an uprising of white diggers on the diamond fields of Kimberley, in the Crown colony of Griqualand West, in 1875. Led by Alfred Aylward and others, the diggers raised a black flag in protest against the government of Lieutenant-Governor Richard…

battle-of-maharajpur.s: The Battle of Maharajpur was fought on 29 December 1843 near Gwalior between a British army under Sir Hugh Gough and the forces of the Gwalior State. On the same day a second British force won at Punniar.

burao.s: Burao is a city in the Togdheer region of Somaliland, on the seasonal Togdheer river. It was a seat of the Habr Yunis sultans and a centre of the Isaaq clans, and in May 1991 it hosted the conference at which the Somali National Movement declared the restoration of…

battle-of-poley.s: The Battle of Poley was fought in 891 near Poley, the modern town of Aguilar de la Frontera south of Córdoba, between the army of the Umayyad emir Abd Allah and the rebel Umar ibn Hafsun. The emir's victory ended the most dangerous threat to Córdoba itself, though Ibn Hafsun…

baalshamin.s: Baalshamin, 'Lord of Heaven', was a Semitic sky and weather god worshipped across Syria and northern Mesopotamia from the early 1st millennium BCE to late antiquity. The Aramaic stele of Zakkur, king of Hamath, from around 800 BCE thanks him for saving the king from a siege,…

banu-taghlib.s: The Banu Taghlib were an Arab tribe of the Rabi'a group, settled in the Jazira of upper Mesopotamia in late antiquity. Largely Christian before Islam, many kept their faith under the early caliphs, who taxed them on special terms.

burdur.s: Burdur is a city in the Lakes Region of south-western Turkey, near Lake Burdur. In the 14th century it belonged to the Turkmen beylik of the Hamidids before passing to the Ottomans later in that century.

badis-ibn-al-mansur.s: Badis ibn al-Mansur was the Zirid emir of Ifriqiya from 996 to 1016, ruling as a vassal of the Fatimid Caliphate. He placed his uncle Hammad ibn Buluggin in charge of the western lands, but in 1015 Hammad broke away and founded the independent Hammadid dynasty.

badis-ibn-habus.s: Badis ibn Habus was the Zirid king of the Taifa of Granada from 1038 to 1073. He made Granada a strong Berber taifa, defeated Almería in 1038, annexed Málaga in 1057 and built much of the Alcazaba of Granada.

bejaia.s: Béjaïa, formerly known in Europe as Bougie, is a port city on the Mediterranean coast of north-eastern Algeria, in Kabylia. The Hammadid emir al-Nasir ibn Alnas made it his capital in the 1060s, and under the Hammadids and Hafsids it was a centre of trade and learning where…

binnya-u.s: Binnya U was king of the Mon kingdom of Martaban–Hanthawaddy in lower Burma from 1348 to 1384. His long reign was troubled by rebellions of vassals and attacks from neighbouring states, and in 1369 he moved the capital from Martaban to Pegu.

bago.s: Bago, formerly Pegu, is a city in southern Myanmar, north-east of Yangon. It was the capital of the Mon kingdom of Hanthawaddy from 1369, of the Toungoo kings Tabinshwehti and Bayinnaung in the 16th century, when it was one of the great cities of South-East Asia, and of the…

battle-of-chelenqo.s: The Battle of Chelenqo was fought on 6 January 1887 in eastern Ethiopia between the army of Menelik II, then king of Shewa, and the forces of Emir Abdullahi of Harar. Menelik's victory led to the occupation of Harar and its annexation to his realm, a key step in the southern…

berbera.s: Berbera is a port city on the Gulf of Aden in Somaliland. A trading port since antiquity, it was long famous for an annual fair, held in the cool season, where caravans from the interior met merchants from Arabia and India.

bisotun.s: Bisotun is a village and archaeological site in Kermanshah province, western Iran, at the foot of a mountain on the ancient road from Mesopotamia to the Iranian plateau. Its cliff bears the trilingual Behistun Inscription of Darius I, carved around 520 BCE, along with later…

black-september.s: Black September was the armed conflict of September 1970 in which the Jordanian army of King Hussein fought the Palestinian guerrilla groups of the Palestine Liberation Organization, which had built a state within a state in Jordan. A Syrian armoured incursion in support of…

brazos-reserve.s: The Brazos Reserve was a reservation set up by the State of Texas in 1854–55 on the Brazos River in north-central Texas for the Caddo, Anadarko, Waco, Tonkawa and other peoples. Hostility and attacks from white settlers led to its closure in 1859, when its inhabitants were…

battle-of-lugalo.s: The Battle of Lugalo was fought on 17 August 1891 near Iringa in present-day Tanzania, when Hehe warriors of Mkwawa ambushed a German column under Emil von Zelewski. Zelewski and most of his officers and askaris were killed.

battle-of-waterberg.s: The Battle of Waterberg was fought on 11 August 1904 at the Waterberg plateau in German South West Africa, now Namibia, between German troops under Lothar von Trotha and the Herero. The Herero broke out to the east, where many thousands died in the Omaheke desert, which the…

bingo-province.s: Bingo Province was an old province of Japan on the Inland Sea, now the eastern part of Hiroshima Prefecture. With neighbouring Aki it was held by the Mōri clan until 1600 and then by Fukushima Masanori.

benevento.s: Benevento is a city in Campania, southern Italy, in a valley of the southern Apennines. Originally the Samnite town of Maleventum, it became the Latin colony of Beneventum in 268 BCE and a station on the Via Appia, with the Arch of Trajan.

battle-of-ilerda.s: The Battle of Ilerda was Julius Caesar's campaign of June to August 49 BCE near modern Lleida in north-eastern Spain against the Pompeian legates Afranius and Petreius, at the start of his civil war. By manoeuvre and by cutting off their supplies rather than in a pitched…

bagaudae.s: The Bagaudae were bands of rebels in the late Roman West, drawn from impoverished peasants, runaway slaves and others outside imperial control. They rose in Gaul from the late 3rd century and in Gaul and Hispania in the 5th, when they were active in Tarraconensis in the 440s…

battle-of-munda.s: The Battle of Munda was fought on 17 March 45 BCE in southern Spain between Julius Caesar and the Pompeian army of Gnaeus and Sextus Pompeius and Titus Labienus. After a hard fight Caesar won; Labienus was killed, and Gnaeus Pompeius was caught and executed soon afterwards.

buffalo-river-kwazulu-natal.s: The Buffalo River, or Mzinyathi, is a river in KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa, a major tributary of the Tugela. In the 19th century it formed part of the boundary between the British colony of Natal and the Zulu Kingdom.

birgu.s: Birgu is an old fortified town on the Grand Harbour of Malta, guarded by Fort St Angelo. It was the first seat of the Knights Hospitaller after their arrival in 1530 and withstood the Ottoman Great Siege of 1565, after which it was renamed Città Vittoriosa.

belur.s: Belur is a town in Hassan district, Karnataka, India, on the Yagachi river. It was an early capital of the Hoysala dynasty and is famous for the Chennakeshava temple, consecrated in 1117 by King Vishnuvardhana.

beifu-army.s: The Beifu Army was the main field army of the Eastern Jin dynasty of China, raised by Xie Xuan in the late 370s from northern refugees settled around Guangling and Jingkou. It won the great victory over the Former Qin at the Battle of Fei River in 383.

bela-kun.s: Béla Kun was a Hungarian communist who led the Hungarian Soviet Republic of March to August 1919. A former prisoner of war in Russia, he founded the Hungarian Communist Party in November 1918, and his regime nationalised industry and land and carried out a Red Terror.

bertalan-szemere.s: Bertalan Szemere was a Hungarian politician who served as minister of the interior in the first Hungarian government of 1848 and as prime minister from May to August 1849, after the declaration of independence. When the revolution was defeated he hid the Holy Crown of Hungary…
