bleda.s: Bleda was a king of the Huns who ruled jointly with his younger brother Attila from the death of their uncle Rua around 435. Together they forced the Eastern Roman Empire to pay large tributes in gold under the Treaty of Margus and led raids into the Balkans in the early 440s.

battle-of-nedao.s: The Battle of Nedao was fought in 454 in Pannonia between the sons of Attila and a coalition of their former subject peoples led by the Gepid king Ardaric. The rebels won, and Attila's eldest son Ellac was killed.

burushaski.s: Burushaski is a language spoken in the Hunza, Nagar and Yasin valleys of Gilgit-Baltistan in northern Pakistan. It is a language isolate, with no proven relationship to any other language.

battle-of-shakar-kheda.s: The Battle of Shakar Kheda was fought on 11 October 1724 in Berar, in the Deccan, between Nizam-ul-Mulk, the future Asaf Jah I, and Mubariz Khan, the Mughal governor of Hyderabad backed by the court. Nizam-ul-Mulk won, and Mubariz Khan was killed.

bihac.s: Bihać is a city in north-western Bosnia and Herzegovina on the Una river, near the Croatian border. A royal free town of medieval Croatia, it fell to the Ottomans in 1592.

battle-of-qudayd.s: The Battle of Qudayd was fought in 747 at Qudayd, between Mecca and Medina, where Ibadi Kharijite rebels from Hadramawt under Abu Hamza al-Mukhtar ibn Awf defeated an army raised in Medina. Many of the Medinan fighters were killed, and the rebels went on to occupy Medina.

battle-of-alcantara-1580.s: The Battle of Alcântara was fought on 25 August 1580 near Lisbon, where a Spanish army under the Duke of Alba defeated the forces of António, Prior of Crato, the Portuguese claimant to the throne. The victory let Philip II of Spain take Lisbon and secure the Portuguese crown.

battle-of-fakhkh.s: The Battle of Fakhkh was fought in June 786 near Mecca, where Abbasid forces crushed a revolt of the Alid al-Husayn ibn Ali, a descendant of Hasan ibn Ali. Al-Husayn and many of his followers were killed.

battle-of-imagbon.s: The Battle of Imagbon was fought in May 1892 between a British expeditionary force from Lagos and the army of the Ijebu Kingdom in south-western Nigeria. It followed Ijebu's closure of its trade routes to Lagos merchants.

bardylis.s: Bardylis was an Illyrian king who in the early 4th century BCE built a powerful state on the north-western borders of Macedon. He defeated the Macedonians repeatedly, and in 359 BCE killed King Perdiccas III and thousands of his men.

baloch.s: The Baloch are an Iranian people living mainly in Balochistan, a region divided between south-eastern Iran, south-western Pakistan and southern Afghanistan, with communities in Oman and the Gulf. They speak Balochi, are largely Sunni Muslims and were traditionally organised in…

battle-of-okehazama.s: The Battle of Okehazama was fought in June 1560 in Owari Province, Japan, when Oda Nobunaga with a small force made a surprise attack on the much larger army of Imagawa Yoshimoto, which was resting during its march west. Yoshimoto was killed and the Imagawa never recovered.

bokar-biro.s: Bokar Biro was the last independent almamy of the Imamate of Futa Jallon in present-day Guinea, who took power in the 1890s amid feuds between the ruling houses. His resistance to French control brought a French military expedition, which defeated and killed him at the Battle…

battle-of-elchingen.s: The Battle of Elchingen was fought on 14 October 1805 near Ulm in Swabia during the Ulm campaign of the War of the Third Coalition. French troops under Marshal Michel Ney forced the crossing of the Danube and stormed the heights of Elchingen, defeating an Austrian corps under…

bad-gandersheim.s: Bad Gandersheim is a spa town in Lower Saxony, Germany, west of the Harz. It grew up around Gandersheim Abbey, founded in 852 by the Saxon count Liudolf and his wife Oda and moved there in 856, which as the family foundation of the Ottonian kings became a princely imperial…

bertrada-of-laon.s: Bertrada of Laon was a Frankish queen, the wife of Pippin the Short and mother of Charlemagne and Carloman. She was anointed with her husband by Pope Stephen II in 754 and remained an influential adviser after Pippin's death in 768, trying to reconcile her sons.

bertrada-of-prum.s: Bertrada of Prüm, also called Bertrada the Elder, was a Frankish noblewoman of the early 8th century. In 721 she and her son Charibert founded the abbey of Prüm in the Eifel, which was refounded and richly endowed in 752 by her granddaughter Bertrada of Laon and Pippin the Short.

bad-schussenried.s: Bad Schussenried is a spa town in the district of Biberach in upper Swabia, Baden-Württemberg, Germany. It grew around a Premonstratensian house founded in 1183, which became an imperial abbey.

blutritt.s: The Blutritt, or Blood Ride, is a mounted procession held each year on the Friday after Ascension Day at Weingarten in upper Swabia, Germany. Thousands of riders accompany a relic of the Holy Blood, believed to contain the blood of Christ, which Judith of Flanders gave to…

buyuk-menderes-river.s: The Büyük Menderes, the ancient Maeander, is a river of south-western Turkey that flows west into the Aegean Sea near ancient Miletus. Its winding course gave the word 'meander' to English, and its valley was a major route from the coast into Anatolia.

bleiburg-repatriations.s: The Bleiburg repatriations took place in May 1945, when British forces in southern Austria refused the surrender of retreating soldiers of the Independent State of Croatia and accompanying civilians near the town of Bleiburg and handed them over to Yugoslav Partisans. Many…

balochistan.s: Balochistan is an arid, mountainous region on the Iranian plateau, divided between Pakistan, Iran and Afghanistan and named after the Baloch people. It lies between the Indus valley and the Iranian heartland and has long been a route for armies and trade.

battle-of-mahidpur.s: The Battle of Mahidpur was fought on 21 December 1817 near Mahidpur in Malwa, central India, between the army of the Holkar state of Indore and British forces under Sir Thomas Hislop and Sir John Malcolm. The British won after hard fighting against the Holkar artillery.

battle-of-clastidium.s: The Battle of Clastidium was fought in 222 BCE near Clastidium, modern Casteggio in Lombardy, between the Roman Republic and the Insubres with their Gaesatae allies. The consul Marcus Claudius Marcellus killed the Gallic king Viridomarus in single combat and won the spolia…

battle-of-telamon.s: The Battle of Telamon was fought in 225 BCE near Telamon on the coast of Etruria between the Roman Republic and an invading army of Gauls from northern Italy, led by the Insubres and Boii with Gaesatae from across the Alps. The Gauls were trapped between two consular armies…

bureau-of-insular-affairs.s: The Bureau of Insular Affairs was an agency of the United States War Department that oversaw the civil government of territories acquired after the Spanish-American War, chiefly the Philippines and, for a time, Puerto Rico. Created in 1898 and given its name in 1902, it was…

bochica.s: Bochica was a culture hero and god of the Muisca of the Colombian highlands. In Muisca tradition he came from the east as a bearded old man, taught weaving, farming and moral laws, and opened the Tequendama Falls to drain a flood.

bartatua.s: Bartatua was a Scythian king of the 7th century BCE known from Assyrian texts and usually identified with Protothyes, named by Herodotus as the father of Madyes. He asked the Assyrian king Esarhaddon for the hand of an Assyrian princess, and his people thereafter generally…

buddhas-of-bamiyan.s: The Buddhas of Bamiyan were two monumental standing Buddha statues, 55 and 38 metres tall, carved into a cliff in the Bamiyan valley of central Afghanistan in the 6th century. Painted and plastered, they stood near a large Buddhist monastic complex on a branch of the Silk Road.

bonn-agreement-2001.s: The Bonn Agreement was signed on 5 December 2001 in Bonn, Germany, by Afghan factions opposed to the Taliban under United Nations auspices. It set up an Afghan Interim Authority led by Hamid Karzai, provided for a loya jirga to choose a transitional government and a new…

battle-of-uhud.s: The Battle of Uhud was fought in March 625 at Mount Uhud, north of Medina, between the Muslims under Muhammad and the Quraysh of Mecca led by Abu Sufyan. Archers who left their posts allowed a Meccan cavalry charge under Khalid ibn al-Walid, and the Muslims were defeated, with…

battle-of-keren.s: The Battle of Keren was fought from February to March 1941 in the mountains around the town of Keren in Eritrea, between Italian forces and British and Indian troops. After weeks of costly attacks on the strong Italian positions, the British broke through on 27 March.

battle-of-dogali.s: The Battle of Dogali was fought on 26 January 1887 near Massawa, on the Red Sea coast of Eritrea, when an Ethiopian army under Ras Alula destroyed an Italian column of some 500 men marching to relieve a besieged fort. The defeat shocked Italy and briefly checked its expansion…

battle-of-leros.s: The Battle of Leros was fought in November 1943 on the Aegean island of Leros, which British and Italian troops had held since Italy's armistice in September. After weeks of air attacks, German paratroopers and seaborne forces landed on 12 November and forced the garrison to…

bloody-christmas-1920.s: Bloody Christmas was the Italian army and navy attack on Fiume, now Rijeka, from 24 to 29 December 1920, ending Gabriele D'Annunzio's occupation of the city. After the Treaty of Rapallo made Fiume a free state, D'Annunzio refused to leave, and Italian forces under General…

bharmal.s: Bharmal was the Kachhwaha Raja of Amber in Rajasthan from 1548 until his death in 1574. In 1562 he became one of the first Rajput rulers to submit to the Mughal emperor Akbar, and gave him his daughter in marriage; she became the mother of Jahangir.

bob-marley.s: Bob Marley was a Jamaican singer and songwriter who brought reggae to a worldwide audience with his band the Wailers. A follower of Rastafari, he wrote songs of spiritual faith, protest and love, such as No Woman, No Cry, Get Up, Stand Up and Redemption Song.

batu-sawar.s: Batu Sawar was the capital of the Johor Sultanate on the upper Johor River in the southern Malay Peninsula from the late 16th century. It was sacked by Aceh under Iskandar Muda in 1613, when the sultan was carried off, and again by Jambi in 1673, after which the court moved…

batu-lintang-camp.s: Batu Lintang camp was a Japanese internment camp at Kuching in Sarawak, Borneo, from 1942 to 1945. It held British, Australian and Dutch prisoners of war together with civilian men, women and children, who suffered starvation and disease.

banu-kalb.s: The Banu Kalb were an Arab tribe of the Syrian steppe, part of the Quda'a confederation. They were key allies of the Umayyad Caliphate in the 7th century, and Mu'awiya's wife Maysun was a Kalbi.

battle-of-al-uqhuwana.s: The Battle of al-Uqhuwana was fought in 1029 near Lake Tiberias in Palestine, where a Fatimid army under Anushtakin al-Dizbari defeated an alliance of the Jarrahids and the Mirdasids. The Mirdasid emir Salih ibn Mirdas was killed.

battle-of-sammel.s: The Battle of Sammel was fought in January 1544 near Sammel in Rajasthan between the army of Sher Shah Suri and the Rathore forces of Rao Maldeo of Marwar. Maldeo withdrew before the battle, but his commanders Jaita and Kumpa attacked and were killed after heavy fighting.

battle-of-sanluri.s: The Battle of Sanluri was fought in June 1409 in southern Sardinia, where an Aragonese army led by Martin the Younger, King of Sicily, defeated the forces of the Judicate of Arborea under William of Narbonne. The defeat broke Arborea's resistance, and within a decade the last…

benedetta-of-cagliari.s: Benedetta was judge, or ruler, of the Judicate of Cagliari in Sardinia from 1214 until her death around 1232. Her reign was dominated by the growing power of Pisa, which in 1216 built the fortress of Castel di Castro on the hill above Cagliari.

baiuly.s: The Baiuly are the largest of the three tribal groupings of the Junior Zhuz, the western branch of the Kazakh people, made up of twelve clans, including the Adai. They grazed their herds between the Ural river, the Caspian Sea and the Mangyshlak peninsula.

bazm-u-razm.s: Bazm u Razm, "Feast and Battle", is a Persian chronicle by Aziz ibn Ardashir Astarabadi, court historian of Kadi Burhan al-Din, ruler of Sivas in central Anatolia. Completed around 1398, it describes his reign, campaigns and court life in an ornate literary style.

battle-of-kirkdilim.s: The Battle of Kırkdilim was fought in 1392 in north-central Anatolia between the forces of Kadi Burhan al-Din, ruler of Sivas, and an Ottoman army of Sultan Bayezid I. Kadi Burhan al-Din won, checking Ottoman expansion eastwards for a time.

buguma.s: Buguma is a town in Rivers State in the Niger Delta of Nigeria and the seat of the Amanyanabo of Kalabari. It was founded in the early 1880s by Kalabari people who left their old capital, Elem Kalabari, after a civil war and conflict with the Bonny Kingdom.

buddhadatta.s: Buddhadatta was a Theravada Buddhist scholar from the Chola country of southern India who wrote in Pali in the 5th century, traditionally as a contemporary of Buddhaghosa. His works include the Vinayavinicchaya, a summary of monastic discipline, and the Abhidhammavatara.

buddharaja.s: Buddharaja was the last known king of the Kalachuris of Mahishmati, who ruled Malwa and parts of the western Deccan in the 6th and early 7th centuries. The grandson of Krishnaraja, he was defeated around 600 to 610 by Mangalesha of the Chalukyas of Badami, and his kingdom was…

bhaskar-ram-kolhatkar.s: Bhaskar Ram Kolhatkar, known as Bhaskar Pant, was a general of Raghuji Bhonsle of the Maratha Nagpur Kingdom. In 1741 he conquered Ratanpur, ending the Kalachuri line in Chhattisgarh, and from 1742 he led the bargi raids into Bengal against the Nawab Alivardi Khan.

bheraghat.s: Bheraghat is a town on the Narmada river near Jabalpur in Madhya Pradesh, India. It is known for the Marble Rocks, where the river flows through a gorge of white marble cliffs, and the nearby Dhuandhar Falls.

bhoja-paramara.s: Bhoja was a king of the Paramara dynasty of Malwa in central India, ruling from about 1010 to 1055. Celebrated as a polymath, he was credited with works on poetics, architecture and medicine, made Dhar a centre of learning and built the Bhojpur Shiva temple.

bhawanipatna.s: Bhawanipatna is a town in western Odisha, India, and the headquarters of Kalahandi district. It became the capital of the princely state of Kalahandi in 1849, when the ruling family moved there from Junagarh.

bhaskaravarman.s: Bhaskaravarman was the greatest king of the Varman dynasty of Kamarupa in Assam, ruling in the first half of the 7th century. He allied with Harsha of Kannauj against Shashanka of Gauda and, after Shashanka's death, took his capital Karnasuvarna.

buea.s: Buea is a town on the eastern slopes of Mount Cameroon and the capital of the Southwest Region of Cameroon. Its cool climate led the Germans to make it the seat of government of Kamerun from 1901 to 1909.

bulu-people.s: The Bulu are a Bantu-speaking people of the forests of southern Cameroon, part of the Beti-Pahuin group, with Ebolowa as their main town. In the 1890s they controlled trade routes inland and fought the advance of German colonial forces, which defeated them around 1901.

bajreshwari-devi-temple.s: The Bajreshwari Devi Temple is a Hindu temple to the goddess Vajreshwari in Kangra, Himachal Pradesh, India, and one of the major goddess shrines of northern India. Its great wealth attracted Mahmud of Ghazni, who plundered it in 1009, and it was attacked again by later invaders.

basse-santa-su.s: Basse Santa Su is a town on the south bank of the upper Gambia River and the chief town of the Upper River Region of the Gambia. It grew as a river port and market for groundnuts and other trade.

bhumimitra.s: Bhumimitra was the second king of the Kanva dynasty of Magadha in northern India in the 1st century BCE, according to the Puranas, which give him a reign of fourteen years. He succeeded the founder, Vasudeva Kanva.

balasagun.s: Balasagun was a medieval city in the Chu valley of northern Kyrgyzstan, near modern Tokmok. Founded by Sogdian settlers, it became a capital of the Kara-Khanid Khanate in the 10th and 11th centuries and then of the Qara Khitai, and was the birthplace of the poet Yusuf Balasaguni.

balikesir.s: Balıkesir is a city in north-western Turkey, in the historic region of Mysia south of the Sea of Marmara. Around 1300 it became the seat of the Karasid (Karesi) beylik, which the Ottomans absorbed in the mid-14th century, gaining the troops and coastland that carried them into…

bayana.s: Bayana is a historic town in Bharatpur district of eastern Rajasthan, India, overlooked by the hill fort of Vijayamandirgarh. In the early medieval period it was a seat of the Jadaun Rajputs, and it later became an important fortress and indigo centre under the Delhi Sultanate…

bawlake.s: Bawlake was one of the Karenni States in the hills of eastern Burma, a small chiefdom ruled by a hereditary saopha. Like its neighbours Kantarawaddy and Kyebogyi, it was recognised as independent by Britain and the Burmese king in 1875 and became a British feudatory in 1892.

badr-abu-tuwayriq.s: Badr Abu Tuwayriq was a sultan of the Kathiri dynasty in the Hadramawt, in southern Arabia, in the 16th century. Using firearms and soldiers obtained through contacts with the Ottomans, he extended Kathiri rule over most of the Hadramawt and into Dhofar.

baijnath-uttarakhand.s: Baijnath is a town on the Gomti River in Bageshwar district of Uttarakhand, India, known for a group of medieval Shiva temples. It is usually identified with Kartikeyapura, capital of the Katyuri kings, in the Katyur valley.

battle-of-the-elleporus.s: The Battle of the Elleporus was fought in 389 BCE in southern Italy between Dionysius I of Syracuse and the Italiote League of Greek cities led by Croton. Dionysius surprised and routed the League's army near the Elleporus river, then released the prisoners without ransom.

bhoramdeo-temple.s: The Bhoramdeo Temple is a Hindu temple dedicated to Shiva near Kawardha in Kabirdham district of Chhattisgarh, India. Built in the 11th century under a local Nagavanshi dynasty, it is noted for its carved sculpture, which has earned it the name 'Khajuraho of Chhattisgarh'.

baikonur-cosmodrome.s: The Baikonur Cosmodrome is a space launch site on the steppe of southern Kazakhstan, near the Syr Darya. Built by the Soviet Union from 1955, it launched Sputnik 1 in 1957 and Yuri Gagarin, the first man in space, in 1961.

bohol.s: Bohol is an island province in the Central Visayas of the Philippines, known for the Chocolate Hills. Before Spanish rule it had coastal communities led by datus, and in 1565 its chief Sikatuna made a blood compact with Miguel López de Legazpi.

battle-of-ganter.s: The Battle of Ganter was fought in 1222 in East Java between Ken Arok, ruler of Tumapel, and Kertajaya, king of Kediri. Ken Arok's victory ended the Kediri Kingdom and made him founder of the kingdom of Singhasari under the name Rajasa.

bednur.s: Bidanur, also known as Bednore and now called Nagar, is a town in the Shimoga district of Karnataka, India. The Keladi Nayakas made it their capital around 1639, and it grew rich on the trade in pepper and areca.

battle-of-tit.s: The Battle of Tit was fought in May 1902 near the village of Tit in the Ahaggar region of southern Algeria. A French force of camel-mounted Saharan auxiliaries defeated the Kel Ahaggar Tuareg, inflicting heavy losses.

bilma.s: Bilma is an oasis town in the Kaouar region of north-eastern Niger, in the Sahara. Its salt works have for centuries produced salt and dates carried south by great Tuareg camel caravans, the azalai, to the Hausa lands.

battle-of-minatogawa.s: The Battle of Minatogawa was fought in 1336 near modern Kobe, Japan, between the forces of Ashikaga Takauji and the loyalists of Emperor Go-Daigo. Takauji defeated Nitta Yoshisada and killed Kusunoki Masashige, then took Kyoto.

bhuyan.s: The Bhuyan are an Adivasi people of eastern India, living mainly in the hills of northern Odisha, Jharkhand and West Bengal. The hill Bhuyan of Keonjhar practised shifting cultivation and held hereditary duties at the installation of the Rajas.

bacchylides.s: Bacchylides was a Greek lyric poet from Ioulis on the island of Keos and the nephew of Simonides. He wrote victory odes, dithyrambs and other choral poems for patrons such as Hieron I of Syracuse.

battle-of-miani.s: The Battle of Miani was fought on 17 February 1843 near Hyderabad in Sindh, where a small British-Indian army under General Sir Charles Napier defeated the much larger forces of the Talpur amirs of Sindh. Napier won again at Dubba in March, and Britain annexed Sindh, which was…

borjigin.s: The Borjigin were the Mongol clan to which Genghis Khan belonged. His ancestors, including Khabul Khan, led the Khamag Mongol confederation in the 12th century, and after the founding of the Mongol Empire descent from Genghis Khan's branch of the clan became the condition for…

bayat-tribe.s: The Bayat are a Turkic tribe of the Oghuz confederation, listed among its tribes by Mahmud al-Kashgari in the 11th century. Bayat groups moved west with the Seljuk and later migrations into Iran, Anatolia and the Caucasus, and under the Safavids they were one of the Qizilbash…

burhanpur.s: Burhanpur is a city on the Tapti river in Madhya Pradesh, India. Founded around 1400 by Nasir Khan of the Faruqi dynasty, it was the capital of the Khandesh Sultanate and, after Akbar's conquest of 1601, a major Mughal base for campaigns in the Deccan.

bedia-cathedral.s: Bedia Cathedral is a medieval church in eastern Abkhazia, founded in 999 by Bagrat III, king of the Abkhazians and the first king of a united Georgia, who was buried there in 1014. Its gold Bedia Chalice, a gift of the king, is one of the masterpieces of Georgian metalwork.

battle-of-salamis.s: The Battle of Salamis was a naval battle fought in 480 BCE in the straits between the island of Salamis and the coast of Attica, during the second Persian invasion of Greece. The allied Greek fleet, led by Athens under Themistocles, defeated the larger fleet of Xerxes I, who…

berat.s: Berat is a city in south-central Albania on the Osum river, dominated by a hilltop citadel. Contested in the Middle Ages by Byzantines, Bulgarians, Angevins and Serbs, it withstood an Angevin siege in 1281.

biskra.s: Biskra is an oasis city in north-eastern Algeria, on the southern edge of the Aurès Mountains at the gateway to the Sahara. Known in Roman times as Vescera, it lay on routes between the Mediterranean coast and the desert.

battle-of-vescera.s: The Battle of Vescera was fought near Biskra in present-day Algeria in 682 or 683, when Berber forces under Kusaila, with Byzantine support, ambushed the Arab commander Uqba ibn Nafi as he returned from a campaign that had reached the Atlantic. Uqba and most of his escort were…

benteshina.s: Benteshina was a king of Amurru in the Levant in the 13th century BCE. After the Battle of Kadesh he was deposed by the Hittite king Muwatalli II, apparently for siding with Egypt, and taken to Hatti, where he came under the protection of the future Hattusili III.

bhagalpur.s: Bhagalpur is a city in Bihar, India, on the southern bank of the Ganges. Nearby lay Champa, capital of the ancient kingdom of Anga, and in its district are the ruins of the Buddhist monastic university of Vikramashila, founded under the Pala dynasty.

bagyendanwa.s: Bagyendanwa is the royal drum of the Kingdom of Ankole (Nkore) in south-western Uganda. In Ankole tradition it was inherited by Ruhinda, founder of the Hinda dynasty, when Chwezi rule dissolved, and it embodied the kingship itself: it was kept in its own shrine, attended by…

bahima.s: The Bahima are the pastoral, cattle-keeping people of the kingdoms of the Great Lakes region of East Africa, especially Ankole in Uganda and Karagwe in Tanzania. In these kingdoms they formed the ruling stratum, holding herds of long-horned cattle and supplying the royal…

bairu.s: The Bairu are the farming people of the Kingdom of Ankole in south-western Uganda and of neighbouring kingdoms such as Karagwe. They formed the majority of the population but held lower status than the cattle-owning Bahima, from whom the kings and leading chiefs came, and owed…

barcelona.s: Barcelona is the capital of Catalonia and the second-largest city of Spain, on the Mediterranean coast between the Llobregat and Besòs rivers. Founded as the Roman colony of Barcino, it was taken by the Franks in 801 and became the seat of the counts of Barcelona, whose union…

battle-of-renfrew.s: The Battle of Renfrew was fought in 1164 near Renfrew on the Clyde, when Somerled, King of the Isles, invaded the Scottish kingdom with a large fleet drawn from Argyll, the Isles and Dublin. Somerled was killed early in the engagement, possibly by treachery, and his army…

bagratuni-dynasty.s: The Bagratuni dynasty was an Armenian noble house that rose from among the great princely families of the Arsacid kingdom to become the leading power in Armenia. Ashot I was recognised as king in 884–885 by both the Abbasid caliph and the Byzantine emperor, and the dynasty…

battle-of-rhandeia.s: The Battle of Rhandeia was fought in 62 CE in Armenia during the war between Rome and Parthia over the Armenian throne. A Roman army under Lucius Caesennius Paetus was besieged by the Parthian king Vologases I at Rhandeia and forced to accept humiliating terms.

battle-of-covadonga.s: The Battle of Covadonga was fought in the mountains of Asturias, traditionally in 718 but more probably in 722, between a Muslim force and Asturian rebels led by the Visigothic noble Pelagius. Pelagius's victory, magnified in later chronicles, secured the independence of a…

bamenda.s: Bamenda is a city in the Grassfields of north-western Cameroon and the capital of the North-West Region. It grew from a German military station established in the early 20th century near older Grassfields kingdoms such as Bafut, Mankon and Bali-Nyonga, and became an…

bono-region.s: The Bono Region is an administrative region of western Ghana, created in 2019 when the old Brong-Ahafo Region was divided. Its capital is Sunyani.

bali-aga.s: The Bali Aga, or Bali Mula, are Balinese communities that preserve customs older than the Hindu-Javanese court culture that spread on Bali after the Majapahit conquest of the 14th century. They live mainly in mountain villages such as Trunyan on Lake Batur and Tenganan in…

bobovac.s: Bobovac is a ruined royal fortress in central Bosnia and Herzegovina, near the town of Vareš. First recorded in the mid-14th century, it was a chief residence of the kings of Bosnia, several of whom were buried in its chapel.

battle-of-ballon.s: The Battle of Ballon was fought on 22 November 845 near Bains-sur-Oust in eastern Brittany, between the Breton ruler Nominoe and the West Frankish king Charles the Bald. The Bretons defeated the Frankish army, and Charles was forced to accept Nominoe's authority in Brittany, a…

battle-of-jengland.s: The Battle of Jengland was fought in August 851 near Grand-Fougeray on the border of Brittany, between Erispoe, son of the Breton ruler Nominoe, and the West Frankish king Charles the Bald. The Bretons won a decisive victory, and by the Treaty of Angers that followed Charles…

battle-of-questembert.s: The Battle of Questembert was fought around 888 or 890 near Questembert in southern Brittany, where Alan, count of Vannes, later called Alan the Great, defeated a large Viking army. Medieval tradition says only a few hundred of the raiders escaped.

brecknockshire.s: Brecknockshire, or Breconshire, is a historic county of south-central Wales with its county town at Brecon. It was created in 1536 from the Norman marcher lordship of Brecknock, itself carved out of the Welsh kingdom of Brycheiniog after 1093.

brychan.s: Brychan is a legendary 5th-century king who gave his name to the Welsh kingdom of Brycheiniog. Medieval genealogies make him the son of an Irish prince and a Welsh princess and credit him with a great many children, a large number of whom were venerated as saints in Wales,…

buganda-agreement.s: The Buganda Agreement was signed on 10 March 1900 between Britain, represented by Sir Harry Johnston, and the regents of the young kabaka Daudi Chwa of Buganda, led by the chief minister Apolo Kagwa. It confirmed the kabaka and the Lukiiko under British protection, fixed the…

battle-of-jagaraga.s: The Battle of Jagaraga refers to the fighting at the fortified village of Jagaraga in the Balinese kingdom of Buleleng during the Dutch expeditions of 1848 and 1849. In 1848 Balinese forces under the patih Gusti Ketut Jelantik repulsed a Dutch attack with heavy losses.

balkan-league.s: The Balkan League was the alliance formed in 1912 by Bulgaria, Serbia, Greece and Montenegro against the Ottoman Empire, built on a series of bilateral treaties. Its members defeated the Ottomans in the First Balkan War of 1912–1913, driving them from most of their European…

bokar-saada.s: Bokar Saada was almamy of Bundu, the Muslim clerical state on the upper Senegal, in the second half of the 19th century. Brought to power with French support, he sided with France against Umar Tall and other rivals and used French backing to strengthen his rule.

boulebane.s: Boulebane is a village in eastern Senegal, near the Falémé river, that served as a capital of the almamys of Bundu. In the 18th and 19th centuries it was a royal residence of the Sisibe dynasty and, with other towns of Bundu such as Koussan, a centre of Islamic learning on the…

baganda.s: The Baganda, or Ganda, are a Bantu-speaking people of central Uganda, the country's largest ethnic group, whose kingdom of Buganda lay on the northern shore of Lake Victoria. In the late 19th century Ganda chiefs and soldiers allied with the British, fighting Bunyoro and…

babito-dynasty.s: The Babito are the royal dynasty of Bunyoro-Kitara in western Uganda, founded around 1500, according to tradition, by rulers of Luo origin from the north. They succeeded the legendary Bachwezi as rulers of Kitara, and branches of the dynasty also ruled Toro and other kingdoms…

bulawayo.s: Bulawayo is the second-largest city of Zimbabwe, in the south-west of the country. It began in the 1870s as the royal town of Lobengula, king of the Ndebele, and was rebuilt by the British South Africa Company after its occupation in 1893.

battle-of-jingxing.s: The Battle of Jingxing was fought in 204 BCE at the Jingxing pass in the Taihang Mountains, in present-day Hebei, during the Chu–Han Contention. The Han general Han Xin drew up part of his smaller army with its back to a river and sent cavalry to seize the enemy camp, routing…

battle-of-julu.s: The Battle of Julu was fought in 207 BCE near Julu, in present-day Hebei, between rebel forces led by Xiang Yu and the Qin armies besieging the city. Xiang Yu crossed the river, had his boats sunk and cooking pots broken so his men could not retreat, and defeated the Qin…

brechin.s: Brechin is a small cathedral city in Angus, eastern Scotland. It grew around an early medieval church, and its Irish-style round tower, built in the 11th century, is one of only two in mainland Scotland.

battle-of-hingston-down.s: The Battle of Hingston Down was fought in 838 at Hingston Down in east Cornwall, near the River Tamar, where Ecgberht of Wessex defeated a combined army of Cornish Britons and Danish Vikings. Recorded in the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle, it is the last recorded battle between the…

battle-of-krbava-field.s: The Battle of Krbava Field was fought on 9 September 1493 on the Krbava plain in Lika, Croatia, between a Croatian army under Ban Emerik Derenčin and Ottoman raiders led by Hadım Yakub Pasha. The Croatian nobility suffered a heavy defeat: the ban was captured and many nobles…

baska-tablet.s: The Baška tablet is a stone slab from the church of St Lucy at Jurandvor near Baška, on the island of Krk in Croatia, dated to around 1100. Its inscription in Glagolitic script records King Zvonimir's gift of land to the Benedictine abbey there, and it is one of the oldest and…

biograd-na-moru.s: Biograd na Moru is a coastal town in northern Dalmatia, Croatia, south of Zadar. It was one of the royal seats of the medieval Croatian kings and the seat of a bishop, and in 1102 Coloman of Hungary was crowned king of Croatia and Dalmatia there.

battle-of-gvozd-mountain.s: The Battle of Gvozd Mountain was fought in 1097 in the Gvozd range of central Croatia, where the Croatian king Petar Snačić was defeated and killed by the Hungarian army of King Coloman. It ended the last native Croatian kingship, and in 1102 Coloman was crowned king of…

bellapais-abbey.s: Bellapais Abbey is a ruined monastery near Kyrenia in northern Cyprus, founded around 1200 and largely rebuilt under the Lusignan kings in the 13th and 14th centuries. Built for Premonstratensian canons, its church, cloister and great refectory are among the finest Gothic…

battus-i-of-cyrene.s: Battus I was the founder and first king of Cyrene in Libya, who, according to Herodotus, led settlers from the island of Thera there around 631 BCE on the advice of the Delphic oracle. He ruled for about 40 years and founded the Battiad dynasty, whose kings were alternately…

battle-of-irasa.s: The Battle of Irasa was fought around 570 BCE in Cyrenaica, in present-day Libya, where the Greeks of Cyrene under Battus II defeated an Egyptian army sent by the pharaoh Apries to help the local Libyans. Herodotus records the battle, whose outcome provoked a mutiny in Egypt…

battle-of-adibo.s: The Battle of Adibo was fought in 1896 near Yendi, in what is now northern Ghana, between German colonial forces advancing from Togo and the army of the Dagomba kingdom of Dagbon. The Germans, with modern rifles, defeated the Dagomba cavalry and then burned Yendi.

battle-of-lissa-1866.s: The Battle of Lissa was fought on 20 July 1866 off the island of Vis (Lissa) in the Adriatic during the Third Italian War of Independence. An Austrian fleet under Wilhelm von Tegetthoff defeated a larger Italian fleet under Carlo Persano, ramming and sinking the ironclad Re…

battle-of-callann.s: The Battle of Callann was fought in 1261 near Kilgarvan in County Kerry, Ireland, where Fínghin Mac Carthaigh, king of Desmond, defeated the Anglo-Norman FitzGeralds. John FitzThomas and his son Maurice were killed, and the victory checked Norman expansion into south-west…

bantham.s: Bantham is a coastal site at the mouth of the River Avon in south Devon, England. Finds of imported Mediterranean amphorae and fine wares show that it was a trading and landing place in the 5th and 6th centuries, probably linked to the export of tin to the Byzantine world.

bury-st-edmunds.s: Bury St Edmunds is a market town in Suffolk, England. It grew around the abbey that housed the relics of Edmund, the East Anglian king killed by the Great Heathen Army in 869, whose shrine became one of the great pilgrimage centres of medieval England.

birr.s: Birr is a town in County Offaly, Ireland, on the Camcor River. It grew around the monastery founded by Saint Brendan of Birr in the 6th century, which produced the Macregol Gospels, and later around the O'Carroll stronghold that became Birr Castle.

brendan-of-birr.s: Brendan of Birr was an Irish abbot of the 6th century, founder of the monastery of Birr in what is now County Offaly. Counted among the Twelve Apostles of Ireland, he was a friend of Columba, whom he is said to have defended at the synod that tried to excommunicate him.

barwick-in-elmet.s: Barwick-in-Elmet is a village in West Yorkshire, England, east of Leeds. It keeps large earthworks of an Iron Age hillfort, later reused for a Norman motte, and its name recalls the British kingdom of Elmet, which survived in the area until the early 7th century.

battle-of-hastings.s: The Battle of Hastings was fought on 14 October 1066 near Hastings in Sussex, where Duke William of Normandy defeated and killed King Harold Godwinson of England. The victory began the Norman Conquest: William was crowned king on Christmas Day 1066, and a new Norman…

belle-isle-fermanagh.s: Belle Isle is an island and estate in Upper Lough Erne, County Fermanagh, Northern Ireland. In the 15th century it was the home of Cathal Mac Maghnusa, dean of Lough Erne, under whose direction the Annals of Ulster were compiled there.

bakel.s: Bakel is a town on the Senegal River in eastern Senegal, near the borders with Mali and Mauritania. The French built a fort there around 1820 as a trading post in the Soninke kingdom of Gajaaga, and it later served as a base for French expansion along the upper Senegal.

boryslav.s: Boryslav is a town in Lviv Oblast in western Ukraine, in the foothills of the Carpathians. From the mid-19th century it became the centre of the Galician oil industry, and in the early 20th century the oil basin around Boryslav and Drohobych made Austrian Galicia one of the…

bhir-mound.s: The Bhir Mound is the oldest of the city sites at Taxila in northern Pakistan, occupied from about the 6th to the 2nd century BCE. Its excavated remains, with irregular streets and stone houses, represent the city of the Achaemenid and Mauryan periods that Alexander the Great…

battle-of-catraeth.s: The Battle of Catraeth was fought around 600 between a war band of the British kingdom of Gododdin and the Angles of Deira and Bernicia. Known from the poem Y Gododdin attributed to Aneirin, it ended in the near-total destruction of the British warriors.

battle-of-embabo.s: The Battle of Embabo was fought on 6 June 1882 in western Ethiopia between King Menelik of Shewa and King Tekle Haymanot of Gojjam, rivals for the Oromo lands south of the Abay. Menelik won and captured Tekle Haymanot, securing the south-west for Shewa.

biafada.s: The Biafada are a people of southern Guinea-Bissau, living along the Rio Grande de Buba and the Corubal. In the 16th and 17th centuries their small kingdoms, such as Guinala, traded with Portuguese and Cape Verdean merchants, but they declined under pressure from Kaabu and the…

battle-of-mynydd-carn.s: The Battle of Mynydd Carn was fought in 1081 at an unidentified site in south-west Wales. Gruffudd ap Cynan and Rhys ap Tewdwr defeated a coalition of Trahaearn ap Caradog of Gwynedd, Caradog ap Gruffudd of Gwent and Morgannwg, and Meilyr ap Rhiwallon, all three of whom were…

bobo-people.s: The Bobo are a Mande-speaking people of western Burkina Faso and neighbouring Mali, living mainly around Bobo-Dioulasso, the city that bears their name. Farmers organised in largely autonomous villages, they are known for masks associated with Do, a spirit of renewal, used in…

bobo-dioulasso.s: Bobo-Dioulasso is the second-largest city of Burkina Faso, in the south-west of the country. It grew from the village of Sya, a market of Dyula Muslim traders, which in the 19th century became the main centre of the Kingdom of Gwiriko.

bwa-people.s: The Bwa are a Gur-speaking people of west-central Burkina Faso and south-eastern Mali, in the region of the Black Volta. Living in largely independent farming villages without kings, they are known for leaf masks and painted wooden plank masks used in the cult of Do.

bono-people.s: The Bono, also called Abron, are an Akan people of west-central Ghana and eastern Côte d'Ivoire. Their state of Bono-Manso is regarded as one of the earliest Akan kingdoms, and groups of Bono migrants moving west from the late 17th century founded the Kingdom of Gyaman around…

bondoukou.s: Bondoukou is a town in north-eastern Côte d'Ivoire near the border with Ghana. An old centre of Dyula Muslim traders on the route between the Akan goldfields and the middle Niger, it lay at the heart of the Abron Kingdom of Gyaman, whose kings held court nearby.

battle-of-gaixia.s: The Battle of Gaixia, fought in 202 BCE in what is now Anhui province, was the final battle of the Chu–Han Contention. Han forces under Liu Bang and his general Han Xin surrounded Xiang Yu, whose troops, hearing Chu songs sung in the enemy camp, believed their homeland lost.

black-army-of-hungary.s: The Black Army was the standing mercenary army of King Matthias Corvinus of Hungary, built up from the 1460s. Made up of Czech, German, Polish, Serbian and Hungarian soldiers, with heavy cavalry, light hussars, handgunners and Hussite-style wagon forts, it won Moravia, Silesia…

bushenyi-district.s: Bushenyi District is a district in western Uganda, in the former Ankole region. Its green hills grow tea, coffee and bananas.

battle-of-chikhori-1757.s: The Battle of Chikhori was fought in 1757 in western Georgia, where King Solomon I of Imereti defeated an Ottoman army supporting his rebellious nobles. The victory strengthened his hold on the kingdom against Ottoman-backed rivals, and he went on to ban the slave trade from…

battle-of-chikhori.s: The Battle of Chikhori was fought in 1463 in western Georgia, where Bagrat, a prince who had made himself king of Imereti, defeated King George VIII of Georgia with the help of the atabeg of Samtskhe. The victory confirmed the break-up of the united Georgian kingdom into the…

bethel.s: Bethel was an ancient town north of Jerusalem, usually identified with Beitin in the West Bank. The Bible links it with Abraham and Jacob, and after the division of the kingdom Jeroboam I set up a royal shrine there with a golden calf to rival Jerusalem.

bali-strait.s: The Bali Strait is the narrow channel, only about 2.4 kilometres wide at its narrowest, that separates eastern Java from Bali in Indonesia and links the Bali Sea with the Indian Ocean. Ferries cross it between Ketapang near Banyuwangi and Gilimanuk on Bali.

baldwin-iv-of-jerusalem.s: Baldwin IV, known as the Leper King, was king of Jerusalem from 1174. Although he suffered from leprosy from childhood, he led his army in person and defeated Saladin at the Battle of Montgisard in 1177.

bhubaneswar.s: Bhubaneswar is the capital of the Indian state of Odisha. Near it lie Sisupalgarh, a fortified city of the last centuries BCE often linked with ancient Kalinga, and the Jain caves of Udayagiri and Khandagiri.

battle-of-danture.s: The Battle of Danture was fought in 1594 near Kandy in central Sri Lanka, where King Vimaladharmasuriya I of Kandy destroyed a Portuguese army under Pedro Lopes de Sousa that had come to install a client queen, Dona Catarina. The Portuguese commander was killed, and…

bagauda.s: Bagauda is the legendary first king of Kano in northern Nigeria, who according to the Kano Chronicle came to power around 999 among the farming and iron-working communities near Dala Hill. Hausa tradition makes him a grandson of Bayajidda, the hero from whom the rulers of the…

battle-of-langensalza-1866.s: The Battle of Langensalza was fought on 27 June 1866 in Thuringia during the Austro-Prussian War. The Hanoverian army of King George V defeated a Prussian force, but surrounded by larger Prussian armies it surrendered two days later.

battle-of-langensalza-1075.s: The Battle of Langensalza, also called the Battle of Homburg on the Unstrut, was fought on 9 June 1075 in Thuringia during the Saxon rebellion against the Salian king Henry IV. Henry defeated the rebel Saxon nobility, whose leaders submitted to him later that year.

bayonet-constitution.s: The Bayonet Constitution was the constitution forced on King Kalākaua of Hawaii in July 1887 by a group of mainly American planters and businessmen backed by an armed militia. It sharply reduced the king's powers and imposed property and income qualifications that gave wealthy…

book-of-joshua.s: The Book of Joshua is the sixth book of the Hebrew Bible, describing the Israelite conquest and division of Canaan under Moses' successor Joshua. Its accounts of the fall of Jericho, Ai and Hazor were long read as history, but archaeology shows a more complex picture, and most…

battle-of-sabilla.s: The Battle of Sabilla was fought on 29 March 1929 in Najd, central Arabia, between the forces of Ibn Saud and the Ikhwan, the tribal religious warriors who had helped him conquer Arabia but rebelled against his ban on raiding into Iraq and Kuwait and his acceptance of modern…

baiyue.s: The Baiyue, or Hundred Yue, were the various non-Chinese peoples of southern China and northern Vietnam in the first millennium BCE, living in states such as Minyue, Nanyue and Ouyue. The Qin conquered much of their land in the late 3rd century BCE, and the Han dynasty…

bosten-lake.s: Bosten Lake is the largest freshwater lake in Xinjiang, China, lying in the Yanqi basin on the southern side of the Tian Shan, near the town of Karasahr. Fed mainly by the Kaidu River and drained by the Konqi River towards the Tarim Basin, it supported the ancient oasis…

battle-of-krtsanisi.s: The Battle of Krtsanisi was fought on 11 September 1795 near Tbilisi between the Qajar army of Agha Mohammad Khan and the much smaller Georgian force of Erekle II of Kartli-Kakheti. Left without the Russian help promised by the Treaty of Georgievsk, the Georgians were…

bainuk.s: The Bainuk are a people of the Casamance region of southern Senegal, The Gambia and Guinea-Bissau, regarded as among the oldest inhabitants of the area. In the 15th and 16th centuries Portuguese sources describe a Bainuk kingdom of Kasa on the south bank of the Casamance…

balanta.s: The Balanta are a West African people living mainly in Guinea-Bissau, where they form the largest ethnic group, and in the Casamance region of Senegal. Skilled rice farmers who built polders in coastal mangrove swamps, they traditionally lived without chiefs or kings in…

baixa-de-kasanje.s: The Baixa de Kasanje, or Baixa de Cassanje, is a broad fertile lowland in the valley of the Kwango River in northern Angola. Around 1620 an Imbangala band settled there and founded the Kingdom of Kasanje, which dominated the slave trade between the interior and Portuguese Luanda.

brihadaranyaka-upanishad.s: The Brihadaranyaka Upanishad is one of the oldest and longest Upanishads, part of the Shatapatha Brahmana of the White Yajurveda, usually dated to around the 7th century BCE. Its dialogues, many featuring the sage Yajnavalkya, set out ideas of the self (atman), brahman, karma…

bede.s: Bede was a Northumbrian monk and scholar of the twin monastery of Wearmouth–Jarrow. His Ecclesiastical History of the English People, completed in 731, is the principal source for the history of the Anglo-Saxon kingdoms and their conversion, and his works on chronology…

bertha-of-kent.s: Bertha was a Frankish princess, daughter of the Merovingian king Charibert I of Paris, who married Æthelberht of Kent. A Christian, she came to Kent with her chaplain, Bishop Liudhard, and worshipped at St Martin's Church in Canterbury.

battle-of-salamis-in-cyprus.s: The Battle of Salamis in Cyprus was fought in 497 BCE during the Ionian Revolt, when the Greek cities of Cyprus, led by Onesilus of Salamis, rose against Persian rule. An Ionian fleet beat the Phoenician navy at sea, but on land the Persians won after Stasanor of Kourion…

bukoba.s: Bukoba is a town on the western shore of Lake Victoria in north-western Tanzania and the capital of Kagera Region. Founded as a German military post in 1890 among the Haya kingdoms, it became an administrative centre under German and British rule and a port for lake steamers…

betsileo.s: The Betsileo are a Malagasy people of the southern central highlands of Madagascar, around Fianarantsoa and Ambalavao. Skilled builders of terraced rice fields, they were organised in the 18th century into several kingdoms, including Lalangina, Isandra, Manandriana and…

battle-of-simancas.s: The Battle of Simancas was fought in August 939 near Simancas on the Pisuerga, close to the Douro, between Ramiro II of León and the army of Abd al-Rahman III, caliph of Córdoba. The Christian forces, with Navarrese and Castilian allies, won a decisive victory, and the caliph…

basotho-national-party.s: The Basotho National Party is a political party in Lesotho, founded in 1959 by Leabua Jonathan. Conservative and supported by the Catholic Church, it won the 1965 elections and led Lesotho to independence in 1966.

battle-of-sulcoit.s: The Battle of Sulcoit was fought in 967 near the town of Tipperary in Munster, Ireland. The Dál gCais under Mathgamain mac Cennétig and his brother Brian Boru defeated the Norse of Limerick under Ivar and their Irish allies, then sacked Limerick.

battle-of-the-trent.s: The Battle of the Trent was fought in 679 near the River Trent between Æthelred of Mercia and Ecgfrith of Northumbria. Ælfwine, Ecgfrith's young brother, was killed, and Archbishop Theodore of Canterbury negotiated a peace in which Æthelred paid compensation for his death. The…

black-ruthenia.s: Black Ruthenia is a historical region in the upper Neman basin of present-day western Belarus, around Navahrudak, Hrodna and Slonim. Brought under Lithuanian rule by Mindaugas in the mid-13th century, it was one of the first Ruthenian lands of the Grand Duchy of Lithuania, and…

battle-of-durbe.s: The Battle of Durbe was fought on 13 July 1260 near Durbe in present-day western Latvia, where Samogitian forces routed the combined army of the Livonian Order and the Teutonic Order. About 150 knights died, including the Livonian master Burchard von Hornhausen.

buto.s: Buto was an ancient city in the north-western Nile Delta of Egypt, at modern Tell el-Fara'in. Formed from the twin settlements of Pe and Dep, it was in later tradition the capital of the predynastic kingdom of Lower Egypt and the seat of the cobra goddess Wadjet.

buto-maadi-culture.s: The Buto-Maadi culture was the main prehistoric culture of Lower Egypt in the 4th millennium BCE, named after the sites of Buto in the Delta and Maadi near Cairo. Its people lived in villages, farmed and herded, and traded copper, pottery and other goods with the southern Levant.

bin-tepe.s: Bin Tepe, Turkish for 'thousand mounds', is a royal cemetery of the Kingdom of Lydia north of Sardis in western Turkey. It contains over a hundred burial mounds, including the tumulus of Alyattes, more than 350 metres across, which Herodotus ranked among the greatest works of…

baraqish.s: Baraqish, ancient Yathill, is a walled ruined city in the al-Jawf region of Yemen, north-east of Sanaa. It was the second city of the Kingdom of Ma'in and a station on the incense route, enclosed by stone walls with dozens of towers.

battle-of-llucmajor.s: The Battle of Llucmajor was fought on 25 October 1349 near Llucmajor in southern Majorca. James III, the deposed king of Majorca, landed with mercenaries to retake his kingdom from Peter IV of Aragon, but was defeated and killed by the Aragonese army.

bodhachandra-singh.s: Bodhachandra Singh was the last ruling Maharaja of Manipur, succeeding his father Churachand Singh in 1941. After Indian independence Manipur adopted its own constitution and held elections in 1948, but in September 1949 he signed a merger agreement in Shillong, and Manipur…

bambandyanalo.s: Bambandyanalo, known to archaeologists as K2, is an archaeological site in the Limpopo valley of northern South Africa, near Mapungubwe Hill. Occupied from around 1000 to 1220 CE, it was a large settlement whose people grew rich from cattle and the trade in ivory and gold with…

barbara-of-matamba.s: Barbara, born Kambu or Mukambu Mbande, was queen of Ndongo and Matamba from 1663 to 1666, succeeding her sister Njinga. Captured by the Portuguese in 1646, she was released in 1656 under a peace treaty and married Njinga's general João Guterres Ngola Kanini.

baga-of-mauretania.s: Baga was a king of the Mauri, the first ruler of Mauretania known by name, in the late 3rd century BCE. Livy records that in 206 BCE, during the Second Punic War, he provided an escort of 4,000 Moorish warriors to the Numidian prince Masinissa on his way back to his kingdom.

bocchus-i.s: Bocchus I was king of Mauretania in north-west Africa and father-in-law of Jugurtha of Numidia. He joined Jugurtha against Rome in the Jugurthine War, but in 105 BCE betrayed him to Lucius Cornelius Sulla, the quaestor of Marius, ending the war.

bocchus-ii.s: Bocchus II was king of Mauretania, ruling its eastern part from around 49 BCE and the whole kingdom after expelling his brother Bogud in 38 BCE. He supported Julius Caesar and then Octavian in the Roman civil wars.

battle-of-bangkusay-channel.s: The Battle of Bangkusay Channel was fought on 3 June 1571 in Manila Bay, off Tondo near the mouth of the Pasig River. A fleet of Tagalog and Kapampangan warriors led by Tarik Sulayman of Macabebe attacked the Spanish under Martín de Goiti and was defeated, Sulayman being killed.

battle-of-the-winwaed.s: The Battle of the Winwaed was fought on 15 November 655, probably near Leeds, when Oswiu of Northumbria defeated and killed the pagan king Penda of Mercia. Many of Penda's allied kings also died.

babuza-people.s: The Babuza are an indigenous plains people of west-central Taiwan, who in the 17th century lived along the coast of present-day Changhua and southern Taichung. They appear in Dutch East India Company records among the villages of the region and later came under Qing rule,…

battle-of-stracathro.s: The Battle of Stracathro was fought in 1130 near Brechin in Angus, Scotland, where royal forces led by Edward, the constable of King David I, defeated an army from Moray. Angus, mormaer of Moray, was killed with many of his men.

boyle-abbey.s: Boyle Abbey is a ruined Cistercian monastery in Boyle, County Roscommon, Ireland, founded in 1161 as a daughter house of Mellifont. Its church, completed in the early 13th century, combines Romanesque and Gothic features.

battle-of-tolentino.s: The Battle of Tolentino was fought on 2–3 May 1815 near Tolentino in the Marche, Italy, between Joachim Murat's Neapolitan army and the Austrians. Murat had declared war on Austria during Napoleon's Hundred Days, hoping to unite Italy, but the defeat broke his army.

barra-war.s: The Barra War was a conflict in 1831–32 between the British colony at Bathurst (Banjul) and the Mandinka kingdom of Niumi, also called Barra, on the north bank of the mouth of the Gambia River. After fighting began at Essau and Barra Point, British and French forces defeated…

battle-of-stiklestad.s: The Battle of Stiklestad was fought on 29 July 1030 in Trøndelag, Norway, where King Olaf Haraldsson, returning from exile to reclaim his throne, was killed by an army of Norwegian farmers and chieftains loyal to Cnut the Great. Olaf was soon venerated as a saint, and his cult…

battle-of-vezeronce.s: The Battle of Vézeronce was fought on 25 June 524 near Vézeronce in the Dauphiné, France, between the Franks and the Burgundians. The Frankish king Chlodomer of Orléans was killed in the fighting, and although the Franks are said to have won, the Burgundian kingdom under…

bylazora.s: Bylazora was the largest city of ancient Paeonia, on the Vardar near modern Sveti Nikole in North Macedonia. It controlled the passes between Paeonia and Dardania, and Polybius records that Philip V of Macedon captured it in 217 BCE.

baschurch.s: Baschurch is a village in Shropshire, England, north-west of Shrewsbury. It is often identified with Eglwysau Bassa, the burial place of the 7th-century prince Cynddylan in the Welsh poems of the Canu Heledd, and has been suggested as a possible centre of the kingdom of Pengwern.

bagadates-i.s: Bagadates I was a ruler of Persis in south-western Iran in the early 3rd century BCE, often regarded as the first of the frataraka dynasts who governed the region after Alexander's conquest. His coins, struck at Persepolis or Istakhr with Aramaic legends, show him wearing a…

battle-of-sakarya.s: The Battle of Sakarya was fought from 23 August to 13 September 1921 along the Sakarya River west of Ankara, during the Greco-Turkish War. The Turkish nationalist army under Mustafa Kemal halted the Greek advance on Ankara after three weeks of fighting, forcing the Greeks to…

battle-of-aljubarrota.s: The Battle of Aljubarrota was fought on 14 August 1385 in central Portugal, between the army of John I of Portugal, with English archers, and the larger army of John I of Castile. Using defensive tactics devised by the constable Nuno Álvares Pereira, the Portuguese won…

bleddyn-ap-cynfyn.s: Bleddyn ap Cynfyn was king of Gwynedd and Powys from 1063 until his death in 1075. Set up with his brother Rhiwallon as a ruler under the overlordship of Edward the Confessor after the fall of their half-brother Gruffudd ap Llywelyn, he fought the Normans after 1066 and is…

boso-of-provence.s: Boso was a Frankish noble who in 879 became the first king outside the Carolingian family since 751. Brother-in-law of Charles the Bald, he was count of Vienne and duke in Provence, and after the death of Louis the Stammerer the bishops and nobles meeting at Mantaille elected…

beshbaliq.s: Beshbaliq, 'five towns', was a city in the north of the Tian Shan, near modern Jimsar in Xinjiang, China. Under the Tang dynasty it was the seat of the Beiting Protectorate, and from the 9th century it served as the summer capital of the Uyghur kingdom of Qocho.

bezeklik-caves.s: The Bezeklik Thousand Buddha Caves are a complex of Buddhist cave temples in the Flaming Mountains near Turfan in Xinjiang, China, dating from the 5th to the 14th century. Many were painted under the Uyghur kingdom of Qocho, with murals of Buddhist scenes and Uyghur donors.

bayajidda.s: Bayajidda is the legendary founder of the Hausa states in the traditions of northern Nigeria and Niger. The story tells that he came from Baghdad by way of Bornu, killed a snake that guarded a well at Daura, and married its queen, Daurama.

bryn-euryn.s: Bryn Euryn is a limestone hill between Colwyn Bay and Rhos-on-Sea in north Wales, crowned by the remains of a hillfort. It has been suggested that it was the 'Bear's Stronghold' of Cuneglasus, a 6th-century king denounced by Gildas, and a seat of the kings of Rhos.

battle-of-chenggao.s: The Battle of Chenggao was a prolonged struggle in 204–203 BCE between Liu Bang of Han and Xiang Yu of Chu for the strategic town of Chenggao, near the Ao granary in modern Henan, China. While Xiang Yu was away, the Han forces lured the Chu commander Cao Jiu across the Si…

battle-of-bannockburn.s: The Battle of Bannockburn was fought on 23–24 June 1314 near Stirling, Scotland, between the army of Robert the Bruce and a much larger English army under Edward II. Edward's attempt to relieve Stirling Castle ended in a heavy English defeat on the boggy ground by the Bannock…

bahnar-people.s: The Bahnar are a Mon-Khmer-speaking people of the Central Highlands of Vietnam, living mainly in Gia Lai and Kon Tum provinces. They traditionally farmed upland rice and lived in villages centred on a tall communal house.

brskovo.s: Brskovo was a medieval mining town in the north of present-day Montenegro, near Mojkovac. Developed in the mid-13th century under King Stefan Uroš I with the help of Saxon miners, it was the first important silver mine of medieval Serbia, with its own mint and colonies of…

battle-of-velbazhd.s: The Battle of Velbazhd was fought on 28 July 1330 near Velbazhd, modern Kyustendil in western Bulgaria, between the Serbian army of Stefan Dečanski and the Bulgarian army of Tsar Michael Shishman. The Serbs, with the young Stefan Dušan leading the heavy cavalry, won a decisive…

bhutia.s: The Bhutia are a people of Tibetan origin in Sikkim and neighbouring parts of India, whose ancestors migrated from Tibet in medieval times. They speak the Sikkimese language and follow Tibetan Buddhism.

battle-of-fandane-thiouthioune.s: The Battle of Fandane-Thiouthioune, also called the Battle of Somb, was fought on 18 July 1867 in the kingdom of Sine in present-day Senegal. The Serer army of Maad a Sinig Kumba Ndoffene Famak Joof defeated the forces of the Muslim reformer Maba Diakhou Ba, who was killed in…

bhuvanaikabahu-vii-of-kotte.s: Bhuvanaikabahu VII was king of Kotte in Sri Lanka from 1521 to 1551. Threatened by his brother Mayadunne of Sitawaka, he relied on Portuguese support and sent an embassy to Lisbon that had his grandson Dharmapala recognised as heir.

battle-of-strathcarron.s: The Battle of Strathcarron was fought in 642 in the valley of the River Carron near Falkirk, Scotland. The Britons of Strathclyde under Owain son of Beli defeated and killed Domnall Brecc, king of Dál Riata.

battle-of-ellendun.s: The Battle of Ellendun was fought in 825 near Wroughton in Wiltshire, England, between Ecgberht of Wessex and Beornwulf of Mercia. Ecgberht's victory ended Mercian supremacy over southern England, and Kent, Surrey, Sussex and Essex soon submitted to Wessex.

bergslagen.s: Bergslagen is a historic mining region in central Sweden, stretching across parts of Dalarna, Västmanland, Örebro and Värmland. From the Middle Ages its iron ore and the forests that supplied charcoal supported many mines and ironworks, which made iron one of Sweden's main…

branicevo.s: Braničevo is a historical region in north-eastern Serbia along the Danube, named after a medieval town near modern Kostolac, close to the ruins of Roman Viminacium. It was a Byzantine frontier fortress and bishopric, and in the late 13th century it was held by the…

baghaberd.s: Baghaberd is a ruined medieval fortress in Syunik Province of southern Armenia, near Kapan. It was a main stronghold of the kings of Syunik and held out against Seljuk attacks in the 11th and 12th centuries, until the Eldiguzid atabegs took it in 1170, ending the kingdom.

battle-of-fei-pi.s: The Battle of Fei Pi was fought on Tahiti in November 1815 between Pōmare II, returning from exile on Moorea, and the chiefs opposed to him. Pōmare's victory, won with the support of Christian converts and firearms, made him ruler of all Tahiti.

burkina-faso.s: Burkina Faso is a landlocked country in West Africa, with its capital at Ouagadougou. Its central plateau was the home of the Mossi kingdoms, whose rulers still hold traditional authority, and the country was the French colony of Upper Volta before independence in 1960.

burgundians.s: The Burgundians were an East Germanic people who crossed the Rhine in the early 5th century and founded a kingdom as Roman allies around 411, traditionally centred on Worms. After its destruction by Hunnic troops in Roman service in 436, the survivors were settled in Sapaudia…

beowulf.s: Beowulf is an Old English epic poem of about 3,180 lines, preserved in a single manuscript copied around 1000; its date of composition is debated. Set in southern Scandinavia, it tells how the Geatish hero Beowulf kills the monster Grendel and his mother at the Danish court…

battle-of-dyrham.s: The Battle of Deorham was fought in 577 at Dyrham, north of Bath in Gloucestershire. According to the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle, the West Saxon leaders Ceawlin and Cuthwine killed three British kings and took the towns of Gloucester, Cirencester and Bath.

bardas-skleros.s: Bardas Skleros was a Byzantine general who rebelled against Emperor Basil II in 976 and took much of Anatolia. He was defeated in 979 by Bardas Phokas with the help of Georgian troops sent by David III Kuropalates of Tao, and fled to the Buyid court in Baghdad.

battle-of-stamford-bridge.s: The Battle of Stamford Bridge was fought on 25 September 1066 near York, where King Harold II of England defeated an invading Norwegian army. The Norwegian king Harald Hardrada and Harold's exiled brother Tostig were killed.

battle-of-largs.s: The Battle of Largs was fought on 2 October 1263 on the Ayrshire coast between Scots and part of the Norwegian fleet of King Haakon IV, which had been battered by storms. The clash itself was indecisive, but Haakon withdrew and died in Orkney that winter.

bridei-son-of-maelchon.s: Bridei son of Maelchon was a powerful king of the Picts in the second half of the 6th century. Adomnán's Life of Columba describes the saint visiting him at his fortress near the River Ness in the 560s.

birka.s: Birka was a Viking Age trading town on the island of Björkö in Lake Mälaren, Sweden, flourishing from the mid 8th to the late 10th century. Its merchants traded furs and slaves for silver and goods from the Frankish, Byzantine and Abbasid worlds, and the missionary Ansgar…

battle-of-fyrisvellir.s: The Battle of Fýrisvellir was fought in the 980s on the plains near Uppsala, where King Eric the Victorious of the Swedes defeated his nephew Styrbjörn the Strong, who had come with a Danish and Jomsviking force. It is known mainly from Norse sagas and skaldic poetry, with…

battle-of-dysert-odea.s: The Battle of Dysert O'Dea was fought on 10 May 1318 in County Clare, Ireland. Irish forces allied to Muirchertach O'Brien defeated the Anglo-Norman lord Richard de Clare, who was killed.

battle-of-kinsale.s: The Battle of Kinsale was fought on 24 December 1601 near Kinsale in County Cork, Ireland. The armies of Hugh O'Neill and Red Hugh O'Donnell, who had marched south to relieve a Spanish force besieged in the town, were routed by the English under Lord Mountjoy.

baal.s: Baal, meaning lord, was the title of the Canaanite storm and fertility god Hadad, widely worshipped in the ancient Levant. At Ugarit the Baal cycle tells of his battles with Yam, the sea, and Mot, death, and in Egypt he was identified with Seth.

brian-oconnor-faly.s: Brian O'Connor Faly was the last independent lord of Uí Failge, in the Irish midlands, in the 16th century. He took part in risings against English rule, and after rebelling again in the 1540s he surrendered in 1548 and was imprisoned in England.

book-of-ui-maine.s: The Book of Uí Maine is an Irish manuscript compiled in the late 14th century for the O'Kelly family, lords of Uí Maine in Connacht. It contains genealogies, poems, historical tracts and lore, much of it on the families of Connacht.

battle-of-clontarf.s: The Battle of Clontarf was fought on 23 April 1014 north of Dublin. The army of Brian Bóruma, high king of Ireland, defeated the king of Leinster, the Norse of Dublin and their allies from Orkney and the Isles, but Brian himself was killed.

battle-of-almansa.s: The Battle of Almansa was fought on 25 April 1707 near Almansa in south-eastern Spain during the War of the Spanish Succession. A Franco-Spanish army under the Duke of Berwick defeated the allied forces of Britain, Portugal and the Netherlands led by the Earl of Galway.

bhasa.s: Bhasa was one of the earliest known Sanskrit dramatists, praised by Kalidasa as a famous predecessor, though his dates are uncertain. A group of thirteen plays attributed to him was discovered in manuscripts in Kerala in 1912.

battle-of-torrevicente.s: The Battle of Torrevicente was fought in 981 in the province of Soria, Spain, between the Córdoban general Almanzor and his father-in-law Ghalib, who had rebelled against him with the support of Castile and Pamplona. Ghalib died during the fighting and his army was routed,…

birinus.s: Birinus was a missionary bishop sent from Rome by Pope Honorius I who converted the West Saxons. In 635 he baptised their king, Cynegils, with King Oswald of Northumbria as godfather, and received Dorchester-on-Thames as the seat of his bishopric.

battle-of-edington.s: The Battle of Edington was fought in May 878 in Wiltshire, England, between the West Saxons under Alfred the Great and the Viking army of Guthrum. Months earlier a surprise attack had driven Alfred into hiding in the Somerset marshes, but he rallied his forces and won a…

battle-of-orakau.s: The Battle of Ōrākau was fought from 31 March to 2 April 1864 in the Waikato, New Zealand, the last major battle of the British invasion of the Waikato. About 300 Māori under Rewi Maniapoto, including women, defended a hastily built pā against a much larger British force.

battle-of-rangiriri.s: The Battle of Rangiriri was fought on 20–21 November 1863 in the Waikato, New Zealand, during the British invasion of the Waikato. General Duncan Cameron's troops attacked a strong Māori defensive line between the Waikato river and a lake and suffered heavy losses in repeated…

bishkek.s: Bishkek is the capital and largest city of Kyrgyzstan, in the Chüy valley at the foot of the Kyrgyz Range. It grew from Pishpek, a fortress of the Khanate of Kokand taken by the Russians in 1862.

bani-thani.s: Bani Thani is a painting of a woman in profile made at Kishangarh in Rajasthan around 1750, usually attributed to Nihal Chand. Its elongated face, arched eyebrows and lotus-shaped eyes became the hallmark of the Kishangarh school of miniature painting.

belagavi.s: Belagavi, known as Belgaum until 2014, is a city in northern Karnataka, India, near the border with Maharashtra and Goa. Its fort dates from the 13th century, and the town was held in turn by the Bahmani and Adil Shahi sultans, the Marathas and the British.

battle-of-itakhuli.s: The Battle of Itakhuli was fought in 1682 at Guwahati, in present-day Assam, India, between the Ahom kingdom and the Mughal Empire. Ahom forces sent by King Gadadhar Singha defeated the Mughal garrison and drove it west beyond the Manas river.

buzen-province.s: Buzen was an old province of Japan in north-eastern Kyushu, now divided between Fukuoka and Ōita prefectures. It contained the Usa Shrine, the chief shrine of the god Hachiman.

bhim-singh-ii-of-kotah.s: Bhim Singh II was the last ruling Maharao of Kotah, a Hada Chauhan Rajput state in the Chambal valley of Rajasthan, succeeding his father in 1940. In 1948 he took Kotah into the new Rajasthan union of princely states and became its Rajpramukh, or constitutional head, before…

bhimtal.s: Bhimtal is a lake and town in the Nainital district of Uttarakhand, India, in the Kumaon hills about 22 kilometres from Nainital. The lake is one of the largest in the region, and on its shore stands the Bhimeshwar temple, attributed to the 17th-century Chand ruler Baz Bahadur…

benue-river.s: The Benue is the main tributary of the Niger, about 1,400 kilometres long, rising in northern Cameroon and joining the Niger at Lokoja in Nigeria. Navigable for much of its course in the rainy season, it was a corridor for trade and migration, and the Jukun kingdom of…

bages.s: Bages is a comarca, or county, in central Catalonia, Spain, with its capital at Manresa. Lying in the basins of the Llobregat and Cardener rivers and bordering the massif of Montserrat, it developed a textile industry in the 19th century and potash mining in the 20th.

battle-of-aliwal.s: The Battle of Aliwal was fought on 28 January 1846 near the Sutlej River in Punjab during the First Anglo-Sikh War. A British force under Sir Harry Smith defeated a Sikh army under Ranjodh Singh Majithia, driving it back across the river and removing the threat to Ludhiana.

battle-of-baddowal.s: The Battle of Baddowal was an engagement on 21 January 1846 near Ludhiana in Punjab during the First Anglo-Sikh War. Sikh forces under Ranjodh Singh Majithia attacked a British column under Sir Harry Smith marching to relieve Ludhiana and captured much of its baggage.

barcino.s: Barcino was the Roman colony founded under Augustus around 15–10 BCE on the site of modern Barcelona, in north-eastern Spain. Its full name was Colonia Iulia Augusta Faventia Paterna Barcino, and it was a small walled town of the province of Hispania Tarraconensis on the low…

baetulo.s: Baetulo was a Roman town on the Catalan coast, on the site of modern Badalona north-east of Barcelona. Founded around 100 BCE in the lands of the Iberian Laietani, it prospered on wine production and trade.

battle-of-dhi-qar.s: The Battle of Dhi Qar was fought in southern Iraq in the early 7th century, probably between 604 and 611, between Arab tribes led by the Banu Shayban and a Sasanian Persian army with its Arab allies. The Arab victory followed Khosrow II's deposition of the Lakhmid king…

belisarius.s: Belisarius was the leading general of the Byzantine emperor Justinian I. He defeated the Persians at Dara in 530, helped crush the Nika riots in 532, destroyed the Vandal Kingdom in Africa in 533–534 and led the long reconquest of Italy from the Ostrogoths, taking Ravenna in 540.

brahmanas.s: The Brahmanas are Vedic prose texts, composed roughly between 900 and 700 BCE, that explain the meaning and correct performance of the sacrificial rituals of the four Vedas. Attached to particular Vedic schools, they include the Aitareya and Shatapatha Brahmanas, and they…

bharatas.s: The Bharatas were an Indo-Aryan tribe of the early Vedic period, prominent in the Rigveda, where their king Sudas defeats a coalition of tribes in the Battle of the Ten Kings. They later merged with the Purus to form the Kuru tribe of the upper Ganges–Yamuna region.

battle-of-mongua.s: The Battle of Mongua was fought on 18–20 August 1915 in southern Angola between a Portuguese army under General António Pereira de Eça and the forces of the Kwanyama king Mandume ya Ndemufayo. After three days of fighting the Portuguese, with artillery and machine guns, won…

battle-of-bayan.s: The Battle of Bayan, also called the Battle of Bayang or Pandapatan, was fought on 2 May 1902 near Lake Lanao on Mindanao between United States troops and Maranao warriors. American forces under Colonel Frank Baldwin stormed the Maranao fortifications at Bayang after Maranao…

battle-of-fehrbellin.s: The Battle of Fehrbellin was fought on 28 June 1675 near the town of Fehrbellin, north-west of Berlin, between the army of Brandenburg under Frederick William, the Great Elector, and a Swedish army that had invaded the electorate. Brandenburg's cavalry, led in the attack by…

bad-homburg-vor-der-hohe.s: Bad Homburg vor der Höhe is a spa town at the foot of the Taunus hills, north of Frankfurt in Hesse, Germany. From 1622 it was the residence of the landgraves of Hesse-Homburg, who built a baroque palace there, and in the 19th century its mineral springs and casino made it a…

bergpark-wilhelmshohe.s: The Bergpark Wilhelmshöhe is a large landscape park on a hillside west of Kassel, Germany, laid out by the landgraves of Hesse-Kassel from the late 17th century. It contains the Hercules monument, water cascades and fountains, and Wilhelmshöhe Palace, built from 1786 for…

bahauddin-zakariya.s: Bahauddin Zakariya was a Sufi master of Multan, in what is now Pakistan, who brought the Suhrawardi order to South Asia. A disciple of Shihab al-Din Umar al-Suhrawardi in Baghdad, he settled at Multan and made it a major centre of Sufism, keeping a large hospice.

bhagadatta.s: Bhagadatta is a legendary king of Pragjyotisha, the ancient name of Kamarupa in Assam, son of the demon king Naraka. In the Mahabharata he is a mighty warrior who rides the elephant Supratika and fights for the Kauravas at Kurukshetra, where he is slain by Arjuna.

boten-vientiane-railway.s: The Boten–Vientiane railway, known as the Laos–China Railway, is a railway of about 420 kilometres from the Chinese border at Boten to Vientiane, the capital of Laos. Built by Chinese companies under the Belt and Road Initiative, with many tunnels and bridges through the…

balochi-language.s: Balochi is an Iranian language spoken by the Baloch people in Pakistan's Balochistan province, south-eastern Iran, southern Afghanistan and among communities in Oman and the Gulf. It belongs to the north-western branch of the Iranian languages and has several dialects.

baluchistan-agency.s: The Baluchistan Agency was the British political agency that oversaw the princely states and tribal areas of Baluchistan from 1877, with its headquarters at Quetta. It was set up under Robert Sandeman, who managed the region through agreements with the Khan of Kalat and the…

battle-of-illicheon.s: The Battle of Illicheon was fought in 936 near Gumi in Korea, when Wang Geon, founder of Goryeo, defeated the army of Later Baekje led by Gyeon Singeom. Gyeon Hwon, the deposed founder of Later Baekje, fought on Goryeo's side against his own son.

brahmaputra.s: The Brahmaputra is one of the great rivers of Asia, about 2,900 kilometres long. It rises in western Tibet as the Yarlung Tsangpo, cuts through the Himalayas into Arunachal Pradesh, flows west through the Assam valley in India and enters Bangladesh, where it joins the Ganges…

battle-of-ningyuan.s: The Battle of Ningyuan was fought in 1626 at Ningyuan, in modern Xingcheng in Liaoning, China, when the Ming commander Yuan Chonghuan defended the walled town against Nurhaci's Later Jin army. Using Portuguese-style cannon, the defenders inflicted heavy losses and forced the…

battle-of-sarhu.s: The Battle of Sarhu was a series of engagements in 1619 in which Nurhaci's Later Jin army defeated a Ming expedition sent in four columns to destroy his state. Concentrating his forces, Nurhaci beat the columns one by one in a few days.

battle-of-bo-co.s: The Battle of Bô Cô was fought in late 1408 in what is now Nam Định province, Vietnam, between the Later Tran forces of Emperor Gian Dinh and a Ming army under Mu Sheng. The Vietnamese, led by the generals Dang Tat and Nguyen Canh Chan, won a major victory, killing the Ming…

battle-of-gaoping.s: The Battle of Gaoping was fought in 954 in Shanxi, northern China, between the Later Zhou under Emperor Chai Rong and the Northern Han allied with the Khitan Liao. After part of his army fled, Chai Rong led a counter-attack, supported by Zhao Kuangyin, that defeated the invaders.

baltic-landeswehr.s: The Baltic Landeswehr was a volunteer force formed in Latvia in late 1918, mainly from Baltic German nobles and townspeople, with Latvian and Russian units. Fighting alongside German Freikorps against the Bolsheviks, it recaptured Riga in May 1919.

battle-of-crannon.s: The Battle of Crannon was fought in 322 BCE in Thessaly between the Macedonian armies of Antipater and Craterus and the Greek allies led by Athens and the Aetolians. The Macedonians won a limited victory, but the Greek coalition broke up as cities made separate peace.

bregaglia.s: Bregaglia, in German Bergell, is an Italian-speaking alpine valley in the Swiss canton of Graubünden, running from the Maloja Pass down to Chiavenna in Italy. It belonged to the Prince-Bishopric of Chur and joined the League of God's House, and its route over the Maloja linked…

battle-of-albulena.s: The Battle of Albulena was fought on 2 September 1457 in central Albania, when Skanderbeg defeated a large Ottoman army under Isa Bey Evrenos. Skanderbeg had withdrawn into the mountains, letting the Ottomans spread out to plunder, before attacking their camp by surprise.

battle-of-torvioll.s: The Battle of Torvioll was fought on 29 June 1444 in the plain of Torvioll in Albania, where Skanderbeg, leading the forces of the League of Lezhë, defeated an Ottoman army under Ali Pasha. Skanderbeg hid part of his troops in the woods and attacked the Ottomans from the…

books-of-chilam-balam.s: The Books of Chilam Balam are manuscripts written in Yucatec Maya using the Latin alphabet in the colonial period, named after a Maya prophet. Kept in towns such as Chumayel, Tizimin and Maní, they combine history, prophecy, calendars, medical lore and Christian material.

battle-of-nicopolis.s: The Battle of Nicopolis was fought on 25 September 1396 at Nicopolis on the lower Danube, in modern Bulgaria. A crusading army led by King Sigismund of Hungary, with French, Burgundian and other Western knights, was routed by the Ottoman sultan Bayezid I.
