bojang-of-goguryeo.s: Bojang was the last king of Goguryeo. He was placed on the throne in 642 by the general Yeon Gaesomun, who held real power during his reign.

battle-of-marengo.s: The Battle of Marengo was fought on 14 June 1800 near Alessandria in Piedmont between the French army of the First Consul Napoleon Bonaparte and an Austrian army under General Michael von Melas. Close to defeat in the afternoon, the French won after the arrival of General…

byelorussian-ssr.s: The Byelorussian Soviet Socialist Republic was the Soviet republic in the territory of modern Belarus, with its capital at Minsk. First proclaimed on 1 January 1919 as the Socialist Soviet Republic of Byelorussia, it was briefly merged with Soviet Lithuania as Litbel and…

book-of-the-later-han.s: The Book of the Later Han (Hou Hanshu) is the official history of the Eastern Han dynasty (25–220 CE), compiled by the historian Fan Ye under the Liu Song dynasty. Fan Ye wrote its annals and biographies before his execution in 445, and its treatises were later taken from Sima…

battle-of-wilkomierz.s: The Battle of Wiłkomierz, or Pabaiskas, was fought on 1 September 1435 near Ukmergė in Lithuania during the Lithuanian civil war between Sigismund Kęstutaitis and Švitrigaila. Sigismund's Lithuanian and Polish forces crushed Švitrigaila's army and its Livonian Order allies,…

battle-of-ergeme.s: The Battle of Ergeme was fought on 2 August 1560 near Ērģeme in northern Latvia during the Livonian War. A Russian army of Ivan IV destroyed a force of the Livonian Order, capturing the land marshal Philipp Schall von Bell, who was later executed in Moscow.

battle-of-lake-smolino.s: The Battle of Lake Smolino was fought on 13 September 1502 near Pskov, when the Livonian Order under Master Wolter von Plettenberg defeated a much larger Muscovite army. Fought during the Muscovite–Lithuanian War of 1500–1503, in which the order was allied with Lithuania, the…

battle-of-cortenuova.s: The Battle of Cortenuova was fought on 27 November 1237 in Lombardy, when the emperor Frederick II defeated the army of the revived Lombard League led by Milan. The Milanese carroccio, the city's battle-wagon, was captured and sent to Rome as a trophy.

beaujeu.s: Beaujeu is a small town in the Rhône department of eastern France, in the hills west of the Saône. Its castle was the seat of the lords of Beaujeu from the 10th century, who gave their name to the surrounding Beaujolais and later founded Villefranche-sur-Saône.

bilbao.s: Bilbao is the largest city of the Basque Country in northern Spain, on the estuary of the Nervión. Founded in 1300 by Diego López V de Haro, lord of Biscay, it grew into a major port for Castilian wool and later a centre of iron, steel and shipbuilding.

biscay.s: Biscay (Basque: Bizkaia) is a province of the Basque Country in northern Spain, with its capital at Bilbao. In the Middle Ages it was a lordship ruled by the Haro family; it passed to the Crown of Castile in 1379 but kept its own fueros, or customary laws, and its assembly at…

bohun-family.s: The de Bohuns were an Anglo-Norman noble family who were earls of Hereford from 1200, later also earls of Essex, and hereditary constables of England. They held large marcher lordships in Wales, including Brecknock, which came to them by marriage from the de Braose family.

braose-family.s: The de Braose family were Anglo-Norman barons from Briouze in Normandy who became some of the most powerful marcher lords in Wales, holding Brecknock, Radnor, Builth, Abergavenny and Gower. William de Braose, 4th Lord of Bramber, fell out with King John, who had his wife and…

brecon-castle.s: Brecon Castle is a Norman castle at Brecon in mid Wales, built by Bernard de Neufmarché after his conquest of the Welsh kingdom of Brycheiniog around 1093. It was the centre of the marcher lordship of Brecknock, held in turn by the de Braose, de Bohun and Stafford families.

brecon-cathedral.s: Brecon Cathedral, in Brecon in mid Wales, was founded as a Benedictine priory of St John the Evangelist by Bernard de Neufmarché around 1093, as a cell of Battle Abbey. After the priory was dissolved in the 1530s the church served the parish, and in 1923 it became the…

brian-macphelim-oneill.s: Sir Brian MacPhelim O'Neill was lord of Lower Clandeboye in Ulster in the mid-16th century. He resisted the Earl of Essex's attempt to colonise Antrim and Down, and in 1574, after a feast with Essex at Belfast, he was seized and his followers massacred; he and his wife were…

battle-of-maritsa.s: The Battle of the Maritsa was fought on 26 September 1371 at Chernomen on the Maritsa river, in modern Greece, where an Ottoman force under Lala Şahin Pasha destroyed the army of the Serbian king Vukašin and the despot Jovan Uglješa, both of whom were killed. The defeat opened…

bremen-roland.s: The Bremen Roland is a stone statue of the paladin Roland, about 5.5 m tall, set up in 1404 in the market square of Bremen, Germany, facing the cathedral. It symbolised the city's rights and freedoms against the archbishops of Bremen, and the inscription on its shield refers…

beauchamp-family.s: The Beauchamps were an English noble family who held the earldom of Warwick from 1268 until the 1440s. Richard Beauchamp, 13th Earl of Warwick, gained the lordship of Glamorgan through his marriage to the Despenser heiress Isabel.

bernabo-visconti.s: Bernabò Visconti was lord of Milan, ruling the eastern half of the Visconti dominions from 1354 while his brother Galeazzo II held the west. Known for his cruelty and his constant wars with the papacy, he governed from Milan.

battle-of-desio.s: The Battle of Desio was fought on 21 January 1277 north of Milan between the Visconti and the della Torre family, who then dominated the city. The forces of Archbishop Ottone Visconti defeated the della Torre and captured their leader Napo della Torre, allowing the archbishop…

battle-of-grunwald.s: The Battle of Grunwald, fought on 15 July 1410 in Prussia, was one of the largest battles of medieval Europe. An allied army of the Kingdom of Poland and the Grand Duchy of Lithuania under Władysław II Jagiełło and Vytautas crushed the Teutonic Knights, killing Grand Master…

battle-of-montgisard.s: The Battle of Montgisard was fought on 25 November 1177 near Ramla, in the Kingdom of Jerusalem. The young King Baldwin IV, with a small force of knights including Raynald of Châtillon and the Ibelin brothers, surprised and routed the much larger army of Saladin, who narrowly…

beaufort-castle-lebanon.s: Beaufort Castle is a crusader fortress in southern Lebanon, standing on a cliff high above the Litani river. Held by the lords of Sidon from 1139, it was surrendered to Saladin in 1190 after a long siege, returned to the crusaders in 1240 and sold to the Templars in 1260, and…

battle-of-harlaw.s: The Battle of Harlaw was fought on 24 July 1411 near Inverurie in Aberdeenshire. Donald, Lord of the Isles, pressing his wife's claim to the earldom of Ross, led a Highland army against forces raised by Alexander Stewart, Earl of Mar.

battle-of-cuarte.s: The Battle of Cuarte was fought in October 1094 outside Valencia, months after El Cid had captured the city. An Almoravid army sent by Yusuf ibn Tashfin to recover Valencia camped on the plain of Cuarte and besieged it, but El Cid sallied out and routed it.

battle-of-bairen.s: The Battle of Bairén was fought in January 1097 near Gandia, south of Valencia, between El Cid, supported by King Peter I of Aragon, and an Almoravid army. The Christians defeated the Almoravids, securing El Cid's hold on Valencia and the coastal route to the south.

ben-hadad-iii.s: Ben-Hadad III, Aramaic Bar-Hadad, was king of Aram-Damascus around 800 BCE, son and successor of Hazael. The Zakkur stele records that he led a coalition of kings that besieged Zakkur, king of Hamath and Luash, at Hazrek.

basilicata.s: Basilicata is a mountainous region of southern Italy between Campania, Apulia and Calabria, with short coastlines on the Tyrrhenian and Ionian seas. In antiquity most of it was the land of the Lucanians and later part of the Roman region of Lucania.

battle-of-pandosia.s: The Battle of Pandosia was fought in 331 BCE near the town of Pandosia in Bruttium, southern Italy. King Alexander I of Epirus, uncle of Alexander the Great, who had come to help Taras against the Italic peoples, was defeated and killed there by the Lucanians and Bruttians.

brora.s: Brora is a village on the east coast of Sutherland in the Scottish Highlands, at the mouth of the River Brora. The surrounding valley, Strath Brora, is rich in Iron Age brochs.

banu-kilab.s: The Banu Kilab were an Arab tribe of the Qays group who migrated from Arabia to northern Syria in the 10th century. They raided and pressed the rulers of Aleppo, and in 1024 their chief Salih ibn Mirdas took the city and founded the Mirdasid emirate.

burchard-ii-of-halberstadt.s: Burchard II was Bishop of Halberstadt from 1059 to 1088. In the winter of 1067–1068 he led a campaign against the Lutici, destroyed their temple at Rethra and rode home on its sacred horse.

battle-of-nhu-nguyet-river.s: The Battle of Như Nguyệt River was fought in 1077 on the Cầu river, then called Như Nguyệt, north of the Vietnamese capital Thăng Long. Lý Thường Kiệt's fortified line held back a Song Chinese army under Guo Kui, sent in response to Đại Việt's raid of 1075–1076.

bukka-raya-i.s: Bukka Raya I was a co-founder and ruler of the Vijayanagara Empire in southern India, reigning from about 1356 to 1377 after his brother Harihara I. A member of the Sangama family, he extended the kingdom across the south, fought the Bahmani Sultanate, and through his son…

bat-al-khutm-and-al-ayn.n: Archaeological Sites of Bat, Al-Khutm and Al-Ayn
bat-al-khutm-and-al-ayn.s: Bat, Al-Khutm and Al-Ayn are archaeological sites in the interior of north-western Oman, together a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1988. They preserve one of the most complete groups of settlements and necropolises of the 3rd millennium BCE, including round stone towers and…

battle-of-gallabat.s: The Battle of Gallabat, or Metemma, was fought on 9–10 March 1889 on the Sudan–Ethiopia border between the Ethiopian emperor Yohannes IV and the army of the Mahdist State. The Ethiopians broke into the Mahdist fortifications, but Yohannes was mortally wounded by a bullet and…

battle-of-shaykan.s: The Battle of Shaykan was fought on 3–5 November 1883 in the forest of Shaykan near El Obeid in Kordofan, Sudan. The Mahdi's Ansar surrounded and destroyed an Egyptian army under the British officer William Hicks, leaving few survivors.

battle-of-toski.s: The Battle of Toski was fought on 3 August 1889 near Toshki on the Nile in southern Egypt. An Anglo-Egyptian army under Francis Grenfell defeated a Mahdist invasion force led by Abd al-Rahman al-Nujumi, who was killed in the fighting.

battle-of-umm-diwaykarat.s: The Battle of Umm Diwaykarat was fought on 24 November 1899 in Kordofan, Sudan, and ended the Mahdist State. An Anglo-Egyptian force under Reginald Wingate caught the Khalifa Abdallahi ibn Muhammad, who had fled after Omdurman, with his remaining followers.

bhatarka.s: Bhatarka was the founder of the Maitraka dynasty of western India, which ruled from Valabhi in Saurashtra. A military commander (senapati) of the Gupta Empire, he established himself as a local ruler around 475 as Gupta power weakened.

bargal.s: Bargal is a coastal town in the Bari region of Puntland in north-eastern Somalia, on the Indian Ocean south of Cape Guardafui. In the 19th and early 20th centuries it was one of the residences of the boqors of the Majeerteen Sultanate, until the Italian conquest of the…

baqt.s: The Baqt was the agreement made in 652 between the Nubian kingdom of Makuria and the Arab rulers of Egypt, after Makurian archers repelled Abdallah ibn Sa'd's attack on Old Dongola. Makuria sent a yearly tribute of slaves in return for grain, wine and cloth, and each side…

barisan-nasional.s: Barisan Nasional (National Front) is a Malaysian coalition of parties formed in 1973 as the successor of the Alliance, led by the United Malays National Organisation together with Chinese and Indian parties. It governed Malaysia continuously until it lost the 2018 general…

bhaktapur.s: Bhaktapur is a city in the Kathmandu Valley of Nepal, about 13 km east of Kathmandu. It was the capital of the Malla kings of the whole valley until the late 15th century and then of the independent Kingdom of Bhaktapur until the Gorkha conquest of 1769.

battle-of-the-longanus-river.s: The Battle of the Longanus River was fought in north-eastern Sicily in the 260s BCE between Hieron II of Syracuse and the Mamertines, Campanian mercenaries who held Messana. Hieron's victory broke Mamertine power and led him to take the title of king.

bantva.s: Bantva is a town in Junagadh district of Gujarat, western India, on the Saurashtra peninsula. In the princely era it was the seat of a small estate held by a branch of the Babi family, the rulers of Junagadh, and was closely linked with neighbouring Manavadar.

baba-gurgur.s: Baba Gurgur is an oil field near Kirkuk in northern Iraq. On 14 October 1927 the Turkish Petroleum Company, later the Iraq Petroleum Company, struck oil there in a huge gusher, the discovery that made Iraq a major oil producer.

balfour-declaration.s: The Balfour Declaration was a public statement issued by the British government on 2 November 1917, in a letter from Foreign Secretary Arthur Balfour to Lord Rothschild, supporting 'a national home for the Jewish people' in Palestine. It also stated that the rights of existing…

boudican-revolt.s: The Boudican revolt was an uprising of the Iceni and neighbouring peoples of Britain against Roman rule in 60 or 61 CE, led by Boudica, widow of the Iceni king Prasutagus. Provoked by the seizure of the Iceni kingdom and the abuse of Boudica and her daughters by Roman…

battle-of-valmy.s: The Battle of Valmy, fought on 20 September 1792 in Champagne in north-eastern France, halted the Prussian-led invasion that threatened revolutionary Paris. French armies under Dumouriez and Kellermann held their ground in an artillery duel, and the Duke of Brunswick's army…

boxer-rebellion.s: The Boxer Rebellion was an anti-foreign and anti-Christian uprising in northern China led by the Yihetuan, the 'Militia United in Righteousness', known in the West as the Boxers for their martial rituals. Spreading through Shandong and Zhili in 1899 and 1900, the Boxers killed…

battle-of-france.s: The Battle of France was the German invasion of France and the Low Countries in May and June 1940. German armoured forces broke through the Ardennes, where the Allies least expected an attack, reached the English Channel and trapped the British, French and Belgian armies in…

balfour-declaration-of-1926.s: The Balfour Declaration of 1926 was a report of the Imperial Conference in London, named after Arthur Balfour, which defined Britain and the dominions as autonomous communities within the British Empire, equal in status and freely associated as members of the British…

book-of-chilam-balam-of-mani.n: Book of Chilam Balam of Maní
book-of-chilam-balam-of-mani.s: The Book of Chilam Balam of Maní is one of the Books of Chilam Balam, colonial manuscripts written in the Yucatec Maya language with the Latin alphabet. Kept by the Xiu lineage of Maní in Yucatán, it contains prophecies, chronicles organised by the katun cycles of the Maya…

bartolome-ruiz.s: Bartolomé Ruiz was a Spanish pilot from Moguer who served on Francisco Pizarro's early expeditions down the Pacific coast of South America. In 1526, sailing south ahead of the others, he crossed the equator and captured a large balsa sailing raft loaded with textiles,…

baltistan.s: Baltistan is a high mountain region in Gilgit-Baltistan, northern Pakistan, around the upper Indus and its tributaries, with Skardu as its main town. Its people, the Balti, speak a Tibetic language and are mainly Shia and Noorbakhshi Muslims.

badia-fiorentina.s: The Badia Fiorentina is a Benedictine abbey in the centre of Florence, founded in 978 by Willa, widow of the Margrave of Tuscany, and richly endowed by her son Hugh, whose tomb by Mino da Fiesole stands in the church. Its tall bell tower is a city landmark, and the abbey was…

berthold-i-of-zahringen.s: Berthold I of Zähringen, called the Bearded, was a Swabian noble and founder of the power of the house of Zähringen. In 1061 he was made Duke of Carinthia and Margrave of Verona, but he hardly ruled there in person.

bou-inania-madrasa-fez.s: The Bou Inania Madrasa in Fez, Morocco, was built between 1350 and 1355 by the Marinid sultan Abu Inan Faris, after whom it is named. Unusually for a madrasa, it also served as a congregational mosque, with its own minaret.

battle-of-rio-salado.s: The Battle of Río Salado was fought on 30 October 1340 near Tarifa in southern Spain. Alfonso XI of Castile and Afonso IV of Portugal defeated the Marinid sultan Abu al-Hasan and Yusuf I of Granada, who had crossed from Africa to besiege Tarifa.

boniface-del-vasto.s: Boniface del Vasto was a marquis of the Aleramici family who ruled wide lands in southern Piedmont and western Liguria in the late 11th and early 12th centuries. After his death his lands were divided among his sons, creating several marquisates, including Saluzzo, Busca, Ceva…

buco-di-viso.s: The Buco di Viso is a tunnel about 75 metres long cut through the rock below the Colle delle Traversette, at nearly 2,900 metres near Monviso, on the border between Italy and France. Marquis Ludovico II of Saluzzo had it dug around 1480 to carry salt, cloth and other goods by…

badh.s: Badh was a Kurdish chief who in the 980s took advantage of the weakness of the Buyids to seize Mayyafariqin, Amid and much of Diyar Bakr, and briefly Mosul. He was killed in 990 fighting the Hamdanids.

battle-of-zama.s: The Battle of Zama, fought in 202 BCE in present-day Tunisia, was the decisive battle of the Second Punic War. A Roman army under Publius Cornelius Scipio, strengthened by the Numidian cavalry of Masinissa, defeated Hannibal.

battle-of-noukouma.s: The Battle of Noukouma was fought in 1818 in the inner Niger delta of present-day Mali. The Fulbe preacher Seku Amadu and his followers defeated the forces of the Fulbe ardo chiefs and their allies from the Bamana Empire of Ségou.

bairat.s: Bairat, or Viratnagar, is a town in the Jaipur district of Rajasthan, India. It is identified with Viratanagara, capital of the ancient Matsya kingdom, named after King Virata of the Mahabharata.

bhabru-edict.s: The Bhabru edict, also called the Calcutta-Bairat edict, is an inscription of the Mauryan emperor Ashoka found near Bairat in Rajasthan and now kept in Kolkata. Addressed to the Buddhist monastic community, it declares Ashoka's faith in the Buddha, the Dharma and the Sangha…

banasa.s: Banasa was an ancient town on the Sebou river in northern Morocco. A Mauretanian settlement, it became a Roman colony under Augustus, Colonia Iulia Valentia Banasa, and was one of the towns of the province of Mauretania Tingitana.

baquates.s: The Baquates were a Berber people of Roman Mauretania Tingitana, in present-day northern Morocco. Altars set up at Volubilis between the second and fourth centuries CE record agreements and renewed treaties of peace between their chiefs and Roman governors, which show how Rome…

baripada.s: Baripada is a city in northern Odisha, India, and the headquarters of Mayurbhanj district. It was the capital of the princely state of Mayurbhanj, whose Bhanja rulers had earlier ruled from Haripur.

bhanja-dynasty.s: The Bhanja dynasty is a ruling family of Odisha in eastern India, known from early medieval inscriptions and claiming ancient descent. Branches ruled the princely states of Mayurbhanj and Keonjhar, and related lines held other small states in Odisha, until these merged into…

bhumij-people.s: The Bhumij are an Adivasi people of eastern India, living mainly in Odisha, Jharkhand and West Bengal. Speaking a Munda language closely related to Mundari, they traditionally farmed in the hills and forests of the Chota Nagpur plateau.

banu-asad.s: The Banu Asad are an Arab tribe originally from north-central Arabia. After Muhammad's death they joined the Ridda Wars under the prophet Tulayha, and later many settled in Iraq around Kufa.

balitung.s: Balitung, or Dyah Balitung, was king of the Medang kingdom of Java from about 899 to 911. His many inscriptions show a realm stretching from Central to East Java, and his Mantyasih inscription of 907 lists the kings who ruled before him, beginning with Sanjaya.

biridiya.s: Biridiya was the ruler of Megiddo in Canaan in the fourteenth century BCE, a vassal of the Egyptian pharaohs. Several of his letters survive in the Amarna archive, in which he stresses his loyalty, reports on labour provided for Egyptian estates and describes his conflict with…

becin.s: Beçin is a ruined medieval town on a rocky plateau near Milas in south-western Turkey. A Byzantine fortress, it was taken in the late thirteenth century by the Menteshe Turkmen and became a capital of the Menteshe beylik, with mosques, a madrasa and baths.

borte.s: Börte was the first and principal wife of Temüjin, later Genghis Khan, and mother of his four main sons, Jochi, Chagatai, Ögedei and Tolui. According to the Secret History of the Mongols, she was abducted by the Merkits soon after her marriage and rescued in a campaign led by…

busiris.s: Busiris was an ancient Egyptian city in the central Nile Delta, near present-day Abusir Bana. Its Greek name comes from the Egyptian Per-Usir, house of Osiris, and it was the god's chief cult centre in Lower Egypt.

basento.s: The Basento is a river of Basilicata in southern Italy. Rising in the Lucanian Apennines, it flows past Potenza and runs south-east to the Gulf of Taranto near Metaponto.

bradano.s: The Bradano is a river of southern Italy that rises in the Lucanian Apennines of Basilicata and flows south-east, partly along the border with Apulia, to the Gulf of Taranto. Its mouth lies just north of Metaponto, and with the Basento it framed the coastal plain of the…

bayinnaung.s: Bayinnaung was king of the First Toungoo Empire of Burma from 1550 to 1581, and created what may have been the largest empire in the history of South-East Asia. He reunited Burma after the death of Tabinshwehti, conquered the Shan states, took Chiang Mai in 1558 and captured…

battles-of-khalkhin-gol.s: The Battles of Khalkhin Gol, known in Japan as the Nomonhan Incident, were fought from May to September 1939 on the Khalkhin Gol river on the border between Mongolia and Japanese-controlled Manchukuo. Soviet and Mongolian forces under Georgy Zhukov encircled and destroyed much…

brades.s: Brades is a village in the north of Montserrat in the Caribbean that has served as the island's de facto capital since the eruptions of the Soufrière Hills volcano destroyed the official capital, Plymouth, in 1997. Government offices moved there after the southern part of the…

boulogne-sur-mer.s: Boulogne-sur-Mer is a port town on the English Channel in northern France. As Gesoriacum it was a major Roman port and the base of the Classis Britannica, the fleet that guarded the Channel and linked Gaul with Britain, and Caligula built a lighthouse there.

battle-of-bud-bagsak.s: The Battle of Bud Bagsak was fought in June 1913 on the island of Jolo in the southern Philippines between American troops under General John J. Pershing, with Philippine Scouts, and several hundred Tausug fighters who had fortified the mountain. Several hundred Moros,…

bluefields.s: Bluefields is a port town on the Caribbean coast of Nicaragua, at the mouth of the Escondido River. Named after a 17th-century Dutch pirate, it became the seat of the Miskito kings under British protection and then of the self-governing Mosquito Reserve created in 1860.

black-warrior-river.s: The Black Warrior River is a river of west-central Alabama in the United States, flowing past Tuscaloosa to join the Tombigbee. Its name translates that of the Muscogean chief Tuskaloosa.

buynaksk.s: Buynaksk, known until 1922 as Temir-Khan-Shura, is a town in Dagestan in the Russian North Caucasus. Founded as a Russian fortress in the 1830s, it was the administrative centre of the Dagestan Oblast until the Revolution and briefly a seat of the Mountainous Republic of the…

bashir-shihab-iii.s: Bashir Shihab III was the last emir of Mount Lebanon from the Shihab family, appointed by the Ottomans in 1840 after the exile of his kinsman Bashir II. Weak and unpopular, he could not control the growing conflict between Druze and Maronites.

beiteddine-palace.s: Beiteddine Palace is a palace in the Chouf mountains of Lebanon, built by Emir Bashir Shihab II over some thirty years from about 1788. It combines Italian and Arab architecture around large courtyards, with fountains, mosaics and baths.

beira.s: Beira is a port city in central Mozambique, at the mouth of the Pungwe River on the Indian Ocean. Founded in 1887, it became the capital of the Mozambique Company and the terminus of a railway that reached the British colonies inland by 1899.

bodawpaya.s: Bodawpaya was the sixth king of the Konbaung dynasty of Burma, reigning from 1782 to 1819. He conquered the kingdom of Arakan in 1784 to 1785, carrying the revered Mahamuni Buddha image to his capital, and made costly failed invasions of Siam.

bagalkot-district.s: Bagalkot district is a district in the north of Karnataka state in India, with its headquarters at Bagalkot. Created in 1997 from part of Bijapur district, it includes the former princely states of Mudhol and Jamkhandi and the Chalukya temple sites of Badami, Aihole and…

boyaca-department.s: Boyacá Department is a department of central Colombia in the Eastern Ranges of the Andes, with its capital at Tunja. Its high plateau was the northern heartland of the Muisca, whose towns included Hunza, Sugamuxi and Tundama, the modern Tunja, Sogamoso and Duitama.

battle-of-boyaca.s: The Battle of Boyacá was fought on 7 August 1819 near Tunja in present-day Colombia, where the patriot army of Simón Bolívar and Francisco de Paula Santander defeated a royalist force after crossing the Andes. The victory opened the road to Bogotá, ended Spanish rule over most…

banu-kinana.s: The Banu Kinana are an Arab tribal group of western Arabia, from which the Quraysh, the tribe of the Prophet Muhammad, descended. Kinana clans took part in the early Islamic conquests and settled across Syria, Iraq and Egypt.

bernhard-rothmann.s: Bernhard Rothmann was a German preacher who led the Reformation in the city of Münster, where he won much of the citizenry to Lutheran views by 1532. He then rejected infant baptism and joined the Anabaptists, becoming the chief writer of the Anabaptist kingdom of Münster…

brims.s: Brims was a leader of Coweta, the principal town of the Lower Muscogee, called 'Emperor' by English colonists. During and after the Yamasee War of 1715 to 1717 he developed a policy of neutrality, playing the British, French and Spanish colonies against each other to protect…

bengaluru.s: Bengaluru, known until 2014 as Bangalore, is the capital of the Indian state of Karnataka. Founded in 1537 by the chief Kempe Gowda, it was held by Mysore under Hyder Ali and Tipu Sultan and became a large British military cantonment in the 19th century.

beni-isguen.s: Beni Isguen is one of the five fortified towns of the Mzab valley in the Algerian Sahara, near Ghardaïa. Considered the holiest of the five, it kept strict Ibadi rules, with gates closed at night and limited access for outsiders.

bou-noura.s: Bou Noura is one of the five fortified Ibadi towns of the Mzab valley in the Algerian Sahara, built on a rocky outcrop near Ghardaïa in the 11th century. Its name means 'the luminous one'.

books-of-maccabees.s: The Books of Maccabees are Jewish writings of the 2nd and 1st centuries BCE. The first two tell of the revolt of the Maccabees against the Seleucid king Antiochus IV and the founding of the Hasmonean state, including the rededication of the Temple remembered at Hanukkah.

bahla.s: Bahla is an oasis town in the interior of Oman, at the foot of the Jebel Akhdar. It was the capital of the Nabhani dynasty from the 12th to the 15th century, and its great mud-brick fort and some twelve kilometres of walls date largely from that period.

battle-of-argaon.s: The Battle of Argaon was fought on 29 November 1803 in the Deccan between a British force under Arthur Wellesley, later Duke of Wellington, and the armies of Raghuji II Bhonsle of Nagpur and Daulat Rao Scindia. The Maratha forces were routed, and soon after the British took…

battle-of-sitabuldi.s: The Battle of Sitabuldi was fought on 26–27 November 1817 at Nagpur, when the forces of the Bhonsle ruler Appa Sahib attacked the British Residency and its small garrison on the Sitabuldi hills. The outnumbered Company troops held out, and a further defeat at Nagpur in…

battle-of-chakirmaut.s: The Battle of Chakirmaut was fought in 1204 in western Mongolia between Temüjin, the future Genghis Khan, and the Naimans under Tayang Khan, who were joined by Jamukha and other opponents of Temüjin. Temüjin's army won decisively, and Tayang Khan was mortally wounded.

barom-kagyu.s: The Barom Kagyu is a school of the Kagyu tradition of Tibetan Buddhism, founded in the 12th century by Barom Darma Wangchuk, a disciple of Gampopa. Named after the Barom monastery he established in northern Tibet, it later found its main base in Nangchen in Kham, where the…

bo-kluea-district.s: Bo Kluea is a district in the mountains of Nan Province in northern Thailand, near the border with Laos. Its name means 'salt well', after the brine wells from which salt has been boiled for centuries.

bambatha-rebellion.s: The Bambatha Rebellion was a Zulu uprising against British rule and taxation in the Colony of Natal in 1906, sparked by a new poll tax. It was led by Bambatha kaMancinza, a chief of the Zondi, and fought largely in the forests of the Nkandla region.

battle-of-congella.s: The Battle of Congella was fought on 23–24 May 1842 at Port Natal, present-day Durban, between Boers of the Natalia Republic and a British force under Captain Thomas Smith. The British night attack failed, and the Boers besieged their camp until Dick King rode to Grahamstown…

battle-of-pokarwis.s: The Battle of Pokarwis was fought in January 1261 in Natangia, Prussia, during the Great Prussian Uprising against the Teutonic Order. Prussian forces led by Herkus Monte defeated an army of the Order and crusaders that had come to relieve its besieged castles.

bosque-redondo.s: Bosque Redondo was an internment reservation on the Pecos River in eastern New Mexico, guarded by Fort Sumner, where the US Army confined about 9,000 Navajo and some 400 Mescalero Apache from 1863. Bad water, crop failures, disease and raids caused thousands of deaths.

battle-of-plassey.s: The Battle of Plassey was fought on 23 June 1757 near Palashi in Bengal, where a British East India Company force under Robert Clive defeated the much larger army of Siraj ud-Daulah, Nawab of Bengal. The outcome was decided largely by the defection of the nawab's commander Mir…

balachadi.s: Balachadi is a coastal village near Jamnagar in Gujarat, India, where during the Second World War Maharaja Digvijaysinhji of Nawanagar sheltered several hundred Polish children who had been evacuated from the Soviet Union. The camp operated from 1942 to 1946.

battle-of-bhuchar-mori.s: The Battle of Bhuchar Mori was fought in 1591 near Dhrol in Saurashtra, Gujarat, between a Mughal army under Mirza Aziz Koka and the Kathiawar chiefs led by the Jam of Nawanagar, who had sheltered the fugitive Sultan Muzaffar Shah III of Gujarat. The Mughals won after heavy…

battle-of-mosega.s: The Battle of Mosega was fought in January 1837 near present-day Zeerust in South Africa, when Voortrekkers under Hendrik Potgieter and Gert Maritz, with Griqua and Tswana allies, attacked the Ndebele settlement at Mosega. Many Ndebele were killed and thousands of cattle taken.

battle-of-gqokli-hill.s: The Battle of Gqokli Hill was fought around 1818 near the White Mfolozi river in present-day KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa, between the Zulu under Shaka and the larger army of the Ndwandwe under Zwide. Shaka's forces held the hilltop and inflicted heavy losses, including several…

battle-of-halule.s: The Battle of Halule was fought in 691 BCE on the Tigris in Mesopotamia between the Neo-Assyrian Empire under Sennacherib and an alliance of Babylonians and Elamites led by the Elamite king Humban-nimena. Both sides claimed victory in their records.

bavay.s: Bavay is a small town in the Nord department of northern France, near the Belgian border. As Bagacum it was the chief town of the Nervii under Roman rule and a major road junction, with a large forum whose remains are among the best preserved in northern Gaul.

boduognatus.s: Boduognatus was the war leader of the Nervii, a Belgic people of northern Gaul, who commanded them against Julius Caesar in 57 BCE. At the Battle of the Sabis he led a surprise attack on Caesar's legions as they built their camp, which nearly succeeded before the Nervii were…

basilica-of-saint-denis.s: The Basilica of Saint-Denis, north of Paris, began as the church of a royal abbey built over the tomb of Saint Denis, the 3rd-century first bishop of Paris. From the Merovingian period it enjoyed the patronage of the Frankish kings and became the burial place of the kings of…

battle-of-toubacanti.s: The Battle of Toubacanti was fought in February 1700 in Darién, present-day Panama, when Scottish colonists of the second Darien expedition under Captain Alexander Campbell of Fonab, with Guna allies, attacked a Spanish force and drove it back. The victory was short-lived:…

battle-of-the-plains-of-abraham.n: Battle of the Plains of Abraham
battle-of-the-plains-of-abraham.s: The Battle of the Plains of Abraham was fought on 13 September 1759 outside Quebec City between British forces under General James Wolfe and French forces under the Marquis de Montcalm. After climbing the cliffs above the St Lawrence by night, the British won in less than an…

branford-connecticut.s: Branford is a town on Long Island Sound in New Haven County, Connecticut, United States, east of New Haven. Settled in 1644 by colonists from Wethersfield, it joined the New Haven Colony.

bolsa-familia.s: Bolsa Família is a Brazilian social programme that pays monthly cash transfers to poor families on condition that their children attend school and are vaccinated. Created in 2003 under President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva by merging earlier schemes, it reached about a quarter…

bagram.s: Bagram is a town north of Kabul in Parwan province, Afghanistan, near the meeting of the Ghorband and Panjshir rivers. It lies near the site of ancient Kapisa, where excavations in the 1930s uncovered the Begram hoard of Indian ivories, Roman glass and Chinese lacquer.

balasore.s: Balasore, or Baleshwar, is a city in northern Odisha, India, near the coast of the Bay of Bengal, and the headquarters of Balasore district. From the 17th century the English, Dutch, French and Danish East India Companies kept trading factories there.

ballana.s: Ballana is an archaeological site in Lower Nubia on the west bank of the Nile, in southern Egypt, now under Lake Nasser. Excavations by Walter Emery in the 1930s uncovered large burial mounds of rulers of the 4th to 6th centuries CE, with silver crowns, weapons and sacrificed…

battle-of-buyur-lake.s: The Battle of Buyur Lake was a Ming victory over the Northern Yuan in 1388 near Lake Buir in eastern Mongolia. A Ming army under Lan Yu surprised the camp of the khan Toghus Temür, capturing tens of thousands of people, including members of his family.

battle-of-shelon.s: The Battle of Shelon was fought on 14 July 1471 on the Shelon river, west of Lake Ilmen, between the army of the Novgorod Republic and the forces of Ivan III of Moscow. The much larger but poorly led Novgorod militia was routed.

bedouin.s: The Bedouin are the nomadic and semi-nomadic Arab tribes of the deserts of Arabia, Syria, Iraq and North Africa, organised in lineages and tribal confederations. Herding camels, sheep and goats, they controlled desert routes and served settled states as soldiers, allies or…

banu-amir.s: The Banu Amir, or Banu Amir ibn Sa'sa'a, were a large confederation of Arab tribes of central and western Arabia, attested before and after the rise of Islam. Its branches included the Banu Kilab, Banu Uqayl and Banu Numayr, which migrated north into Syria and the Jazira.

bizen-ware.s: Bizen ware is a Japanese stoneware made around Imbe in the former Bizen Province, now Okayama Prefecture. One of the Six Old Kilns of Japan, it is fired at high temperature without glaze in wood-burning kilns, which give its reddish-brown surface natural ash and flame markings.

buddhagupta-stone.s: The Buddhagupta stone is an inscribed tablet of about the 5th century CE found in 1834 in Seberang Perai on the Malay Peninsula, south of Kedah. Its Sanskrit inscription, in an early South Indian script, prays for a safe voyage for the master mariner (mahanavika) Buddhagupta…

bujang-valley.s: The Bujang Valley is an archaeological region near Merbok in Kedah, north-western Malaysia, between Gunung Jerai and the Muda River. It contains the remains of more than fifty Hindu and Buddhist brick and laterite shrines, called candi, and the ironworking site of Sungai Batu,…

battle-of-nafels.s: The Battle of Näfels was fought on 9 April 1388 in the canton of Glarus, where the men of Glarus, with help from Schwyz, defeated a much larger Habsburg army. Following the Swiss victory at Sempach in 1386, it secured the independence of Glarus from Habsburg rule.

bottiaeans.s: The Bottiaeans were an ancient people of Macedonia who originally lived in Bottiaea, the plain west of the Axios river. Driven out by the expanding Macedonian kings, they resettled in Chalcidice in a district called Bottice, where Olynthus was their town until the Persians…

battle-of-oriskany.s: The Battle of Oriskany was fought on 6 August 1777 near Oriskany in central New York during the American Revolutionary War. A Patriot militia column under Nicholas Herkimer, with Oneida allies, marching to relieve Fort Stanwix was ambushed by Loyalists and Mohawk and Seneca…

bloemfontein-convention.s: The Bloemfontein Convention was the agreement of 23 February 1854 by which Britain withdrew from the Orange River Sovereignty and recognised the independence of its Boer inhabitants. Signed by the special commissioner Sir George Clerk and representatives of the burghers, it…

battle-of-berea.s: The Battle of Berea was fought on 20 December 1852 on the Berea plateau in present-day Lesotho between British forces under Sir George Cathcart and the Basotho of Moshoeshoe I. Cathcart's punitive expedition to seize cattle met stiff resistance, and the fighting was indecisive.

battle-of-viervoet.s: The Battle of Viervoet was fought on 30 June 1851 near the Lesotho border between a force led by the British Resident Henry Warden and the Basotho of Moshoeshoe I. Warden's British troops, Boer burghers and African allies were defeated.

bloemfontein.s: Bloemfontein is a city in central South Africa, capital of the Free State province and the country's judicial capital. Founded in 1846 by Major Henry Warden as a British post, it became the capital of the Orange River Sovereignty and from 1854 of the Orange Free State.

betwa-river.s: The Betwa is a river of central India that rises in the Vindhya Range in Madhya Pradesh and flows north-east for about 590 km to join the Yamuna in Uttar Pradesh. It runs through the Bundelkhand region, and the Bundela capital of Orchha was built on an island in its course in…

bundelas.s: The Bundelas are a Rajput clan of central India who gave their name to Bundelkhand. Rising in the 16th century under Rudra Pratap Singh, who founded Orchha in 1531, they built kingdoms that alternately served and resisted the Mughals, and Chhatrasal of Panna won independence…

battle-of-coronea-394-bc.s: The Battle of Coronea of 394 BCE was fought in Boeotia during the Corinthian War between a Spartan army under King Agesilaus II, newly returned from Asia, and a coalition of Thebes, Athens, Argos and Corinth. Agesilaus held the field after a fierce clash with the Thebans, but…

battle-of-coronea-447-bc.s: The Battle of Coronea of 447 BCE was fought in Boeotia, where Boeotian exiles and their allies defeated an Athenian force under Tolmides as it withdrew. The Athenian defeat ended Athens' control of Boeotia, won after Oenophyta in 457 BCE, and allowed the Boeotian League to…

broad-front-uruguay.s: The Broad Front, or Frente Amplio, is a left-wing coalition of parties in Uruguay founded in 1971. Banned under the military dictatorship of 1973–1985, it governed from 2005 to 2020 under Tabaré Vázquez and José Mujica and returned to office in 2025 under Yamandú Orsi.

boethius.s: Boethius was a Roman senator and philosopher who served Theodoric the Great, becoming consul in 510 and master of offices. Accused of treason, he was imprisoned and executed in 524, and in prison he wrote The Consolation of Philosophy, one of the most widely read books of the…

battle-of-taginae.s: The Battle of Taginae, also called Busta Gallorum, was fought in the Apennines of central Italy in the summer of 552. A Byzantine army under the eunuch general Narses defeated the Ostrogoths, and their king Totila was mortally wounded.

battle-of-mons-lactarius.s: The Battle of Mons Lactarius was fought near Mount Vesuvius in Campania in 552 or 553 between the Byzantine army of Narses and the last Ostrogothic king, Teia. After a stand-off of about two months the Goths attacked, and Teia was killed in the fighting.

bungo-province.s: Bungo Province was an old province of Japan in north-eastern Kyushu, corresponding to most of modern Ōita Prefecture. From the Kamakura period it was the home base of the Ōtomo clan, whose port town of Funai traded with China and the Portuguese in the 16th century.

battle-of-mimikawa.s: The Battle of Mimikawa was fought in 1578 on the Mimi River in Hyūga Province, Kyushu, between the Ōtomo and the Shimazu. Ōtomo Sōrin's army, advancing to restore an exiled client lord, was drawn into a trap and routed with heavy losses. The defeat broke Ōtomo power and…

battle-of-ridaniya.s: The Battle of Ridaniya was fought on 22 January 1517 outside Cairo between the Ottoman army of Selim I and the Mamluks under Sultan Tuman bay II. Ottoman artillery and musketry outflanked the Mamluk fortified line, and Cairo was taken soon after.

battle-of-miyajima.s: The Battle of Miyajima was fought in 1555 on the island of Itsukushima in the Inland Sea of Japan. Mōri Motonari lured the much larger army of Sue Harukata onto the island and attacked it by night from land and sea, destroying it; Sue killed himself.

bustan-al-salatin.s: The Bustan al-Salatin, 'Garden of Kings', is a Malay encyclopaedic work written by Nuruddin ar-Raniri at the court of Aceh, begun in 1638 at the command of Sultan Iskandar Thani. In seven books it covers the creation of the world, the prophets, the history of kings in the…

bura.s: Bura was an ancient city of Achaea in the northern Peloponnese, above the Gulf of Corinth. It was destroyed with neighbouring Helike by the earthquake of 373 BCE and rebuilt on higher ground.

battle-of-the-hekatombaion.s: The Battle of the Hekatombaion was fought in 226 BCE near Dyme in western Achaea, where Cleomenes III of Sparta crushed the full army of the Achaean League. Coming after earlier defeats at Mount Lykaion and Ladokeia, the disaster convinced Aratus of Sicyon to seek help from…

battle-of-ladoceia.s: The Battle of Ladoceia was fought in 227 BCE near Megalopolis in Arcadia during the Cleomenean War. Cleomenes III of Sparta defeated the Achaean League army under Aratus, and the Megalopolitan leader Lydiadas was killed when he pursued with the cavalry without support.

battle-of-scarpheia.s: The Battle of Scarpheia was fought in 146 BCE near Scarpheia in eastern Locris, at the start of the Achaean War. The Roman commander Quintus Caecilius Metellus caught the Achaean army of Critolaus, which was retreating from the siege of Heraclea, and destroyed it.

battle-of-mantinea-207-bce.s: The Battle of Mantinea of 207 BCE was fought in Arcadia between the Achaean League under Philopoemen and the Spartans under Machanidas. Philopoemen's reformed phalanx held a line behind a ditch while the Spartan mercenaries pursued too far, and Machanidas was killed,…

battle-of-cunaxa.s: The Battle of Cunaxa was fought in 401 BCE on the Euphrates north of Babylon between the Persian king Artaxerxes II and his younger brother Cyrus the Younger, who sought the throne. Cyrus' Greek mercenaries routed the royal troops facing them, but Cyrus was killed charging at…

bardo-national-museum.s: The Bardo National Museum in Tunis, opened in 1888 in a former palace of the Husainid beys, is the national archaeological museum of Tunisia. It holds one of the world's largest collections of Roman mosaics, gathered from sites such as Carthage, Dougga, El Djem and Sousse,…

baal-hammon.s: Baal Hammon was the chief god of Carthage and the Punic world, worshipped with the goddess Tanit. His sanctuaries, called tophets, contain urns of burnt infants and animals whose interpretation as child sacrifice is still debated.

battle-of-murche-khort.s: The Battle of Murche-Khort was fought in November 1729 north of Isfahan, when Nader, then general of the Safavid claimant Tahmasp II, defeated the Afghan army of the Hotaki ruler Ashraf. Following Nader's victory at Damghan weeks earlier, it forced the Afghans to abandon…

burhagohain.s: The Burhagohain was the senior of the great ministers of the Ahom kingdom of Assam, an office traditionally dated to the reign of the founder Sukaphaa in the 13th century. Held by members of particular hereditary Ahom clans, it acted as chief counsellor of the king and…

borgohain.s: The Borgohain was one of the two oldest ministerial offices of the Ahom kingdom of Assam, alongside the Burhagohain, traditionally dated to the founder Sukaphaa in the 13th century. Hereditary in a particular Ahom noble clan, it formed with the Burhagohain and the later…

borpatrogohain.s: The Borpatrogohain was a ministerial office of the Ahom kingdom of Assam, created by King Suhungmung in the early 16th century as a third great counsellor beside the Burhagohain and the Borgohain. Like them it was reserved for particular Ahom noble clans, and the three Gohains…

borbarua.s: The Borbarua was a high office of the Ahom kingdom of Assam, created by King Pratap Singha in the early 17th century. Its holder, who could be drawn from outside the old Gohain families, was responsible for revenue, justice and military affairs in Upper Assam.

badan-chandra-borphukan.s: Badan Chandra Borphukan was the Ahom viceroy of Lower Assam in the early 19th century. Threatened by the powerful minister Purnananda Burhagohain, he fled to Calcutta and then to the Konbaung court of Burma, whose army he brought into Assam in 1817.

burhi-dihing-river.s: The Burhi Dihing is a river of Upper Assam in north-east India, a major south-bank tributary of the Brahmaputra. Rising in the Patkai range in eastern Arunachal Pradesh, it flows west through the Tinsukia and Dibrugarh districts to join the Brahmaputra at Dihingmukh.

bengal-subah.s: The Bengal Subah was the province of the Mughal Empire covering Bengal, roughly present-day Bangladesh and the Indian state of West Bengal, at times with parts of Bihar and Odisha. Conquered from the Karrani sultans in 1576, it became one of the empire's richest provinces,…

battle-of-argentovaria.s: The Battle of Argentovaria was fought in 378 in Alsace between the Western Roman army of the emperor Gratian and the Alemannic Lentienses, who had crossed the frozen Rhine. Gratian's generals Nannienus and the Frankish king Mallobaudes crushed the invaders and killed their…

battle-of-strasbourg.s: The Battle of Strasbourg, or Argentoratum, was fought in August 357 near Strasbourg between a Roman army under the Caesar Julian and a coalition of Alemannic kings led by Chnodomar and his nephew Serapio. Julian's roughly 13,000 men defeated a force that Ammianus Marcellinus…

bucinobantes.s: The Bucinobantes were an Alemannic people of the fourth century, living on the right bank of the Rhine opposite Mainz. Their king Macrianus resisted the emperor Valentinian I, who tried in vain to capture him and to replace him with Fraomarius, before making peace with him on…

butilin.s: Butilin, or Buccelin, was an Alemannic duke in the service of the Frankish Merovingian kings. With his brother Leuthari he led a large Frankish and Alemannic army into Italy in 553 during the Gothic War, raiding as far south as Campania.

battle-of-solicinium.s: The Battle of Solicinium was fought in 368 between the Roman army of Valentinian I and his young son Gratian and the Alemanni, at a hill site in south-west Germany whose location is uncertain. After Rando's raid on Mainz, Valentinian invaded Alemannic territory; the Alemanni…

boris-skossyreff.s: Boris Skossyreff was a Russian émigré adventurer who in July 1934 proclaimed himself King Boris I of Andorra and issued a constitution for the principality. Within days the bishop of Urgell had him arrested by the Spanish Civil Guard, and he was tried in Barcelona and expelled…

battle-of-cynoscephalae.s: The Battle of Cynoscephalae was fought in 197 BCE in Thessaly between the Roman army of Titus Quinctius Flamininus and the Macedonian army of Philip V. In hilly ground and mist, the Roman legions, helped by elephants and by a tribune's attack on the rear of the phalanx,…

baysunghur-aq-qoyunlu.s: Baysunghur was ruler of the Aq Qoyunlu from 1490 to 1493, succeeding his father Ya'qub as a boy. Unable to control the tribal emirs, he was overthrown by his cousin Rustam, and the fiscal reforms of his father's reign were abandoned.

barings-bank.s: Barings Bank, founded in London in 1762, was one of Britain's oldest merchant banks and a leading lender to governments in the nineteenth century, helping to finance the Louisiana Purchase. Its heavy lending in Argentina brought it close to collapse in the crisis of 1890.

battle-of-cepeda-1859.s: The Battle of Cepeda was fought on 23 October 1859 in Buenos Aires province between the army of the Argentine Confederation under Justo José de Urquiza and the forces of the State of Buenos Aires under Bartolomé Mitre. Urquiza's victory led to the Pact of San José de Flores,…

battle-of-curupayty.s: The Battle of Curupayty was fought on 22 September 1866 in southern Paraguay, when allied Argentine and Brazilian troops under Bartolomé Mitre assaulted Paraguayan entrenchments near Humaitá. The attack failed with several thousand allied casualties against very light…

bernardo-houssay.s: Bernardo Houssay was an Argentine physiologist who shared the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 1947 for discovering the part played by hormones of the pituitary gland in the metabolism of sugar. He was the first Latin American laureate in the sciences, and he founded…

battle-of-amoaful.s: The Battle of Amoaful was fought on 31 January 1874 in the forest south of Kumasi, when a British expedition under Sir Garnet Wolseley defeated a large Asante army. The British advanced in a square through dense bush, using artillery and rockets, and the victory opened the…

battle-of-ordashu.s: The Battle of Ordashu was fought on 4 February 1874 a few miles south of Kumasi, the last engagement of Sir Garnet Wolseley's expedition against the Asante. After hard fighting the British broke through and entered Kumasi the same day, burning the city before withdrawing to…

battle-of-pallene.s: The Battle of Pallene was fought in Attica around 546 BCE, when Peisistratus, returning from exile with mercenaries and allies, surprised and routed the Athenian forces near the sanctuary of Athena at Pallene. The victory gave him his third and lasting tyranny over Athens,…

battle-of-aspern-essling.s: The Battle of Aspern-Essling was fought on 21–22 May 1809 on the north bank of the Danube near Vienna, where Archduke Charles of Austria repulsed Napoleon's attempt to cross the river. It was the first major defeat of Napoleon in person in more than a decade, though he…

biedermeier.s: Biedermeier is the name given to the middle-class culture of Central Europe, especially Austria and Germany, between the Congress of Vienna in 1815 and the revolutions of 1848. Under censorship and political repression, it turned to private and domestic life, producing simple,…

burgtheater.s: The Burgtheater is the national theatre of Austria in Vienna, founded in 1741 by Maria Theresa beside the imperial palace and made a court and national theatre by Joseph II in 1776. It staged the plays of Franz Grillparzer, and in 1888 it moved to a new building on the…

battle-of-cer.s: The Battle of Cer was fought on 15–24 August 1914 on and around Mount Cer in western Serbia, when the Serbian army under Stepa Stepanović defeated the first Austro-Hungarian invasion of Serbia. It forced the invaders back across the Drina and is often described as the first…

battle-of-kolubara.s: The Battle of Kolubara was fought in western Serbia in November and December 1914, when the Serbian army, reorganised under Radomir Putnik and Živojin Mišić, counter-attacked an Austro-Hungarian army that had taken Belgrade. The Austro-Hungarians were driven out of Serbia with…

battle-of-nong-sarai.s: The Battle of Nong Sarai was fought in early 1593 near Suphan Buri, where King Naresuan of Ayutthaya defeated a Burmese invasion army. According to the chronicles Naresuan killed the Burmese crown prince Mingyi Swa in single combat on war elephants.

baekje-historic-areas.s: The Baekje Historic Areas are a UNESCO World Heritage Site in South Korea, listed in 2015. They group eight sites from the later capitals of Baekje at Gongju, Buyeo and Iksan, including Gongsanseong fortress, the Songsan-ri tombs with the tomb of King Muryeong, Busosanseong,…

battle-of-gwansanseong.s: The Battle of Gwansanseong was fought in 554 at the fortress of Gwansanseong, near modern Okcheon in Korea, between Baekje and Silla. King Seong of Baekje attacked Silla in revenge for its seizure of the Han River basin, but was killed and his army destroyed; the Samguk sagi…

boksin.s: Boksin was a Baekje general and member of the royal family who led the movement to restore Baekje after its conquest by Tang and Silla in 660. With the monk Dochim he held out at Juryu fortress, brought Prince Buyeo Pung back from Japan and won Yamato support.

buyeo-pung.s: Buyeo Pung was a prince of Baekje, son of its last king Uija, who lived at the Yamato court in Japan as a hostage. After Baekje fell to Tang and Silla in 660, the restoration leaders brought him back to Korea as king with Japanese support.

balhaego.s: The Balhaego, "A Study of Balhae", is a history of the kingdom of Balhae written by the Joseon scholar Yu Deuk-gong and completed in 1784. Drawing on Chinese, Korean and Japanese sources, it treated Balhae as a Korean state and coined the idea of a period of Northern and…

bara-sona-mosque.s: The Bara Sona Mosque, the Great Golden Mosque, is a ruined mosque at Gaur in West Bengal, India, the largest surviving monument of the city. Begun under Alauddin Husain Shah and completed by his son Nasiruddin Nusrat Shah in 1526, it is built of brick faced with stone and once…

battle-of-rajmahal.s: The Battle of Rajmahal was fought on 12 July 1576 near Rajmahal on the Ganges, in present-day Jharkhand, India, between the Mughal army of Akbar under Khan Jahan and Todar Mal and the forces of Daud Khan Karrani, the last sultan of Bengal. Daud was defeated, captured and…

battle-of-ghaghra.s: The Battle of Ghaghra was fought on 6 May 1529 near the confluence of the Ghaghra and the Ganges, in present-day Bihar, India. The Mughal emperor Babur defeated the Afghan chiefs of eastern India and the army of Nasiruddin Nusrat Shah, sultan of Bengal, who had supported them.

battle-of-tukaroi.s: The Battle of Tukaroi was fought on 3 March 1575 near the village of Tukaroi in present-day Balasore district, Odisha, India, between the Mughal army of Akbar under Munim Khan and Todar Mal and Daud Khan Karrani, sultan of Bengal. Daud was defeated and signed the Treaty of…

battle-of-surajgarh.s: The Battle of Surajgarh was fought in 1534 near Surajgarha on the Kiul river in Bihar, India, between the Afghan leader Sher Khan Sur and the army of Ghiyasuddin Mahmud Shah, sultan of Bengal, allied with the Lohani rulers of Bihar. Sher Khan's victory made him master of Bihar…

battle-of-cynoscephalae-364-bce.s: The Battle of Cynoscephalae in 364 BCE was fought in Thessaly between a Theban-led army under Pelopidas and Alexander, tyrant of Pherae. The Thebans and their Thessalian allies won the battle, but Pelopidas was killed while charging at Alexander in person.

battle-of-delium.s: The Battle of Delium was fought in 424 BCE near Delium on the Boeotian coast during the Peloponnesian War. The Boeotian army under the Theban commander Pagondas, drawn up 25 ranks deep and supported by a surprise cavalry attack, defeated an Athenian army under Hippocrates, who…

battle-of-haliartus.s: The Battle of Haliartus was fought in 395 BCE outside the Boeotian city of Haliartus at the start of the Corinthian War. The Spartan commander Lysander attacked the city before the main Spartan army under King Pausanias arrived, and was killed when the Thebans and the…

battle-of-oenophyta.s: The Battle of Oenophyta was fought in Boeotia in 457 BCE, about two months after the Spartan victory at Tanagra. An Athenian army under Myronides defeated the Boeotians, and Athens then dominated Boeotia, Phocis and Opuntian Locris, supporting friendly regimes in the Boeotian…

battle-of-tegyra.s: The Battle of Tegyra was fought in 375 BCE near Orchomenus in Boeotia, when the Theban commander Pelopidas, leading the Sacred Band and a small force of cavalry, met a larger Spartan force. The Thebans broke the Spartans and killed both their commanders.

battle-of-leuctra.s: The Battle of Leuctra was fought in Boeotia in 371 BCE between Thebes and its Boeotian allies under Epaminondas and a Spartan army under King Cleombrotus I. Epaminondas massed his left wing 50 ranks deep, with the Sacred Band under Pelopidas, and smashed the Spartan right,…

benjamin-constant-botelho-de-magalhaes.s: Benjamin Constant Botelho de Magalhães was a Brazilian army officer, mathematician and teacher at the military school in Rio de Janeiro. A follower of the positivism of Auguste Comte, he spread republican ideas among young officers and was a leading organiser of the military…

brazilian-historical-and-geographic-inst.s: The Brazilian Historical and Geographic Institute is a learned society founded in Rio de Janeiro in 1838 to collect documents and write a national history of Brazil. Closely patronised by Emperor Pedro II, who attended hundreds of its sessions, it shaped the official image of…

bengal-army.s: The Bengal Army was the army of the Bengal Presidency of the East India Company and later of the British Crown, the largest of the three presidency armies of India. Its high-caste sepoys from Awadh and Bihar formed the core of the rebellion of 1857, which began at Meerut.

batu-tarsilah.s: The Batu Tarsilah is an inscribed stone tablet in Brunei, set up in 1807 under Sultan Muhammad Tajuddin, recording in Malay in Jawi script the genealogy of the sultans of Brunei. Together with written genealogies such as the Salasilah Raja-Raja Brunei, it is a principal source…

brunei-shell-petroleum.s: Brunei Shell Petroleum is the main oil and gas producer of Brunei, jointly owned by the government of Brunei and the Shell group. As the British Malayan Petroleum Company, a Shell subsidiary, it discovered oil at Seria in 1929, which transformed the small sultanate into one of…

brunei-peoples-party.s: The Brunei People's Party was a political party founded in 1956 under the leadership of A. M. Azahari, calling for independence, democracy and the union of Brunei, Sarawak and North Borneo under the sultan. It won every elected seat in the 1962 elections to Brunei's…

book-of-fixed-stars.s: The Book of Fixed Stars is an astronomical treatise written around 964 by the Persian astronomer Abd al-Rahman al-Sufi and dedicated to the Buyid ruler Adud al-Dawla. It revised the star catalogue of Ptolemy's Almagest with new observations of positions and brightness,…

battle-of-batoche.s: The Battle of Batoche, fought on 9–12 May 1885 in present-day Saskatchewan, was the decisive battle of the North-West Rebellion. Canadian troops under General Frederick Middleton overran the Métis settlement held by the forces of Louis Riel and Gabriel Dumont.

battle-of-the-atlantic.s: The Battle of the Atlantic was the longest continuous campaign of the Second World War, fought between Allied navies and air forces and German U-boats and surface raiders over the convoy routes from North America to Britain. The Royal Canadian Navy grew into one of the largest…

battle-of-vimy-ridge.s: The Battle of Vimy Ridge, fought on 9–12 April 1917 in northern France as part of the Battle of Arras, was the first attack in which all four divisions of the Canadian Corps fought together. They captured the heavily fortified ridge at a cost of some 10,600 casualties.

british-commonwealth-air-training-plan.s: The British Commonwealth Air Training Plan was a Second World War programme for training aircrew from Britain, Canada, Australia, New Zealand and other Allied countries, run largely in Canada, far from enemy action. Agreed in December 1939, it trained more than 130,000 pilots,…

battle-of-st-jakob-an-der-sihl.n: Battle of St. Jakob an der Sihl
battle-of-st-jakob-an-der-sihl.s: The Battle of St. Jakob an der Sihl was fought on 22 July 1443 at the gates of Zürich during the Old Zürich War. The confederate army led by Schwyz defeated the Zürich forces and their Austrian allies outside the city, and the burgomaster Rudolf Stüssi was killed defending the…

battle-of-marignano.s: The Battle of Marignano was fought on 13–14 September 1515 near Melegnano, south-east of Milan, between the French army of Francis I and Swiss forces defending the duchy of Milan. After two days of hard fighting, with French artillery and the arrival of Venetian allies, the…

british-kaffraria.s: British Kaffraria was a British territory between the Keiskamma and Kei rivers in present-day Eastern Cape, South Africa, annexed by Governor Sir Harry Smith in 1847 after the War of the Axe. Governed from King William's Town and made a separate crown colony in 1860, it was…

balash.s: Balash was king of the Sasanian Empire from 484 to 488, succeeding his brother Peroz I, who died fighting the Hephthalites. Facing an exhausted treasury and unrest in the Caucasus, he reached a settlement with the Armenian rebels that granted freedom of Christian worship and…

battle-of-avarayr.s: The Battle of Avarayr was fought in 451 on the Avarayr plain, south-east of Lake Van in the historical province of Vaspurakan, between Armenian rebels led by Vardan Mamikonian and the army of the Sasanian king Yazdegerd II, who sought to impose Zoroastrianism. The Armenians…

battle-of-the-great-plains.s: The Battle of the Great Plains was fought in 203 BCE in the Bagradas valley of North Africa, in present-day Tunisia. Scipio Africanus defeated a Carthaginian and Numidian army under Hasdrubal Gisco and Syphax, which included about 4,000 Celtiberian mercenaries who fought to…

bilbilis.s: Bilbilis was a Celtiberian and then Roman town on a hill near modern Calatayud in Aragon, Spain. It became a Roman municipium under Augustus, with a forum, temple and theatre, and was known for the iron worked from local ores.

belshazzar.s: Belshazzar was the son of Nabonidus, the last king of the Neo-Babylonian Empire, and governed Babylon as regent for about a decade while his father lived at the Arabian oasis of Tayma. In the Book of Daniel he is the king who sees the writing on the wall at a feast on the…

bharavi.s: Bharavi was a Sanskrit poet of the sixth century, author of the Kiratarjuniya, an epic on Arjuna's combat with the god Shiva disguised as a mountain hunter. It is counted among the great court epics, or mahakavyas, and is noted for its dense meaning and elaborate verse.

battle-of-mycale.s: The Battle of Mycale was fought in 479 BCE at Mount Mycale on the coast of Ionia, opposite Samos. A Greek force under the Spartan king Leotychidas and the Athenian Xanthippus landed and destroyed a Persian army and its beached fleet, traditionally on the same day as the…

barquq.s: Barquq was a Circassian Mamluk who became sultan of Egypt and Syria in 1382, founding the Burji line of sultans. Briefly deposed in 1389, he regained the throne in 1390 and ruled until his death in 1399.

battle-of-bziyuk.s: The Battle of Bziyuk was fought in 1796 in western Circassia, on the Bziyuk river, between the free communities of the Shapsugs and Natukhaj and the forces of the Circassian princes and nobles, led by the Bzhedug aristocracy. The victory of the commoners broke princely power…

battle-of-kanzhal.s: The Battle of Kanzhal was fought in 1708 near Mount Kanzhal in Kabarda, in the North Caucasus. Kabardian forces under Prince Kurgoko Atazhukin defeated a reportedly much larger Crimean Tatar army sent by Khan Kaplan I Giray to enforce tribute.

black-sea-coastal-line.s: The Black Sea Coastal Line was a chain of Russian forts built from the late 1830s along the Black Sea coast of Circassia, from Anapa towards Abkhazia, to cut the Circassians off from Ottoman trade and supplies. Its isolated garrisons suffered heavily from disease, and in 1840…

burji-mamluks.s: The Burji Mamluks were the Circassian-dominated line of Mamluk sultans who ruled Egypt and Syria from the accession of Barquq in 1382 until the Ottoman conquest of 1517. They took their name from the regiment housed in the towers, or burj, of the Cairo citadel.

billy-hughes.s: Billy Hughes was prime minister of Australia from 1915 to 1923 and led the country through the First World War. His campaign for conscription, rejected in referendums in 1916 and 1917, split the Labor Party and led him to form the Nationalist Party.

battle-of-hamel.s: The Battle of Hamel was fought on 4 July 1918 near Le Hamel on the Somme in France. Planned by Sir John Monash, the Australian Corps, with American infantry, British tanks and aircraft, captured its objectives in about 93 minutes.

bob-hawke.s: Bob Hawke was the Labor prime minister of Australia from 1983 to 1991, after leading the Australian Council of Trade Unions. His government floated the Australian dollar, deregulated finance and lowered tariffs, governed through a prices and incomes accord with the unions,…

brussels-anti-slavery-conference-1889-18.s: The Brussels Anti-Slavery Conference of 1889–1890 was an international meeting convened at the invitation of Leopold II of Belgium. Its General Act of 2 July 1890 committed the European colonial powers to suppress the slave trade in Africa and to restrict the trade in firearms…

baldwin-v-count-of-hainaut.s: Baldwin V was count of Hainaut from 1171 and, through his wife Margaret I of Flanders, count of Flanders as Baldwin VIII from 1191 until his death in 1195. He also secured Namur, raised into a margraviate for him by imperial grant.

battle-of-cassel-1071.s: The Battle of Cassel was fought on 22 February 1071 near Cassel in Flanders over the succession to the county. Robert the Frisian, brother of the late Count Baldwin VI, defeated Baldwin's widow Richilde, who was supported by the French king Philip I, and her young son Count…

battle-of-sluys.s: The Battle of Sluys was a naval battle fought on 24 June 1340 in the Zwin estuary off Sluis in Flanders, early in the Hundred Years' War. The English fleet of Edward III attacked the French fleet assembled for an invasion of England and destroyed it almost entirely.

battle-of-gavere.s: The Battle of Gavere was fought on 23 July 1453 on the Scheldt south of Ghent, ending the revolt of Ghent against Philip the Good, duke of Burgundy. The Ghent militia was routed with heavy losses.

battle-of-mons-en-pevele.s: The Battle of Mons-en-Pévèle was fought on 18 August 1304 south of Lille between the army of Philip IV of France and the Flemish militias that had defeated the French at Kortrijk two years earlier. The hard-fought battle ended in a French victory, and the Treaty of…

battle-of-roosebeke.s: The Battle of Roosebeke was fought on 27 November 1382 near Westrozebeke in Flanders. A French royal army led by the young Charles VI, supporting Count Louis of Male, crushed the Flemish militias of Philip van Artevelde, who was killed.

battle-of-malplaquet.s: The Battle of Malplaquet was fought on 11 September 1709 near Mons, in Hainaut, during the War of the Spanish Succession. An allied army under the Duke of Marlborough and Prince Eugene of Savoy attacked the French under Marshal Villars and forced them to withdraw, but at such…

borinage.s: The Borinage is a former coal-mining district west of Mons in the Belgian province of Hainaut. Coal was dug there from the Middle Ages, and in the nineteenth century it became one of the main industrial areas of Belgium, known for harsh working conditions, poverty and labour…

bouchain.s: Bouchain is a small town on the Scheldt in the Nord department of northern France, formerly part of the County of Hainaut. A fortress on the frontier, it was taken by Louis XIV in 1676 and confirmed to France by the Treaty of Nijmegen in 1678, after which Vauban strengthened it.

battle-of-jemappes.s: The Battle of Jemappes was fought on 6 November 1792 near Mons in the Austrian Netherlands. A French revolutionary army under General Dumouriez defeated the Austrians under Duke Albert of Saxe-Teschen, one of the first large victories of the new French armies.

balingen.s: Balingen is a town on the river Eyach in the Zollernalb district of Baden-Württemberg, Germany, below the Swabian Jura. It was founded as a town by the counts of Zollern in the mid-thirteenth century and belonged to their Schalksburg line until it was sold, with the…

berthold-of-reichenau.s: Berthold of Reichenau was a monk of the abbey of Reichenau on Lake Constance and a chronicler of the eleventh century. A pupil of Hermann of Reichenau, he continued his master's chronicle and wrote a history of the early years of the Investiture Controversy from the papal side.

burgraviate-of-nuremberg.s: The Burgraviate of Nuremberg was the office and territory of the burgraves who commanded the imperial castle of Nuremberg for the Holy Roman Emperor. From about 1192 it was held by the Hohenzollerns, who built up lands in Franconia around Ansbach and Bayreuth.

beaucaire.s: Beaucaire is a town on the Rhône in the Gard department of southern France, opposite Tarascon. A possession of the counts of Toulouse, it was held by the crusaders and recaptured by the young Raymond VII in 1216 after a long siege.

basilica-of-saint-sernin.s: The Basilica of Saint-Sernin in Toulouse is a large Romanesque church built from about 1080 over the tomb of Saint Saturninus, the city's first bishop. Pope Urban II consecrated its altar in 1096.

battle-of-taillebourg.s: The Battle of Taillebourg was fought on 21–22 July 1242 at the bridge over the Charente at Taillebourg in Saintonge. Louis IX of France defeated Henry III of England and his allies the Lusignans, and a further victory at Saintes followed.

battle-of-konotop.s: The Battle of Konotop was fought in the summer of 1659 near Konotop in Ukraine, during the Russo-Polish War. The Cossack hetman Ivan Vyhovsky, allied with the Crimean khan Mehmed IV Giray, defeated a Muscovite army besieging the town under Prince Aleksey Trubetskoy, destroying…

battle-of-molodi.s: The Battle of Molodi was fought in late July and early August 1572 near the village of Molodi, south of Moscow. A Russian army under Prince Mikhail Vorotynsky defeated the much larger army of the Crimean khan Devlet I Giray, which had burned Moscow the year before.

belgorod-line.s: The Belgorod Line was a fortified defensive line built by Muscovy in 1635–1658 along its southern steppe frontier against Crimean and Nogai Tatar raids. Running some 800 km from the Vorskla to the Tambov area, with Belgorod as its centre, it combined towns, forts, earthen…

battle-of-berestechko.s: The Battle of Berestechko was fought from 28 June to 10 July 1651 in Volhynia, in present-day Ukraine, during the Khmelnytsky Uprising. The army of King John II Casimir of Poland defeated Bohdan Khmelnytsky's Cossacks after their ally, the Crimean khan Islam III Giray,…

burkhard-christoph-von-munnich.s: Burkhard Christoph von Münnich was a German-born soldier and engineer who became a field marshal of Russia. He completed the Ladoga Canal, and in the Russo-Turkish War of 1735–1739 he stormed the Perekop lines and burned Bakhchysarai in 1736, took Ochakov and won at Stavuchany…

bakhchisaray-fountain.s: The Bakhchisaray Fountain, also called the Fountain of Tears, is a marble wall fountain in the Khan's Palace at Bakhchysarai in Crimea, made in 1764 by the Persian master Omer for Khan Qırım Giray. Water drips slowly from one small bowl to the next, a symbol of endless grief.

battle-of-ponza.s: The Battle of Ponza was a naval battle fought on 5 August 1435 off the island of Ponza in the Tyrrhenian Sea. A Genoese fleet, acting for the duke of Milan, defeated the Aragonese fleet of Alfonso V, who was captured with his brothers.

battle-of-cerignola.s: The Battle of Cerignola was fought on 28 April 1503 in Apulia, southern Italy. A Spanish army under Gonzalo Fernández de Córdoba defeated the French under the Duke of Nemours, who was killed.

battle-of-epila.s: The Battle of Épila was fought on 21 July 1348 near Épila in Aragon. King Peter IV defeated the forces of the Union of Aragon, the league of nobles and towns that had forced him to confirm its privileges.

battle-of-les-formigues.s: The Battle of Les Formigues was a naval battle fought in 1285 near the Formigues islets off the coast of Catalonia, during the War of the Sicilian Vespers. An Aragonese and Catalan fleet defeated a French fleet supporting Philip III of France's invasion of Catalonia.

battle-of-najera.s: The Battle of Nájera was fought on 3 April 1367 in La Rioja during the Castilian civil war. Edward the Black Prince, with an Anglo-Gascon army, restored Peter I of Castile by defeating his half-brother Henry of Trastámara and the French captain Bertrand du Guesclin, who was…

battle-of-villalar.s: The Battle of Villalar was fought on 23 April 1521 near Valladolid, where royalist cavalry routed the army of the Castilian Comuneros. Their leaders Juan de Padilla, Juan Bravo and Francisco Maldonado were beheaded the next day.

battle-of-montiel.s: The Battle of Montiel was fought on 14 March 1369 in La Mancha, where Henry of Trastámara and Bertrand du Guesclin defeated Peter I of Castile. Peter took refuge in the castle of Montiel and was killed by Henry during a parley on 23 March.

bren-light-machine-gun.s: The Bren light machine gun was the standard light machine gun of the British and Commonwealth armies in the Second World War. It was developed from the Czechoslovak ZB vz. 26 and made under licence at the Royal Small Arms Factory at Enfield from 1937.

book-of-kells.s: The Book of Kells is an illuminated manuscript of the four Gospels in Latin, made around 800, probably in part at the monastery of Iona and completed at Kells in Ireland. Its elaborate decoration of interlace, animals and human figures makes it the masterpiece of Insular art.

battle-of-koge-bay.s: The Battle of Køge Bay was fought on 1 July 1677 south of Copenhagen during the Scanian War. The Danish-Norwegian fleet under Niels Juel decisively defeated the Swedish fleet under Henrik Horn, capturing or destroying several ships.

bokmal.s: Bokmål is the more widely used of the two official written standards of Norwegian, alongside Nynorsk. It descends from the Danish written language used in Norway during the union with Denmark, adapted to Norwegian speech through spelling reforms from 1907, and received its…

battle-of-dynekilen.s: The Battle of Dynekilen was fought on 8 July 1716 in a narrow fjord on the Swedish coast near the Norwegian border. A Danish-Norwegian squadron under Peter Tordenskjold attacked the Swedish transport fleet supplying Charles XII's invasion of Norway, capturing or destroying…

battle-of-poitiers-1356.s: The Battle of Poitiers was fought on 19 September 1356 near Poitiers in western France during the Hundred Years' War. An Anglo-Gascon army under Edward the Black Prince, returning from a raid across France, defeated a much larger French army and captured King John II.

bertrand-du-guesclin.s: Bertrand du Guesclin was a Breton knight who became constable of France in 1370 and the leading French commander of the Hundred Years' War under Charles V. Captured at Auray in 1364 and at Nájera in 1367, he helped place Henry of Trastámara on the throne of Castile in 1369.

bordelais.s: The Bordelais is the region around Bordeaux in south-western France, on the Garonne and Dordogne rivers and the Gironde estuary. Under English rule from 1152 to 1453 its wine was shipped in great quantities to England, and it remained the core of English Aquitaine to the end.

bad-reichenhall.s: Bad Reichenhall is a spa town in south-eastern Bavaria, near the Austrian border. Its brine springs were worked from prehistoric times, and in the Middle Ages its salt was a main source of wealth for the Bavarian dukes and the archbishops of Salzburg, carried along salt roads…

battle-of-baesweiler.s: The Battle of Baesweiler was fought on 22 August 1371 near Baesweiler, north-east of Aachen, between Duke Wenceslaus of Brabant and Duke William II of Jülich, allied with Edward of Guelders. Wenceslaus's army was defeated and he was captured, though Edward of Guelders was…

battle-of-ramillies.s: The Battle of Ramillies was fought on 23 May 1706 near the village of Ramillies in Brabant, in present-day Belgium, during the War of the Spanish Succession. An allied army under the Duke of Marlborough routed the French and Bavarian forces of Marshal Villeroi.

battle-of-scheut.s: The Battle of Scheut was fought on 17 August 1356 at Scheut, near Anderlecht west of Brussels, during the War of the Brabantine Succession. Louis of Male, Count of Flanders, defeated the army of Duchess Joanna and Duke Wenceslaus of Brabant and occupied Brussels and other towns.

bergen-op-zoom.s: Bergen op Zoom is a city in North Brabant, in the southern Netherlands, near the Scheldt estuary. In the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries its two annual fairs, together with those of Antwerp, formed the leading commercial market of the Low Countries.

battle-of-conquereuil.s: The Battle of Conquereuil was fought in 992 near Conquereuil in eastern Brittany, north of Nantes, between Conan I of Rennes, who claimed the rule of all Brittany, and Fulk Nerra, Count of Anjou, protector of the counts of Nantes. Conan was killed and his army defeated, which…
