battle-of-formigny.s: The Battle of Formigny was fought on 15 April 1450 in Normandy, near Bayeux, during the Hundred Years' War. A French army under the Count of Clermont, joined by Breton troops under Arthur de Richemont, destroyed an English relief force under Sir Thomas Kyriell.

bay-of-bourgneuf.s: The Bay of Bourgneuf is an inlet of the Atlantic on the west coast of France, south of the Loire estuary, between the Pays de Retz and the island of Noirmoutier. Its salt marshes produced large quantities of sea salt in the Middle Ages, and Hanseatic and Dutch fleets came each…

broceliande.s: Brocéliande is a legendary forest of Arthurian romance, first placed in Brittany by the poet Wace in the twelfth century. It is linked with the fountain of Barenton, the fairy Viviane and the enchanter Merlin.

battle-of-grandson.s: The Battle of Grandson was fought on 2 March 1476 near Grandson on Lake Neuchâtel, during the Burgundian Wars. Charles the Bold, who had just massacred the garrison of Grandson castle, was routed by the army of the Swiss Confederates, and his camp, with its artillery and rich…

battle-of-othee.s: The Battle of Othée was fought on 23 September 1408 near Othée, north-west of Liège. John the Fearless of Burgundy, with his brother-in-law William, Count of Hainaut, crushed the citizens of Liège, who had rebelled against their bishop-elect, John of Bavaria.

beaune.s: Beaune is a town in the Côte-d'Or department of Burgundy, eastern France, at the heart of the Côte d'Or wine country between Dijon and Chalon-sur-Saône. It was the seat of the ducal parlement in the Middle Ages and is known for the Hospices de Beaune, a hospital founded in…

bernard-of-clairvaux.s: Bernard of Clairvaux was a French Cistercian monk, born at Fontaine-lès-Dijon in 1090, who founded the abbey of Clairvaux in 1115 and became the most influential churchman of his age. He made the Cistercians one of Europe's largest orders, supported the Templars, helped settle…

battle-of-lodi.s: The Battle of Lodi was fought on 10 May 1796 at the bridge over the Adda at Lodi in Lombardy, when Napoleon Bonaparte's French army stormed the crossing against the rearguard of the retreating Austrian army. The victory opened the way to Milan, which Bonaparte entered on 15…

battle-of-maclodio.s: The Battle of Maclodio was fought in October 1427 near Brescia between the Venetian army under Francesco Bussone da Carmagnola and the forces of Filippo Maria Visconti, duke of Milan. Carmagnola, formerly Milan's leading captain, drew the Milanese into marshy ground and won a…

barfleur.s: Barfleur is a small port on the north-east coast of the Cotentin peninsula in Normandy. In the Middle Ages it was one of the main harbours for crossings between Normandy and England.

battle-of-bremule.s: The Battle of Brémule was fought on 20 August 1119 in the Norman Vexin between Henry I of England, duke of Normandy, and Louis VI of France, who supported the claim of William Clito, son of Robert Curthose. Henry's largely dismounted knights routed the French cavalry, and…

battle-of-mortemer.s: The Battle of Mortemer was fought in February 1054 in upper Normandy, when forces of Duke William of Normandy surprised and destroyed one of two French armies that King Henry I of France had sent to invade the duchy. The other army withdrew on hearing of the defeat.

battle-of-tinchebray.s: The Battle of Tinchebray was fought on 28 September 1106 in south-western Normandy between Henry I of England and his elder brother Robert Curthose, duke of Normandy. Henry won quickly and captured Robert, who spent the rest of his life in captivity.

battle-of-val-es-dunes.s: The Battle of Val-ès-Dunes was fought in 1047 near Caen, where the young Duke William of Normandy and his overlord King Henry I of France defeated a coalition of rebel barons from western Normandy led by Guy of Burgundy. It was William's first major victory and the beginning…

battle-of-varaville.s: The Battle of Varaville was fought in August 1057 near the mouth of the Dives in Normandy. Duke William attacked the invading army of Henry I of France and Geoffrey Martel of Anjou as it crossed the river, destroying the rearguard cut off by the rising tide.

bessin.s: The Bessin is a historical region of Normandy around Bayeux, between the Cotentin and the plain of Caen along the Channel coast. King Rudolph of West Francia granted it to the Normans in 924, and it became part of the duchy of Normandy.

barbara-sanseverino.s: Barbara Sanseverino, Countess of Sala, was an Italian noblewoman celebrated for her beauty and culture at the court of Parma, praised by poets including Torquato Tasso. Accused with members of the Sanvitale family and other nobles of conspiring against Duke Ranuccio I Farnese,…

busseto.s: Busseto is a small town in the province of Parma, Emilia-Romagna, on the Po plain. It was the seat of the Pallavicino family's small state before passing to the Farnese dukes of Parma in the sixteenth century.

barnim-i-duke-of-pomerania.s: Barnim I was duke of Pomerania of the Griffin dynasty from 1220 until 1278. He promoted German settlement and granted town law to many towns, including Szczecin in 1243, and in 1250 ceded the Uckermark to Brandenburg by the Treaty of Landin.

battle-of-verchen.s: The Battle of Verchen was fought on 6 July 1164 near Demmin in Pomerania, where an army of Henry the Lion, duke of Saxony, allied with Valdemar I of Denmark, defeated the Pomeranian dukes Bogislaw I and Casimir I and the Obotrite prince Pribislav. The defeat forced the…

basilica-of-superga.s: The Basilica of Superga is a baroque church on a hill east of Turin, designed by Filippo Juvarra and built in 1717–1731. Victor Amadeus II had vowed to build it during the French siege of Turin in 1706, and it became the burial place of the house of Savoy.

battle-of-saint-quentin-1557.s: The Battle of Saint-Quentin was fought on 10 August 1557 in Picardy, when a Spanish army under Emmanuel Philibert, duke of Savoy, serving Philip II of Spain, crushed a French relief force under Anne de Montmorency, who was captured. The town of Saint-Quentin fell later that…

battle-of-assietta.s: The Battle of the Assietta was fought on 19 July 1747 on the Assietta ridge in the Cottian Alps west of Turin. Piedmontese and Austrian troops of Charles Emmanuel III of Sardinia, entrenched on the heights, repulsed a much larger French army under the chevalier de Belle-Isle,…

bugey.s: The Bugey is a historical region in the Ain department of eastern France, between the Jura mountains and the Rhône, with Belley as its chief town. Long held by the counts and dukes of Savoy, it was ceded to France with Bresse and Gex by the Treaty of Lyon in 1601 in exchange…

battle-of-marsaglia.s: The Battle of Marsaglia was fought on 4 October 1693 in Piedmont, south-west of Turin, during the Nine Years' War. A French army under Marshal Catinat defeated the allied army of Victor Amadeus II of Savoy with Spanish and imperial troops.

battle-of-staffarda.s: The Battle of Staffarda was fought on 18 August 1690 near the abbey of Staffarda, south of Turin, during the Nine Years' War. A French army under Marshal Catinat defeated Duke Victor Amadeus II of Savoy and his Spanish allies, after the duke had joined the Grand Alliance…

battle-of-riade.s: The Battle of Riade was fought in March 933, probably near the Unstrut river in Thuringia, between King Henry the Fowler of East Francia and a Magyar raiding army. Henry had used a nine-year truce to build fortifications and train armoured cavalry, and when he refused further…

battle-of-welfesholz.s: The Battle of Welfesholz was fought on 11 February 1115 in the Mansfeld area of Saxony. Saxon princes led by Duke Lothair of Supplinburg defeated the army of Emperor Henry V, whose efforts to extend royal power and lands in Saxony had provoked revolt.

belitung.s: Belitung is an island in the Java Sea off the east coast of Sumatra, part of the Indonesian province of the Bangka Belitung Islands. Like neighbouring Bangka it is rich in tin, which a Dutch company mined from the 1850s, making it one of the colony's main sources of the metal.

boven-digoel.s: Boven-Digoel was an internment camp on the upper Digul River in southern New Guinea, set up by the Dutch colonial government in 1927 after the failed communist uprisings of 1926–1927. Isolated by jungle and swamp and rife with malaria, it held more than a thousand political…

budi-utomo.s: Budi Utomo was the first modern Indonesian political organisation, founded on 20 May 1908 in Batavia by students of the STOVIA medical school. Led mainly by Javanese aristocrats and officials, it promoted education and Javanese culture rather than independence, and it later…

bogor.s: Bogor is a city in West Java, Indonesia, about 60 kilometres south of Jakarta, known in the colonial period as Buitenzorg. From the eighteenth century the governors-general of the Dutch East Indies had a residence there, and the botanical garden founded beside the palace in…

bank-of-amsterdam.s: The Bank of Amsterdam (Wisselbank) was a public exchange bank founded by the city of Amsterdam in 1609. It accepted coins of many kinds and credited merchants with bank money of stable value, which they could transfer between accounts to settle bills of exchange.

battle-of-nieuwpoort.s: The Battle of Nieuwpoort was fought on 2 July 1600 on the beach and dunes near Nieuwpoort in Flanders, during the Eighty Years' War. Maurice of Nassau's Dutch army, marching on Dunkirk, defeated a Spanish army under Archduke Albert of Austria.

battle-of-the-downs.s: The Battle of the Downs was a naval battle fought on 21 October 1639 off the coast of Kent, during the Eighty Years' War. A Dutch fleet under Lieutenant-Admiral Maarten Tromp destroyed most of a large Spanish armada carrying troops to Flanders, which had sheltered in English…

beemster.s: The Beemster is a polder in North Holland, north of Amsterdam, created by draining a lake between 1609 and 1612 with dozens of windmills under the direction of Jan Leeghwater, with money from Amsterdam merchants. Its fields, roads and canals were laid out in a regular grid…

brielle.s: Brielle is a small fortified town in South Holland near the mouth of the Maas, known in English as Brill. On 1 April 1572 the Sea Beggars, Calvinist privateers recently expelled from English ports, captured it from the Spanish, giving the rebels their first foothold in the…

battle-of-jao-modo.s: The Battle of Jao Modo was fought in June 1696 near the Tuul River in present-day Mongolia, south-east of Ulaanbaatar. A Qing army under Fiyanggu, part of a great expedition led by the Kangxi Emperor, destroyed the forces of the Dzungar ruler Galdan Boshugtu Khan.

battle-of-hoton-nor.s: The Battle of Hoton Nor was fought in the summer of 1731 near the lake of that name in western Mongolia, between the Dzungar Khanate and the Qing dynasty. Dzungar forces sent by Galdan Tseren lured a Qing army under the general Furdan into an ambush and destroyed most of it,…

battle-of-ulan-butung.s: The Battle of Ulan Butung was fought in September 1690 a few hundred kilometres north of Beijing, between the Dzungar ruler Galdan Boshugtu Khan and a Qing army led by Prince Fuquan, the Kangxi Emperor's half-brother. Galdan's troops fought behind a line of kneeling camels…

bacharach.s: Bacharach is a small town on the left bank of the Rhine in Rhineland-Palatinate, Germany. In the Middle Ages it belonged to the counts palatine of the Rhine, who levied tolls on river traffic there, and it was a leading market for Rhine wine.

battle-of-seckenheim.s: The Battle of Seckenheim was fought on 30 June 1462 near Seckenheim, now part of Mannheim, during the Mainz Diocesan Feud. Elector Palatine Frederick I the Victorious defeated an allied army and captured its leaders, Margrave Charles I of Baden, Count Ulrich V of Württemberg…

bavarian-palatinate.s: The Bavarian Palatinate was the territory on the left bank of the Rhine that belonged to the Kingdom of Bavaria from 1816 to 1946, at first called the Rhine District. Formed from former lands of the Electoral Palatinate, the prince-bishopric of Speyer, Zweibrücken and other…

bibliotheca-palatina.s: The Bibliotheca Palatina was the library of the electors palatine at Heidelberg, housed in the Church of the Holy Spirit, and in the sixteenth century one of the finest collections of manuscripts and books in Europe. After Catholic League troops took Heidelberg in 1622 during…

battle-of-muhlberg.s: The Battle of Mühlberg was fought on 24 April 1547 near Mühlberg on the Elbe and decided the Schmalkaldic War. Emperor Charles V and the Duke of Alba crossed the river, surprised the Protestant army of Elector John Frederick I of Saxony and captured the elector.

battle-of-sievershausen.s: The Battle of Sievershausen was fought on 9 July 1553 near Lehrte in Lower Saxony between Elector Maurice of Saxony and Margrave Albert Alcibiades of Brandenburg-Kulmbach, whose plundering campaigns threatened the peace of the Empire. Maurice won, but he was mortally wounded…

battle-of-kesselsdorf.s: The Battle of Kesselsdorf was fought on 15 December 1745 west of Dresden, in the Second Silesian War. A Prussian army under Leopold I of Anhalt-Dessau defeated a Saxon army supported by Austrian troops, and Dresden was occupied soon after.

banu-qasi.s: The Banu Qasi were a Muslim dynasty of Hispano-Roman or Visigothic origin who ruled much of the upper Ebro valley from the eighth to the early tenth century, descended according to tradition from a count Cassius who converted to Islam after the Arab conquest. Based at Tudela,…

battle-of-musara.s: The Battle of Musara was fought in May 756 on the banks of the Guadalquivir near Córdoba. Abd al-Rahman, an Umayyad prince who had escaped the Abbasid massacre of his family, defeated the governor of al-Andalus, Yusuf al-Fihri, and his ally al-Sumayl, then entered Córdoba and…

battle-of-tablada.s: The Battle of Tablada was fought in November 844 near Seville, where the army of the Umayyad emir Abd al-Rahman II defeated Viking raiders who had sacked the city. Many of the Northmen were killed or captured and the survivors withdrew to their ships.

battle-of-la-higueruela.s: The Battle of La Higueruela was fought on 1 July 1431 outside Granada between the army of John II of Castile, led by Álvaro de Luna, and the forces of the Nasrid emir Muhammad IX. The Castilians won but did not attack the city; instead they backed a rival claimant, Yusuf IV,…

battle-of-lucena.s: The Battle of Lucena was fought in April 1483 near Lucena in the kingdom of Córdoba, during the Granada War. The Nasrid emir Muhammad XII, known as Boabdil, attacked the town but was defeated and captured by Castilian forces.

biblioteca-marciana.s: The Biblioteca Marciana (Library of St Mark) in Venice is one of the oldest public libraries in Italy and holds one of the world's finest collections of Greek manuscripts. It was founded on Cardinal Bessarion's gift of his library to the Republic of Venice in 1468.

battle-of-iwo-jima.s: The Battle of Iwo Jima was fought from 19 February to 26 March 1945, when United States Marines captured the volcanic island of Iwo Jima from Japan in the Pacific War. The Japanese garrison of about 21,000 under General Kuribayashi Tadamichi fought from tunnels and almost all…

battle-of-notium.s: The Battle of Notium was a naval battle of 406 BCE near Notium, the port of Colophon, close to Ephesus, in the Peloponnesian War. The Spartan admiral Lysander defeated an Athenian squadron left under the helmsman Antiochus, who disobeyed the orders of the absent Alcibiades.

battle-of-chalchuapa.s: The Battle of Chalchuapa was fought on 2 April 1885 near the town of Chalchuapa in western El Salvador. The Guatemalan president Justo Rufino Barrios, who had proclaimed the union of Central America and invaded El Salvador to impose it by force, was killed in the fighting.

battle-of-gualcho.s: The Battle of Gualcho was fought in July 1828 in El Salvador during the civil war that divided the Federal Republic of Central America. The Honduran liberal Francisco Morazán defeated the federal forces backed by the Guatemalan conservatives, strengthening the liberal alliance.

battle-of-la-trinidad.s: The Battle of La Trinidad was fought on 11 November 1827 in Honduras during the civil war of the Federal Republic of Central America. Francisco Morazán's liberal forces defeated the federal troops under Justo Milla, who had deposed the Honduran head of state on behalf of…

battle-of-achelous.s: The Battle of Achelous was fought on 20 August 917 by the river Achelous, near Anchialus on the Black Sea coast of present-day Bulgaria. Tsar Simeon I of Bulgaria destroyed a large Byzantine army under Leo Phokas, one of the heaviest defeats in Byzantine history.

battle-of-anchialus-763.s: The Battle of Anchialus was fought on 30 June 763 near Anchialus on the Black Sea coast. The Byzantine emperor Constantine V defeated the Bulgarian khan Telets, one of the greatest victories of his long campaigns against Bulgaria.

battle-of-markellai.s: The Battle of Markellai was fought in 792 near the fortress of Markellai, close to present-day Karnobat in Bulgaria. Khan Kardam defeated the Byzantine emperor Constantine VI, who fled the field, and Byzantium was forced to resume paying tribute to Bulgaria.

battle-of-versinikia.s: The Battle of Versinikia was fought on 22 June 813 near Versinikia, not far from Adrianople in Thrace. Khan Krum routed the Byzantine army of Emperor Michael I Rangabe, whose defeat led to his overthrow in favour of Leo V the Armenian.

battle-of-bulgarophygon.s: The Battle of Bulgarophygon was fought in 896 near the town of that name in eastern Thrace, now Babaeski in Turkey. Simeon I of Bulgaria destroyed a Byzantine army after his Pecheneg allies had driven Byzantium's allies, the Magyars, from their lands north of the Danube.

battle-of-katasyrtai.s: The Battle of Katasyrtai was fought in 917 near Constantinople, shortly after Simeon I's victory at Achelous. The Bulgarian army defeated a Byzantine force under Leo Phokas in a night attack.

battle-of-the-spercheios.s: The Battle of the Spercheios was fought in 997 on the river Spercheios in central Greece. The Byzantine general Nikephoros Ouranos surprised the army of Tsar Samuel of Bulgaria, returning from a raid into southern Greece, and destroyed it; Samuel and his son Gavril Radomir…

bogomilism.s: Bogomilism was a dualist religious movement founded in Bulgaria in the 10th century, during the reign of Tsar Peter I, by a priest named Bogomil. Its followers rejected the church hierarchy, the sacraments and the material world, which they held to be the work of an evil…

boris-ii-of-bulgaria.s: Boris II (c. 931–977) was tsar of Bulgaria from 969 to 971, succeeding his father Peter I during the invasion of Sviatoslav of Kiev. When John I Tzimiskes captured Preslav in 971, Boris was taken to Constantinople, where he was stripped of his regalia, and eastern Bulgaria was…

battle-of-the-frigidus.s: The Battle of the Frigidus was fought on 5–6 September 394 by the river Frigidus, probably the Vipava in present-day Slovenia. The eastern emperor Theodosius I defeated the western usurper Eugenius and his Frankish general Arbogast, helped by a strong wind, the bora, blowing…

battle-of-vouille.s: The Battle of Vouillé was fought in 507 near Poitiers, in western France. Clovis I and his Franks defeated the Visigoths, whose king Alaric II was killed, according to Gregory of Tours by Clovis himself.

belgica-secunda.s: Belgica Secunda was a late Roman province in north-eastern Gaul, formed by the division of Gallia Belgica around 300, with its capital at Reims. It covered much of present-day northern France and western Belgium, including Tournai, Cambrai and Soissons.

battle-of-vicus-helena.s: The Battle of Vicus Helena was fought in the 440s, probably around 448, at an unidentified place in Artois in northern Gaul. The Roman general Aetius and the future emperor Majorian surprised the Salian Franks of King Chlodio during a wedding celebration and defeated them.

bismarck-battleship.s: Bismarck was a German battleship built by Blohm & Voss at Hamburg, launched in 1939 and commissioned in 1940. On her only operation, in May 1941, she sank the British battlecruiser Hood in the Denmark Strait.

blohm-voss.s: Blohm & Voss is a shipbuilding company founded in Hamburg in 1877 by Hermann Blohm and Ernst Voss. It built liners and warships and, in the Second World War, the battleship Bismarck and many U-boats, as well as aircraft through a subsidiary.

bouches-de-l-elbe.s: Bouches-de-l'Elbe was a department of the French Empire created in 1811, when Napoleon annexed the north German coast to enforce his blockade of British trade. Named after the mouths of the Elbe, it had Hamburg as its capital and also included Lübeck and neighbouring lands.

bremer-vulkan.s: Bremer Vulkan was a shipbuilding company founded in 1893 at Vegesack, then a town near Bremen. It built merchant ships and, in both world wars, warships and U-boats, and after 1945 grew into a large shipbuilding group.

blue-riband.s: The Blue Riband is an unofficial honour given to the passenger liner making the fastest regular crossing of the Atlantic. Held by British ships for much of the 19th century, it was won by Norddeutscher Lloyd's Kaiser Wilhelm der Grosse in 1897 and by its liner Bremen in 1929.

bouches-du-weser.s: Bouches-du-Weser was a department of the French Empire created in 1811, when Napoleon annexed the north German coast to enforce his blockade of British trade. Named after the mouths of the Weser, it had Bremen as its capital.

bremen-verden.s: Bremen-Verden was the territory formed from the secularised prince-archbishopric of Bremen and prince-bishopric of Verden, granted to Sweden by the Peace of Westphalia in 1648. Sweden claimed the city of Bremen as part of it and attacked it in 1654 and 1666.

bremen-ratskeller.s: The Bremen Ratskeller is the wine cellar beneath the town hall of Bremen, in use since the early 15th century. It holds one of the largest collections of German wines and keeps what is reputed to be the oldest cask wine in Germany, a Rüdesheim wine from 1653.

battle-of-algiers.s: The Battle of Algiers was the campaign of 1956–1957 in which the FLN waged a bombing and assassination offensive in Algiers and French paratroopers under General Jacques Massu broke its network in the city. Massu's troops relied on mass arrests and the systematic use of…

blida.s: Blida is a city in northern Algeria at the foot of the Tell Atlas, south-west of Algiers, on the edge of the Mitidja plain. Founded in the 16th century, it was occupied by the French during the conquest of Algeria in the 1830s and grew into a garrison and market town.

blum-viollette-proposal.s: The Blum–Viollette proposal was a bill of 1936 put forward by the Popular Front government of Léon Blum and Maurice Viollette, a former governor-general of Algeria, to give French citizenship to a small elite of Algerian Muslims without requiring them to give up Muslim…

berber-languages.s: The Berber languages, also called Tamazight, are a branch of the Afroasiatic family spoken by the Amazigh peoples of North Africa, from Morocco and Algeria to Libya, Egypt's Siwa Oasis and the Tuareg regions of the Sahara and Sahel. They have their own ancient script, Tifinagh.

bank-of-indochina.s: The Bank of Indochina was a private French bank founded in Paris in 1875 that held the privilege of issuing the currency of French Indochina, the piastre. It financed trade, plantations, mines and public works across Indochina and expanded into China and the Pacific, becoming…

battle-of-ko-chang.s: The Battle of Ko Chang was a naval engagement fought on 17 January 1941 off the island of Ko Chang in the Gulf of Thailand, during the Franco-Thai War. A French squadron led by the light cruiser Lamotte-Picquet surprised the Thai fleet at anchor and sank or disabled several…

battle-of-route-coloniale-4.s: The Battle of Route Coloniale 4 was a series of engagements in September and October 1950 along the road linking French frontier posts near the Chinese border in northern Vietnam. Viet Minh forces under Vo Nguyen Giap, newly supplied by communist China, destroyed French…

badi-ii-abu-diqn.s: Badi II Abu Diqn was a sultan of the Funj Sultanate of Sennar who reigned from 1644 to 1681. He campaigned against the Shilluk on the White Nile and the hill kingdom of Taqali in the Nuba Mountains, and settled captives taken there around the capital, founding a slave army…

badi-iv.s: Badi IV, called Abu Shulukh, was the last Funj sultan of Sennar to hold real power, reigning from 1724 to 1762. His forces defeated an Ethiopian invasion under Iyasu II in 1744, but his reliance on new favourites alienated the nobility.

bu-njem.s: Bu Njem, ancient Gholaia, is the site of a Roman fort in the Libyan desert south-east of Tripoli, built in 201 CE by a detachment of the Third Augustan Legion under Septimius Severus to control routes to the Fezzan and the Garamantes. Excavations have revealed the fort, baths…

bundesrat-germany.s: The Bundesrat is the federal council of the Federal Republic of Germany, established under the Basic Law of 1949, through which the governments of the sixteen states, or Länder, take part in federal legislation. Its members are delegates of the state governments, with votes…

battle-of-jutland.s: The Battle of Jutland, fought on 31 May and 1 June 1916 in the North Sea off Denmark, was the largest naval battle of the First World War, between the British Grand Fleet and the German High Seas Fleet. Britain lost more ships and men, but the German fleet returned to port and…

battle-of-andkhud.s: The Battle of Andkhud was fought in 1204 near Andkhoy in northern Afghanistan, where an army of the Khwarazmshah Muhammad II, reinforced by the Qara Khitai, crushed the Ghurid sultan Mu'izz al-Din Muhammad, who escaped with difficulty. The defeat ended Ghurid expansion into…

bahram-shah-of-ghazna.s: Bahram Shah was a sultan of the Ghaznavid dynasty who reigned from 1117 to 1157, having taken the throne with Seljuk help as a vassal of Sultan Sanjar. His court at Ghazni patronised the poet Sana'i.

battle-of-kasahrada.s: The Battle of Kasahrada was fought in 1178 near Mount Abu in present-day Rajasthan, where the Chaulukya army of Gujarat, led in the name of the young king Mularaja II, defeated the Ghurid sultan Mu'izz al-Din Muhammad. It was his first major defeat in India and turned Ghurid…

battle-of-the-vorskla-river.s: The Battle of the Vorskla River was fought on 12 August 1399 on the Vorskla, a tributary of the Dnieper in modern Ukraine. The Golden Horde army of the emir Edigu and Khan Temür Qutlugh crushed Grand Duke Vytautas of Lithuania, his Polish and Teutonic allies and the exiled…

berdibeg.s: Berdibeg was khan of the Golden Horde from 1357 to 1359. He seized the throne after the death of his father Jani Beg, whom he is said to have murdered, and killed many of his brothers to secure his position.

battle-of-the-kondurcha-river.s: The Battle of the Kondurcha River was fought on 18 June 1391 near the Kondurcha, a tributary of the Volga basin east of modern Samara. Timur, after a long march across the steppe, defeated the army of Tokhtamysh, khan of the Golden Horde and his former protégé.

battle-of-mohi.s: The Battle of Mohi was fought on 11 April 1241 at the Sajó River in north-eastern Hungary. Mongol armies under Batu and Subutai surrounded and destroyed the army of King Béla IV of Hungary, who barely escaped.

byeolmuban.s: The Byeolmuban was a special army of the Korean kingdom of Goryeo, created in 1104 on the advice of Yun Gwan after defeats by the Jurchen. It combined cavalry, infantry and a corps of Buddhist monks and drew recruits from all classes.

byeongnando.s: Byeongnando was the main international port of the Korean kingdom of Goryeo, on the Yeseong River near the capital Kaegyong (modern Kaesong). Song Chinese, Japanese, Khitan and Jurchen merchants traded there, and in the eleventh century Arab merchants also arrived, through…

battle-of-jinpo.s: The Battle of Jinpo was fought in 1380 at the mouth of the Geum River on the west coast of Korea. A Goryeo fleet whose ships carried cannon developed by Choe Mu-seon destroyed a large fleet of Japanese pirates.

bibliotheque-nationale-de-france.s: The Bibliothèque nationale de France is the national library of France in Paris, which grew from the royal library of the French kings. It holds one of the world's largest collections of books, manuscripts, maps, coins and prints.

battle-of-bombona.s: The Battle of Bomboná was fought on 7 April 1822 near Pasto in southern New Granada between Simón Bolívar's army and royalist forces under Colonel Basilio García. Bolívar's troops held the field after costly frontal attacks, and the royalists withdrew.

battle-of-junin.s: The Battle of Junín was a cavalry battle fought on 6 August 1824 on the high plain of Junín in the central Andes of Peru. The patriot horsemen of Simón Bolívar's Colombian and Peruvian army, fighting with lances and sabres, routed the royalist cavalry of José de Canterac.

battle-of-lake-maracaibo.s: The Battle of Lake Maracaibo was a naval battle fought on 24 July 1823 on Lake Maracaibo in western Venezuela. The Gran Colombian squadron of Admiral José Prudencio Padilla defeated the Spanish flotilla of Ángel Laborde.

battle-of-tarqui.s: The Battle of Tarqui was fought on 27 February 1829 at Portete de Tarqui near Cuenca in modern Ecuador. Gran Colombian forces under Antonio José de Sucre and Juan José Flores defeated the Peruvian army of President José de La Mar.

battenberg-family.s: The Battenberg family was a morganatic branch of the grand ducal house of Hesse, founded when Prince Alexander of Hesse married Countess Julia Hauke, who was created Princess of Battenberg in 1858. Their sons included Alexander, the first prince of Bulgaria, and Louis, First…

battle-of-gravelotte.s: The Battle of Gravelotte, also called Gravelotte–St. Privat, was fought on 18 August 1870 west of Metz and was the largest battle of the Franco-Prussian War. German armies under Helmuth von Moltke, including a Hessian division, suffered heavy losses but forced Marshal…

battle-of-laufach.s: The Battle of Laufach was fought on 13 July 1866 at Laufach and Frohnhofen in the Spessart hills of Lower Franconia during the Main campaign of the Austro-Prussian War. Prussian troops under August von Goeben defeated the division of the Grand Duchy of Hesse, part of the…

battle-of-orsha.s: The Battle of Orsha was fought on 8 September 1514 on the Dnieper near Orsha in modern Belarus. A Polish-Lithuanian army under Hetman Konstanty Ostrogski defeated a larger Muscovite army, shortly after Vasily III had captured Smolensk.

battle-of-vedrosha.s: The Battle of Vedrosha was fought on 14 July 1500 on the Vedrosha River near Dorogobuzh in western Russia. The Muscovite army of Ivan III defeated the Lithuanian army of Grand Duke Alexander, and its commander Konstanty Ostrogski was captured.

braclaw-voivodeship.s: The Bracław Voivodeship was a province of the Grand Duchy of Lithuania and, from 1569, of the Crown of Poland, in eastern Podolia in modern Ukraine. Its seat was the town of Bracław (Bratslav) on the Southern Bug.

battle-of-the-bulge.s: The Battle of the Bulge was the last major German offensive on the Western Front in the Second World War, launched on 16 December 1944 through the Ardennes in Belgium and Luxembourg. German armies drove a bulge into the American lines but failed to reach Antwerp, were held at…

belgium-luxembourg-economic-union.s: The Belgium–Luxembourg Economic Union is a customs and monetary union created by a treaty signed in 1921, after Luxembourg had left the German Zollverein. It abolished customs barriers between the two countries and tied the Luxembourg franc to the Belgian franc, an arrangement…

belsky-family.s: The Belskys were a princely family descended from Algirdas, Grand Duke of Lithuania, through his son Vladimir, and named after their appanage of Bely. Prince Fyodor Belsky fled from Lithuania to Moscow in 1482 and married a niece of Ivan III, giving the family high rank among…

battle-of-marciano.s: The Battle of Marciano, also called Scannagallo, was fought on 2 August 1554 in the Valdichiana between the forces of Cosimo I de' Medici and the Emperor Charles V and a Franco-Sienese army under Piero Strozzi. Strozzi's defeat left Siena isolated, and after a long siege the…

bernardo-buontalenti.s: Bernardo Buontalenti was a Florentine architect, engineer, stage designer and artist in the service of the Medici grand dukes. He designed the Forte di Belvedere and the Medici villa at Pratolino, completed the Uffizi with its Tribuna, built the Grotta Grande in the Boboli…

boboli-gardens.s: The Boboli Gardens are the park behind the Pitti Palace in Florence, laid out for Cosimo I de' Medici and Eleonora of Toledo from about 1550 to designs by Niccolò Tribolo and later extended. With their terraces, avenues, grottoes, fountains and statues, they became a model for…

battle-of-curtatone-and-montanara.s: The Battle of Curtatone and Montanara was fought on 29 May 1848 near Mantua, during the First Italian War of Independence. About 5,000 Tuscan and Neapolitan troops, including volunteer battalions of students and professors from Pisa and Siena, held off a much larger Austrian…

bateshwar-hindu-temples.s: The Bateshwar Hindu temples are a group of about 200 sandstone temples dedicated to Shiva and Vishnu near Morena in Madhya Pradesh, built mainly between the eighth and tenth centuries CE under the Gurjara-Pratiharas. Abandoned and largely collapsed, perhaps through…

battle-of-zenta.s: The Battle of Zenta was fought on 11 September 1697 at Zenta, modern Senta in Serbia, on the Tisza River. Prince Eugene of Savoy surprised the Ottoman army of Sultan Mustafa II while it was crossing the river and destroyed it, killing tens of thousands, including the grand…

belvedere-vienna.s: The Belvedere is a Baroque palace complex in Vienna built for Prince Eugene of Savoy by Johann Lukas von Hildebrandt, with the Lower Belvedere completed in 1716 and the Upper Belvedere in 1723. Its two palaces, linked by terraced gardens, are among the masterpieces of Viennese…

battle-of-hohenlinden.s: The Battle of Hohenlinden was fought on 3 December 1800 in Bavaria, east of Munich, between a French army under Jean Moreau and an Austrian and Bavarian army under Archduke John. Moreau's divisions caught the Austrians strung out in the forest and routed them, taking many…

battle-of-kolin.s: The Battle of Kolín was fought on 18 June 1757 in Bohemia, east of Prague, during the Seven Years' War. An Austrian army under Field Marshal Leopold Joseph von Daun defeated Frederick II of Prussia, his first major defeat, forcing him to raise the siege of Prague and withdraw…

battle-of-petrovaradin.s: The Battle of Petrovaradin was fought on 5 August 1716 at the fortress of Peterwardein, now part of Novi Sad in Serbia, at the start of the Austro-Turkish War of 1716–1718. Prince Eugene of Savoy defeated a much larger Ottoman army under the grand vizier Silahdar Ali Pasha,…

battle-of-wagram.s: The Battle of Wagram was fought on 5–6 July 1809 on the Marchfeld plain north-east of Vienna between Napoleon and the Austrian army of Archduke Charles. After crossing the Danube, the French won in two days of fighting, one of the largest battles in Europe up to that time,…

bartolome-esteban-murillo.s: Bartolomé Esteban Murillo was a Spanish Baroque painter from Seville, where he spent almost his entire career. He was celebrated for gentle religious paintings, especially of the Immaculate Conception, and for scenes of street children, and in 1660 he helped found an academy…

battle-of-gravelines-1558.s: The Battle of Gravelines was fought on 13 July 1558 near Gravelines on the coast of Flanders. A Spanish army under Lamoral, Count of Egmont, supported by fire from English ships, destroyed a French force under Marshal de Termes that had raided Dunkirk.

battle-of-tabkin-kwotto.s: The Battle of Tabkin Kwotto, fought in June 1804, was the first major victory of the followers of Usman dan Fodio over the army of Yunfa, ruler of Gobir. Fought near a lake in north-western Hausaland, it was won by a small force against a larger Gobir army and became…

book-of-the-himyarites.s: The Book of the Himyarites is a Syriac Christian work of the 6th century that recounts the persecution of the Christians of Najran under the Himyarite king Yusuf, known as Dhu Nuwas, and the Aksumite invasion of Yemen that followed. It survives only in fragments of a single…

battle-of-kharda.s: The Battle of Kharda was fought in March 1795 near Kharda in the Deccan between the Maratha Confederacy and the army of Nizam Ali Khan of Hyderabad. The Marathas, united for the last time under the Peshwa's minister Nana Phadnavis, won decisively, and the Nizam had to cede…

battle-of-palkhed.s: The Battle of Palkhed was fought in February 1728 near Aurangabad between the Maratha Peshwa Baji Rao I and Nizam-ul-Mulk of Hyderabad. By rapid cavalry manoeuvres Baji Rao cut off the Nizam's army from its supplies and forced him to come to terms.

battle-of-rakshasbhuvan.s: The Battle of Rakshasbhuvan was fought in August 1763 on the Godavari between the Marathas under the young Peshwa Madhavrao I and the army of Nizam Ali Khan of Hyderabad. The Nizam had tried to exploit Maratha losses at Panipat in 1761, but his defeat restored Maratha power in…

battle-of-udgir.s: The Battle of Udgir was fought in early 1760 in the Deccan between the Marathas under Sadashivrao Bhau and the army of the Nizam of Hyderabad. The Marathas won decisively, and the Nizam ceded large territories, including Ahmednagar, Daulatabad and Bijapur.

bandung-conference.s: The Asian–African Conference, or Bandung Conference, was a meeting of 29 newly independent and emerging states of Asia and Africa held at Bandung, Indonesia, in April 1955. Hosted by President Sukarno and attended by leaders such as Nehru, Zhou Enlai and Nasser, it condemned…

battle-of-surabaya.s: The Battle of Surabaya was fought in October and November 1945 in the East Javanese port of Surabaya between Indonesian nationalist fighters and British and British Indian troops sent to accept the Japanese surrender. After the British brigadier A. W. S. Mallaby was killed,…

b-j-habibie.s: B. J. Habibie was an Indonesian aeronautical engineer and politician who served as the country's third president from May 1998 to October 1999. Trained in Germany, he became Suharto's minister of research and technology and his vice-president, and succeeded him when Suharto…

battle-of-lake-george.s: The Battle of Lake George was fought on 8 September 1755 at the southern end of Lake George in the colony of New York, early in the French and Indian War. British colonial troops under William Johnson and Mohawk warriors under Hendrick Theyanoguin, who was killed, repulsed an…

battle-of-caishi.s: The Battle of Caishi was fought in November 1161 on the Yangtze River near Caishi, in present-day Anhui, between the Southern Song and the Jurchen Jin. The Jin emperor Wanyan Liang, Prince Hailing, tried to cross the river with a large army, but Song warships, including…

battle-of-sanfengshan.s: The Battle of Sanfengshan was fought in February 1232 in Henan, China, between the Mongols under Tolui and the main field army of the Jin dynasty. Caught in snow and cold after a long pursuit, the Jin army was destroyed and its commanders killed or captured.

battle-of-yehuling.s: The Battle of Yehuling, or Badger Mouth, was fought in 1211 at a mountain pass north-west of present-day Zhangjiakou in Hebei, China, during Genghis Khan's first invasion of the Jin dynasty. The Mongols destroyed a much larger Jin army, killing a great part of it and opening…

bugis.s: The Bugis are a people of South Sulawesi in Indonesia, known for their seafaring and trade and for their epic La Galigo, written in their own Lontara script. Their kingdoms included Bone, Wajo and Soppeng.

bemoim.s: Bemoim was a prince of the Jolof Empire in present-day Senegal who ruled for a time before being driven out in a succession struggle. In 1488 he went to Portugal to seek help from King João II, was baptised with the king as his godfather and took the name João.

battle-of-hansan-island.s: The Battle of Hansan Island was fought on 14 August 1592 off the south coast of Korea during the Japanese invasion of Joseon. Admiral Yi Sun-sin lured a Japanese fleet under Wakisaka Yasuharu into open water near Hansan Island and encircled it in a crane-wing formation,…

battle-of-noryang.s: The Battle of Noryang was the last major battle of the Japanese invasions of Korea, fought on 16 December 1598 in the Noryang Strait off the south coast. A combined Korean and Ming Chinese fleet under Yi Sun-sin and Chen Lin attacked Japanese ships gathering to withdraw after…

battle-of-myeongnyang.s: The Battle of Myeongnyang was fought on 26 October 1597 in the Myeongnyang Strait off the south-western tip of Korea during the second Japanese invasion. With only thirteen warships left after an earlier Korean defeat, Admiral Yi Sun-sin used the narrow strait and its strong…

burana-tower.s: The Burana Tower is a brick minaret in the Chuy Valley near Tokmok in northern Kyrgyzstan, built in the eleventh century under the Kara-Khanids. It stands on the site of a medieval town usually identified with Balasagun, one of the dynasty's capitals.

battle-of-anyrakai.s: The Battle of Anyrakai was fought around 1729–1730 in the Anyrakai Mountains of south-eastern Kazakhstan, near Lake Balkhash, between the Kazakhs and the Dzungars. The combined forces of the three Kazakh juzes under Abulkhair Khan and batyrs such as Kabanbai and Bogenbai won a…

battle-of-orbulaq.s: The Battle of Orbulaq was fought in 1643 in the mountains of Zhetysu in south-eastern Kazakhstan between the Kazakhs under Jahangir Khan and the Dzungars under Erdeni Batur. According to accounts, Jahangir, with a small force of musketeers in entrenchments in a mountain pass,…

bogenbai-batyr.s: Bogenbai Batyr was a Kazakh military leader of the Middle Juz and one of the best-known commanders in the eighteenth-century wars against the Dzungars. With other batyrs such as Kabanbai, he led Kazakh forces in the victories of Bulanty and Anyrakai around 1727–1730, which…

bukhar-zhyrau.s: Bukhar Zhyrau was a Kazakh poet and adviser of the eighteenth century, the most famous of the zhyrau, poet-counsellors who advised rulers in verse. He served Abylai Khan and urged unity among the Kazakhs against the Dzungars and caution towards Russia and China.

battle-of-bulanty.s: The Battle of Bulanty was a victory of the united forces of the three Kazakh juzes over the Dzungars near the Bulanty River, in what is now central Kazakhstan, around 1727–1728. Coming a few years after the disastrous Dzungar invasion of 1723, it was the first major Kazakh…

burunduk-khan.s: Burunduk Khan was a khan of the Kazakhs and a son of Kerei, one of the two founders of the Kazakh Khanate. Ruling from about 1480, he led long wars against Muhammad Shaybani and his Uzbeks for the towns of the middle Syr Darya, among them Sauran, Sygnak and Turkistan.

battle-of-marj-ardabil.s: The Battle of Marj Ardabil was fought in December 730 near Ardabil, in north-western Iran, between a Khazar army and the forces of the Umayyad Caliphate. The Khazars destroyed the Arab army and killed its commander, al-Jarrah ibn Abdallah al-Hakami, and then raided deep into…

bayon.s: The Bayon is a Buddhist temple at the centre of Angkor Thom in Cambodia, built as the state temple of Jayavarman VII in the late twelfth and early thirteenth centuries. Its towers carry some two hundred huge serene stone faces, and its bas-reliefs show battles against the Cham…

banyoro.s: The Banyoro are a Bantu-speaking people of western Uganda, east of Lake Albert, whose language is Runyoro. They are the people of the kingdom of Bunyoro-Kitara, which under its Babito kings was the strongest state of the Great Lakes region from the sixteenth to the eighteenth…

battle-of-alcoraz.s: The Battle of Alcoraz was fought in November 1096 near Huesca, where Peter I of Aragon and Navarre defeated the army of the taifa of Zaragoza, which had Castilian support. Huesca surrendered shortly afterwards and became a royal seat of the kingdom.

battle-of-cutanda.s: The Battle of Cutanda was fought in June 1120 near Calamocha in Aragon, where Alfonso I of Aragon, aided by southern French lords, defeated an Almoravid army sent to recover Zaragoza. The victory secured his conquest of the Ebro valley and opened the way to the capture of…

battle-of-fraga.s: The Battle of Fraga was fought in July 1134 when an Almoravid relief army defeated Alfonso I of Aragon, who was besieging the town of Fraga on the Cinca. Alfonso escaped but died a few weeks later, leaving his kingdom by will to the military orders.

battle-of-graus.s: The Battle of Graus was fought in 1063 at Graus, in the Pyrenean foothills of Aragon, where Ramiro I of Aragon was killed attacking the town, held by the taifa of Zaragoza. The ruler of Zaragoza, al-Muqtadir, was supported by a Castilian force, which according to tradition…

battle-of-clavijo.s: The Battle of Clavijo is a legendary battle said to have been fought in 844 near Clavijo in La Rioja, in which Ramiro I of Asturias defeated a Muslim army with the help of Saint James, who appeared on a white horse. The story, first recorded in the twelfth century, supported…

beatus-of-liebana.s: Beatus of Liébana was a monk of the monastery of Santo Toribio de Liébana in Cantabria. Around 776 he wrote a Commentary on the Apocalypse, and with Bishop Etherius of Osma he attacked the Adoptionist teaching of Elipandus of Toledo.

battle-of-lutos.s: The Battle of Lutos was fought in 794 in Asturias, when Alfonso II ambushed a Muslim army of the emir Hisham I returning from a campaign that had sacked Oviedo. The Asturian victory, at a place usually identified near Grado, was one of the few successes of the kingdom against…

battle-of-polvoraria.s: The Battle of Polvoraria was fought in 878 near the confluence of the Órbigo and Esla rivers in León, where the forces of Alfonso III of Asturias defeated an army of the emir Muhammad I of Córdoba. Together with the capture of Coimbra the same year, the victory strengthened…

battle-of-hanau.s: The Battle of Hanau was fought on 30–31 October 1813 near Hanau in Hesse, where an Austro-Bavarian army under Karl Philipp von Wrede tried to cut off Napoleon's retreat to France after his defeat at Leipzig. Napoleon broke through and reached the Rhine.

bavarian-alps.s: The Bavarian Alps are the part of the Northern Limestone Alps along Bavaria's border with Austria, including the Zugspitze, at 2,962 metres the highest mountain in Germany. Resorts such as Garmisch-Partenkirchen and Berchtesgaden lie among them, as do Ludwig II's castles of…

battle-of-kissingen.s: The Battle of Kissingen was fought on 10 July 1866 at Bad Kissingen in Lower Franconia during the Austro-Prussian War. The Prussian Army of the Main defeated the Bavarian army, which was fighting on Austria's side, and forced it back across the Franconian Saale.

baudouin-of-belgium.s: Baudouin was King of the Belgians from 1951 to 1993, succeeding his father Leopold III, who abdicated after the Royal Question. His reign saw the independence of the Belgian Congo in 1960 and the transformation of Belgium into a federal state.

brussels-capital-region.s: The Brussels-Capital Region is one of the three regions of federal Belgium, together with Flanders and Wallonia. Planned in the state reform of 1970 but only set up with its own parliament and government in 1989, it comprises the City of Brussels and eighteen other…

battle-of-saio.s: The Battle of Saïo was fought in south-western Ethiopia in June and July 1941, during the East African campaign of the Second World War. Troops of the Force Publique of the Belgian Congo, under General Auguste-Éduard Gilliaert, attacked the Italian positions, and on 6 July…

battle-of-lipany.s: The Battle of Lipany was fought east of Prague on 30 May 1434 near the end of the Hussite Wars. An alliance of moderate Utraquists and Catholics defeated the radical Taborite and Orphan field armies, and their leader Prokop the Great was killed.

battle-of-domazlice.s: The Battle of Domažlice was fought in western Bohemia on 14 August 1431, when the fifth crusade against the Hussites, led by Frederick of Brandenburg and the papal legate Cardinal Giuliano Cesarini, broke up in panic as the Hussite armies under Prokop the Great approached. Its…

battle-of-kressenbrunn.s: The Battle of Kressenbrunn was fought in July 1260 on the March River east of Vienna, between Ottokar II of Bohemia and Béla IV of Hungary. It was part of their struggle for the inheritance of the extinct Babenberg dukes of Austria and Styria.

battle-of-vitkov-hill.s: The Battle of Vítkov Hill was fought on 14 July 1420 on a hill on the eastern edge of Prague. Hussite forces under Jan Žižka repulsed an assault by the army of the first crusade against the Hussites, led by Emperor Sigismund, who lifted the siege of Prague soon afterwards.

battle-of-mengo.s: The Battle of Mengo was fought in Kampala on 24 January 1892 between the Protestant and Catholic factions of Buganda. Frederick Lugard of the Imperial British East Africa Company supported the Protestants, and his Maxim gun helped decide the fighting.

buddu.s: Buddu was a county, or saza, of the Kingdom of Buganda on the western shore of Lake Victoria, around present-day Masaka in Uganda. It was taken from Bunyoro by the kabakas in the late eighteenth century, giving Buganda access to the iron and bark-cloth production and trade of…

busiro.s: Busiro is one of the original core counties of the Kingdom of Buganda, lying west of Kampala along the shore of Lake Victoria in present-day Wakiso District of Uganda. Its name refers to the royal tombs: many early kabakas were buried there, and their shrines were maintained…

butambala.s: Butambala is a county of the Kingdom of Buganda in central Uganda, west of Kampala. Absorbed by Buganda during its expansion from the seventeenth century, it was long part of Mpigi District and became a district of its own in 2010.

batembuzi.s: The Batembuzi are the first, legendary dynasty of the kingdom of Kitara in the traditions of Bunyoro and its neighbours. Remembered as gods or semi-divine rulers associated with the creation of the world and the origins of kingship, they are said to have been followed by the…

buyaga.s: Buyaga is a county in western Uganda, part of the historic heartland of Bunyoro. After Britain's conquest of Bunyoro it was transferred to Buganda under the agreement of 1900, becoming one of the "lost counties" claimed by the Banyoro.

bugangaizi.s: Bugangaizi is a county in western Uganda that was part of the heartland of Bunyoro and contained the burial sites of several of its kings. After the British conquest it was transferred to Buganda in 1900 and became one of the "lost counties".

bunyoro-agreement-1933.s: The Bunyoro Agreement was signed in 1933 between the British colonial government of the Uganda Protectorate and Omukama Tito Winyi IV. It gave Bunyoro formal recognition as an agreement kingdom, comparable to Buganda, Toro and Ankole, with a defined role for the omukama and…

battle-of-ucles-1108.s: The Battle of Uclés was fought on 29 May 1108 near Uclés in central Spain. An Almoravid army under Tamim ibn Yusuf defeated a Castilian-Leonese force, and Sancho Alfónsez, the only son and heir of Alfonso VI, was killed.

berengaria-of-castile.s: Berengaria was the eldest daughter of Alfonso VIII of Castile and Eleanor of England. Married to Alfonso IX of León in 1197, she bore him several children before the pope annulled the marriage.

bermudo-iii-of-leon.s: Bermudo III was king of León from 1028 until 1037, the last of the male line descended from the Astur-Leonese kings. After losing ground to Sancho III of Navarre, he went to war with Ferdinand, count of Castile and husband of his sister Sancha.

bernard-of-sedirac.s: Bernard of Sédirac was a French Cluniac monk who became abbot of Sahagún and, after Alfonso VI's conquest of Toledo, the city's first archbishop from 1086. Named primate of the Spanish churches by Pope Urban II, he promoted the Roman liturgy in place of the Mozarabic rite and…

battle-of-golpejera.s: The Battle of Golpejera was fought in January 1072 near Carrión de los Condes between the brothers Sancho II of Castile and Alfonso VI of León. Sancho, whose army included Rodrigo Díaz de Vivar, El Cid, won and captured Alfonso, who was exiled to Muslim Toledo.

battle-of-llantada.s: The Battle of Llantada was fought in July 1068 on the border between Castile and León, between Sancho II of Castile and his brother Alfonso VI of León. The brothers, who had divided the kingdom of their father Ferdinand I, agreed that the victor would take the loser's realm.

battle-of-lutter.s: The Battle of Lutter was fought on 27 August 1626 near Lutter am Barenberge in Brunswick, during the Thirty Years' War. The Catholic League army under Count Tilly defeated Christian IV of Denmark, who had entered the war as leader of the Protestant cause in northern Germany.

battle-of-copenhagen-1801.s: The Battle of Copenhagen was fought on 2 April 1801 when a British fleet under Sir Hyde Parker, with Horatio Nelson leading the attack, engaged the Danish-Norwegian fleet moored before Copenhagen. Britain struck because Denmark had joined the League of Armed Neutrality.

battle-of-grathe-heath.s: The Battle of Grathe Heath was fought on 23 October 1157 near Viborg in Jutland, ending the Danish civil wars. Valdemar I defeated his rival Sweyn III, who was killed while fleeing; Sweyn had already tried to murder Valdemar and his co-king Canute V at the Bloodfeast of…

battle-of-dybbol.s: The Battle of Dybbøl was the decisive engagement of the Second Schleswig War. After weeks of bombardment, Prussian troops stormed the Danish fortifications at Dybbøl in Schleswig on 18 April 1864, inflicting heavy losses.

battle-of-agincourt.s: The Battle of Agincourt was fought on 25 October 1415 in northern France, where Henry V of England's small, exhausted army, made up largely of longbowmen, defeated a much larger French force. Heavy rain and a narrow muddy field helped the English archers, and many leading…

battle-of-bosworth-field.s: The Battle of Bosworth Field was fought on 22 August 1485 in Leicestershire between Richard III of England and Henry Tudor, the Lancastrian claimant. Richard was killed after some of his supporters, notably the Stanleys, failed to fight for him or turned against him.

battle-of-brunanburh.s: The Battle of Brunanburh was fought in 937 between Æthelstan, king of the English, and an alliance of Olaf Guthfrithson, king of Dublin, Constantine II of Scotland and Owain of Strathclyde. Æthelstan's victory confirmed his rule over a united English kingdom and was celebrated…

battle-of-naseby.s: The Battle of Naseby was fought on 14 June 1645 in Northamptonshire between the main Royalist army of Charles I and Parliament's New Model Army under Sir Thomas Fairfax and Oliver Cromwell. The Parliamentarians destroyed the Royalist infantry and captured the king's baggage,…

ben-jonson.s: Ben Jonson was an English playwright and poet, the leading dramatist of the Jacobean stage after Shakespeare. His satirical comedies, among them Volpone, The Alchemist and Bartholomew Fair, mocked greed and folly in London life, and he wrote many court masques for James I.

book-of-common-prayer.s: The Book of Common Prayer is the prayer book of the Church of England, first issued in 1549 under Edward VI and largely composed by Archbishop Thomas Cranmer. It replaced the Latin services with a single English liturgy, revised in 1552, 1559 and 1662.

brest-france.s: Brest is a port city at the western tip of Brittany, France, on a large natural harbour opening onto the Atlantic. Cardinal Richelieu under Louis XIII and later Colbert under Louis XIV developed it into the main base of the French Atlantic fleet, fortified by Vauban.

bagrat-vi-of-georgia.s: Bagrat VI was a prince of a branch of the Georgian Bagrationi dynasty who made himself king of Imereti in western Georgia. In 1463 he defeated King George VIII at Chikhori, a major step in the break-up of the united kingdom, and after George's capture by the atabeg of Samtskhe…

bagrati-cathedral.s: Bagrati Cathedral is an eleventh-century cathedral in Kutaisi, western Georgia, built under Bagrat III, the first king of united Georgia, and completed in the early 1000s. It was a masterpiece of medieval Georgian architecture until an explosion during the Ottoman invasion of…

battle-of-basiani.s: The Battle of Basiani was fought around 1202 in the Basiani valley in north-eastern Anatolia, where the Georgian army of Queen Tamar under the Zakarid brothers defeated the army of the Seljuk sultan of Rum, Süleymanshah II. The victory confirmed Georgia's position as the…

battle-of-garni.s: The Battle of Garni was fought in 1225 near Garni, in present-day Armenia, where the Khwarazmian ruler Jalal al-Din, who had fled the Mongols, routed the Georgian army. The defeat left Georgia open to invasion, and in 1226 Jalal al-Din took and sacked Tbilisi with great loss…

battle-of-khunan.s: The Battle of Khunan was fought in 1221 in southern Georgia, where the Mongol vanguard led by Jebe and Subutai defeated the Georgian army of King George IV. It was the first Mongol attack on Georgia, part of a long reconnaissance raid around the Caspian Sea.

bachkovo-monastery.s: Bachkovo Monastery, known in Georgian as Petritsoni, is an Eastern Orthodox monastery in the Rhodope Mountains of southern Bulgaria. It was founded in 1083 by Gregory Pakourianos, a Byzantine general of Georgian origin, for Georgian monks, and was a centre of Georgian learning…

battle-of-culloden.s: The Battle of Culloden was fought on 16 April 1746 near Inverness, where the government army under the Duke of Cumberland destroyed the Jacobite army of Charles Edward Stuart in less than an hour. It was the last pitched battle fought on British soil.

battle-of-sheriffmuir.s: The Battle of Sheriffmuir was fought on 13 November 1715 near Dunblane in Scotland between the Jacobite army of the Earl of Mar and a smaller government army under the Duke of Argyll. Neither side won clearly, but Mar withdrew, and the Jacobite rising of 1715 lost its momentum.

bridgewater-canal.s: The Bridgewater Canal is a canal in north-west England, built for the Duke of Bridgewater to carry coal from his mines at Worsley to Manchester. Engineered by James Brindley and John Gilbert, its first section opened in 1761 and halved the price of coal in Manchester.

bristol.s: Bristol is a city and port in south-west England on the River Avon, near its mouth on the Severn estuary. A major trading town since the Middle Ages, it sent John Cabot's expedition to North America in 1497.

battle-of-oudenarde.s: The Battle of Oudenarde was fought on 11 July 1708 on the Scheldt in the Spanish Netherlands, where an allied army under the Duke of Marlborough and Prince Eugene of Savoy defeated a French army under the Dukes of Burgundy and Vendôme. The victory let the allies recover the…

battle-of-porto-bello.s: The Battle of Porto Bello was a British naval attack in November 1739 on Porto Bello, a Spanish port on the Caribbean coast of Panama. Admiral Edward Vernon captured it with only six ships and destroyed its fortifications.

battle-of-hatfield-chase.s: The Battle of Hatfield Chase was fought in 633 near Doncaster in Yorkshire, where Cadwallon ap Cadfan of Gwynedd and Penda of Mercia defeated and killed Edwin, the Christian king of Northumbria. Northumbria split into its two kingdoms of Deira and Bernicia and was ravaged by…

battle-of-heavenfield.s: The Battle of Heavenfield was fought in 634 near Hexham in Northumberland, where Oswald of Bernicia defeated and killed Cadwallon ap Cadfan of Gwynedd, who had ravaged Northumbria after the Battle of Hatfield Chase. According to Bede, Oswald raised a wooden cross before the…

beaumaris-castle.s: Beaumaris Castle is a castle on Anglesey in north Wales, begun by Edward I in 1295 after a Welsh revolt and designed by Master James of St George. Built to a symmetrical concentric plan with a moat and dock, it is regarded as a masterpiece of medieval military architecture,…

berwyn-range.s: The Berwyn range is a range of moorland mountains in north-east Wales, rising to 832 metres at Cadair Berwyn. In 1165 Henry II of England led a great army into Wales against a coalition of Welsh rulers under Owain Gwynedd, but storms and rain on the Berwyn forced him to…

battle-of-bryn-derwin.s: The Battle of Bryn Derwin was fought in June 1255 at a pass in the hills of Caernarfonshire, where Llywelyn ap Gruffudd defeated his brothers Owain and Dafydd, with whom he had shared Gwynedd. Llywelyn imprisoned Owain and became sole ruler of Gwynedd west of the Conwy, the…

battle-of-moel-y-don.s: The Battle of Moel-y-don was fought on 6 November 1282 on the Menai Strait, during Edward I's final war against Llywelyn ap Gruffudd. An English force under Luke de Tany crossed from Anglesey by a bridge of boats in breach of a truce and was routed by the Welsh, many men…

battle-of-rhyd-y-groes.s: The Battle of Rhyd-y-groes was fought in 1039 at a ford on the River Severn near Welshpool, where Gruffudd ap Llywelyn, newly king of Gwynedd and Powys, defeated a Mercian army. Edwin, brother of Earl Leofric of Mercia, was killed.

banska-stiavnica.s: Banská Štiavnica, Hungarian Selmecbánya and German Schemnitz, is a town in central Slovakia. Silver and gold mining there expanded in the thirteenth century with German settlers and made it one of the richest mining towns of the Kingdom of Hungary.

battle-of-menfo.s: The Battle of Ménfő was fought on 5 July 1044 near Győr, where Emperor Henry III defeated King Samuel Aba of Hungary. Aba was captured and killed soon afterwards, and Henry restored Peter Orseolo, who did homage to him for the kingdom.

battle-of-sirmium.s: The Battle of Sirmium was fought on 8 July 1167 near Sirmium (Sremska Mitrovica) in Syrmia, where the Byzantine army of Manuel I Komnenos under Andronikos Kontostephanos decisively defeated the Hungarians. The peace that followed left Byzantium in control of Syrmia, Dalmatia…

bela-iii-of-hungary.s: Béla III was king of Hungary from 1172 to 1196. Raised at the Byzantine court as the intended heir of Manuel I Komnenos, he returned to take the Hungarian throne and recovered Dalmatia and Syrmia after Manuel's death.

battle-of-breadfield.s: The Battle of Breadfield (Kenyérmező) was fought on 13 October 1479 near Orăștie in Transylvania, where Hungarian forces under Stephen Báthory and Paul Kinizsi destroyed a large Ottoman raiding army. It was the greatest Hungarian victory over the Ottomans in the reign of…

battle-of-varna.s: The Battle of Varna was fought on 10 November 1444 near the Black Sea port of Varna in Bulgaria, where the Ottoman army of Murad II defeated a crusading army of Hungarians, Poles and Wallachians. King Vladislaus I of Hungary (Władysław III of Poland) was killed and John…

bibliotheca-corviniana.s: The Bibliotheca Corviniana was the library of Matthias Corvinus, king of Hungary, assembled at Buda mainly in the 1470s and 1480s. With perhaps two thousand volumes, many of them richly illuminated manuscripts made in Florence and Buda, it was one of the largest libraries of…

bakur-iii-of-iberia.s: Bakur III was king of Iberia in eastern Georgia in the sixth century. After his death around 580 the Sasanian king Hormizd IV abolished the Iberian monarchy and placed the country under a Persian governor, while Bakur's heirs kept only the highland province of Kakheti.

bir-el-qutt.s: Bir el Qutt is the site of a Georgian monastery of the fifth and sixth centuries near Bethlehem, excavated in the 1950s. Its mosaic floors carry some of the earliest dated inscriptions in the Georgian Asomtavruli script and show the early presence of Georgian monks in the Holy…

bolnisi-sioni.s: Bolnisi Sioni is a basilica church in the Kvemo Kartli region of southern Georgia, built between 478 and 493 and the oldest surviving dated church in Georgia. Its building inscription in the Asomtavruli script, which dates the work by the reign of the Persian king Peroz, is…

bagdati.s: Bagdati is a town in the Imereti region of western Georgia, south of Kutaisi. A fortress there guarded the southern routes into Imereti during the wars of the kings of Imereti with the Ottomans and the princes of Samtskhe.

battle-of-murjakheti.s: The Battle of Murjakheti was fought in 1535 in south-western Georgia between King Bagrat III of Imereti and Qvarqvare III, atabeg of Samtskhe. Bagrat won, captured Qvarqvare and occupied Samtskhe, but the Ottoman victory over a Georgian coalition at Sokhoista in 1545 restored…

battle-of-sokhoista.s: The Battle of Sokhoista was fought in 1545 in Samtskhe, south-western Georgia, where an Ottoman army defeated a coalition of Georgian rulers led by King Bagrat III of Imereti. The Ottomans restored their ally, the atabeg of Samtskhe, and the defeat opened western Georgia to…

bantry-bay.s: Bantry Bay is a long inlet of the Atlantic on the coast of County Cork in south-west Ireland. In December 1796 a French expedition under General Hoche, with Wolfe Tone on board, reached the bay to support a rising of the United Irishmen, but storms scattered the fleet and…

battle-of-aughrim.s: The Battle of Aughrim was fought on 12 July 1691 near Aughrim in County Galway, between the Jacobite army of the Marquis de St Ruth and the Williamite army under Godert de Ginkel. St Ruth was killed by a cannonball and his army broke with heavy losses, making it perhaps the…

battle-of-the-boyne.s: The Battle of the Boyne was fought on 1 July 1690 (Old Style) on the River Boyne near Drogheda, Ireland, between the Protestant William III and the deposed Catholic king James II. William's victory forced James to flee to France and secured Dublin, though the war continued…

battle-of-the-yellow-ford.s: The Battle of the Yellow Ford was fought on 14 August 1598 on the Callan river near Armagh, where the Irish forces of Hugh O'Neill, Earl of Tyrone, and Red Hugh O'Donnell routed an English army under Sir Henry Bagenal marching to relieve the Blackwater fort. Bagenal and many…

baasha.s: Baasha was king of Israel in the early ninth century BCE, reigning about twenty-four years according to the Books of Kings. An officer from the tribe of Issachar, he killed King Nadab, son of Jeroboam I, during the siege of Gibbethon and wiped out Jeroboam's house.

black-obelisk-of-shalmaneser-iii.s: The Black Obelisk of Shalmaneser III is a black limestone monument from Nimrud, erected around 825 BCE and now in the British Museum. Its relief panels show tribute brought to the Assyrian king from five lands; one panel shows Jehu of Israel, or his envoy, prostrate before…

brindisi.s: Brindisi is a port city on the Adriatic coast of Apulia in south-eastern Italy. As Roman Brundisium it was the end of the Via Appia and the main port for crossings to Greece.

battle-of-cape-matapan.s: The Battle of Cape Matapan was a naval battle fought on 27–29 March 1941 off the south-western coast of the Peloponnese, Greece, between the British Mediterranean Fleet under Admiral Andrew Cunningham and the Italian navy. Helped by intercepted signals and radar, the British…

battle-of-caporetto.s: The Battle of Caporetto was an Austro-Hungarian and German offensive on the Isonzo front, launched on 24 October 1917 near the town of Caporetto, now Kobarid in Slovenia. Using gas, infiltration tactics and surprise, the attackers broke through and drove the Italian army back…

battle-of-vittorio-veneto.s: The Battle of Vittorio Veneto was the final Italian offensive of the First World War, fought from 24 October to 4 November 1918. Italian forces with British and French support crossed the Piave and split the Austro-Hungarian army, which disintegrated as the empire itself broke…

battle-of-ascalon.s: The Battle of Ascalon was fought on 12 August 1099 near Ascalon on the coast of southern Palestine, soon after the capture of Jerusalem in the First Crusade. Godfrey of Bouillon and the other crusader leaders surprised and routed a Fatimid army led by the vizier al-Afdal.

belvoir-fortress.s: Belvoir Fortress is a crusader castle on a plateau above the Jordan valley, south of the Sea of Galilee in present-day Israel. Built by the Knights Hospitaller from 1168, it is one of the earliest concentric castles.

bethlehem.s: Bethlehem is a Palestinian city in the West Bank, about 10 kilometres south of Jerusalem. In the Bible it is the home of David's family, and Christian tradition holds it to be the birthplace of Jesus, marked by the Church of the Nativity, first built under Constantine the Great.

beth-shemesh.s: Beth-shemesh is an ancient town in the Shephelah west of Jerusalem, excavated at Tel Beth Shemesh beside the modern Israeli city of the same name. In the Iron Age it lay on the border between Judah and the Philistine plain.

book-of-deuteronomy.s: Deuteronomy is the fifth book of the Torah and the Hebrew Bible, presented as the farewell speeches of Moses to the Israelites before they enter Canaan. It insists on the worship of Yahweh alone at a single central sanctuary and sets out a code of law.

battle-of-tamaron.s: The Battle of Tamarón was fought on 4 September 1037 near Tamarón, west of Burgos, between Bermudo III of León and his brother-in-law Ferdinand, count of Castile, aided by his brother García Sánchez III of Navarre. Bermudo was killed, ending the old Asturian-Leonese male line,…

beatus-of-facundus.s: The Beatus of Facundus is an illuminated manuscript of Beatus of Liébana's Commentary on the Apocalypse, copied in 1047 by the scribe Facundus for King Ferdinand I of León and Queen Sancha. Its vivid Mozarabic-style miniatures make it one of the finest of the Beatus manuscripts.

bermudo-ii-of-leon.s: Bermudo II was King of León from 984 to 999, having first been proclaimed in Galicia in 982 against his cousin Ramiro III. His reign coincided with the height of the power of al-Mansur, the regent of the Caliphate of Córdoba, whose raids sacked León and, in 997, the shrine of…

basilica-of-san-isidoro.s: The Basilica of San Isidoro is a Romanesque church in León, Spain, built to house the relics of Isidore of Seville, brought there in 1063, and consecrated in its rebuilt form in 1149. Its Pantheon of the Kings, the burial place of the Leonese royal family, preserves…

battle-of-pteria.s: The Battle of Pteria was fought around 547 BCE in Cappadocia, east of the Halys river, between Croesus of Lydia and Cyrus the Great of Persia. According to Herodotus the battle was indecisive and Croesus withdrew to Sardis for the winter, but Cyrus followed him, defeated the…

beornred-of-mercia.s: Beornred briefly held the throne of Mercia in 757, after King Æthelbald was murdered by his own bodyguard at Seckington. His origins and kinship are unknown.

breedon-on-the-hill.s: Breedon on the Hill is a village in north-western Leicestershire, England, where a monastery was founded around 675 inside an Iron Age hillfort as a daughter house of Medeshamstede (Peterborough). The present church of St Mary and St Hardulph keeps one of the finest…

bridgnorth.s: Bridgnorth is a market town on the River Severn in Shropshire, England. Æthelflæd, Lady of the Mercians, built a burh, or fortified town, there in 912 against the Vikings, who had camped nearby in 895–896. In 1102 Henry I besieged and took the castle of the rebel Robert of…

burgred-of-mercia.s: Burgred was king of Mercia from 852 to 874. He allied with Wessex, which helped him against the Welsh, and in 853 married Æthelswith, sister of Alfred the Great.

battle-of-maserfield.s: The Battle of Maserfield was fought on 5 August 642 between Penda of Mercia and Oswald of Northumbria, probably at Oswestry in Shropshire. Oswald, the leading Christian king of his day, was killed and his body dismembered, and he was afterwards venerated as a saint and martyr.

battle-of-pollilur-1780.s: The Battle of Pollilur was fought on 10 September 1780 near Kanchipuram in south-eastern India, during the Second Anglo-Mysore War. Forces under Tipu Sultan and Hyder Ali surrounded and destroyed a British East India Company detachment under Colonel William Baillie, most of…

battle-of-bitonto.s: The Battle of Bitonto was fought on 25 May 1734 in Apulia during the War of the Polish Succession. A Spanish army under the Count of Montemar defeated the Austrian forces holding the Kingdom of Naples.

battle-of-tagliacozzo.s: The Battle of Tagliacozzo was fought on 23 August 1268 in the Abruzzi. Charles of Anjou, using a hidden reserve, defeated Conradin, the sixteen-year-old last heir of the Hohenstaufen dynasty, who had come to reclaim the Kingdom of Sicily.

battle-of-the-garigliano-1503.s: The Battle of the Garigliano was fought on 29 December 1503 on the river Garigliano between Lazio and Campania, during the Italian Wars. After weeks of stalemate, Gonzalo Fernández de Córdoba crossed the river by surprise and routed the French army.

bernardo-tanucci.s: Bernardo Tanucci (1698–1783) was a Tuscan jurist who became the leading minister of the Kingdom of Naples under Charles of Bourbon and regent during the minority of Ferdinand IV. A champion of royal authority, he curbed the privileges of the church and the barons, restricted…

battle-of-atapuerca.s: The Battle of Atapuerca was fought on 1 September 1054 near Burgos between two sons of Sancho III of Navarre. Ferdinand I of León and Castile defeated and killed his elder brother García Sánchez III of Pamplona, who had been pressing claims to Castilian border lands.

benjamin-of-tudela.s: Benjamin of Tudela was a Jewish traveller from Tudela in Navarre who journeyed from Spain through southern France, Italy, Greece and Constantinople to the Levant, Mesopotamia and Baghdad, probably between about 1165 and 1173. His Book of Travels, written in Hebrew, describes…

blanche-i-of-navarre.s: Blanche I (1387–1441) was queen of Navarre from 1425 to 1441. A daughter of Charles III the Noble, she was first married to Martin I of Sicily and then, in 1420, to John of Aragon, later John II.

battle-of-noain.s: The Battle of Noáin was fought on 30 June 1521 near Pamplona. A Castilian army defeated the Franco-Navarrese force under André de Foix that had briefly recovered Pamplona and most of Navarre for the exiled king Henry II of Albret.

battle-of-valdejunquera.s: The Battle of Valdejunquera was fought on 26 July 920 in Navarre. Abd al-Rahman III of Córdoba, on campaign against the Christian north, defeated the combined armies of Ordoño II of León and Sancho Garcés I of Pamplona, capturing several leading men.

bhimsen-thapa.s: Bhimsen Thapa (1775–1839) was the chief minister (mukhtiyar) of Nepal from 1806 to 1837. He dominated the court during the minority of the kings, built up the army and continued the kingdom's westward expansion, which led to the Anglo-Nepalese War of 1814–1816 and the loss of…

birendra-of-nepal.s: Birendra (1945–2001) was king of Nepal from 1972 to 2001. He ruled at first through the partyless panchayat system, but the People's Movement of 1990 forced him to legalise political parties and accept a constitution making him a constitutional monarch.

battle-of-nalapani.s: The Battle of Nalapani was the first major engagement of the Anglo-Nepalese War, fought in October and November 1814 at the hill fort of Khalanga (Kalunga) near Dehradun. A small Gorkhali garrison under Balbhadra Kunwar repulsed repeated British assaults, killing General…

b-p-koirala.s: B. P. Koirala (1914–1982) was a leader of the Nepali Congress and Nepal's first democratically elected prime minister, taking office in 1959. In December 1960 King Mahendra dismissed his government and imprisoned him, introducing the partyless panchayat system.

benedict-biscop.s: Benedict Biscop (c. 628–690) was a Northumbrian nobleman who became a monk and founded the monasteries of Wearmouth in 674 and Jarrow around 682. On repeated journeys to Rome he collected books, relics and paintings, and he brought masons and glaziers from Gaul to build in stone.

bewcastle-cross.s: The Bewcastle Cross is an Anglo-Saxon stone cross standing in the churchyard of Bewcastle in Cumbria, probably carved in the early eighth century. Its shaft, which has lost its head, bears figures of Christ, John the Baptist and John the Evangelist, vine scrolls, chequer…

bagler.s: The Bagler were a faction in the Norwegian civil wars, formed in 1196 by opponents of King Sverre with the backing of the church, led by Bishop Nicholas Arnesson of Oslo. Strongest in the east around the Oslofjord, they set up rival kings and fought the Birkebeiner for two…

birkebeiner.s: The Birkebeiner ("birch-legs", from the birch bark some wore as footwear) were a rebel party in the Norwegian civil wars, formed in 1174 among poor and landless men. Under Sverre Sigurdsson from 1177 they defeated Magnus Erlingsson and became the royal party.

borgarting.s: The Borgarting was the medieval law assembly for the region of Viken around the Oslofjord in south-eastern Norway, meeting at Borg, the present Sarpsborg. Like the Gulating, Frostating and Eidsivating, it had its own law book until Magnus the Lawmender's national code of 1274.

borgund-stave-church.s: Borgund Stave Church is a wooden church in Lærdal in western Norway, built around 1180–1250 and dedicated to the apostle Andrew. With its tiered roofs, dragon-head gables and carved portals it is the best-preserved of Norway's medieval stave churches and the model for many…

bryggen.s: Bryggen is the old wharf of Bergen in western Norway, lined with wooden merchant buildings. From around 1360 to 1754 it was the seat of the Hanseatic Kontor, the German merchants' office that controlled the export of dried fish from northern Norway in exchange for grain.

battle-of-fimreite.s: The Battle of Fimreite was a naval battle fought on 15 June 1184 in the Sognefjord in western Norway. King Sverre and his Birkebeiner defeated the fleet of the crowned king Magnus Erlingsson, who drowned with many of his men.

battle-of-nesjar.s: The Battle of Nesjar was a naval battle fought in 1016 near the mouth of the Oslofjord. Olaf Haraldsson, who had returned to Norway to claim the throne, defeated Sweyn Haakonsson, jarl of Lade, who ruled the country under Danish overlordship.

battle-of-cabira.s: The Battle of Cabira was fought near Cabira in Pontus, in the Third Mithridatic War, in 72 or 71 BCE. The Roman general Lucius Licinius Lucullus, after cutting the enemy supply lines, routed the army of Mithridates VI, who fled to his son-in-law Tigranes the Great of Armenia.

battle-of-ameixial.s: The Battle of Ameixial was fought on 8 June 1663 near Estremoz in the Alentejo, during the Portuguese Restoration War. A Portuguese army under the Count of Vila Flor, with the Count of Schomberg and English and French auxiliaries, defeated the Spanish army of Don John of…

battle-of-montes-claros.s: The Battle of Montes Claros was fought on 17 June 1665 near Vila Viçosa in the Alentejo, the last major battle of the Portuguese Restoration War. A Portuguese army under the Marquis of Marialva, advised by the Count of Schomberg, routed the Spanish army of the Marquis of…
