bangor-on-dee.s: Bangor-on-Dee (Bangor-is-y-coed) is a village on the River Dee in Wrexham county borough, north-east Wales. In the early Middle Ages it was the site of a large British monastery.

battle-of-lincoln-1141.s: The Battle of Lincoln was fought on 2 February 1141 during the Anarchy, the English civil war between King Stephen and the Empress Matilda. Forces under Robert of Gloucester and Ranulf, Earl of Chester, including Welsh contingents led by Madog ap Maredudd of Powys, defeated…

battle-of-leipzig.s: The Battle of Leipzig, or Battle of the Nations, was fought on 16–19 October 1813 around Leipzig in Saxony. The armies of Russia, Prussia, Austria and Sweden defeated Napoleon in a battle involving some 600,000 soldiers, and his German allies began to desert him.

battle-of-sedan-1870.s: The Battle of Sedan was fought on 1–2 September 1870 in the Franco-Prussian War. Prussian and other German armies under Helmuth von Moltke the Elder surrounded the French Army of Châlons at Sedan in north-eastern France, and Emperor Napoleon III surrendered with more than…

battle-of-kunersdorf.s: The Battle of Kunersdorf was fought on 12 August 1759 near Frankfurt an der Oder in the Seven Years' War. A Russian army under Pyotr Saltykov and an Austrian corps under Ernst Gideon von Laudon crushed Frederick II's Prussian army, which lost about half its men.

battle-of-leuthen.s: The Battle of Leuthen was fought on 5 December 1757 west of Breslau in Silesia during the Seven Years' War. Frederick II used the oblique order of attack to rout an Austrian army about twice the size of his own under Prince Charles of Lorraine.

battle-of-mollwitz.s: The Battle of Mollwitz was fought on 10 April 1741 in Silesia, the first major battle of the First Silesian War. Frederick II's army defeated the Austrians under Wilhelm Reinhard von Neipperg, although Frederick himself left the field when the battle seemed lost and Field…

battle-of-shangi.s: The Battle of Shangi was fought in 1896 in south-western Rwanda, near Lake Kivu, when a Rwandan army attacked a post set up by the Congo Free State. The Rwandan forces were driven back with heavy losses by rifle fire.

baran-temple.s: The Bar'an Temple, known locally as Arsh Bilqis ('Throne of Bilqis'), is a Sabaean temple of the god Almaqah near Marib in Yemen. Built and enlarged over several centuries from the early first millennium BCE, it is known for its row of tall stone pillars.

battle-of-macomer.s: The Battle of Macomer was fought on 19 May 1478 in central Sardinia between Leonardo Alagon, Marquis of Oristano, and the forces of the Aragonese viceroy. Alagon, the last great Sardinian feudal rebel, was defeated, captured and imprisoned in Spain until his death.

battle-of-the-chernaya.s: The Battle of the Chernaya was fought on 16 August 1855 on the Chernaya river near Sevastopol during the Crimean War. French and Sardinian troops beat off a Russian attack meant to relieve the besieged city, which fell three weeks later.

battle-of-lucocisterna.s: The Battle of Lucocisterna was fought on 29 February 1324 near Cagliari in Sardinia during the Aragonese conquest of the island. The Infante Alfonso of Aragon defeated a Pisan relief army, and Pisa soon made peace, ceding its Sardinian territories except the castle of…

battle-of-magenta.s: The Battle of Magenta was fought on 4 June 1859 near Magenta in Lombardy, in the Second Italian War of Independence. A French army under Napoleon III and Patrice de MacMahon, with Sardinian support, defeated the Austrians under Ferenc Gyulai, who abandoned Milan.

battle-of-carham.s: The Battle of Carham was fought around 1018 at Carham on the River Tweed, where Malcolm II of Scotland, with Owen the Bald of Strathclyde, defeated a Northumbrian army. The victory secured Scottish control of Lothian, the land between the Forth and the Tweed, and set the Tweed…

battle-of-flodden.s: The Battle of Flodden was fought on 9 September 1513 in Northumberland, where an English army under the Earl of Surrey destroyed the invading Scottish army of James IV, who had attacked England in support of his French ally. James IV was killed together with many of his nobles…

battle-of-nevilles-cross.s: The Battle of Neville's Cross was fought on 17 October 1346 near Durham, when David II of Scotland invaded England in support of France after the English victory at Crécy. An English army raised in the northern counties defeated the Scots, and David II was captured and held in…

battle-of-stirling-bridge.s: The Battle of Stirling Bridge was fought on 11 September 1297, when Scottish forces under William Wallace and Andrew Moray destroyed an English army under the Earl of Surrey as it crossed the narrow bridge over the River Forth. The victory revived Scottish resistance to Edward…

berwick-upon-tweed.s: Berwick-upon-Tweed is a town at the mouth of the River Tweed, now the northernmost town in England. In the thirteenth century it was the richest Scottish burgh and the kingdom's main port for wool exports.

battle-of-dunbar-1296.s: The Battle of Dunbar was fought on 27 April 1296 near Dunbar in East Lothian, where an English army under John de Warenne, Earl of Surrey, routed the Scots after Edward I's invasion and sack of Berwick. Scottish resistance collapsed, King John Balliol surrendered and abdicated…

battle-of-dunbar-1650.s: The Battle of Dunbar was fought on 3 September 1650 near Dunbar in East Lothian, where Oliver Cromwell's English army defeated a larger Covenanter army under David Leslie, which had supported Charles II. Thousands of Scots were killed or captured, and Cromwell took Edinburgh.

battle-of-falkirk-1298.s: The Battle of Falkirk was fought on 22 July 1298, when Edward I of England defeated the Scottish army of William Wallace. English longbowmen and cavalry broke the Scottish schiltrons, the dense formations of spearmen that had to stand still to resist mounted attack.

battle-of-halidon-hill.s: The Battle of Halidon Hill was fought on 19 July 1333 outside Berwick, where Edward III of England and Edward Balliol defeated a Scottish army under the regent Archibald Douglas that was trying to relieve the besieged town. English archers inflicted heavy losses, Douglas was…

battle-of-newburn.s: The Battle of Newburn was fought on 28 August 1640 at a ford over the River Tyne west of Newcastle, where the Covenanter army under Alexander Leslie defeated an English force and went on to occupy Newcastle. The defeat in this Second Bishops' War left Charles I unable to pay…

battle-of-solway-moss.s: The Battle of Solway Moss was fought on 24 November 1542 near the River Esk on the English border, where a small English force routed a larger Scottish army sent by James V. Many Scottish nobles were captured.

battle-of-cape-passaro.s: The Battle of Cape Passaro was fought on 11 August 1718 off the south-eastern tip of Sicily, where a British fleet under Admiral Sir George Byng destroyed a Spanish fleet supporting Spain's invasion of Sicily. Although Britain and Spain were not yet formally at war, the battle…

battle-of-galluccio.s: The Battle of Galluccio was fought on 22 July 1139 in Campania, where forces led by Roger of Apulia, son of Roger II of Sicily, ambushed a papal army and captured Pope Innocent II. Three days later, by the Treaty of Mignano, the captive pope recognised Roger II as King of…

battle-of-brunkeberg.s: The Battle of Brunkeberg was fought on 10 October 1471 on a ridge outside Stockholm, where the Swedish regent Sten Sture the Elder, with peasants, miners and burghers, defeated King Christian I of Denmark, who sought to enforce his rule over Sweden under the Kalmar Union. The…

beatrix-of-the-netherlands.s: Beatrix was Queen of the Netherlands from 1980 to 2013, succeeding her mother Juliana. Her marriage to the German diplomat Claus von Amsberg in 1966 provoked protests, but she became a respected and active head of state who took a close interest in government.

bastam.s: Bastam is the site of a large Urartian fortress in Iran's West Azerbaijan province, north of Khoy, built by Rusa II in the seventh century BCE. Excavated by German archaeologists between 1968 and 1978, it yielded storerooms, stables, clay bullae, seals and tablets that…

book-of-genesis.s: The Book of Genesis is the first book of the Hebrew Bible and the Christian Old Testament, recounting the creation of the world, the Flood and the stories of Abraham, Isaac, Jacob and Joseph. It states that Noah's ark came to rest on the mountains of Ararat, a name derived…

book-of-jeremiah.s: The Book of Jeremiah is a book of the Hebrew Bible containing the prophecies and life of Jeremiah, who was active in Judah from the late seventh century BCE until after the Babylonian destruction of Jerusalem in 587 BCE. It calls on the kingdoms of Ararat, Minni and Ashkenaz…

boris-piotrovsky.s: Boris Piotrovsky was a Soviet archaeologist and orientalist and the leading scholar of Urartu. From 1939 he directed the excavations at Karmir Blur near Yerevan, which revealed the Urartian fortress of Teishebaini with its storerooms, weapons and inscriptions, and his books…

battle-of-aclea.s: The Battle of Aclea was fought in 851 between the West Saxons under King Æthelwulf and his son Æthelbald and a large Viking army that had sacked Canterbury and London. The Anglo-Saxon Chronicle calls the West Saxon victory the greatest slaughter of a heathen army ever heard of.

battle-of-ashdown.s: The Battle of Ashdown was fought on 8 January 871 between the West Saxons, led by King Æthelred I and his brother Alfred, and the Great Heathen Army of the Danes. Alfred's attack uphill began a West Saxon victory in which the Danish king Bagsecg and five earls were killed.

battle-of-bensington.s: The Battle of Bensington was fought in 779 at Bensington, now Benson in Oxfordshire, where Offa of Mercia defeated Cynewulf of Wessex and took the town. The victory secured Mercian control of the upper Thames valley, including lands north of the river that had belonged to…

beorhtric-of-wessex.s: Beorhtric was king of Wessex from 786 to 802. He married Eadburh, a daughter of Offa of Mercia, in 789 and ruled as Offa's ally, while his rival Ecgberht was driven into exile among the Franks.

beornwulf-of-mercia.s: Beornwulf was king of Mercia from 823 to 826, after displacing Ceolwulf I. In 825 he was decisively defeated by Ecgberht of Wessex at the Battle of Ellendun, after which Kent, Surrey, Sussex and Essex passed to Wessex.

battle-of-burford.s: The Battle of Burford was fought in 752 near Burford in Oxfordshire, where, according to the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle, Cuthred of Wessex defeated Æthelbald of Mercia. The victory briefly freed Wessex from Mercian overlordship, though Mercian dominance returned under Offa later in…

burghal-hidage.s: The Burghal Hidage is an Anglo-Saxon document listing 33 fortified places, or burhs, in Wessex, with the number of hides of land assigned to the upkeep and defence of each. It reflects the system of burhs created by Alfred the Great and his son Edward the Elder against the…

battle-of-tauberbischofsheim.s: The Battle of Tauberbischofsheim was fought on 24 July 1866 during the Austro-Prussian War, when Prussian troops of the Army of the Main defeated the Württemberg division of the Federal VIII Army Corps at the crossing of the River Tauber. It was one of the last engagements of…

balkan-pact.s: The Balkan Pact, or Balkan Entente, was an agreement signed in Athens on 9 February 1934 by Greece, Romania, Turkey and Yugoslavia. The four states guaranteed one another's Balkan frontiers against revision, chiefly by Bulgaria, which refused to join.

baranja.s: Baranja is a historical region in the Pannonian Plain between the Danube and the Drava, divided since 1920 between Hungary and Croatia. Its southern part passed to the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes after the First World War, was annexed by Hungary in 1941–1944, and now…

bor-serbia.s: Bor is a mining town in eastern Serbia and the centre of one of Europe's largest copper deposits. Mining began in 1903 and was developed between the world wars by a French company, making Bor a major site of foreign investment in the Kingdom of Yugoslavia.

bosniaks.s: The Bosniaks are a South Slavic people, mainly Muslim, native to Bosnia and Herzegovina and the Sandžak region of Serbia and Montenegro. Their identity took shape under Ottoman rule, during which much of the population converted to Islam.

bagyidaw.s: Bagyidaw was king of Burma from 1819 to 1837, the grandson and successor of Bodawpaya. Burmese expansion into Assam and Manipur under him led to the First Anglo-Burmese War, and by the Treaty of Yandabo of 1826 he ceded Arakan and Tenasserim and paid a large indemnity.

bombay-burmah-trading-corporation.s: The Bombay Burmah Trading Corporation is a company founded in 1863 by the Wallace brothers in Bombay, which became the largest extractor of teak in Burma. In 1885 the court of King Thibaw imposed a heavy fine on it for under-reporting timber, and the dispute served as a…

byedaik.s: The Byedaik was the privy council of the Burmese kings, which handled the monarch's private affairs and served as an inner office between the palace and the Hluttaw, the council of state. Under the Konbaung dynasty its ministers, the atwinwun, controlled access to the king and…

battle-of-danubyu.s: The Battle of Danubyu was fought in March and April 1825 during the First Anglo-Burmese War, when a British force attacked the Burmese fortified position at Danubyu in the Irrawaddy delta. The Burmese commander Maha Bandula was killed by a mortar shell on 1 April 1825, and his…

battle-of-kaungton.s: The Battle of Kaungton was the final campaign of the Sino-Burmese War, fought in late 1769 around Kaungton on the Irrawaddy near Bhamo. A large Qing army under Fuheng was surrounded by Burmese forces under Maha Thiha Thura, and the Qing commanders agreed to a negotiated…

battle-of-maymyo.s: The Battle of Maymyo was fought in early 1768 near Maymyo, now Pyin Oo Lwin, in Upper Burma during the third Qing invasion of the Sino-Burmese War. Burmese armies under Maha Thiha Thura surrounded the main Qing army of Ming Rui, which was almost entirely destroyed, and Ming…

barbarikon.s: Barbarikon was an ancient seaport in the Indus delta, near modern Karachi in Pakistan. The 1st-century Periplus of the Erythraean Sea describes it as the port of the Indus region, exporting costus, bdellium, lapis lazuli, turquoise, indigo and Chinese furs and silk, and…

bharuch.s: Bharuch is a city on the estuary of the Narmada River in Gujarat, western India, and one of the oldest ports of the subcontinent. Known to Greek and Roman merchants as Barygaza, it was the great harbour of western India in the early centuries CE, shipping goods from Ujjain and…

battle-of-chi-lang-xuong-giang.s: The Battle of Chi Lăng–Xương Giang was fought in late 1427 when the forces of Lê Lợi ambushed a Ming relief army marching south from China through the Chi Lăng pass, killing its commander Liu Sheng and then destroying the remaining troops at Xương Giang. The defeat led the…

binh-ngo-dai-cao.s: The Bình Ngô đại cáo is a proclamation written in classical Chinese by Nguyễn Trãi in 1428 on behalf of Lê Lợi to announce victory over the Ming and the restoration of Đại Việt. Asserting that Vietnam had its own territory, customs and dynasties equal to China's, it is…

battle-of-gaoliang-river.s: The Battle of Gaoliang River was fought in 979 near modern Beijing between the Song emperor Taizong and the army of the Liao dynasty. Having conquered the Northern Han, Taizong marched to take the Sixteen Prefectures, but Liao cavalry routed his army and he fled wounded.

battle-of-hubudagang.s: The Battle of Hubudagang was fought in 1115 in Manchuria between the Jurchen leader Wanyan Aguda, newly proclaimed emperor of the Jin dynasty, and the Liao emperor Tianzuo. Aguda's small army routed a far larger Liao force, a defeat that broke Liao power in the north-east and…

battle-of-ningjiang.s: The Battle of Ningjiang was fought in 1114 when the Jurchen chieftain Wanyan Aguda rebelled against the Liao dynasty and attacked its fortress of Ningjiang in Manchuria. His victory over the Liao garrison and relief forces began the Jurchen rising that led to the founding of…

bomi-hills.s: Bomi Hills is an iron ore district in north-western Liberia, in present-day Bomi County. Mining by the Liberia Mining Company began there in 1951, making it the country's first iron mine, and its exports helped make Liberia one of the world's fastest-growing economies in the…

bong-mines.s: Bong Mines is an iron mining town in Bong County, central Liberia. The Bong Mining Company, backed mainly by German investors, began exporting ore from the Bong Range in 1965 by rail to Monrovia.

bioko.s: Bioko, formerly Fernando Po, is a volcanic island in the Gulf of Guinea, part of Equatorial Guinea and the site of its capital, Malabo. Spanish from 1778, it developed cocoa plantations that depended on contract labour from West Africa; a 1930 League of Nations inquiry into…

battle-of-the-hydaspes.s: The Battle of the Hydaspes was fought in 326 BCE on the banks of the Hydaspes (Jhelum) in the Punjab between Alexander the Great and the Indian king Porus. Alexander crossed the swollen river upstream of Porus' army under cover of a storm and defeated it despite its war…

banu-kanz.s: The Banu Kanz were an Arab tribal dynasty of the Aswan region on Egypt's southern frontier, descended from Rabi'a Arabs who settled there in the 9th century and intermarried with the Nubians. Their leaders bore the title Kanz al-Dawla, granted by the Fatimid caliph.

bumiputera.s: Bumiputera, 'sons of the soil', is the Malaysian term for the Malays and the indigenous peoples of the country, including the Orang Asli and the peoples of Sabah and Sarawak. Article 153 of the constitution protects their special position, and since 1971 the New Economic…

balaji-baji-rao.s: Balaji Baji Rao, known as Nanasaheb, was Peshwa of the Maratha Empire from 1740 to 1761, the son of Baji Rao I. Under him Maratha power reached its widest extent, from the Punjab to Bengal and the south, and the Peshwa became the real ruler of the Maratha state.

battle-of-jena-auerstedt.s: The twin battles of Jena and Auerstedt were fought on 14 October 1806 in Thuringia: Napoleon defeated part of the Prussian army at Jena, while Marshal Davout routed the main Prussian force at Auerstedt. The collapse of the Prussian army that followed let French troops enter…

brandenburg-recess-of-1653.s: The Recess of 1653 was the agreement concluded in 1653 between Frederick William, the Great Elector, and the estates of Brandenburg. The nobility granted him 530,000 thalers over five years to maintain a standing army, and in return he confirmed their privileges, including…

bruno-of-schauenburg.s: Bruno of Schauenburg was Bishop of Olomouc from 1245 to 1281, a German noble from Holstein who became the chief adviser of King Ottokar II of Bohemia. He promoted the settlement of German colonists in Moravia, founding villages and towns under German law, among them Kroměříž.

babad-tanah-jawi.s: The Babad Tanah Jawi ('Chronicle of the Land of Java') is a group of Javanese court chronicles in verse, written down in several versions from the late seventeenth century onwards at the courts of Kartasura and Surakarta. They trace the kings of Java from legendary origins…

battle-of-gegodog.s: The Battle of Gegodog was fought in October 1676 near Tuban on the north coast of Java during the Trunajaya rebellion. Madurese and Makassarese forces under Trunajaya defeated a large Mataram army led by the crown prince, the future Amangkurat II.

blambangan.s: Blambangan was a Hindu kingdom at the eastern tip of Java, the last Hindu-Buddhist state on the island, which survived into the eighteenth century. Often allied with or subject to Balinese kingdoms, it resisted the campaigns of Sultan Agung of Mataram in the 1630s.

betsimitatatra.s: The Betsimitatatra is the plain of the Ikopa river below Antananarivo in the central highlands of Madagascar. From the late eighteenth century Andrianampoinimerina organised communal labour to drain it and build dikes, turning it into the main rice-growing land of Imerina.

battle-of-puebla.s: The Battle of Puebla was fought on 5 May 1862 during the French intervention in Mexico, when Mexican troops under General Ignacio Zaragoza repulsed a French assault on the forts above Puebla. Although the French took Puebla the following year, the victory became a national…

battle-of-celaya.s: The Battle of Celaya, in April 1915, was a pair of engagements near Celaya in Guanajuato in which Constitutionalist forces under Álvaro Obregón defeated Pancho Villa's Division of the North. Using trenches, barbed wire and machine guns, Obregón broke repeated cavalry charges…

bay-of-campeche.s: The Bay of Campeche, or Gulf of Campeche, is the southern part of the Gulf of Mexico, bordered by the Mexican states of Veracruz, Tabasco and Campeche. Its offshore fields, above all Cantarell, discovered in the 1970s, made it the centre of Mexico's oil production.

bahr-yusuf.s: The Bahr Yusuf ('waterway of Joseph') is a channel that branches from the Nile in Middle Egypt and flows into the Faiyum depression. Kings of the Twelfth Dynasty, especially Senusret II and Amenemhat III, controlled its waters to reclaim land and extend cultivation in the Faiyum.

beni-hasan.s: Beni Hasan is an ancient cemetery on the east bank of the Nile in Middle Egypt, near Minya. Its rock-cut tombs of the Eleventh and Twelfth Dynasties belonged to the nomarchs of the Oryx nome, and their paintings show daily life, wrestling, warfare and a caravan of Asiatic…

buhen.s: Buhen was an Egyptian fortress and settlement on the west bank of the Nile near the Second Cataract, in Lower Nubia. Built in its massive form under Senusret I, with mud-brick walls, bastions and a ditch, it controlled the river frontier with Nubia and was reused in the New…

burma-independence-army.s: The Burma Independence Army was a nationalist force formed in Bangkok in December 1941 by Aung San and the Thirty Comrades with Japanese support. It advanced into Burma alongside the Japanese invasion of 1942, growing rapidly, and was reorganised by the Japanese as the Burma…

burma-socialist-programme-party.s: The Burma Socialist Programme Party was the ruling party of Burma under Ne Win. Founded by the Revolutionary Council in 1962, it became the sole legal party in 1964 and under the 1974 constitution ruled the Socialist Republic of the Union of Burma, following the ideology of…

battle-of-kursk.s: The Battle of Kursk was fought on the Eastern Front in July and August 1943, when Germany attacked the Soviet salient around Kursk in Operation Citadel. Prepared Soviet defences halted the offensive within days, and Soviet counter-offensives retook Oryol and Kharkov.

battle-of-stalingrad.s: The Battle of Stalingrad was fought from August 1942 to February 1943 for the city of Stalingrad, now Volgograd, on the Volga. After German forces took most of the city in brutal street fighting, the Soviet Operation Uranus in November 1942 encircled the Sixth Army, whose…

belzec-extermination-camp.s: Bełżec was a Nazi extermination camp in south-eastern German-occupied Poland, the first built for Operation Reinhard, the plan to murder the Jews of the General Government. Between March and December 1942 some 430,000 to 500,000 Jews were killed there in gas chambers, and only…

battle-of-carillon.s: The Battle of Carillon was fought on 8 July 1758 at Fort Carillon, later Ticonderoga, on Lake Champlain. About 3,600 French troops under the Marquis de Montcalm, behind a log entrenchment, repulsed repeated frontal attacks by a British army of some 16,000 under James…

battle-of-the-monongahela.s: The Battle of the Monongahela was fought on 9 July 1755 near the Monongahela River, east of Fort Duquesne in present-day Pennsylvania. A British and colonial army under General Edward Braddock, marching to take the fort, was ambushed by a smaller force of French troops and…

bartolome-de-medina.s: Bartolomé de Medina was a Spanish merchant who in the 1550s at Pachuca in New Spain developed the patio process, which extracted silver from ore by mixing it with mercury, salt and copper sulphate in open yards. The method made it profitable to work low-grade ores, and it…

battle-of-calderon-bridge.s: The Battle of Calderón Bridge was fought on 17 January 1811 near Guadalajara during the Mexican War of Independence. A disciplined royalist army of about 6,000 under Félix María Calleja routed the much larger but poorly armed insurgent host of Miguel Hidalgo and Ignacio…

british-nationality-and-new-zealand-citi.n: British Nationality and New Zealand Citizenship Act 1948
british-nationality-and-new-zealand-citi.s: The British Nationality and New Zealand Citizenship Act 1948 created a separate New Zealand citizenship for the first time, taking effect on 1 January 1949. New Zealand citizens remained British subjects, in line with the arrangements agreed among Commonwealth countries after…

battle-of-ky-hoa.s: The Battle of Kỳ Hòa was fought on 24–25 February 1861 near Saigon, when a French force under Admiral Léonard Charner stormed the Vietnamese fortified lines commanded by Nguyễn Tri Phương. The victory broke the siege of the French garrison in Saigon and allowed France to…

battle-of-thapsus.s: The Battle of Thapsus was fought on 6 April 46 BCE near Thapsus, on the coast of present-day Tunisia, between Julius Caesar and the Pompeian forces of Metellus Scipio, supported by King Juba I of Numidia. Caesar's decisive victory destroyed the republican cause in Africa, and…

battle-of-the-bagradas-river-49-bce.n: Battle of the Bagradas River (49 BCE)
battle-of-the-bagradas-river-49-bce.s: The Battle of the Bagradas River was fought in August 49 BCE in the province of Africa, near the river now called the Medjerda in Tunisia. Gaius Scribonius Curio, leading Caesar's invasion of Africa, was lured into an ambush by Saburra, general of King Juba I of Numidia, and…

battle-of-the-muthul.s: The Battle of the Muthul was fought in 109 BCE near the Muthul River in Numidia between the Roman army of the consul Quintus Caecilius Metellus and King Jugurtha. Jugurtha ambushed the Romans on the march, but after a hard day's fighting Metellus drove off the Numidians.

bulla-regia.s: Bulla Regia is an ancient city in north-western Tunisia, near Jendouba. A residence of the Numidian kings, as its name suggests, it became a prosperous Roman town after the annexation of Numidia.

bellum-iugurthinum.s: The Bellum Iugurthinum is a historical monograph by Sallust, written around 40 BCE, on Rome's war against the Numidian king Jugurtha in 112–105 BCE. Using the war to show the corruption of the Roman nobility and the rise of Gaius Marius, it also includes a description of North…

berisades.s: Berisades was one of the three kings among whom the Odrysian Kingdom was divided after the murder of Cotys I in 360 BCE, ruling the western part towards the Strymon. He and his successor Cetriporis allied with Athens against Cersobleptes and, from 356 BCE, against Philip II of…

battle-of-novara-1513.s: The Battle of Novara was fought on 6 June 1513 near Novara in northern Italy, when a Swiss army defending Duke Massimiliano Sforza of Milan made a surprise attack on the French army under Louis de La Trémoille and routed it. The victory marked the height of Swiss military…

battle-of-st-jakob-an-der-birs.n: Battle of St. Jakob an der Birs
battle-of-st-jakob-an-der-birs.s: The Battle of St. Jakob an der Birs was fought on 26 August 1444 outside Basel, when about 1,500 Swiss Confederates attacked a far larger French army of Armagnac mercenaries led by the Dauphin Louis, the future Louis XI. The Swiss force was almost entirely destroyed, but its…

battle-of-boomplaats.s: The Battle of Boomplaats was fought on 29 August 1848 in the south of the present-day Free State of South Africa, between British troops under Sir Harry Smith and Boer forces under Andries Pretorius. The British victory confirmed the annexation of the Orange River Sovereignty,…

bloemfontein-conference.s: The Bloemfontein Conference was a meeting held in Bloemfontein from 31 May to 5 June 1899 between Paul Kruger, president of the South African Republic, and Alfred Milner, the British High Commissioner, hosted by President Steyn of the Orange Free State. The talks, chiefly…

battle-of-magersfontein.s: The Battle of Magersfontein was fought on 11 December 1899 near Kimberley, in the Second Boer War, when Boer forces under Piet Cronjé and Koos de la Rey, dug into trenches at the foot of the hills, repulsed a British attack under Lord Methuen. The defeat, which fell in the…

battle-of-paardeberg.s: The Battle of Paardeberg was fought from 18 to 27 February 1900 on the Modder River, in the Second Boer War. British forces under Lord Roberts and Lord Kitchener surrounded Piet Cronjé's retreating army and, after a costly assault and a siege of the Boer laager, forced about…

battle-of-sannas-post.s: The Battle of Sanna's Post was fought on 31 March 1900 at the waterworks east of Bloemfontein, in the Second Boer War. Boer forces under Christiaan de Wet ambushed a British column under Brigadier Robert Broadwood at a river crossing, inflicting heavy losses and capturing guns…

battle-of-preveza.s: The Battle of Preveza was a naval battle fought on 28 September 1538 off Preveza in north-western Greece, in which the Ottoman fleet under Hayreddin Barbarossa defeated the fleet of the Holy League commanded by Andrea Doria. The victory secured Ottoman naval dominance in the…

badagry.s: Badagry is a coastal town in Lagos State, Nigeria, on a lagoon near the border with Benin. From the eighteenth century it was a major port of the Atlantic slave trade, through which captives from the Oyo Empire and its neighbours were shipped.

bamar-people.s: The Bamar, or Burmans, are the largest ethnic group of Myanmar, forming about two-thirds of its population and living mainly in the central Irrawaddy valley. Speakers of Burmese, a Sino-Tibetan language, they moved south into the dry zone of central Myanmar in the ninth…

battle-of-ngasaunggyan.s: The Battle of Ngasaunggyan was fought in 1277 near the frontier between the Pagan Kingdom and Yunnan, after King Narathihapate refused the tribute demanded by the Mongol Yuan dynasty. Yuan cavalry from Yunnan defeated a Burmese army that included war elephants, a battle…

balaputradeva.s: Balaputradeva was a prince of the Shailendra dynasty of Java who became ruler of Srivijaya in Sumatra in the ninth century. A copper-plate grant of the Pala king Devapala records that, at Balaputradeva's request, five villages were granted to support a monastery he had built…

badal-pillar-inscription.s: The Badal pillar inscription is a Sanskrit inscription on a stone pillar topped by a figure of Garuda at Badal in northern Bangladesh, set up by Guravamishra during the reign of the Pala king Narayanapala. It records a Brahmin family whose members served successive Pala kings…

battle-of-tellaru.s: The Battle of Tellaru was fought in the mid-ninth century at Tellaru, near Vandavasi in northern Tamil Nadu, where the Pallava king Nandivarman III defeated the Pandyas and their allies. The victory restored Pallava prestige and is celebrated in the Tamil poem…

ballari.s: Ballari, formerly Bellary, is a city in eastern Karnataka, India, known for the fort on the great granite rock that overlooks it. The surrounding region, rich in iron ore, has a long history: the earliest Pallava charters of the fourth century record grants of land there, and…

brahma.s: Brahma is the Hindu god of creation, who with Vishnu and Shiva forms the Trimurti. He is usually shown with four faces and four arms, seated on a lotus that rises from the navel of Vishnu.

battle-of-pullalur.s: The Battle of Pullalur was fought around 618–619 near Kanchipuram between the Pallava king Mahendravarman I and the Chalukya king Pulakeshin II, who had invaded Pallava territory. The Pallavas claimed it as a victory that saved their capital, though Pulakeshin took the…

battle-of-ostia.s: The Battle of Ostia was fought in 849 off Ostia, the port of Rome, between Muslim raiders from North Africa and an allied fleet from Naples, Amalfi, Gaeta and Sorrento. Assisted by a storm that scattered the raiding fleet, the Christian allies won, and many captives were put…

battle-of-castelfidardo.s: The Battle of Castelfidardo was fought on 18 September 1860 near Ancona between the army of the Kingdom of Sardinia under Enrico Cialdini and the papal army under the French general Lamoricière. The Sardinian victory allowed the occupation of the Marche and Umbria, which voted…

battle-of-mentana.s: The Battle of Mentana was fought on 3 November 1867 near Mentana, north-east of Rome, between the volunteers of Giuseppe Garibaldi, who were trying to seize Rome, and papal troops supported by a French expeditionary force. The French and papal victory, aided by the new French…

battle-of-chamdo.s: The Battle of Chamdo was fought in October 1950 in eastern Tibet, when the People's Liberation Army crossed the Jinsha River and defeated the Tibetan army around the town of Chamdo, capturing the regional governor Ngapoi Ngawang Jigme. The defeat left Lhasa without effective…

battle-of-brustem.s: The Battle of Brustem was fought on 28 October 1467 near Sint-Truiden, in present-day Belgium, between the army of Liège and Charles the Bold, Duke of Burgundy. The Liège militias were defeated, and the city had to accept harsh terms; after a further rising it was sacked by…

battle-of-steppes.s: The Battle of Steppes was fought on 13 October 1213 near Montenaken, in present-day Belgium, between the forces of the prince-bishop of Liège and Duke Henry I of Brabant. The Liège militias and their allies won a clear victory, checking Brabant's expansion towards Liège; it…

battle-of-karydi.s: The Battle of Karydi was fought in 1258 at the Karydi pass between Megara and Thebes, in central Greece. Prince William II of Villehardouin of Achaea defeated Guy I de la Roche, lord of Athens, and his allies, confirming his supremacy over the Frankish states of Greece.

battle-of-manolada.s: The Battle of Manolada was fought on 5 July 1316 in Elis, in the north-western Peloponnese, between rival claimants to the Principality of Achaea. Louis of Burgundy defeated and killed Ferdinand of Majorca, who had invaded the principality on behalf of his infant son.

battle-of-makryplagi.s: The Battle of Makryplagi was fought in 1264 in a mountain pass of the central Peloponnese between the Principality of Achaea and the Byzantine army. The Franks won, capturing the Byzantine commanders and halting the first Byzantine offensive from Mistras, after the earlier…

battle-of-prinitza.s: The Battle of Prinitza was fought in 1263 near Olympia in the western Peloponnese between a small Frankish force of the Principality of Achaea and a much larger Byzantine army. The Franks won a surprising victory, halting the Byzantine advance from Mistras.

bernat-desclot.s: Bernat Desclot was a Catalan chronicler of the late thirteenth century. His chronicle, written in Catalan, covers the history of the counts of Barcelona and kings of Aragon up to 1285, with a detailed account of Peter III's reign, and is one of the four great Catalan chronicles.

boris-smyslovsky.s: Boris Smyslovsky was a Russian émigré officer who served in the German army in the Second World War, commanding the First Russian National Army against the Soviet Union. In May 1945 he led some 500 of his men into Liechtenstein, which refused Soviet demands for their…

benes-decrees.s: The Beneš decrees were the laws issued by the Czechoslovak president Edvard Beneš in exile and in 1945 before the parliament reconvened. They provided for the confiscation of property of Germans, Hungarians and collaborators and the loss of their citizenship, forming the legal…

baia-romania.s: Baia is a village in Suceava County, Romania, and one of the oldest towns of Moldavia, with an early Saxon community and a Catholic church. In December 1467 Stephen the Great defeated the invading Hungarian king Matthias Corvinus there, ending Hungarian attempts to subdue…

barlad-river.s: The Bârlad is a river in eastern Romania, about 207 kilometres long, a left tributary of the Siret. Near its course, close to Vaslui, Stephen the Great defeated an Ottoman army in January 1475.

battle-of-vaslui.s: The Battle of Vaslui was fought on 10 January 1475 at Podul Înalt near Vaslui, in Moldavia. Stephen the Great, with a much smaller army, destroyed an Ottoman force under Hadım Suleiman Pasha in fog and marshy ground, one of the greatest Christian victories over the Ottomans of…

bender-moldova.s: Bender, also called Tighina, is a city on the Dniester in Moldova, under the control of the breakaway Transnistria. Captured by the Ottomans in 1538 and fortified, it was a key Ottoman fortress, where Charles XII of Sweden sheltered after Poltava; it passed to Russia in 1812.

bogdan-iii-the-one-eyed.s: Bogdan III the One-Eyed was prince of Moldavia from 1504 to 1517, the son and successor of Stephen the Great. He kept the peace with the Ottomans by paying tribute in exchange for autonomy and fought Poland over the border region of Pokuttya.

bilhorod-dnistrovskyi.s: Bilhorod-Dnistrovskyi, known as Cetatea Albă in Romanian and Akkerman in Turkish, is a port on the Dniester estuary in Ukraine, near the Black Sea, on the site of ancient Tyras. A Moldavian port and fortress from the late fourteenth century, it was taken by the Ottomans in…

battle-of-the-cosmin-forest.s: The Battle of the Cosmin Forest was fought on 26 October 1497 in northern Moldavia, in present-day Ukraine. Stephen the Great ambushed the retreating army of the Polish king John I Albert after his failed siege of Suceava, ending Polish attempts to control Moldavia.

book-of-psalms.s: The Book of Psalms is a collection of 150 religious poems and songs in the Hebrew Bible and the Christian Old Testament, composed over several centuries and traditionally attributed in large part to King David. Used in the worship of the Second Temple, synagogue and church,…

battle-of-valea-alba.s: The Battle of Valea Albă, also called the Battle of Războieni, was fought on 26 July 1476 in north-eastern Moldavia, where the Ottoman sultan Mehmed II defeated the outnumbered army of Stephen the Great. Despite the victory, the Ottomans failed to take the fortresses of…

balhara.s: Balhara was the name by which Arab travellers and geographers of the ninth and tenth centuries, such as Sulaiman the Merchant, Ibn Khordadbeh and al-Masudi, referred to the Rashtrakuta kings of the Deccan. It is generally explained as a corruption of the royal title Vallabharaja.

battle-of-takkolam.s: The Battle of Takkolam was fought in 949 near Takkolam, north-west of Kanchipuram in present-day Tamil Nadu, between the Rashtrakuta emperor Krishna III, allied with the Western Ganga king Butuga II, and the army of the Chola king Parantaka I. The Chola crown prince Rajaditya…

bunnag-family.s: The Bunnag family was a noble family of Siam, descended from the Persian merchant Sheikh Ahmad who settled in Ayutthaya in the early seventeenth century. Its members held the great ministries of the Rattanakosin court for much of the nineteenth century, and Si Suriyawong…

burney-treaty.s: The Burney Treaty was an agreement signed in June 1826 between Siam and the British East India Company, negotiated by Captain Henry Burney during the First Anglo-Burmese War. It allowed British merchants to trade in Siam on payment of a fixed duty based on the width of their…

barbary-coast.s: The Barbary Coast was the name used by Europeans from the sixteenth to the nineteenth century for the Mediterranean coast of North Africa, from Morocco through Algiers and Tunis to Tripoli. The term derives from the Berbers.

battle-of-tacna.s: The Battle of Tacna, or of the Alto de la Alianza, was fought on 26 May 1880 near Tacna in southern Peru during the War of the Pacific. The Chilean army defeated the allied Peruvian and Bolivian forces commanded by the Bolivian president Narciso Campero.

battle-of-ayacucho.s: The Battle of Ayacucho was fought on 9 December 1824 in the Peruvian highlands, where a patriot army under Antonio José de Sucre defeated and captured the Spanish viceroy José de la Serna. The capitulation that followed ended the royalist army in Peru and effectively ended…

battle-of-tumusla.s: The Battle of Tumusla was fought on 1 April 1825 in Upper Peru, present-day Bolivia, between the last royalist forces under Pedro Antonio Olañeta and troops who had turned against him. Olañeta was mortally wounded, and royalist resistance in Upper Peru collapsed.

battle-of-angamos.s: The Battle of Angamos was a naval battle fought on 8 October 1879 off the coast of Antofagasta during the War of the Pacific. Chilean warships cornered and captured the Peruvian ironclad Huáscar, and the Peruvian admiral Miguel Grau was killed.

battle-of-iquique.s: The Battle of Iquique was a naval battle fought on 21 May 1879 off the port of Iquique during the War of the Pacific. The Peruvian ironclad Huáscar sank the old Chilean corvette Esmeralda, whose captain Arturo Prat was killed while boarding the enemy ship, while the Peruvian…

battle-of-lircay.s: The Battle of Lircay was fought on 17 April 1830 near Talca and ended the Chilean civil war of 1829–1830. Conservative forces under General Joaquín Prieto defeated the liberal army led by Ramón Freire.

battle-of-yungay.s: The Battle of Yungay was fought on 20 January 1839 in the Peruvian Andes, where a Chilean army under General Manuel Bulnes, joined by Peruvian exiles, defeated the forces of Andrés de Santa Cruz. The defeat destroyed the Peru–Bolivian Confederation, which split back into Peru…

beagle-channel.s: The Beagle Channel is a strait in the Tierra del Fuego archipelago at the southern tip of South America, named after HMS Beagle. Sovereignty over the islands at its eastern end was disputed between Chile and Argentina and brought them close to war in 1978.

battle-of-guningtou.s: The Battle of Guningtou was fought on Kinmen island, off the Fujian coast, from 25 to 27 October 1949. Nationalist forces destroyed a Communist landing force of about 9,000 men, most of whom were killed or captured.

battle-of-shanghai.s: The Battle of Shanghai was fought from August to November 1937 in and around Shanghai, the first major battle of the Second Sino-Japanese War. Chiang Kai-shek committed many of his best German-trained divisions, which held out for three months at a cost of very heavy casualties.

battle-of-zarumilla.s: The Battle of Zarumilla was fought in July 1941 near the Zarumilla River on the border between Ecuador and Peru. A larger, better-equipped Peruvian army, using aircraft and paratroops, defeated the Ecuadorian forces and occupied the province of El Oro.

brasilia-presidential-act.s: The Brasília Presidential Act was signed on 26 October 1998 by Presidents Jamil Mahuad of Ecuador and Alberto Fujimori of Peru, with the guarantor states of the Rio de Janeiro Protocol. It fixed the last undemarcated section of their border in the Cordillera del Cóndor, ending…

battle-of-la-arada.s: The Battle of La Arada was fought on 2 February 1851 near Chiquimula in eastern Guatemala. Guatemalan forces under Rafael Carrera routed a larger allied army from El Salvador and Honduras that had invaded to overthrow him and restore the Central American federation.

battle-of-cesis.s: The Battle of Cēsis was fought in June 1919 around the town of Cēsis in northern Latvia. Estonian forces and the Northern Latvian Brigade defeated the Baltic Landeswehr and German Freikorps units under Rüdiger von der Goltz, ending German attempts to dominate the Baltic region.

battle-of-tannenberg-line.s: The Battle of Tannenberg Line was fought in July and August 1944 at the Sinimäed hills near Narva in north-eastern Estonia. German forces, including many Estonian conscripts and volunteers, held a defensive line against a much larger Soviet offensive, inflicting heavy losses.

battle-of-suomussalmi.s: The Battle of Suomussalmi was fought in the forests of north-eastern Finland from December 1939 to January 1940, during the Winter War. Finnish ski troops under Colonel Hjalmar Siilasvuo cut the road-bound Soviet 163rd and 44th Divisions into isolated pockets, known as motti,…

battle-of-tali-ihantala.s: The Battle of Tali-Ihantala, fought from 25 June to 9 July 1944 north-east of Viipuri, was the largest battle ever fought in the Nordic countries. Finnish forces, supported by German anti-tank weapons and aircraft, halted the Soviet summer offensive on the Karelian Isthmus,…

battle-of-benevento.s: The Battle of Benevento was fought on 26 February 1266 near Benevento in southern Italy between the army of Charles of Anjou and that of Manfred, King of Sicily. Manfred was killed and his army destroyed, giving Charles the Kingdom of Sicily and ending Hohenstaufen power in…

battle-of-gavinana.s: The Battle of Gavinana was fought on 3 August 1530 at the village of Gavinana in the Apennines north-west of Florence. A Florentine relief army under Francesco Ferrucci, trying to break the imperial siege of the city, was defeated by imperial troops whose commander, the Prince…

battle-of-montaperti.s: The Battle of Montaperti was fought on 4 September 1260 near Siena between the Guelph army of Florence and a Ghibelline force of Siena, Florentine exiles under Farinata degli Uberti and German cavalry sent by King Manfred of Sicily. The Florentines were routed with heavy…

balilla.s: Balilla is the nickname of the boy who, according to tradition, started the popular uprising in Genoa against occupying Austrian troops on 5 December 1746 by throwing a stone at soldiers in the Portoria quarter. The revolt drove the Austrians from the city within days.

battle-of-curzola.s: The Battle of Curzola was a naval battle fought on 9 September 1298 off the island of Curzola, now Korčula, in the Adriatic between the fleets of Genoa and Venice. The Genoese admiral Lamba Doria won a crushing victory, capturing most of the Venetian galleys and thousands of…

battle-of-meloria-1284.s: The Battle of Meloria was a naval battle fought on 6 August 1284 near the islet of Meloria off Livorno between Genoa and Pisa. The Genoese fleet under Oberto Doria and Benedetto Zaccaria destroyed the Pisan fleet and took thousands of prisoners, many of whom died in captivity.

bananagate.s: Bananagate was a bribery scandal of 1975 in which the US company United Brands, formerly the United Fruit Company, was found to have paid 1.25 million dollars to Honduran officials to secure a reduction of an export tax on bananas. The revelations, which followed the suicide…

bay-islands.s: The Bay Islands are a group of islands off the Caribbean coast of Honduras, the largest being Roatán, Utila and Guanaja, forming the department of Islas de la Bahía. Settled largely by English-speaking migrants from the Cayman Islands in the nineteenth century, alongside an…

babri-masjid.s: The Babri Masjid was a mosque in Ayodhya in northern India, built in 1528–1529 under the Mughal emperor Babur. Many Hindus believed it stood on the birthplace of the god Rama, and a long campaign by Hindu nationalist organisations culminated on 6 December 1992 in its…

bangladesh-liberation-war.s: The Bangladesh Liberation War was the conflict of 1971 in which East Pakistan won independence as Bangladesh. After the Pakistani army began a crackdown in March 1971, Bengali nationalist forces, the Mukti Bahini, fought a guerrilla war and some ten million refugees fled to…

bharatiya-janata-party.s: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) is an Indian political party founded in 1980 as the successor of the Bharatiya Jana Sangh, with close links to the Hindu nationalist Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh. It rose through the Ayodhya campaign of the late 1980s and early 1990s and led…

battle-of-sirvintos.s: The Battle of Širvintos was fought on 17–21 November 1920 near the town of Širvintos, north-west of Vilnius, between Lithuanian forces and the Polish troops of Lucjan Żeligowski, who had seized Vilnius in October. Together with the simultaneous Battle of Giedraičiai, it halted…

battle-of-giedraiciai.s: The Battle of Giedraičiai was fought on 19–21 November 1920 around Giedraičiai, north of Vilnius, where Lithuanian forces defeated troops of Lucjan Żeligowski, who had seized Vilnius for Poland the month before. Alongside the Battle of Širvintos, the victory stopped the Polish…

battle-of-radviliskis.s: The Battle of Radviliškis was fought in November 1919 around the railway town of Radviliškis in northern Lithuania, where Lithuanian forces defeated the West Russian Volunteer Army of Pavel Bermondt-Avalov. The victory, on 21–22 November, forced the Bermontians to withdraw…

benjamin-zeledon.s: Benjamín Zeledón was a Nicaraguan lawyer, politician and general who led a Liberal rising in 1912 against the Conservative government of Adolfo Díaz. United States Marines landed to support the government, and Zeledón was killed in October 1912 after the fall of his positions…

bryan-chamorro-treaty.s: The Bryan–Chamorro Treaty was signed in 1914 by the US Secretary of State William Jennings Bryan and the Nicaraguan minister Emiliano Chamorro, and ratified in 1916. For three million dollars it gave the United States perpetual rights to build a canal through Nicaragua, leases…

bocas-del-toro-province.s: Bocas del Toro is a province in north-western Panama on the Caribbean coast, bordering Costa Rica and including the Bocas del Toro archipelago. From the late nineteenth century it became a centre of banana growing, dominated from 1899 by the United Fruit Company, which brought…

battle-of-callao.s: The Battle of Callao was fought on 2 May 1866 between a Spanish naval squadron under Casto Méndez Núñez and the coastal fortifications of Callao, Peru's main port, during the Chincha Islands War. After a day-long bombardment both sides claimed victory, but the Spanish fleet…

battle-of-ingavi.s: The Battle of Ingavi was fought on 18 November 1841 near Viacha, south-west of La Paz, between the Bolivian army under José Ballivián and an invading Peruvian army led by President Agustín Gamarra. The Bolivians won a decisive victory and Gamarra was killed, ending Peruvian…

battle-of-khotyn-1621.s: The Battle of Khotyn was fought in September and October 1621 at the fortress of Khotyn on the Dniester, where a Polish-Lithuanian army under Jan Karol Chodkiewicz, aided by Zaporozhian Cossacks, withstood a much larger Ottoman army led by Sultan Osman II. The siege ended in a…

benedikt-kotruljevic.s: Benedikt Kotruljević (Benedetto Cotrugli) was a merchant, diplomat and writer from Ragusa (Dubrovnik) who served the Aragonese kings of Naples. His treatise on trade and the merchant's life, written in 1458 and printed in Venice in 1573, contains one of the earliest known…

bantu-education-act-1953.s: The Bantu Education Act of 1953 was a South African apartheid law that placed African schooling under the central government's Native Affairs Department and enforced a separate, deliberately inferior curriculum for black children. Most mission schools, which had educated many…

black-consciousness-movement.s: The Black Consciousness Movement was a South African anti-apartheid movement of the late 1960s and 1970s led by Steve Biko and others, beginning with the South African Students' Organisation in 1968. It urged black South Africans to reject white tutelage and build…

black-economic-empowerment.s: Black Economic Empowerment is a South African government policy, given legal form by the Broad-Based Black Economic Empowerment Act of 2003, that aims to redress the economic inequalities of apartheid. It encourages black ownership, management, employment and procurement…

battle-of-cuito-cuanavale.s: The Battle of Cuito Cuanavale was a series of engagements in south-eastern Angola between August 1987 and March 1988, in which Angolan government forces backed by Cuba fought UNITA and the South African Defence Force. The South African advance failed to take the town, while…

bajamonte-tiepolo.s: Bajamonte Tiepolo was a Venetian nobleman who led a conspiracy in June 1310 to overthrow Doge Pietro Gradenigo, whose policies, including the closing of the Great Council in 1297, had angered rival noble houses. The plotters were defeated in fighting near St Mark's Square, and…

bartolomeo-colleoni.s: Bartolomeo Colleoni was an Italian condottiere from Bergamo who served both Venice and Milan before becoming captain-general of the Venetian army for life in 1455. He left much of his fortune to the republic on condition that a statue of him be raised in Venice.

battle-of-agnadello.s: The Battle of Agnadello was fought on 14 May 1509 in Lombardy, when the French army of Louis XII routed the Venetian army. Coming early in the War of the League of Cambrai, it cost Venice almost all of its mainland territories within weeks.

bab-el-mandeb.s: The Bab-el-Mandeb is the strait, about 30 kilometres wide at its narrowest, between Yemen on the Arabian Peninsula and Djibouti and Eritrea in Africa, joining the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden. Since the opening of the Suez Canal in 1869 it has been one of the world's busiest…

bernt-notke.s: Bernt Notke was a painter and sculptor based in Lübeck, the leading artist of the Baltic region in the late 15th century. His works include the Danse Macabre now in St Nicholas' Church in Tallinn (Reval), the high altar of Tallinn's Church of the Holy Spirit and the monumental…

brotherhood-of-blackheads.s: The Brotherhood of Blackheads was an association of unmarried merchants, ship-owners and foreign traders in the towns of Livonia, first recorded in Reval (Tallinn) around 1400 and later in Riga. Its members joined in the defence of the town and held festivities in their own…

battle-of-myonessus.s: The Battle of Myonessus was a naval battle fought off the coast of Ionia in 190 BCE, in which a Roman and Rhodian fleet under Lucius Aemilius Regillus defeated the Seleucid fleet commanded by Polyxenidas. The victory gave the Romans control of the Aegean and allowed their army…

bignor-roman-villa.s: Bignor Roman Villa is the site of a large Roman courtyard villa near Chichester in West Sussex, England, discovered in 1811. Developed from a modest farmhouse into one of the largest villas in Britain by the fourth century, it is known for its fine mosaics, including scenes of…

boudica.s: Boudica was queen of the Iceni of eastern Britain who led a great revolt against Roman rule in 60 or 61 CE after the Romans seized her late husband's kingdom and mistreated her family. Her forces destroyed Camulodunum (Colchester), Londinium (London) and Verulamium (St…

britannia-inferior.s: Britannia Inferior was the northern of the two provinces into which Roman Britain was divided in the early third century, governed from Eboracum (York) and including Hadrian's Wall and the legion at York. The division, attributed to Septimius Severus or Caracalla, aimed to…

britannia-superior.s: Britannia Superior was the southern of the two provinces into which Roman Britain was divided in the early third century, governed from Londinium (London) and including the legions at Caerleon and Chester. The division, attributed to Septimius Severus or Caracalla, aimed to…

britannia-prima.s: Britannia Prima was one of the provinces created in Roman Britain by the reforms of Diocletian around 300. It probably covered western Britain, including Wales and the West Country, with its capital likely at Corinium (Cirencester).

britannia-secunda.s: Britannia Secunda was one of the provinces created in Roman Britain by the reforms of Diocletian around 300. It covered northern England, including Hadrian's Wall, with its capital at Eboracum (York).

berenice-troglodytica.s: Berenice Troglodytica, or Berenike, was a port on the Red Sea coast of Egypt founded by Ptolemy II in the third century BCE. Under Roman rule it was one of the main harbours for trade with Arabia, East Africa and India, linked by desert roads to Coptos on the Nile.

battle-of-beneventum-275-bc.s: The Battle of Beneventum was fought in southern Italy in 275 BCE between a Roman army under the consul Manius Curius Dentatus and Pyrrhus of Epirus. It was the last battle of the Pyrrhic War.

battle-of-the-allia.s: The Battle of the Allia was fought around 390 BCE, or 387 BCE by Greek reckoning, near the River Allia north of Rome, where a Gallic army under Brennus routed the Romans. The Gauls then sacked Rome, and the day of the defeat, 18 July, was long regarded as unlucky.

battle-of-vercellae.s: The Battle of Vercellae was fought in 101 BCE on the Raudine Plain in northern Italy, where Roman armies under Gaius Marius and Quintus Lutatius Catulus destroyed the Cimbri. Coming a year after Marius's victory over the Teutones at Aquae Sextiae, it ended the Cimbrian War,…

battle-of-warsaw-1920.s: The Battle of Warsaw was fought in August 1920 during the Polish–Soviet War, when Polish forces under Józef Piłsudski counter-attacked the Red Army advancing on the Polish capital. The Soviet armies under Mikhail Tukhachevsky were routed and driven back.

battle-of-okinawa.s: The Battle of Okinawa was fought from April to June 1945 between American and Japanese forces on Okinawa, the largest battle of the Pacific War on Japanese territory. It killed about 100,000 Japanese soldiers and conscripts, more than 12,000 Americans and tens of thousands of…

battle-of-tadla.s: The Battle of Tadla was fought in September 1554 near Tadla in central Morocco between the Saadi sultan Muhammad al-Shaykh and the Wattasid Ali Abu Hassun, who had retaken Fez earlier that year with Ottoman troops from Algiers. Abu Hassun was defeated and killed, ending the…

ben-youssef-madrasa.s: The Ben Youssef Madrasa is an Islamic college in the medina of Marrakesh, founded in the fourteenth century under the Marinids and rebuilt on a larger scale by the Saadi sultan Abdallah al-Ghalib in the 1560s. Arranged around a courtyard with a pool and about 130 student…

battle-of-wadi-al-laban.s: The Battle of Wadi al-Laban was fought in 1558 near Fez between the Saadi sultan Abdallah al-Ghalib and an Ottoman army from Algiers led by Hasan Pasha, son of Hayreddin Barbarossa. The Saadi army checked the invaders, who withdrew to Algiers.

battle-of-the-jaxartes.s: The Battle of the Jaxartes was fought in 329 BCE on the Syr Darya, near the newly founded Alexandria Eschate, between Alexander the Great and Saka nomads from beyond the river. Using catapults to cover the crossing and combining cavalry with light troops to pin the mounted…

besshatyr-kurgans.s: The Besshatyr kurgans are a Saka burial ground on the right bank of the Ili river in south-eastern Kazakhstan, dated to around the fifth and fourth centuries BCE. The cemetery has some thirty mounds, the largest about 17 metres high and over 100 metres across, with log burial…

battle-of-amorgos.s: The Battle of Amorgos was a naval battle fought in 322 BCE near the island of Amorgos during the Lamian War. The Macedonian fleet under Cleitus the White defeated the Athenian navy, which had joined the Greek rising against Antipater after the death of Alexander the Great.

bahram-chobin.s: Bahram Chobin was a Sasanian general of the Mihran family who defeated the Turks in 588–589. Dismissed by Hormizd IV after a setback against the Byzantines, he rebelled and, after Hormizd's overthrow, drove the young Khosrow II from the throne, ruling as Bahram VI in 590–591.

bhaja-caves.s: The Bhaja Caves are a group of twenty-two rock-cut Buddhist caves near Lonavala in Maharashtra, India, dating from about the second century BCE. They include one of the earliest chaityas, or prayer halls, with a horseshoe-shaped facade imitating wooden architecture, and early…

brihatkatha.s: The Brihatkatha, 'Great Story', was a vast collection of tales attributed to the poet Gunadhya and written in Paishachi Prakrit, traditionally at a Satavahana court. The original is lost, but it is known through later retellings, including the Kathasaritsagara of Somadeva and…

bad-lippspringe.s: Bad Lippspringe is a spa town at the source of the Lippe river near Paderborn in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany. Charlemagne held Frankish assemblies there during the Saxon Wars, notably in 782, when he organised Saxony into counties shortly before the Saxon rising under…

battle-of-the-suntel.s: The Battle of the Süntel was fought in 782 in the Süntel hills near the Weser, in present-day Lower Saxony, when a Saxon army raised by Widukind destroyed a Frankish force that had been sent against the Sorbs. The defeat provoked Charlemagne's harsh response, the massacre of…

battle-of-klokotnitsa.s: The Battle of Klokotnitsa was fought on 9 March 1230 near the village of Klokotnitsa in southern Bulgaria. Tsar Ivan Asen II routed the army of Theodore Komnenos Doukas, ruler of Epirus and Thessalonica, who had broken a treaty and invaded Bulgaria, and took him prisoner.

battle-of-rusokastro.s: The Battle of Rusokastro was fought on 18 July 1332 near the fortress of Rusokastro, west of Burgas in south-eastern Bulgaria. Tsar Ivan Alexander defeated the Byzantine emperor Andronikos III Palaiologos and regained towns in northern Thrace lost in previous years.

boyana-church.s: Boyana Church is a medieval Bulgarian Orthodox church in the Boyana quarter of Sofia, built in stages from the tenth to the nineteenth centuries. Its second layer of frescoes, painted in 1259 for the sebastokrator Kaloyan and his wife Desislava, is famous for its lifelike…

battle-of-tryavna.s: The Battle of Tryavna was fought in 1190 in a pass of the Balkan Mountains near Tryavna, in present-day Bulgaria. The Bulgarian leaders Asen and Peter ambushed the army of the Byzantine emperor Isaac II Angelos as it withdrew from a failed siege of Tarnovo, and the emperor…

battle-of-jabani.s: The Battle of Jabani was fought in 1500 in Shirvan, in present-day Azerbaijan, between the young Safavid leader Ismail and the Shirvanshah Farrukh Yasar. Ismail's Qizilbash won, and Farrukh Yasar was killed, avenging the deaths of Ismail's father and grandfather at the hands…

battle-of-jamrud.s: The Battle of Jamrud was fought on 30 April 1837 at the fort of Jamrud, at the entrance to the Khyber Pass, between the Sikh Empire and an Afghan army sent by Dost Mohammad Khan. The Sikh general Hari Singh Nalwa was killed, but the garrison held out until relief came, and the…

battle-of-gwansan-fortress.s: The Battle of Gwansan Fortress was fought in 554 near present-day Okcheon in South Korea between Silla and an army of Baekje and its Gaya allies. Baekje had attacked to avenge Silla's seizure of the Han River valley, but King Seong of Baekje was ambushed and killed and his…

battle-of-hwangsanbeol.s: The Battle of Hwangsanbeol was fought in 660 near present-day Nonsan in South Korea between a large Silla army under Kim Yu-sin and a small Baekje force led by General Gyebaek. After several Baekje successes, Gyebaek was killed and his army destroyed.

bidam.s: Bidam was a Silla noble who held the highest court office, sangdaedeung, under Queen Seondeok. In 647 he rose in rebellion, reportedly declaring that a woman could not rule the country.

bukhansan.s: Bukhansan is a granite mountain on the northern edge of Seoul, South Korea, now the centre of a national park. On one of its peaks stood a stele set up by King Jinheung of Silla in the mid-sixth century to mark his conquest of the Han River region, now kept in the National…

battle-of-gibeolpo.s: The Battle of Gibeolpo was a naval battle fought in 676 near the mouth of the Geum River in western Korea between Silla and Tang China. After an initial defeat, the Silla fleet under Sideuk won a series of engagements against the Tang.

battle-of-maeso-fortress.s: The Battle of Maeso Fortress was fought in 675 at Maesoseong, a fortress north of present-day Seoul, between Silla and a Tang Chinese army. Silla's victory, followed by the naval battle of Gibeolpo in 676, ended the Silla–Tang War and forced the Tang to give up their attempt…

barack-obama.s: Barack Obama is an American politician who was the 44th president of the United States from 2009 to 2017, the first African American to hold the office. His presidency saw the response to the 2008 financial crisis, the Affordable Care Act and a 'pivot' of US policy towards Asia.

battle-of-tangdao.s: The Battle of Tangdao was a naval battle fought off the Shandong peninsula in late 1161, in which a small Southern Song fleet under Li Bao surprised and destroyed a much larger Jin fleet preparing to sail south. The Song used fire arrows and incendiary weapons against the…

battle-of-laings-nek.s: The Battle of Laing's Nek was fought on 28 January 1881 at a pass in the Drakensberg on the border between Natal and the Transvaal, during the First Boer War. A British force under Major-General Sir George Pomeroy Colley attacked Boer positions blocking the road into the…

battle-of-majuba-hill.s: The Battle of Majuba Hill, fought on 27 February 1881, was the decisive engagement of the First Boer War. A British force under Sir George Pomeroy Colley occupied the summit of Majuba, overlooking the Boer positions at Laing's Nek, but Boer riflemen climbed the slopes and…

boris-pasternak.s: Boris Pasternak was a Russian poet, novelist and translator, one of the major lyric poets of the twentieth century. His novel Doctor Zhivago, rejected by Soviet publishers, appeared in Italy in 1957 and became an international success.

battle-of-manila-bay.s: The Battle of Manila Bay was fought on 1 May 1898, at the start of the Spanish–American War, when the US Asiatic Squadron under Commodore George Dewey destroyed the Spanish Pacific squadron of Admiral Patricio Montojo off Cavite in the Philippines. The Americans lost no ships…

battle-of-santiago-de-cuba.s: The Battle of Santiago de Cuba was a naval battle fought on 3 July 1898 during the Spanish–American War. Admiral Pascual Cervera's Spanish squadron, blockaded in the harbour of Santiago, tried to break out and was destroyed by the American fleet, losing all its ships.

battle-of-artemisium.s: The Battle of Artemisium was a series of naval engagements fought over three days in August 480 BCE off the northern tip of Euboea, at the same time as the land battle at Thermopylae. The Greek fleet under the Spartan Eurybiades, with the Athenian contingent led by…

battle-of-hysiae.s: The Battle of Hysiae was fought between Argos and Sparta near Hysiae in the Argolid, traditionally dated by the geographer Pausanias to 669 BCE. The Argives defeated the Spartans, a victory often linked with the reign of the Argive king Pheidon, and it held back Spartan…

battle-of-the-champions.s: The Battle of the Champions was fought about 546 BCE between Sparta and Argos for the border district of Thyreatis. According to Herodotus, each side chose 300 men to settle the dispute; two Argives and one Spartan, Othryades, survived, and both sides claimed victory.

battle-of-sphacteria.s: The Battle of Sphacteria was fought in 425 BCE on the island of Sphacteria, which closes the bay of Pylos in Messenia, during the Peloponnesian War. After Athenian forces fortified Pylos, a Spartan force was cut off on the island; Athenian troops under Cleon and Demosthenes…

bai-qi.s: Bai Qi was a general of the State of Qin in the Warring States period and one of the most successful commanders of ancient China. He defeated Han and Wei at Yique in 293 BCE, captured the Chu capital Ying in 278 BCE and destroyed the army of Zhao at Changping in 260 BCE, where…

battle-of-bi.s: The Battle of Bi was fought in 597 BCE near the Yellow River in modern Henan, when King Zhuang of Chu defeated an army of Jin that had come to relieve the State of Zheng. The victory, described in the Zuo zhuan, made Chu the leading power of the central plain for a time and…

battle-of-chengpu.s: The Battle of Chengpu was fought in 632 BCE in modern Shandong between the State of Jin, under Duke Wen, with its allies Qi and Qin, and the forces of Chu and its allies. Jin's victory, won by feigned retreat and attacks on the weaker Chu wings, halted Chu's advance into the…

battle-of-yanling.s: The Battle of Yanling was fought in 575 BCE in modern Henan between the State of Jin and the State of Chu, which had come to support Zheng. Jin won, and King Gong of Chu was wounded in the eye by an arrow.

battle-of-boju.s: The Battle of Boju was fought in 506 BCE in modern Hubei, when King Helü of Wu, advised by the Chu exile Wu Zixu and traditionally by Sun Wu, invaded Chu and defeated its main army. Wu forces then took the Chu capital Ying, and King Zhao of Chu fled.

bao-shuya.s: Bao Shuya was a minister of the State of Qi in the seventh century BCE and the lifelong friend of Guan Zhong. After Duke Huan of Qi won the throne, Bao persuaded him to appoint Guan Zhong, who had served Huan's rival and even shot at him, as chief minister, which led to Qi's…

battle-of-an.s: The Battle of An was fought in 589 BCE in modern Shandong, when the State of Jin and its allies Lu and Wey defeated the State of Qi. Duke Qing of Qi narrowly escaped capture when his charioteer changed places with him.

battle-of-guiling.s: The Battle of Guiling was fought in 354 or 353 BCE during the Warring States period. When the State of Wei besieged Handan, capital of Zhao, Qi sent an army under Tian Ji and the strategist Sun Bin, which instead marched on the Wei capital Daliang and ambushed the returning…

battle-of-maling.s: The Battle of Maling was fought in 342 BCE between the State of Qi and the State of Wei, which had attacked Han. The Qi strategist Sun Bin feigned retreat, reducing the number of campfires each day to suggest desertion, and ambushed the pursuing Wei army in a narrow pass at…

baili-xi.s: Baili Xi was a minister of the State of Qin under Duke Mu in the seventh century BCE. Originally an official of the small state of Yu, he was taken captive when Jin conquered it; tradition says Duke Mu ransomed him for five ram skins.

battle-of-hanyuan.s: The Battle of Hanyuan, or Battle of Han, was fought in 645 BCE between the Chinese states of Qin and Jin. Duke Mu of Qin defeated Jin and captured Duke Hui of Jin, who had broken his promises to Qin and refused it grain during a famine.

book-of-lord-shang.s: The Book of Lord Shang is a Chinese political text attributed to Shang Yang, the reforming minister of Qin, though it was largely compiled by his followers in the fourth and third centuries BCE. It argues that a state grows strong by concentrating its people on farming and…

battle-of-changping.s: The Battle of Changping, fought from 262 to 260 BCE near present-day Gaoping in Shanxi, was the decisive clash between the Chinese states of Qin and Zhao. The Qin general Bai Qi surrounded the Zhao army under Zhao Kuo, who was killed.

battle-of-yique.s: The Battle of Yique was fought in 293 BCE near Luoyang, in present-day Henan, between the State of Qin and the allied armies of Han and Wei. The Qin general Bai Qi won a crushing victory; the Shiji claims 240,000 enemy dead.

battle-of-rudau.s: The Battle of Rudau was fought on 17 February 1370 near Rudau in Sambia, present-day Kaliningrad Oblast, Russia. The Teutonic Knights under Grand Master Winrich von Kniprode defeated a Lithuanian army led by the grand duke Algirdas and his brother Kęstutis, who had invaded…

braniewo.s: Braniewo, German Braunsberg, is a town in Warmia in north-eastern Poland, near the Vistula Lagoon. Founded in the thirteenth century in the lands of the Prince-Bishopric of Warmia under the Teutonic Order, it became a member of the Hanseatic League and a centre of trade.

bull-of-rieti.s: The Bull of Rieti was a papal bull issued by Pope Gregory IX at Rieti on 3 August 1234. It took the lands that the Teutonic Order held and would conquer in Prussia into the ownership of the Holy See and granted them to the Order as a perpetual possession under papal protection.

burzenland.s: The Burzenland, Romanian Țara Bârsei, is a historical region in south-eastern Transylvania, Romania, around the city of Brașov. In 1211 King Andrew II of Hungary granted it to the Teutonic Knights to defend Hungary's frontier against the Cumans; they built castles and brought…

ban-mueang.s: Ban Mueang was the second king of Sukhothai, the elder son of its founder Si Inthrathit. According to the inscription attributed to his younger brother Ram Khamhaeng, he succeeded his father and ruled while Ram Khamhaeng served as a commander.

borommaracha-i.s: Borommaracha I, also known as Khun Luang Pha Ngua, was king of Ayutthaya from 1370 to 1388. He campaigned repeatedly against the northern towns of Sukhothai, besieging Chakangrao (Kamphaeng Phet), and in 1378 forced Sukhothai's king Maha Thammaracha II to become his vassal.

borommarachathirat-ii.s: Borommaracha II, known before his accession as Chao Sam Phraya, was king of Ayutthaya from 1424 to 1448. In 1431 his armies took the Khmer capital Angkor, contributing to its abandonment.

baba-ishaq.s: Baba Ishaq was a Turkmen preacher in Anatolia and disciple of the mystic Baba Ilyas. In 1239–1240 he led the Babai revolt, a large rising of Turkmen against the Seljuk sultan Kaykhusraw II, spreading from the south-east towards Amasya.

babai-revolt.s: The Babai revolt was a rising of Turkmen in Anatolia against the Seljuk Sultanate of Rum in 1239–1240, inspired by the preachers Baba Ilyas and Baba Ishaq. Fuelled by religious fervour and resentment of heavy taxes and the Persianised court, the rebels defeated several Seljuk…

baiju.s: Baiju was a Mongol general who succeeded Chormaqan as commander of the Mongol forces in north-western Iran about 1242. In 1243 he defeated the Seljuk sultan Kaykhusraw II at the Battle of Köse Dağ, making the Sultanate of Rum a Mongol vassal.

battle-of-dorylaeum-1097.s: The Battle of Dorylaeum was fought on 1 July 1097 near Dorylaeum in north-western Anatolia, during the First Crusade. The Seljuk sultan Kilij Arslan I attacked the crusader vanguard, but the arrival of the main crusader army turned the battle into a heavy Seljuk defeat.

battle-of-myriokephalon.s: The Battle of Myriokephalon was fought on 17 September 1176 in the mountains of western Anatolia, near Lake Eğirdir. The Seljuk sultan Kilij Arslan II ambushed the army of the Byzantine emperor Manuel I Komnenos in a narrow pass as it marched on Konya.

battle-of-yassicemen.s: The Battle of Yassıçemen was fought in August 1230 near Erzincan in eastern Anatolia. The Seljuk sultan Kayqubad I, allied with the Ayyubids, defeated the Khwarazmian shah Jalal al-Din Mingburnu, whose expansion threatened both.

barghash-bin-said.s: Barghash bin Said was Sultan of Zanzibar from 1870 to 1888, a son of Said bin Sultan. Under British pressure he signed the treaty of 1873 that closed the Zanzibar slave market.

bartle-frere.s: Sir Bartle Frere was a British colonial administrator. After a career in India, where he was Governor of Bombay, he led a mission to Zanzibar in 1873 that pressed Sultan Barghash to sign a treaty ending the seaborne slave trade.

balambangan-island.s: Balambangan Island is an island off the northern tip of Borneo, in present-day Sabah, Malaysia. In 1773 the British East India Company founded a trading post there, intended to tap the trade between China and the Sulu and Malay worlds.

balangingi-sama.s: The Balangingi Sama were a Sama people based in the Balangingi islands of the Sulu archipelago, in the southern Philippines. In the early nineteenth century they became the most feared maritime raiders of the Sulu zone, seizing captives across the Philippines and the…

basilan.s: Basilan is an island in the southern Philippines, lying between the Zamboanga Peninsula of Mindanao and the Sulu archipelago. Its coastal communities were long linked by tributary ties to the Sulu Sultanate, and Spain built a fort at Isabela on its northern coast in the…

baduy.s: The Baduy, or Kanekes, are a Sundanese community living in the hills of Lebak Regency in Banten, western Java, Indonesia. They follow an ancestral religion, Sunda Wiwitan, and strict customary rules that limit contact with the outside world.

bodleian-library.s: The Bodleian Library is the main research library of the University of Oxford, opened in 1602 through the refounding of the university library by Sir Thomas Bodley. One of the oldest libraries in Europe and a legal deposit library, it holds millions of books and manuscripts,…

battle-of-bubat.s: The Battle of Bubat took place in 1357 at Bubat, near the Majapahit capital in East Java. According to the Pararaton and the Kidung Sunda, King Linggabuana of Sunda came to Majapahit to marry his daughter Dyah Pitaloka to King Hayam Wuruk, but the minister Gajah Mada demanded…

bujangga-manik.s: Bujangga Manik is an Old Sundanese poem of about 1,600 lines, preserved in a single palm-leaf manuscript held in the Bodleian Library at Oxford since 1627. It tells of a Sundanese prince of the Pakuan court who became a hermit and travelled through Java and to Bali, and its…

black-rangers.s: The Black Rangers were a corps of formerly enslaved men raised by the colony of Suriname in 1772 to fight maroon groups, especially those led by Boni, in return for their freedom. Known from their red caps as the Redi Musu, they knew the forest well and proved more effective…

battle-of-the-berezina.s: The Battle of the Berezina, fought from 26 to 29 November 1812, was the crossing of the Berezina River in present-day Belarus by Napoleon's retreating Grande Armée under Russian attack. Engineers built bridges under fire, and rearguards, among them Swiss regiments that…

benjamin-mkapa.s: Benjamin Mkapa was a Tanzanian journalist, diplomat and politician who served as the third president of Tanzania from 1995 to 2005, the first elected under the multi-party system. A protégé of Julius Nyerere, he pursued privatisation, fiscal discipline and debt relief, winning…

bhrikuti.s: Bhrikuti is the Nepalese princess who, according to Tibetan tradition, married the emperor Songtsen Gampo in the seventh century, alongside the Tang princess Wencheng. Tradition credits her with bringing Buddhist images to Tibet and with a part in founding the Jokhang temple…

bibi-khanym-mosque.s: The Bibi Khanym Mosque is a monumental congregational mosque in Samarkand, built for Timur between 1399 and 1404 after his Indian campaign and named after his chief wife. One of the largest mosques of its age, with a vast courtyard, towering portal and blue-tiled domes, it…

boris-godunov.s: Boris Godunov was regent of Russia under the feeble Tsar Feodor I and, after Feodor's death ended the Rurikid line in 1598, was elected tsar by an assembly of the land. As regent he oversaw the creation of the Moscow Patriarchate in 1589, and he pressed expansion into Siberia,…

boyar-duma.s: The Boyar Duma was the council of leading aristocrats that advised the grand princes of Moscow and the tsars of Russia until the early eighteenth century. Its members, holding the ranks of boyar, okolnichy and duma noble, deliberated on legislation, war and diplomacy, and laws…

battle-of-gangut.s: The Battle of Gangut, fought off the Hanko Peninsula of southern Finland on 7 August 1714 (27 July Old Style), was the first major victory of the Russian navy. Russian galleys under Fyodor Apraksin, with Peter I present, outmanoeuvred a Swedish squadron left becalmed and…
