bappa-rawal.s: Bappa Rawal is the legendary founder of the power of the Guhila dynasty in Mewar, said in dynastic tradition to have taken the fort of Chittor from its Mori rulers in the early eighth century. Later inscriptions and bardic accounts made him a devotee of Ekalinga and a hero of…

battle-of-haldighati.s: The Battle of Haldighati was fought on 18 June 1576 in a mountain pass near Gogunda in Mewar between Maharana Pratap and a Mughal army led by Man Singh I of Amber for the emperor Akbar. The Mughals won the field, but Pratap escaped, according to tradition on his horse Chetak,…

bhim-singh-of-mewar.s: Bhim Singh was Maharana of Mewar from 1778 to 1828. His long reign was a time of decline, marked by Maratha and Pindari raids, feuding nobles and an empty treasury, and by the death of his daughter Krishna Kumari, poisoned in 1810 to end a war between Jaipur and Jodhpur over…

battle-of-khatoli.s: The Battle of Khatoli was fought in 1517 near Khatoli, in the Kota region of Rajasthan, between Rana Sanga of Mewar and Ibrahim Lodi, sultan of Delhi. Sanga's Rajput forces defeated the sultan's army, and Sanga is said to have lost an arm and been lamed in the fighting.

bazilio-olara-okello.s: Bazilio Olara-Okello was a Ugandan army officer who led the coup of July 1985 that overthrew Milton Obote's second government. He briefly headed the new military council before handing over to Tito Okello, and as army commander took part in the government's peace talks with…

bobi-wine.s: Bobi Wine, the stage name of Robert Kyagulanyi Ssentamu, is a Ugandan musician and politician. Elected to parliament in 2017, he led the People Power movement and then the National Unity Platform in opposition to President Yoweri Museveni, and was the main challenger in the…

benedicto-kiwanuka.s: Benedicto Kiwanuka was a Ugandan lawyer and leader of the Democratic Party who became Uganda's first chief minister in 1961 and its first prime minister under internal self-government in 1962, before losing power to Milton Obote in the elections that preceded independence.…

battle-of-the-masts.s: The Battle of the Masts was a naval battle fought in 654 or 655 off the coast of Lycia in south-western Anatolia, in which the young Arab fleet built up under Muawiya as governor of Syria, led by Abd Allah ibn Sa'd, defeated a Byzantine fleet commanded by Emperor Constans II…

battle-of-delville-wood.s: The Battle of Delville Wood was fought from 15 July to 3 September 1916 as part of the Battle of the Somme in northern France. The 1st South African Infantry Brigade was ordered to take the wood and hold it at all costs, and clung on for six days under intense German shelling…

barakah-nuclear-power-plant.s: The Barakah nuclear power plant, in the Al Dhafra region of western Abu Dhabi, is the first nuclear power station in the Arab world. Built by a South Korean consortium led by KEPCO, its four reactors were connected to the grid between 2020 and 2024, and together they supply…

brics.s: BRICS is an intergovernmental grouping of major emerging economies named after its first members, Brazil, Russia, India and China, which held their first summit in 2009; South Africa joined in 2010–2011. It expanded from January 2024 to include Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran and the…

burj-khalifa.s: The Burj Khalifa is a skyscraper in Dubai, at 828 metres the tallest building in the world since its opening on 4 January 2010. Developed by Emaar and designed by Adrian Smith of Skidmore, Owings & Merrill, it was renamed at its opening from Burj Dubai in honour of Khalifa bin…

battle-of-britain.s: The Battle of Britain was the air campaign fought over southern England in the summer and autumn of 1940, in which the Royal Air Force defended the United Kingdom against the German Luftwaffe. Germany's failure to win air superiority led Hitler to postpone the planned invasion…

beveridge-report.s: The Beveridge Report, officially Social Insurance and Allied Services, was a British government report written by the economist William Beveridge and published in December 1942. It proposed a comprehensive system of social insurance to attack the five giants of want, disease,…

big-three-world-war-ii.s: The Big Three were the principal Allied powers of the Second World War, the United Kingdom, the United States and the Soviet Union, and their leaders Winston Churchill, Franklin D. Roosevelt and Joseph Stalin. At the conferences of Tehran in 1943 and Yalta and Potsdam in 1945…

bletchley-park.s: Bletchley Park is a country house and estate in Buckinghamshire, England, that was the centre of British codebreaking during the Second World War. Thousands of staff, among them Alan Turing, broke German Enigma and Lorenz ciphers there, producing the intelligence known as…

bonar-law.s: Andrew Bonar Law was a British Conservative politician, born in the colony of New Brunswick in present-day Canada, who was prime minister of the United Kingdom from October 1922 to May 1923. Leader of the Conservatives from 1911, he opposed Irish Home Rule, served as…

ballot-act-1872.s: The Ballot Act 1872 was an act of the UK Parliament that introduced the secret ballot for parliamentary and local elections. Passed by Gladstone's first government, it replaced open public voting, which had exposed voters to bribery and to intimidation by landlords and…

benjamin-disraeli.s: Benjamin Disraeli was a British Conservative statesman and novelist who served as prime minister in 1868 and from 1874 to 1880. He carried the Second Reform Act of 1867, bought Britain a large stake in the Suez Canal Company, had Queen Victoria proclaimed Empress of India and…

bronte-sisters.s: The Brontë sisters, Charlotte (1816–1855), Emily (1818–1848) and Anne (1820–1849), were English novelists and poets who grew up at Haworth in Yorkshire. Their novels, notably Charlotte's Jane Eyre, Emily's Wuthering Heights and Anne's The Tenant of Wildfell Hall, first…

battle-of-passchendaele.s: The Battle of Passchendaele, or Third Battle of Ypres, was a British-led offensive on the Western Front in Belgium from July to November 1917. Fought in heavy rain over ground churned into mud by shelling, it gained only a few miles before Canadian troops took the ridge and…

bathsheba.s: Bathsheba was the wife of Uriah the Hittite who, according to the Hebrew Bible, became the wife of King David after he committed adultery with her and arranged Uriah's death in battle. She was the mother of Solomon and, with the prophet Nathan, secured his succession to the…

battle-of-mount-gilboa.s: The Battle of Mount Gilboa was the battle in which, according to the Hebrew Bible, the Philistines defeated the Israelites under King Saul on Mount Gilboa, above the Jezreel Valley. Saul's sons, among them Jonathan, were killed and Saul took his own life; the defeat led to the…

book-of-proverbs.s: The Book of Proverbs is a book of the Hebrew Bible, part of its wisdom literature, made up of collections of moral and practical sayings. Several collections are attributed to Solomon, others to the men of King Hezekiah and to sages such as Agur and Lemuel; scholars usually…

birla-family.s: The Birla family is an Indian business family of the Marwari community from Pilani in Rajasthan. Under Ghanshyam Das Birla, a financial supporter of Mahatma Gandhi and the Indian National Congress, its firms grew from trading in Calcutta into one of India's leading industrial…

boston-tea-party.s: The Boston Tea Party was a political protest on 16 December 1773 in which American colonists, some disguised as Mohawk Indians, threw 342 chests of East India Company tea into Boston Harbor in defiance of the Tea Act. Britain answered with the punitive Coercive Acts of 1774,…

bretton-woods-system.s: The Bretton Woods system was the international monetary order agreed at the Bretton Woods Conference in New Hampshire in July 1944. It fixed exchange rates against the US dollar, which was convertible into gold at 35 dollars an ounce, and created the International Monetary…

battles-of-saratoga.s: The Battles of Saratoga were two battles fought near Saratoga, New York, in September and October 1777, in which American forces under Horatio Gates defeated a British army advancing from Canada under John Burgoyne. Burgoyne's surrender on 17 October was a turning point of the…

bolivarian-alliance-for-the-peoples-of-o.n: Bolivarian Alliance for the Peoples of Our America
bolivarian-alliance-for-the-peoples-of-o.s: The Bolivarian Alliance for the Peoples of Our America (ALBA) is a regional organisation of left-wing Latin American and Caribbean governments, founded by Venezuela and Cuba in Havana in December 2004 as an alternative to the US-backed Free Trade Area of the Americas. Bolivia,…

battle-of-anaquito.s: The Battle of Añaquito was fought on 18 January 1546 on the plain of Iñaquito near Quito between the forces of Viceroy Blasco Núñez Vela and the rebel encomenderos led by Gonzalo Pizarro. The rebels won, and the viceroy, the first appointed to Peru, was killed and beheaded on…

battle-of-rancagua.s: The Battle of Rancagua was fought on 1–2 October 1814 in the town of Rancagua, south of Santiago, between royalist troops sent from Peru under Mariano Osorio and Chilean patriots under Bernardo O'Higgins. After a siege in the town square the patriots broke out and fled, and…

battle-of-jaquijahuana.s: The Battle of Jaquijahuana was fought on 9 April 1548 on the plain of Jaquijahuana near Cusco between royal forces under Pedro de la Gasca and the rebel encomenderos of Gonzalo Pizarro. Most of Pizarro's men deserted to Gasca, who had offered pardons, before the fighting…

battle-of-raichur.s: The Battle of Raichur was fought in 1520 between the Vijayanagara Empire under Krishnadevaraya and the Bijapur Sultanate under Ismail Adil Shah near the fortress of Raichur in the Deccan. Krishnadevaraya's victory gave him Raichur and control of the Raichur Doab between the…

battle-of-lipitsa.s: The Battle of Lipitsa was fought in April 1216 near Yuryev-Polsky between the sons of Vsevolod the Big Nest. Konstantin of Rostov, allied with Mstislav the Bold of Novgorod, defeated his brothers Yuri and Yaroslav, whose army suffered heavy losses.

battle-of-the-sit-river.s: The Battle of the Sit River was fought on 4 March 1238 on the Sit, a tributary of the Mologa in north-eastern Rus', between the Mongol army of Batu Khan and Grand Prince Yuri II of Vladimir. The Mongols surprised and destroyed the Russian forces, and Yuri II was killed.

bogolyubovo.s: Bogolyubovo is a village near Vladimir in Russia, founded around 1158 by Andrei Bogolyubsky as his fortified residence, from which his byname derives. Andrei was murdered there by members of his household in 1174.

bryakhimov.s: Bryakhimov was a town of Volga Bulgaria mentioned in the Russian chronicles, whose exact location is uncertain. In 1164 Andrei Bogolyubsky of Vladimir-Suzdal led a major campaign against the Bulgars, defeated their army and took and burned Bryakhimov and other towns.

burtas.s: The Burtas were a people of the middle Volga region mentioned by Arab and Persian geographers of the ninth and tenth centuries, living between the Khazars and the Volga Bulgars. Their language and origin are disputed: many scholars consider them Finno-Ugric, related to the…

battle-of-kousseri.s: The Battle of Kousséri was fought on 22 April 1900 near Kousséri, in present-day northern Cameroon, between French forces under Commandant Amédée-François Lamy and the army of the warlord Rabih az-Zubayr, ruler of Bornu. The French won, and both Lamy and Rabih were killed.

balligave.s: Balligave, now Belagami in Shivamogga district, Karnataka, was a major town of the Western Chalukya and Hoysala periods. It was a religious centre with temples and monasteries of Shaiva, Jain and Buddhist communities, including a large college run by the Kalamukha ascetics,…

battle-of-koppam.s: The Battle of Koppam was fought in 1054 between the Chola king Rajadhiraja I and the Western Chalukya king Someshvara I, probably near the Krishna or Tungabhadra river. Rajadhiraja was killed riding his war elephant, but his younger brother Rajendra II took command and was…

battle-of-kudalasangamam.s: The Battle of Kudalasangamam was fought in the 1060s near the confluence of the Krishna and Tungabhadra rivers between the Chola king Virarajendra and the Western Chalukya king Someshvara I. Virarajendra won a decisive victory, which he celebrated in his inscriptions.

battle-of-maski.s: The Battle of Maski was fought around 1019–1020 at Maski, in present-day Raichur district of Karnataka, between the Chola king Rajendra I and the Western Chalukya king Jayasimha II. Rajendra's victory pushed the Chalukyas back and for a time fixed the Tungabhadra as the…

bhillama-v.s: Bhillama V was a Seuna Yadava ruler who reigned from about 1173 to 1192 and made his dynasty an independent power. Exploiting the collapse of the Western Chalukyas, he seized Kalyani and the northern Chalukya provinces around 1187 and founded Devagiri (Daulatabad) as his capital.

basavakalyan.s: Basavakalyan, historically Kalyani, is a town in Bidar district, Karnataka, India. It was the capital of the Western Chalukya Empire from the mid-eleventh century and later of the Kalachuris of Kalyani, and in the twelfth century it was the centre of the Lingayat movement led…

book-of-documents.s: The Book of Documents (Shangshu) is one of the Five Classics of Chinese literature, a collection of speeches, proclamations and records attributed to the legendary sage kings and to rulers and ministers of the Xia, Shang and Western Zhou. Its oldest chapters, probably composed…

budugen.s: Budugen was a Xianbei chief of the early third century CE and a member of the family of the great leader Tanshihuai, who led a large following in the frontier regions of northern China. He submitted to the Cao Wei court and received titles, but competed with the rival chief…

battle-of-mobei.s: The Battle of Mobei was fought in 119 BCE north of the Gobi Desert between the armies of Han China under Wei Qing and Huo Qubing and the Xiongnu. The Han cavalry drove the chanyu Yizhixie into flight and inflicted heavy losses, pushing the Xiongnu away from the Chinese frontier.

bam-iran.s: Bam is a city in Kerman province in south-eastern Iran, famous for the Arg-e Bam, the largest adobe citadel in the world, which grew on the Silk Road trade routes. In 1794 the last Zand ruler, Lotf Ali Khan, was betrayed and captured there.

battle-of-isandlwana.s: The Battle of Isandlwana was fought on 22 January 1879, at the start of the Anglo-Zulu War, when some 20,000 Zulu warriors overran the camp of Lord Chelmsford's centre column below Isandlwana hill. More than 1,300 British soldiers and African auxiliaries were killed.

battle-of-ndondakusuka.s: The Battle of Ndondakusuka was fought on 2 December 1856 near the Thukela River between two sons of the Zulu king Mpande competing for the succession. Cetshwayo's uSuthu faction routed his half-brother Mbuyazi and his iziGqoza supporters, killing Mbuyazi and thousands of his…

battle-of-ulundi.s: The Battle of Ulundi, fought on 4 July 1879, was the last major battle of the Anglo-Zulu War. Lord Chelmsford's army, formed in a hollow square with artillery and Gatling guns, broke the Zulu attack near the royal kraal of Ulundi, which was then burned.

battle-of-gingindlovu.s: The Battle of Gingindlovu was fought on 2 April 1879 during the Anglo-Zulu War, when a British relief column under Lord Chelmsford, formed in an entrenched square, repulsed a Zulu attack in coastal Zululand. The victory allowed the British to relieve the besieged garrison at…

battle-of-kambula.s: The Battle of Kambula was fought on 29 March 1879 during the Anglo-Zulu War, when a British column under Colonel Evelyn Wood, defending a fortified camp in north-western Zululand, repulsed a major attack by the main Zulu army. The heavy Zulu losses made it a turning point of…

battle-of-rorkes-drift.s: The Battle of Rorke's Drift was fought on 22–23 January 1879 during the Anglo-Zulu War, when about 150 British soldiers defended a mission station on the Buffalo River against some 3,000–4,000 Zulu warriors, hours after the disaster at Isandlwana. The garrison held, and eleven…

brac.s: Brač is a Croatian island in the central Adriatic, south of Split, the largest island of Dalmatia. It is famous for its white limestone, quarried since Roman times and used in Diocletian's Palace in Split.

birkenfeld.s: Birkenfeld is a town in the Hunsrück hills of Rhineland-Palatinate, Germany. Once part of the County of Sponheim, it was from 1569 the seat of the Palatinate-Birkenfeld line of the Wittelsbachs.

bangka.s: Bangka is an island off the east coast of Sumatra, Indonesia, part of the province of Bangka Belitung. Tin was found there around 1710, and under the Sultanate of Palembang and later Dutch rule it became one of the world's main tin producers, worked largely by Chinese miners.

badami.s: Badami, the ancient Vatapi, is a town in northern Karnataka, India, set in a ravine of red sandstone cliffs. Fortified by Pulakeshin I around 543, it was the capital of the Chalukyas of Badami until the Pallava king Narasimhavarman I sacked it in 642.

bel-god.s: Bel, meaning 'lord', was a title of the Babylonian god Marduk that became the name of a chief god worshipped across Mesopotamia, Syria and western Iran. At Palmyra Bel was the supreme deity, honoured in the great Temple of Bel dedicated in 32 CE and destroyed by Islamic State…

battle-of-immae.s: The Battle of Immae was fought in 272 near Antioch in Syria between the Roman emperor Aurelian and the army of the Palmyrene Empire under Zabdas. Aurelian's cavalry feigned flight until the heavily armoured Palmyrene horsemen were exhausted, then turned and defeated them.

bhadrachalam.s: Bhadrachalam is a temple town on the left bank of the Godavari river in Bhadradri Kothagudem district of Telangana, India. It is best known for the Sita Ramachandraswamy temple, a major pilgrimage centre dedicated to Rama, rebuilt in the 17th century by Kancherla Gopanna,…

bhadradri-kothagudem-district.s: Bhadradri Kothagudem district is a district in the north-east of Telangana, India, created in 2016 from part of the former Khammam district. Its headquarters is Kothagudem, and it includes the temple town of Bhadrachalam and the industrial town of Palvancha.

balboa-heights.s: Balboa Heights is a district of Panama City near the Pacific entrance of the Panama Canal. During the period of United States control it was the administrative headquarters of the Panama Canal Zone, where the Administration Building housed the governor and the canal company.

bay-of-bandon.s: The Bay of Bandon is a bay of the Gulf of Thailand on the east coast of the Malay Peninsula, in Surat Thani province of southern Thailand. The Tapi river flows into it at the city of Surat Thani, and the islands of Ko Samui and Ko Pha-ngan lie off its mouth.

bhojeshwar-temple.s: The Bhojeshwar Temple at Bhojpur, near Bhopal in Madhya Pradesh, India, is an unfinished Shiva temple attributed to the Paramara king Bhoja in the 11th century. It houses one of the largest stone lingams in India, about 7.5 metres high including its platform, and the abandoned…

brough-east-riding-of-yorkshire.s: Brough is a town on the north bank of the Humber estuary in the East Riding of Yorkshire, England. It stands on the site of the Roman fort and town of Petuaria, which an inscription names as a vicus of the Parisi with its own aedile, and which probably served as their civitas…

bushati-family.s: The Bushati family was an Albanian dynasty that ruled the Pashalik of Scutari from Shkodër between 1757 and 1831. Taking advantage of Ottoman weakness, Mehmed Pasha Bushati and his son Kara Mahmud Pasha built an autonomous domain over northern Albania and neighbouring lands,…

battle-of-krusi.s: The Battle of Krusi was fought on 22 September 1796 near Podgorica between the Montenegrins under Prince-Bishop Petar I Petrović-Njegoš and the army of Kara Mahmud Pasha Bushati of Scutari. The Montenegrins won a decisive victory in which Kara Mahmud Pasha was killed and his…

balangir.s: Balangir, also spelt Bolangir, is a town in western Odisha, India, and headquarters of Balangir district. It replaced Patnagarh as the capital of the princely state of Patna, which merged with the province of Orissa in 1948.

benedict-xiv.s: Benedict XIV, born Prospero Lambertini in Bologna, was pope from 1740 to 1758 and one of the most learned popes of the 18th century. A noted canon lawyer, he reformed the procedure of canonisation, encouraged scholarship and science and kept good relations with European rulers.

bertrand-of-saint-genies.s: Bertrand of Saint-Geniès was a French churchman who served as Patriarch of Aquileia from 1334 to 1350. He worked to restore the patriarchate's authority in Friuli against the counts of Gorizia and rebellious nobles, and to reform its clergy.

basil-i.s: Basil I was Byzantine emperor from 867 to 886 and founder of the Macedonian dynasty, which ruled for nearly two centuries. A peasant from Thrace who rose as a favourite of Michael III, he had his rival Bardas and then Michael himself murdered.

battle-of-bathys-ryax.s: The Battle of Bathys Ryax was fought in central Anatolia between the Byzantine army of Emperor Basil I and the Paulicians of Tephrike, probably in 872 or 878. The Byzantines surprised the Paulician army as it withdrew from a raid into imperial territory, and its leader…

bogomil.s: Bogomil was a Bulgarian priest of the 10th century who founded the dualist movement named after him during the reign of Tsar Peter I. He is known chiefly from the treatise of Cosmas the Priest, who attacked his teaching that the visible world was the work of the devil and that…

battle-of-afabet.s: The Battle of Afabet was fought in March 1988 around the town of Afabet in northern Eritrea, where the Eritrean People's Liberation Front overran the headquarters of the Ethiopian army's Nadew Command. Several Ethiopian divisions were destroyed and large quantities of…

bangkok.s: Bangkok is the capital and largest city of Thailand, on the Chao Phraya river near the Gulf of Thailand. King Rama I founded it as the capital of the Chakri dynasty in 1782 on Rattanakosin island, opposite Taksin's capital at Thonburi, and laid it out on the model of Ayutthaya.

bandar-e-anzali.s: Bandar-e Anzali is a port city on the southern shore of the Caspian Sea in Gilan province, Iran. Long Iran's main Caspian port for trade with Russia, it was called Bandar-e Pahlavi between 1935 and 1979.

battle-of-pharsalus.s: The Battle of Pharsalus was fought on 9 August 48 BCE near Pharsalus in Thessaly between Julius Caesar and the larger army of Pompey and the Senate. Caesar's veterans routed Pompey's cavalry and then his infantry, and Pompey fled to Egypt, where he was murdered.

borommakot.s: Borommakot was king of the Ayutthaya Kingdom of Siam from 1733 to 1758, after a violent struggle for the throne. His long and largely peaceful reign was remembered as a golden age of Buddhist learning and art, and in 1753 he sent monks to Kandy to restore higher ordination in…

benguela.s: Benguela is a coastal city of western Angola, founded by the Portuguese in 1617 as São Filipe de Benguela. It became the second centre of Portuguese Angola after Luanda and a major port of the Atlantic slave trade, drawing captives from the central highland kingdoms such as…

bissau.s: Bissau is the capital and largest city of Guinea-Bissau, on the estuary of the Geba river. The Portuguese founded a fortified trading post there in 1687, and the Fortaleza de São José da Amura was built in the 18th century.

basilica-of-bom-jesus.s: The Basilica of Bom Jesus is a Jesuit church in Old Goa, India, completed in 1605 in the Baroque style. It holds the tomb and remains of Saint Francis Xavier, which are displayed to pilgrims at intervals.

bernardini-tomb.s: The Bernardini Tomb is a princely burial of the early 7th century BCE at Praeneste, modern Palestrina, in Latium, found in 1876. With the nearby Barberini Tomb, it held gold, silver and ivory objects made in the eastern Mediterranean, showing the wealth of the Orientalising…

banu-hashim.s: Banu Hashim was a clan of the Quraysh tribe of Mecca, named after Hashim ibn Abd Manaf, the great-grandfather of the Prophet Muhammad. It held the right to provide food and water for pilgrims to the Kaaba.

banu-makhzum.s: Banu Makhzum was a wealthy clan of the Quraysh tribe of Mecca, prominent in trade and warfare before Islam. Its leader Abu Jahl was among Muhammad's fiercest opponents, while the clan also produced the general Khalid ibn al-Walid, who later led the early Muslim conquests.

bias-of-priene.s: Bias of Priene was a Greek statesman of the 6th century BCE, counted among the Seven Sages of Greece. Known for his judgement in legal disputes, he advised the Ionians, according to Herodotus, to sail together to Sardinia and found a single city there rather than live under…

balthasar-von-dernbach.s: Balthasar von Dernbach was prince-abbot of Fulda from 1570 to 1606. A determined Counter-Reformer, he brought in the Jesuits and pressed his Protestant subjects to return to Catholicism, which led the chapter and the knights to depose him in 1576.

bremervorde.s: Bremervörde is a town on the Oste in Lower Saxony, Germany, between Bremen and Hamburg. Its castle, held by the archbishops of Bremen from the 13th century, became their main residence in the late Middle Ages as the city of Bremen slipped from their control.

bamberg-horseman.s: The Bamberg Horseman is a life-size stone statue of a crowned rider in Bamberg Cathedral, carved before 1237. One of the first large equestrian statues since antiquity, its subject is unknown, though suggestions include Saint Stephen of Hungary and Emperor Frederick II.

bolzano.s: Bolzano, in German Bozen, is the capital of the autonomous province of South Tyrol in northern Italy, where the Talfer meets the Eisack. A market town on the route over the Brenner Pass, it belonged to the County of Tyrol and passed to Italy after the First World War.

brixen.s: Brixen, in Italian Bressanone, is a town in South Tyrol, northern Italy, where the Rienz joins the Eisack. It was the seat of the bishops of Brixen from about 990, who ruled as prince-bishops until 1803, and its cathedral and bishops' palace dominate the old town.

bruneck.s: Bruneck, in Italian Brunico, is the main town of the Puster Valley in South Tyrol, northern Italy. It was founded in the 13th century by the bishops of Brixen, who built its castle and held the town until 1803.

bobolice.s: Bobolice, in German Bublitz, is a small town in West Pomeranian Voivodeship, north-western Poland. From the 13th century it belonged to the bishops of Cammin as part of their secular territory with Köslin and Kolberg, passing with it to Brandenburg after the Peace of…

baroque.s: Baroque is the style of art, architecture and music that flourished in Europe from about 1600 to the mid-18th century. Born in Rome and spread by the Church of the Counter-Reformation and by royal courts, it favoured movement, drama and rich ornament.

bernward-of-hildesheim.s: Bernward was bishop of Hildesheim from 993 to 1022, after serving as tutor to the young Emperor Otto III. A patron of art and building, he founded the church of St Michael and commissioned the bronze doors of 1015 and a bronze column, masterpieces of Ottonian art.

bautzen.s: Bautzen is a town on the Spree in eastern Saxony, Germany, the historic capital of Upper Lusatia and the cultural centre of the Sorbs. It led the Lusatian League of six towns founded in 1346, and its cathedral of St Peter has been shared by Catholics and Lutherans since the…

bobr.s: The Bóbr, in German Bober, is a river in south-western Poland, flowing about 270 kilometres from the Sudetes north through Lower Silesia to join the Oder. Jelenia Góra, Bolesławiec and Żagań lie on its banks, and it joins the Oder at Krosno Odrzańskie.

battle-of-worth.s: The Battle of Wörth, or Frœschwiller-Wœrth, was fought on 6 August 1870 in northern Alsace in the opening weeks of the Franco-Prussian War. The Prussian Third Army, including Bavarian and Württemberg troops, defeated Marshal MacMahon's army after costly fighting, opening…

berno-of-schwerin.s: Berno was a Cistercian monk who became the first bishop of Schwerin, appointed under Henry the Lion around 1160 to convert the Obotrites. He founded churches and monasteries in Mecklenburg, among them Doberan Abbey in 1171, and laid the foundations of the Church among the…

butzow.s: Bützow is a small town on the Warnow in Mecklenburg, Germany. It was the main residence of the bishops of Schwerin from the 13th century until the bishopric was secularised after the Reformation, and from 1760 to 1789 it had a short-lived university.

bruchsal.s: Bruchsal is a town in the Karlsruhe district of Baden-Württemberg, Germany, north-east of Karlsruhe. From the 1720s it was the residence of the prince-bishops of Speyer, and Cardinal Damian Hugo von Schönborn built a large baroque palace there, with a celebrated staircase…

baden.s: Baden is a historic region of south-western Germany on the right bank of the upper Rhine, between the river and the Black Forest, named after the spa town of Baden-Baden. Ruled by margraves of the Zähringen line from the 12th century, it was greatly enlarged by Napoleon,…

battle-of-hausbergen.s: The Battle of Hausbergen was fought on 8 March 1262 near Strasbourg between the city's citizen militia and the army of its bishop, Walter of Geroldseck. The townsmen won a decisive victory, ending the bishop's lordship over the city.

bernardo-clesio.s: Bernardo Clesio was prince-bishop of Trent from 1514 and a cardinal from 1530. As chief adviser and chancellor of Ferdinand I of Austria, he was one of the leading statesmen of the Habsburg lands.

burchard-of-worms.s: Burchard of Worms was bishop of Worms from 1000 to 1025. Between about 1008 and 1012 he compiled the Decretum, a collection of canon law in twenty books that became the standard handbook of church law until Gratian in the 12th century.

balthasar-neumann.s: Balthasar Neumann was a German architect, the leading master of the late baroque in central Europe. Born in Cheb, he worked as an engineer and architect for the Schönborn prince-bishops of Würzburg, for whom he designed the Würzburg Residence.

burchard-of-wurzburg.s: Burchard of Würzburg was an Anglo-Saxon monk who joined Saint Boniface's mission in Germany. In 742 Boniface consecrated him the first bishop of the newly founded diocese of Würzburg.

berchtesgaden.s: Berchtesgaden is a market town in the Bavarian Alps, near the Austrian border south of Salzburg. It grew around a house of Augustinian canons founded in the early 12th century, whose provosts ruled the surrounding valley as imperial princes until 1803.

berghof.s: The Berghof was Adolf Hitler's mountain residence on the Obersalzberg above Berchtesgaden in Bavaria. Rebuilt from a holiday house in 1935 and 1936, it was where he spent much of his time and received foreign visitors, including the Austrian chancellor Kurt Schuschnigg and the…

battle-of-the-olive-grove-of-koundouros.n: Battle of the Olive Grove of Koundouros
battle-of-the-olive-grove-of-koundouros.s: The Battle of the Olive Grove of Koundouros was fought in Messenia in the south-western Peloponnese in 1205. A small force of crusaders under William of Champlitte and Geoffrey of Villehardouin, put at a few hundred knights and men by the Chronicle of the Morea, defeated a…

bernburg.s: Bernburg is a town on the Saale in Saxony-Anhalt, Germany. Its Renaissance castle on a rock above the river was the residence of the princes, later dukes, of Anhalt-Bernburg from 1603 until the line died out in 1863.

ballenstedt.s: Ballenstedt is a small town on the northern edge of the Harz in Saxony-Anhalt, Germany. Its castle stands on the site of an early medieval monastery associated with the first Ascanian counts, the ancestors of the house of Anhalt.

brandenburg-concertos.s: The Brandenburg Concertos are six instrumental works by Johann Sebastian Bach, among the best-known compositions of the baroque. Bach probably wrote most of them while he was Kapellmeister at the court of Köthen, and in 1721 he presented a fair copy to Christian Ludwig,…

bagrationi-dynasty.s: The Bagrationi were the royal dynasty of Georgia, one of the longest-ruling families in the world. Rising in Tao-Klarjeti in the 9th century, they united Georgia under Bagrat III in the early 11th century and reached their height under David IV and Queen Tamar.

basilica-of-san-nicola.s: The Basilica of San Nicola is a church in Bari in southern Italy, built from 1087 to house the relics of Saint Nicholas, which sailors from Bari had taken from Myra in Asia Minor that year. Consecrated in 1197, it is a model of Apulian Romanesque architecture.

belozersk.s: Belozersk, known in the Middle Ages as Beloozero, is a town on the southern shore of Lake Beloye in Vologda Oblast, Russia. The Primary Chronicle names it under 862 as the seat of Sineus, one of the legendary Varangian brothers.

belz.s: Belz is a small town in Lviv Oblast in western Ukraine, near the Polish border. In the Middle Ages it was one of the Cherven towns disputed between Poland and Rus', the seat of a principality and from 1462 the capital of the Polish Belz Voivodeship.

belz-hasidic-dynasty.s: The Belz Hasidic dynasty is a Hasidic movement founded in the town of Belz in Galicia by Rabbi Shalom Rokeach, who became its leader in 1817. Under his successors Belz became one of the largest Hasidic courts of eastern Europe.

belz-voivodeship.s: The Belz Voivodeship was a province of the Kingdom of Poland, and later of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, created in 1462 when King Casimir IV took over the Principality of Belz after the local line of the Masovian dukes died out. With its capital at Belz, it lay in the…

balsic-noble-family.s: The Balšić were a noble family that ruled Zeta, roughly present-day Montenegro and northern Albania, from about 1360 to 1421 after the break-up of the Serbian Empire. From their seat at Shkodër they fought Ragusa, Bosnia, Venice and Albanian lords.

battle-of-savra.s: The Battle of Savra was fought on 18 September 1385 near present-day Lushnjë in central Albania. An Ottoman army, called in by Karl Thopia, defeated and killed Balša II, the lord of Zeta, who had seized Durrës.

basses-pyrenees.s: Basses-Pyrénées was a department of south-western France created in 1790 from Béarn, Lower Navarre, Labourd and Soule, with Pau as its capital. It covered the western Pyrenees and the French Basque Country on the border with Spain.

bidache.s: Bidache is a village in the Pyrénées-Atlantiques department of south-western France, on the Bidouze river. It was the seat of the Gramont family, whose castle dominated the village, and from the 16th century they claimed it as a sovereign principality on the border of France…

bidouze.s: The Bidouze is a river of the French Basque Country, about 80 kilometres long, a left tributary of the Adour. It rises in the foothills of the Pyrenees near the border of Soule and Lower Navarre and flows north past Bidache to join the Adour.

blankenburg-harz.s: Blankenburg is a town on the northern edge of the Harz in Saxony-Anhalt, Germany. Seat of medieval counts, it passed to the dukes of Brunswick-Wolfenbüttel, whose junior branch made its large castle a residence and, from 1707 to 1731, the capital of the Principality of…

bryansk.s: Bryansk is a city on the Desna in western Russia, first mentioned in 1146 as a town of the Principality of Chernigov. After the Mongol invasion it became the seat of a principality, then passed to Lithuania in the 14th century and to Muscovy around 1500.

bahram-v.s: Bahram V was a Sasanian king of Persia who reigned from 420 to 438. He fought a short war with the Eastern Roman Empire in 421 and 422 and defended the north-eastern frontier against invading nomads.

battle-of-slivnitsa.s: The Battle of Slivnitsa was fought from 17 to 19 November 1885 near the town of Slivnitsa, west of Sofia, during the Serbo-Bulgarian War. The Bulgarian army under Prince Alexander of Battenberg defeated the invading Serbian army of King Milan I.

battle-of-bziyuqo.s: The Battle of Bziyuqo was fought in 1796 in western Circassia between the commoners of the Shapsug and Natukhaj tribes and an alliance of Circassian nobles, including the princes of the Bzhedugh. The commoners won, which confirmed the end of aristocratic rule among the…

baar-region.s: The Baar is a high plateau in south-western Germany between the Black Forest and the Swabian Jura, where the Danube begins near Donaueschingen. In the Middle Ages it was a landgraviate, which passed from the Zähringen heirs to the counts of Fürstenberg in the 13th century and…

baar-switzerland.s: Baar is a municipality in the Swiss canton of Zug, north of the town of Zug. In the Middle Ages it was one of the three rural communes, with Ägeri and Menzingen, that shared government of the canton with the town of Zug through a common assembly.

balkars.s: The Balkars are a Turkic-speaking people of the high valleys of the central North Caucasus, living mainly in Kabardino-Balkaria in Russia, and their language is close to that of the Karachays. Long dependent on the Kabardian princes, they came under Russian rule in the 19th…

babak-khorramdin.s: Babak Khorramdin was the leader of the Khurramite revolt against the Abbasid Caliphate in Azerbaijan and western Iran, which lasted from about 816 to 837. From his mountain stronghold of Badhdh he defeated several caliphal armies until the general Afshin took the fortress in 837.

bad-durkheim.s: Bad Dürkheim is a spa town in Rhineland-Palatinate, Germany, at the foot of the Haardt hills on the German Wine Route. In the 18th century it became the residence of the counts, later princes, of Leiningen-Hardenburg, whose palace was destroyed by French revolutionary troops…

blies.s: The Blies is a river of western Germany and north-eastern France, about 100 km long, rising in the north of Saarland near St. Wendel and flowing south to join the Saar at Sarreguemines. For part of its lower course it forms the border between Germany and France, and its valley…

biella.s: Biella is a city in north-eastern Piedmont, Italy, at the foot of the Alps between Turin and Milan. Ruled by the bishops of Vercelli in the Middle Ages, it submitted to Savoy in 1379 and later became the leading centre of the Italian wool industry.

battle-of-minden.s: The Battle of Minden was fought on 1 August 1759 near Minden in Westphalia during the Seven Years' War. An Anglo-German army under Ferdinand of Brunswick defeated a French army under the Marquis de Contades, after British and Hanoverian infantry advanced against massed French…

battle-on-the-nemiga-river.s: The Battle on the Nemiga River was fought on 3 March 1067 near Minsk between Prince Vseslav of Polotsk and the three sons of Yaroslav the Wise, Iziaslav, Sviatoslav and Vsevolod. The Yaroslavichi, who had sacked Minsk, defeated Vseslav and later seized him by treachery.

bessarabia.s: Bessarabia is a historical region between the Prut and Dniester rivers in eastern Europe, the eastern half of the medieval Principality of Moldavia. Russia annexed it from the Ottoman Empire in 1812.

bogdan-i-of-moldavia.s: Bogdan I was a Romanian voivode from Maramureș who, having quarrelled with the Hungarian crown, crossed the Carpathians around 1359, drove out the descendants of Dragoș and made Moldavia independent of Hungary. He ruled until about 1367.

battle-of-grahovac.s: The Battle of Grahovac was fought in May 1858 at Grahovac in western Montenegro, where Montenegrin forces under Grand Duke Mirko Petrović-Njegoš defeated an Ottoman army. The victory brought diplomatic intervention by the great powers, whose commission drew the first…

biebrich-palace.s: Biebrich Palace is a baroque palace on the Rhine at Wiesbaden-Biebrich in Hesse, Germany, built in stages in the first half of the 18th century for the princes of Nassau-Idstein and Nassau-Usingen. From 1744 it was their main residence, and later that of the dukes of Nassau…

belyov.s: Belyov is a small town in Tula Oblast, Russia, on the Oka river. From the 14th century it was the seat of a small appanage principality of the Upper Oka princes, under Lithuanian and then Muscovite overlordship.

bad-lobenstein.s: Bad Lobenstein is a small spa town in the Thuringian Highlands, in the Saale-Orla district of Germany. From 1647 it was the residence of the counts, later princes, of Reuss-Lobenstein, a branch of the Younger Line of the House of Reuss, until the line died out in 1824.

bergen.s: Bergen is a port city on the west coast of Norway and the country's second-largest city. Founded in the 11th century, traditionally by King Olaf Kyrre, it was medieval Norway's chief town and for a time its royal capital.

bergen-auf-rugen.s: Bergen auf Rügen is the main inland town of the island of Rügen in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, Germany. Its Church of St Mary was begun in the late 12th century by Prince Jaromar I of Rügen and given in 1193 to a convent of Cistercian nuns, around which the town grew.

bocholt.s: Bocholt is a town in the Borken district of North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany, near the Dutch border. A town of the Prince-Bishopric of Münster, it was one of the two districts given to the Principality of Salm in 1803 and served as one of its seats of government until France…

beka-i-jaqeli.s: Beka I Jaqeli was atabeg of Samtskhe in southern Georgia in the late 13th and early 14th centuries. Ruling under Mongol overlordship, he strengthened the autonomy of his principality and issued a law code that was later expanded under King George V and is known as the Code of…

borovsk.s: Borovsk is a small town in Kaluga Oblast, Russia, on the Protva river south-west of Moscow. In the 14th century it belonged to the appanage of Serpukhov.

battle-of-kitombo.s: The Battle of Kitombo was fought in October 1670 between the forces of Soyo, a breakaway province of the Kingdom of Kongo, and a Portuguese army from Angola. The Portuguese, who had invaded Soyo after an earlier victory, were routed and their commander killed.

belaya-river-kuban.s: The Belaya is a river of the north-western Caucasus, a left tributary of the Kuban about 270 kilometres long. It rises in the high mountains, cuts through deep gorges and flows past Maykop, the capital of Adygea.

brandenburg-an-der-havel.s: Brandenburg an der Havel is a city on the Havel in the German state of Brandenburg, west of Berlin. It began as Brenna, the chief stronghold of the Slavic Hevelli, where Otto I founded a bishopric in 948.

boris-and-gleb.s: Boris and Gleb were sons of Vladimir the Great of Kiev who were murdered in 1015 during the succession struggle after their father's death, a crime the chronicles blame on their brother Sviatopolk. Their acceptance of death without resistance led to their veneration as…

battle-of-listven.s: The Battle of Listven was fought in 1024 near Chernigov between Mstislav of Tmutarakan and his brother Yaroslav the Wise, prince of Kiev, who had hired Varangian troops. Mstislav won, and the brothers then divided the Rus' lands along the Dnieper, Mstislav ruling the east from…

brest-belarus.s: Brest is a city in south-western Belarus on the Bug river at the Polish border. As Berestia it was a town of Volhynia first recorded in 1019, later part of the Grand Duchy of Lithuania.

bad-arolsen.s: Bad Arolsen is a small town in northern Hesse, Germany. From the 18th century it was the residence of the counts and princes of Waldeck, who built a large baroque palace there, and it remained the capital of the Free State of Waldeck until 1929.

battle-of-posada.s: The Battle of Posada was fought in November 1330, when the army of Basarab I of Wallachia ambushed King Charles I of Hungary in a narrow pass of the Carpathians as he withdrew from a punitive expedition. The Hungarian army was largely destroyed and the king barely escaped.

battle-of-rovine.s: The Battle of Rovine was fought on 17 May 1395 between Mircea the Elder of Wallachia and the Ottoman sultan Bayezid I, whose army included Serbian vassals. The Serbian lords Marko Mrnjavčević and Konstantin Dragaš were killed.

bernardo-de-monteagudo.s: Bernardo de Monteagudo was a revolutionary of the Spanish American wars of independence, born in Tucumán. He served José de San Martín in Chile and then in Peru, where as minister of war and foreign affairs in the Protectorate he dominated government.

bunce-island.s: Bunce Island is a small island in the Sierra Leone River, upstream from Freetown. From the 1670s it held a fortified British slave-trading post, run in the 18th century by London merchants such as Grant, Oswald and Company, which shipped tens of thousands of captive Africans…

battles-of-lexington-and-concord.s: The Battles of Lexington and Concord, fought on 19 April 1775 in Massachusetts, were the first military engagements of the American Revolutionary War. British troops sent by General Thomas Gage to seize militia stores at Concord exchanged fire with colonists at Lexington and…

benning-wentworth.s: Benning Wentworth was a Portsmouth merchant who served as royal governor of New Hampshire from 1741 to 1766, the longest tenure of any governor in colonial America. He issued many land grants west of the Connecticut River, the New Hampshire Grants, in territory also claimed by…

burlington-new-jersey.s: Burlington is a city on the Delaware River in New Jersey, United States, founded in 1677 by English Quaker settlers. It was the capital of West Jersey and, after 1702, alternated with Perth Amboy as capital of the royal province of New Jersey.

battle-of-alamance.s: The Battle of Alamance was fought on 16 May 1771 in North Carolina, where Governor William Tryon's militia defeated about 2,000 Regulators, backcountry farmers protesting against corrupt officials and excessive fees. The Regulators were poorly armed and led, and several were…

burra-south-australia.s: Burra is a town in the mid-north of South Australia, founded after copper was discovered there in 1845. Its Monster Mine, worked largely by Cornish and Welsh miners, was for a time one of the richest metal mines in Australia and helped rescue the young colony's finances.

battle-of-sullivans-island.s: The Battle of Sullivan's Island was fought on 28 June 1776, when a British fleet under Sir Peter Parker attacked the unfinished palmetto-log fort on Sullivan's Island guarding Charleston harbour. The spongy palmetto logs absorbed the cannon fire, and the defenders under…

blount-report.s: The Blount Report was the 1893 investigation by James Henderson Blount, sent by President Grover Cleveland to Hawaii after the overthrow of Queen Liliʻuokalani. Blount concluded that the US minister John L. Stevens and American marines had improperly helped the conspirators.

battle-of-beth-horon-66.s: The Battle of Beth Horon was fought in the autumn of 66 CE, when Jewish rebels ambushed the retreating army of Cestius Gallus, the Roman governor of Syria, in the Beth Horon pass north-west of Jerusalem. According to Josephus the Romans lost nearly 6,000 men, and the Legio XII…

batoche.s: Batoche is a Métis settlement on the South Saskatchewan River in present-day Saskatchewan, Canada, founded in the early 1870s. In March 1885 Louis Riel proclaimed his provisional government there, and in May 1885 General Frederick Middleton's forces defeated the Métis under…

battleford.s: Battleford is a town in Saskatchewan, Canada, where the Battle River meets the North Saskatchewan. It was the capital of the North-West Territories from 1876 to 1883.

battle-of-duck-lake.s: The Battle of Duck Lake was fought on 26 March 1885 near Duck Lake in present-day Saskatchewan, where Métis and First Nations fighters under Gabriel Dumont defeated a force of North-West Mounted Police and volunteers led by Superintendent Leif Crozier. Twelve of the government…

battle-of-isted.s: The Battle of Isted, or Idstedt, was fought on 24–25 July 1850 near the town of Schleswig and was the largest battle of the First Schleswig War. The Danish army defeated the army of the Schleswig-Holstein provisional government, which fought alone after Prussia made peace with…

beiyang-government.s: The Beiyang government was the internationally recognised government of the Republic of China seated in Beijing from 1912 to 1928, dominated by officers of the Beiyang Army built up by Yuan Shikai under the Qing. After Yuan's death in 1916 rival cliques of warlords fought for…

bolivar-province-ecuador.s: Bolívar is a province in the central highlands of Ecuador, on the western slopes of the Andes south-west of the volcano Chimborazo, with Guaranda as its capital. Named after Simón Bolívar, it rises from subtropical valleys to high páramo grasslands.

banabhatta.s: Banabhatta was a 7th-century Sanskrit prose writer at the court of Harsha, king of Thanesar and Kannauj. His Harshacharita, a partly historical life of his patron, and his unfinished romance Kadambari, completed by his son, are classics of ornate Sanskrit prose.

bayram-khwaja.s: Bayram Khwaja was the first notable leader of the Qara Qoyunlu, a Turkmen tribal confederation of eastern Anatolia and northern Iraq. Active around Lake Van, Erciş and Mosul, he emerged between the 1350s and 1370s as a vassal, and at times a rival, of the Jalayirid dynasty.

blue-mosque-of-tabriz.s: The Blue Mosque of Tabriz, or Goy Masjid, is a mosque in Tabriz, north-western Iran, completed in 1465 during the reign of the Qara Qoyunlu ruler Jahan Shah. It was famed for the blue tile mosaic that covered its walls and domes.

black-stone.s: The Black Stone is a stone set in the eastern corner of the Kaaba in Mecca, revered by Muslims as dating back to Adam and Abraham and kissed or saluted by pilgrims as they circle the Kaaba. In 930 the Qarmatians of Bahrain sacked Mecca and carried it off to their base at…

battle-of-qianshuiyuan.s: The Battle of Qianshuiyuan was fought in 618 in the north of modern Shaanxi between the new Tang dynasty and the Qin state of Xue Ju and his son Xue Rengao. In the summer, while Li Shimin lay ill, Qin forces routed a Tang army there; in the autumn Li Shimin returned, waited…

bidayuh.s: The Bidayuh are an indigenous people of south-western Sarawak in Malaysian Borneo, living mainly in the hills around Kuching, and were formerly called Land Dayaks. Traditionally hill-rice farmers living in longhouses, with distinctive round head-houses, they joined Malays in…

bowring-treaty.s: The Bowring Treaty was signed on 18 April 1855 between Siam and Britain, negotiated by Sir John Bowring, governor of Hong Kong, with King Mongkut. It fixed import duties at 3 per cent, ended most royal trade monopolies, allowed British subjects to own land near Bangkok and…

backa.s: Bačka is a region of the Pannonian Plain between the Danube and the Tisza, divided between Serbia's province of Vojvodina and southern Hungary. A fertile lowland, it was part of medieval Hungary and came under Ottoman rule in the 16th century until the Treaty of Karlowitz in…

banat.s: Banat is a historical region of Central Europe bounded by the Danube, Tisza and Mureș rivers and the Southern Carpathians. Part of medieval Hungary, it fell to the Ottomans in 1552, was conquered by the Habsburgs in 1716 and run from Vienna as a frontier and colonisation zone.

battle-of-seven-oaks.s: The Battle of Seven Oaks was a clash on 19 June 1816 near the Red River Colony, in present-day Winnipeg, Canada. Métis led by Cuthbert Grant, allied with the North West Company, killed Governor Robert Semple and about twenty men of the Hudson's Bay Company's colony, losing one…

barcelona-may-days.s: The Barcelona May Days were street fighting in Barcelona from 3 to 8 May 1937 between anarchists and the POUM on one side and Republican and Communist forces on the other. They began when police tried to take over the CNT-held telephone exchange, and several hundred people…

battle-of-sam-khubis.s: The Battle of Sam Khubis was fought on 8 May 1915 in central Namibia between the Rehoboth Basters and German colonial troops. After the Basters refused to fight against the advancing South African forces in the First World War, German troops attacked them at the mountain of…

bulacan.s: Bulacan is a province of the Philippines on the island of Luzon, just north of Manila. It was a centre of the revolution against Spain: in 1897 Emilio Aguinaldo set up his base in the caves of Biak-na-Bato in San Miguel, and in 1898–1899 the Malolos Congress met at Barasoain…

bentivoglio-family.s: The Bentivoglio were a family who ruled Bologna as unofficial lords for much of the 15th century, under the nominal sovereignty of the Papal States. After Giovanni I briefly seized power in 1401, Annibale, Sante and Giovanni II Bentivoglio dominated the city's government from…

battle-of-fossalta.s: The Battle of Fossalta was fought on 26 May 1249 near Modena between Guelph Bologna and its allies and the Ghibelline forces of Modena and the Emperor Frederick II. The Bolognese captured Frederick's son Enzo, King of Sardinia, who remained their prisoner in Bologna until his…

bay-of-pigs-invasion.s: The Bay of Pigs invasion was a failed landing in southern Cuba on 17–20 April 1961 by about 1,400 Cuban exiles trained and funded by the CIA, aiming to overthrow Fidel Castro. Without the hoped-for uprising or US air cover, they were defeated within three days and most were…

battiad-dynasty.s: The Battiad dynasty ruled the Greek city of Cyrene in Libya for about two centuries, from its foundation around 631 BCE by Battus I, a colonist from Thera. Its kings, named alternately Battus and Arcesilaus, extended the city's power, though their rule was limited by the…

battle-of-cepeda-1820.s: The Battle of Cepeda of 1 February 1820 was fought in the province of Buenos Aires between the federalist caudillos Francisco Ramírez of Entre Ríos and Estanislao López of Santa Fe and the army of the Directory of the United Provinces. The federalist victory brought down the…

bardi-family.s: The Bardi were a Florentine family of merchant-bankers whose company was one of the largest in 14th-century Europe, with branches from London to the Levant. With the Peruzzi they lent heavily to Edward III of England for his war with France and to the kings of Naples.

bernardo-arevalo.s: Bernardo Arévalo is a Guatemalan sociologist, diplomat and politician, son of the reforming president Juan José Arévalo. Leading the anti-corruption Semilla movement, he unexpectedly won the presidential election of 2023 and, despite efforts by prosecutors to suspend his party…

baath-party.s: The Ba'ath Party, or Arab Socialist Ba'ath Party, was a pan-Arab nationalist and socialist party founded in Damascus in 1947 by Michel Aflaq and Salah al-Din al-Bitar. It split into rival Syrian and Iraqi wings after 1966.

batangas.s: Batangas is a province of the Philippines in southern Luzon, south of Manila, with its capital at Batangas City and Taal Volcano within its borders. Its people took a prominent part in the Philippine Revolution against Spain and in resistance to American rule during the…

brigandage-act.s: The Brigandage Act was a law passed by the Philippine Commission, the American colonial legislature of the Philippines, in November 1902 (Act No. 518). It defined armed bands resisting American rule as brigands, made membership of such a band a crime, and punished it with…

bingen-am-rhein.s: Bingen am Rhein is a town in Rhineland-Palatinate, Germany, at the confluence of the Nahe and the Rhine, where the Rhine Gorge begins. A Roman fort and later a possession of the archbishops of Mainz, it passed to the Grand Duchy of Hesse as part of Rhenish Hesse in 1816.

bowdoin-college.s: Bowdoin College is a private liberal arts college in Brunswick, Maine, in the United States, founded in 1794. Its graduates include the writer Nathaniel Hawthorne, the poet Henry Wadsworth Longfellow and President Franklin Pierce.

bacolod.s: Bacolod is a city on the north-western coast of Negros Island in the Philippines, the capital of Negros Occidental province. It grew in the 19th century as a centre of the island's sugar industry, dominated by large planter families.

battle-of-custoza-1848.s: The Battle of Custoza was fought on 24–25 July 1848 near Verona during the First Italian War of Independence, between the Austrian army of Field Marshal Joseph Radetzky and the Sardinian army of King Charles Albert. The Austrian victory forced the Piedmontese to withdraw from…

battle-of-custoza-1866.s: The Battle of Custoza was fought on 24 June 1866 near Verona during the Third Italian War of Independence, part of the Austro-Prussian War. An Austrian army under Archduke Albrecht defeated a larger but poorly led Italian army under Alfonso La Marmora.

banca-monte-dei-paschi-di-siena.n: Banca Monte dei Paschi di Siena
banca-monte-dei-paschi-di-siena.s: Banca Monte dei Paschi di Siena is an Italian bank founded in Siena in 1472 by the city's government as a public pawn bank (monte di pietà). It is regarded as the oldest bank in the world still operating.

borama.s: Borama is a city in the Awdal region of north-western Somaliland, near the border with Ethiopia, inhabited mainly by the Gadabuursi clan. In 1993 it hosted the Borama conference of clan elders, which adopted a national charter for Somaliland and chose Muhammad Haji Ibrahim…

bantustan.s: A Bantustan, or homeland, was a territory set aside for Black South Africans of a particular ethnic group under apartheid. The policy, developed under Hendrik Verwoerd, aimed to strip Black South Africans of South African citizenship by attaching them to ten homelands, four of…

brig-switzerland.s: Brig is a town in the Upper Valais, Switzerland, on the Rhône at the foot of the Simplon Pass, now part of the municipality of Brig-Glis. It was one of the seven tenths (Zenden) that ruled the Valais as a republic.

borba-newspaper.s: Borba ('Struggle') was a Yugoslav communist newspaper founded in 1922 as an organ of the Communist Party of Yugoslavia. During the uprising of 1941 the Partisans printed it in Užice, in the short-lived liberated territory known as the Republic of Užice.

bonnie-blue-flag.s: The Bonnie Blue Flag is a flag of a single white star on a blue field, first flown by the short-lived Republic of West Florida in 1810. It was revived in the southern United States during the secession crisis of 1860–1861 and became an unofficial symbol of the Confederacy,…

barasoain-church.s: Barasoain Church is a Catholic church in Malolos, Bulacan, in the Philippines. In September 1898 it hosted the Malolos Congress, which drafted the Malolos Constitution, and on 23 January 1899 the First Philippine Republic was inaugurated there with Emilio Aguinaldo as president.

bucharest.s: Bucharest is the capital and largest city of Romania, on the Dâmbovița River in the Wallachian plain. First recorded in 1459 under Vlad III, it became the main residence of the princes of Wallachia and in 1862 the capital of the united Romanian state.

battle-of-ivankovac.s: The Battle of Ivankovac was fought in August 1805 near Ćuprija in central Serbia between Serbian rebels led by Milenko Stojković and Petar Dobrnjac and an Ottoman army sent by the sultan. The Serbian victory, the first against a regular imperial army, turned the uprising…

battle-of-misar.s: The Battle of Mišar was fought in August 1806 near Šabac in western Serbia, where Serbian rebels under Karađorđe defeated a larger Ottoman army from Bosnia. Together with the victory at Deligrad, it secured the rebels' control of much of the Belgrade region and is remembered…

baghel.s: The Baghels or Vaghelas are a Rajput clan regarded as a branch of the Solanki (Chaulukya) of Gujarat. A Vaghela dynasty ruled Gujarat in the 13th century, and a Baghel line established itself in the Baghelkhand region of central India, where its rulers held Bandhavgarh and…

bandhavgarh.s: Bandhavgarh is a hill fort in the Umaria district of Madhya Pradesh, India. It was the early stronghold of the Baghel rulers of the region until the Mughals took it in 1597 and the capital moved to Rewa.

battle-of-amalinde.s: The Battle of Amalinde was fought in 1818 in what is now the Eastern Cape province of South Africa, between rival Xhosa forces. Warriors of the regent Ndlambe, joined by Hintsa's Gcaleka, defeated his nephew Ngqika, who then sought help from the Cape Colony.

battle-of-seival.s: The Battle of Seival was fought on 10 September 1836 near Bagé in Rio Grande do Sul, where rebel forces under Antônio de Sousa Neto defeated an imperial column. The following day Neto proclaimed the independent Riograndense Republic, turning the Ragamuffin revolt into a…

bareilly.s: Bareilly is a city in Uttar Pradesh, India, on the Ramganga River, and the main city of the Rohilkhand region. It became the seat of the Rohilla chiefs under Hafiz Rahmat Khan in the mid-18th century.

bujumbura.s: Bujumbura, called Usumbura until 1962, is the largest city of Burundi, on the north-eastern shore of Lake Tanganyika. Founded as a German military post in the 1890s, it was the administrative centre of Belgian Ruanda-Urundi and the capital of Burundi from independence until…

battle-of-okitanawate.s: The Battle of Okitanawate was fought in 1584 near Shimabara in Hizen province, Kyushu. Ryuzoji Takanobu attacked Arima Harunobu, who was supported by a Shimazu army under Shimazu Iehisa; Takanobu was killed and his army routed.

boa-sabir-queen.s: Boa, also called Boarex, was a queen of the Sabirs, a steppe people north of the Caucasus, in the early 6th century. The widow of a chief named Balach, she ruled some 100,000 people and, according to the chronicler John Malalas, allied with the Byzantine emperor Justinian I…

battle-of-dayr-al-aqul.s: The Battle of Dayr al-Aqul was fought in 876 on the Tigris south-east of Baghdad. The Abbasid regent al-Muwaffaq defeated the Saffarid ruler Ya'qub ibn al-Layth, who was marching on Baghdad, after flooding the ground in front of his army.

balaputradewa.s: Balaputradewa was a prince of the Sailendra dynasty of Java who became king of Srivijaya in Sumatra in the 9th century. In a common but debated reconstruction, he left Central Java after the Sanjaya line under Rakai Pikatan prevailed there.

berel.s: Berel is a burial ground in the valley of the Bukhtarma river in the Kazakh Altai, in eastern Kazakhstan, with dozens of kurgans mostly of the 4th and 3rd centuries BCE. Ice lenses in some mounds preserved wooden coffins, felt and the bodies of horses with elaborate harness,…

bayburt.s: Bayburt is a city in north-eastern Turkey, capital of Bayburt province, on the Çoruh river. It lay on the route between Trebizond and Erzurum, and its large medieval castle was rebuilt under the Seljuks of Rum in the 13th century.

bar-rakib.s: Bar-Rakib was a king of Sam'al, an Aramaean kingdom in south-eastern Anatolia, in the later 8th century BCE. A loyal vassal of the Assyrian king Tiglath-Pileser III, he set up Aramaic inscriptions honouring his father Panamuwa II and boasting of his own palace building.

bovianum.s: Bovianum, modern Boiano in Molise, Italy, was the chief town of the Pentri, the largest of the Samnite peoples. It was captured several times by the Romans during the Samnite Wars and served as a headquarters of the Italian allies in the Social War of 91–88 BCE.

bruttium.s: Bruttium was the ancient name of the toe of Italy, roughly modern Calabria, named after its people, the Bruttii. Its coasts were lined with Greek cities such as Croton, Locri and Rhegion, while the Oscan-speaking Bruttii held the mountainous interior.

battle-of-the-caudine-forks.s: The Battle of the Caudine Forks in 321 BCE was a Roman disaster of the Second Samnite War. A Roman army marching through a narrow pass near Caudium in the southern Apennines was trapped by the Samnite general Gaius Pontius and forced to surrender without a fight.

battle-of-the-colline-gate.s: The Battle of the Colline Gate was fought on 1 November 82 BCE outside the walls of Rome. Sulla's army defeated a force of Samnites and Lucanians led by Pontius Telesinus, fighting with Roman opponents of Sulla, in a hard battle that lasted into the night, after which Sulla…

battle-of-wogastisburg.s: The Battle of Wogastisburg was fought in 631 or 632 between the Slavs led by Samo and the army of the Frankish king Dagobert I. According to the Chronicle of Fredegar, the Franks besieged the stronghold for three days before being routed and fleeing, leaving their camp behind.

baji-rao-ii.s: Baji Rao II was the last Peshwa of the Maratha Empire, ruling from Pune from 1795 to 1818. Driven out by Yashwantrao Holkar, he accepted British protection in the Treaty of Bassein in 1802, which helped provoke the Second Anglo-Maratha War.

brennus-4th-century-bce.s: Brennus was a chieftain of the Senones, a Gallic people of northern Italy, who according to Roman tradition defeated the Roman army at the Allia and sacked Rome in 390 BCE (about 387 BCE by modern reckoning). Livy tells that when the Romans complained about false weights used…

brennus-3rd-century-bce.s: Brennus was a Gallic leader who led the great Celtic invasion of Macedonia and Greece in 279 BCE. After forcing the pass at Thermopylae he attacked the sanctuary of Delphi, but was driven back by Aetolian and Phocian forces aided, according to legend, by storms and earthquakes…

brazilian-integralist-action.s: Brazilian Integralist Action was a far-right nationalist movement founded in 1932 by the writer Plínio Salgado, modelled on Italian fascism with green-shirted militias and the motto 'God, Fatherland and Family'. It grew into a mass party in the 1930s and backed Getúlio Vargas…

bela-kovacs-politician.s: Béla Kovács was a Hungarian politician and general secretary of the Independent Smallholders' Party, the largest party after the elections of 1945. In February 1947 Soviet forces arrested him on charges of conspiracy, in defiance of his parliamentary immunity, and deported him…

black-decree.s: The Black Decree was a law issued by Emperor Maximilian I of Mexico on 3 October 1865, declaring that members of armed bands fighting the empire would be tried by court-martial and executed within 24 hours. It rested on the false belief that Benito Juárez had left the country.

belarusians.s: Belarusians are an East Slavic people who form the majority of the population of Belarus and live in neighbouring parts of Poland, Lithuania, Russia and Ukraine. Their lands formed the core of the Grand Duchy of Lithuania, where Ruthenian, an ancestor of their language, was…

battle-of-urica.s: The Battle of Urica was fought on 5 December 1814 in eastern Venezuela between royalist forces under José Tomás Boves and the last patriot army, led by José Félix Ribas. The royalists won, but Boves was killed by a lance during the fighting.

bronze-of-ascoli.s: The Bronze of Ascoli is a Latin inscription on a bronze tablet recording that in 89 BCE the Roman general Gnaeus Pompeius Strabo granted Roman citizenship to a squadron of Iberian horsemen, the Turma Salluitana, for their bravery at the siege of Asculum in the Social War. Most…

bakircay.s: The Bakırçay is a river of western Turkey, known in antiquity as the Caicus, which flows west past Pergamon to the Aegean at the Gulf of Çandarlı. Some scholars place the Bronze Age Seha River Land, a vassal kingdom of the Hittites, in its valley, while others favour the Gediz.

babad-lombok.s: Babad Lombok is a traditional chronicle of the island of Lombok, written on palm leaves in a Javanese-influenced literary language. It recounts the origins of the Sasak kingdoms and the coming of Islam.

berkyaruq.s: Berkyaruq was sultan of the Great Seljuk Empire from 1094 to 1105, the eldest son of Malik Shah. His reign was taken up by wars with his uncle Tutush and his brothers, above all Muhammad Tapar, which divided the empire.

black-seminoles.s: The Black Seminoles were people of African descent, many of them escaped slaves from Georgia and the Carolinas, who lived alongside the Seminole in Florida. They kept their own villages, paid tribute to Seminole leaders and fought with them against the United States.

ballal-sena.s: Ballal Sena was a king of the Sena dynasty of Bengal who ruled in the 12th century, the son of Vijayasena. Tradition credits him with organising the ranking of Bengali Brahmins and other castes known as Kulinism.

bayda-libya.s: Bayda is a city in the Jebel Akhdar of eastern Libya, near the ruins of Cyrene. It grew around the first lodge, or zawiya, of the Senussi order, founded there by Muhammad ibn Ali al-Senussi in 1843.

besancon.s: Besançon is a city on the Doubs in eastern France, the historic capital of Franche-Comté. As Vesontio it was the chief oppidum of the Sequani, which Julius Caesar seized in 58 BCE, and later the capital of the province of Maxima Sequanorum.

brussels-agreement-2013.s: The Brussels Agreement of April 2013 was a deal between the governments of Serbia and Kosovo, mediated by the European Union, to normalise their relations. It provided for the integration of Serb-majority northern Kosovo into Kosovo's legal system in return for a planned…

baranya.s: Baranya is a region between the Danube and the Drava, centred on the city of Pécs. Long part of the Kingdom of Hungary, it was divided after the First World War, with the north remaining in Hungary as Baranya county and a southern strip passing to Yugoslavia and now Croatia.

battle-of-lauron.s: The Battle of Lauron was fought in 76 BCE in eastern Spain during the Sertorian War. Quintus Sertorius besieged the town of Lauron and outmanoeuvred Pompey's relief army, destroying part of it, and then took and burned the town.

battle-of-aegospotami.s: The Battle of Aegospotami was a naval battle in 405 BCE on the Hellespont, near Sestos. The Spartan admiral Lysander surprised the Athenian fleet drawn up on the beach and captured or destroyed almost all of it.

bhaskara-ii.s: Bhaskara II was an Indian mathematician and astronomer, author of the Siddhanta Shiromani, whose parts include the Lilavati on arithmetic and the Bijaganita on algebra. His work marks a high point of classical Indian mathematics.

bhagavad-gita.s: The Bhagavad Gita is a Hindu scripture of 700 Sanskrit verses forming part of the Mahabharata epic, probably composed in the last centuries BCE. It records a dialogue on the eve of battle between the prince Arjuna and the god Krishna on duty, devotion and liberation.

bhilwara.s: Bhilwara is a city in southern Rajasthan, India, and the headquarters of a district of the same name. Long part of the lands of Mewar, it has become one of India's main centres of textile manufacturing.

bayuda-desert.s: The Bayuda Desert is a rocky desert in northern Sudan, lying within the great bend of the Nile between Khartoum and Dongola. Caravan routes crossed it as a shortcut between the river's stretches.

battle-of-muye.s: The Battle of Muye was fought around 1046 BCE between King Wu of Zhou and his allies and Di Xin, the last king of the Shang dynasty. The Shang army was routed near their capital, and Di Xin killed himself.

baal-berith.s: Baal-Berith, "Lord of the Covenant", also called El-Berith, was a god worshipped at Shechem according to the Book of Judges. Judges records that the city's leaders paid Abimelech from his temple's treasury and that the temple was destroyed when Abimelech sacked Shechem.

burgan-field.s: The Burgan field in south-eastern Kuwait is one of the largest oil fields in the world. Oil was struck there in 1938 by the Kuwait Oil Company, a British and American venture, and exports began in 1946, transforming Kuwait from a pearling and trading town into a wealthy oil…

battle-of-al-wajbah.s: The Battle of Al Wajbah was fought in March 1893 near Doha between Qatari forces under Jassim bin Muhammad Al Thani and an Ottoman expedition led by the governor of Basra. Jassim's men defeated the Ottomans and forced them to release the hostages they held.

bandar-lengeh.s: Bandar Lengeh is a port on the Iranian coast of the Persian Gulf, in Hormozgan province. In the 18th and 19th centuries it was ruled by a branch of the Al Qasimi and thrived on pearling and entrepot trade.

battle-of-wuzhang-plains.s: The Battle of Wuzhang Plains was a stand-off in 234 between the Shu Han army of Zhuge Liang and the Wei forces of Sima Yi, on the Wei river in modern Shaanxi, China. It was Zhuge Liang's fifth and last northern expedition.

battle-of-xiaoting.s: The Battle of Xiaoting, also called the Battle of Yiling, was fought in 221–222 in western Hubei, China, between Liu Bei of Shu Han and Sun Quan's Eastern Wu. Liu Bei invaded to avenge Guan Yu and recover Jing province, but the Wu commander Lu Xun waited until summer and then…

bharhut.s: Bharhut is a village in Satna district, Madhya Pradesh, India, site of a Buddhist stupa of the 2nd century BCE. Its carved stone railings and gateways, decorated with scenes from the life of the Buddha and the Jataka tales and with labelled inscriptions, are among the earliest…

brihadratha-maurya.s: Brihadratha Maurya was the last emperor of the Maurya dynasty of India, ruling a much-reduced realm from Pataliputra in the early 2nd century BCE. Around 185 BCE his commander-in-chief, Pushyamitra Shunga, assassinated him while he reviewed the army and seized the throne,…

bai-bureh.s: Bai Bureh was a Temne ruler and war leader in northern Sierra Leone who led the Hut Tax War of 1898 against British rule. Opposing the new tax on dwellings in the protectorate, his fighters waged a skilled guerrilla campaign for months before he surrendered.

banda-singh-bahadur.s: Banda Singh Bahadur was a Sikh military leader who, after meeting Guru Gobind Singh in 1708, led a rising against Mughal rule in Punjab. He captured Sirhind in 1710, set up a Sikh administration with its own coinage and abolished the zamindari estates in the areas he held.

bak-hyeokgeose.s: Bak Hyeokgeose is the legendary founder of Silla, said in the Samguk sagi to have become king in 57 BCE, when the six villages of the Gyeongju basin chose him as ruler. According to legend he hatched from an egg found beside a well.

bulguksa.s: Bulguksa is a Buddhist temple on the slopes of Mount Toham near Gyeongju, South Korea. Its present form was begun in the mid-8th century under the Unified Silla minister Kim Daeseong, and its stone terraces, bridges and the pagodas Dabotap and Seokgatap survive from that time.

battle-of-dumlupinar.s: The Battle of Dumlupınar was the decisive battle of the Greco-Turkish War, fought from 26 to 30 August 1922 in western Anatolia. In the Great Offensive, Turkish forces under Mustafa Kemal broke the Greek lines near Afyonkarahisar and routed the Greek army at Dumlupınar.

battle-of-mogadishu-1993.s: The Battle of Mogadishu was fought on 3–4 October 1993 in the Somali capital, when US special forces trying to capture lieutenants of the warlord Mohamed Farrah Aidid were trapped after two Black Hawk helicopters were shot down. Eighteen American soldiers and hundreds of…

brahmeswara-temple.s: The Brahmeswara Temple is a Hindu temple dedicated to Shiva in Bhubaneswar, Odisha, built around 1058 according to an inscription that credits Queen Kolavati, mother of the Somavamshi king Udyota Keshari. Set in a courtyard with four smaller shrines at its corners, it is a…

batumi.s: Batumi is a port city on the Black Sea coast of south-western Georgia and the capital of the Autonomous Republic of Adjara. Ottoman from the 16th century until 1878, when the Congress of Berlin gave it to Russia, it became an oil-export terminal at the end of the railway and…

basay.s: The Basay were an Austronesian indigenous people of northern Taiwan, living around the harbours of Keelung and Tamsui and along the north-east coast. Known as traders, metalworkers and boatmen, they dealt with Chinese and Japanese merchants and later with the Spanish, who…

bou-craa.s: Bou Craa is a phosphate mine in Western Sahara, about 100 kilometres south-east of El Aaiún. The deposits were discovered by Spanish geologists in 1947 and production began in the early 1970s, with ore carried to the coast on a conveyor belt about 100 kilometres long.

bawbawgyi-pagoda.s: The Bawbawgyi Pagoda is a Buddhist stupa at Sri Ksetra, the ancient Pyu city near Pyay in central Myanmar, built around the fifth to seventh centuries. A tall brick cylinder on circular terraces, about 46 metres high, it is one of the oldest standing stupas in Myanmar and an…

book-of-mormon.s: The Book of Mormon is a sacred text of the Latter Day Saint movement, published in 1830 by Joseph Smith, who said he had translated it from golden plates revealed by an angel. It tells of ancient peoples who migrated from Israel to the Americas and of a visit by the risen…

barcelos-amazonas.s: Barcelos is a town on the middle Rio Negro in the Brazilian state of Amazonas. Founded as the mission village of Mariuá, it was renamed Barcelos in 1758 and became the first capital of the Captaincy of São José do Rio Negro, the forerunner of Amazonas.

branco-river.s: The Branco River is the main tributary of the Rio Negro, flowing through the Brazilian state of Roraima. Its valley was an approach to the Amazon from the Guianas, and in 1775 Portugal built Fort São Joaquim there to keep out the Spanish and the Dutch.

bo-qin.s: Bo Qin was the eldest son of the Duke of Zhou and the first ruler of the State of Lu in the eleventh century BCE. Because his father stayed at the Zhou court as regent for the young King Cheng, Bo Qin went in his place to govern Lu, with its capital at Qufu in Shandong, and…

beckman-revolt.s: The Beckman Revolt was a settlers' rising in São Luís, capital of the State of Maranhão, in February 1684, led by the planter Manuel Beckman. The rebels expelled the Jesuits, who opposed the enslavement of indigenous people, and abolished the trading company that held a…

belem.s: Belém is a port city near the mouth of the Amazon in northern Brazil and the capital of the state of Pará. The Portuguese founded it in 1616 as the fort of Presépio to secure the river against French, Dutch and English rivals.

bao-si.s: Bao Si was a consort of King You of Zhou in the 8th century BCE. According to the Shiji, the king deposed Queen Shen and the crown prince in favour of her and her son, and lit the warning beacons to make her laugh until the lords no longer answered them.

battle-of-hong.s: The Battle of Hong was fought in 638 BCE on the Hong River in Henan between the State of Song and the State of Chu. Duke Xiang of Song refused to attack the Chu army while it was crossing the river or before it had formed up, and was heavily defeated and wounded.

binh-xuyen.s: The Bình Xuyên was an armed organisation in Saigon in the 1940s and 1950s that grew from river pirates and gangs into a private army under Bảy Viễn. It fought the French, then came to terms with them, and under the State of Vietnam controlled the Saigon police, gambling and…

battle-of-xuge.s: The Battle of Xuge was fought in 707 BCE in Henan between King Huan of Zhou, with contingents from Chen, Cai and Wey, and Duke Zhuang of Zheng. Zheng's army routed the royal forces, and an archer wounded the king in the shoulder.
