bohras.s: The Bohras are a Muslim community of western India, chiefly Gujarat, most of whom follow the Musta'li Tayyibi branch of Isma'ili Shi'ism, the largest group being the Dawoodi Bohras. Converted by missionaries sent from Yemen from the 11th century, they took over the leadership…

bassa-people-liberia.s: The Bassa are a Kru-speaking people of central Liberia, living mostly in Grand Bassa and neighbouring counties along the coast and inland. They traded and clashed with the American settlers who founded colonies on their coast in the 1830s, among them Bassa Cove.

benadir.s: Benadir is the southern coast of Somalia on the Indian Ocean, centred on the old trading towns of Mogadishu, Merca and Barawa. From medieval times these ports exported ivory, hides and cloth across the Indian Ocean.

basic-statute-of-oman.s: The Basic Statute of Oman is the country's constitutional document, issued by royal decree of Sultan Qaboos bin Said in November 1996. It defines Oman as an Arab, Islamic and independent state ruled by a hereditary sultan, sets out rules of succession and basic rights, and…

baardheere.s: Baardheere, also written Bardera, is a town on the Jubba river in southern Somalia. In 1819 a community of militant religious reformers founded a settlement there that tried to impose strict Islamic practice on the surrounding region and fought neighbouring powers.

bimaal.s: The Bimaal are a Somali clan of the Dir family living in the coastal region around Merca in southern Somalia. In the 19th century they were rivals of the Geledi sultanate, and in 1878 they killed Sultan Ahmed Yusuf in battle.

banu-djellab.s: The Banu Djellab were the ruling dynasty of Touggourt and the oases of the Oued Righ in the north-eastern Algerian Sahara from about 1414 to 1854. Traditionally said to be of Marinid descent, they ruled as sultans over a mixed oasis population, at times paying tribute to the…

battle-of-gawakuke.s: The Battle of Gawakuke was fought in 1836 in northern Hausaland, where the forces of the Sokoto Caliphate under Sultan Muhammad Bello defeated a coalition of the Hausa states of Gobir and Katsina-Maradi that had risen against the caliphate. The ruler of Gobir was killed.

binokasih.s: The Binokasih is the royal crown of the Sunda Kingdom of western Java. According to tradition, when the Banten Sultanate destroyed the Sundanese capital Pakuan Pajajaran in 1579, Sunda nobles carried the crown and regalia to Sumedang Larang, whose ruler Prabu Geusan Ulun then…

batutulis-inscription.s: The Batutulis inscription is an Old Sundanese stone inscription in Bogor, West Java, set up in 1533 by King Surawisesa in memory of his father Sri Baduga Maharaja. It praises the late king for building a moat around the capital Pakuan Pajajaran, raising an artificial hill,…

borommarachathirat-i.s: Borommarachathirat I, earlier Khun Luang Pa-ngua, ruler of Suphanburi, was king of Ayutthaya from 1370 to 1388. A brother-in-law of U Thong, the founder of Ayutthaya, he seized the throne from U Thong's son Ramesuan and established the Suphannaphum dynasty in power.

battle-of-chausa.s: The Battle of Chausa was fought in June 1539 near Chausa on the Ganges in Bihar, where the Afghan leader Sher Khan surprised and routed the army of the Mughal emperor Humayun. Humayun barely escaped by swimming the river.

baeza.s: Baeza is a town in the province of Jaén, Andalusia, Spain, on a ridge above the Guadalquivir valley. In 1224–1226 it was the base of the Almohad prince al-Bayyasi, who proclaimed himself caliph there and allied with Ferdinand III of Castile, and it passed to Castile in 1227.

banu-birzal.s: The Banu Birzal were a Zanata Berber clan from North Africa brought to al-Andalus as soldiers by the regent al-Mansur in the late 10th century. During the civil war that destroyed the Caliphate of Córdoba they seized Carmona around 1013 and ruled it as an independent taifa,…

book-of-roads-and-kingdoms-al-bakri.s: The Book of Roads and Kingdoms (Kitab al-Masalik wa'l-Mamalik) is a geographical work completed in 1068 by the Andalusi scholar Abu Ubayd al-Bakri in Córdoba. Compiled from earlier writings and travellers' reports rather than his own journeys, it describes the routes and lands…

battle-of-almenar-1082.s: The Battle of Almenar was fought in 1082 near Almenar, north of Lleida in Catalonia. El Cid, commanding for al-Mutaman of the Taifa of Zaragoza, defeated an alliance of al-Mutaman's brother al-Mundhir of Lleida, Tortosa and Dénia with Count Berenguer Ramon II of Barcelona,…

banu-hud.s: The Hudid dynasty (Banu Hud) ruled the Taifa of Zaragoza from 1039 to 1110. Founded by Sulayman ibn Hud al-Mustain, it reached its height under Ahmad al-Muqtadir, who annexed Tortosa and Dénia and built the Aljafería palace, and it employed El Cid in the 1080s.

battle-of-valtierra.s: The Battle of Valtierra was fought on 24 January 1110 near Valtierra in Navarre, Spain. Ahmad al-Mustain II of Zaragoza, returning from a raid into Christian territory, was defeated and killed by the forces of Alfonso I of Aragon.

battle-of-toba-fushimi.s: The Battle of Toba–Fushimi, fought from 27 to 31 January 1868 south of Kyoto, opened the Boshin War in Japan. Forces of the Tokugawa shogunate, including troops from Aizu and Kuwana, were defeated by the smaller but better-armed armies of Satsuma and Chōshū fighting under the…

battles-of-kawanakajima.s: The Battles of Kawanakajima were five battles fought between Takeda Shingen and Uesugi Kenshin from 1553 to 1564 on the plain of Kawanakajima in northern Shinano, Japan. The fourth, in 1561, was one of the bloodiest of the Sengoku period, with heavy losses on both sides, but…

battle-of-mikatagahara.s: The Battle of Mikatagahara was fought on 25 January 1573 near Hamamatsu in Tōtōmi Province, Japan. Takeda Shingen, advancing west, crushed the army of Tokugawa Ieyasu and his Oda allies, and Ieyasu barely escaped to Hamamatsu Castle.

battle-of-nagashino.s: The Battle of Nagashino was fought on 28 June 1575 in Mikawa Province, Japan. Oda Nobunaga and Tokugawa Ieyasu, relieving the besieged Nagashino Castle, defeated the army of Takeda Katsuyori by using massed musketeers behind wooden palisades against the Takeda cavalry.

battle-of-tenmokuzan.s: The Battle of Tenmokuzan was fought in April 1582 in Kai Province, Japan, when the forces of Oda Nobunaga and Tokugawa Ieyasu invaded the Takeda lands. Abandoned by most of his vassals, Takeda Katsuyori was cornered near Mount Tenmoku and killed himself with his son and…

baloch-people.s: The Baloch are an Iranian-speaking people of Balochistan, a region divided between Pakistan, Iran and Afghanistan, who speak the Balochi language. Organised in tribes under hereditary chiefs, many migrated over the centuries into Sindh and Punjab, where Baloch families such as…

battle-of-hyderabad-1843.s: The Battle of Hyderabad, also called the Battle of Dubba, was fought on 24 March 1843 near Hyderabad in Sindh. A British force under Charles Napier defeated the army of the Talpur ruler Mir Sher Muhammad of Mirpur Khas.

battle-of-tanagra.s: The Battle of Tanagra was fought in 457 BCE near Tanagra in Boeotia, Greece, between Athens with its allies and a Spartan-led army returning from central Greece. The Spartans won narrowly but went home, and about two months later Athens defeated the Boeotians at Oenophyta and…

banten.s: Banten is a province at the western tip of Java, Indonesia, separated from West Java in 2000. Its old port of Banten, on the bay of the same name, was the centre of the Banten Sultanate, founded after Muslim forces from Demak and Cirebon took it from the Sunda Kingdom in the…

bayonne.s: Bayonne is a city in the French Basque Country, where the Nive joins the Adour near the Atlantic. Under English rule from 1152 to 1451 it was a busy port of Gascony, and its fortifications were later rebuilt by Vauban.

binh-dinh-province.s: Bình Định is a coastal province of south-central Vietnam with its capital at Quy Nhơn. It was the heartland of the Cham kingdom centred on Vijaya until the Vietnamese conquest of 1471, and in 1771 the Tây Sơn brothers began their rebellion from the village of Tây Sơn in its…

battle-of-rach-gam-xoai-mut.s: The Battle of Rạch Gầm–Xoài Mút was fought on the Mekong in present-day Tiền Giang province, southern Vietnam, in January 1785. Tây Sơn forces under Nguyễn Huệ ambushed and destroyed a Siamese fleet and army that had come to restore Nguyễn Ánh, heir of the Nguyễn lords.

battle-of-the-thames.s: The Battle of the Thames was fought on 5 October 1813 near Moraviantown in Upper Canada, now Ontario. An American army under William Henry Harrison defeated a retreating British and Native force under Henry Procter and Tecumseh, who was killed.

battle-of-tippecanoe.s: The Battle of Tippecanoe was fought on 7 November 1811 near Prophetstown, in present-day Indiana, between United States forces under Governor William Henry Harrison and warriors of Tecumseh's confederacy, led in his absence by his brother Tenskwatawa. Harrison's army repelled…

battle-of-the-fetters.s: The Battle of the Fetters was fought in the 6th century BCE between Sparta and the Arcadian city of Tegea. According to Herodotus, the Spartans marched carrying chains to bind the Tegeans as serfs, but were defeated and forced to work Tegea's fields in their own fetters.

british-garhwal.s: British Garhwal was the eastern part of the Garhwal region in the Himalaya of present-day Uttarakhand, India, annexed by the East India Company after the Anglo-Nepalese War of 1814–1816. The western part was restored to the Garhwal dynasty as Tehri Garhwal State.

bela-i-of-hungary.s: Béla I was king of Hungary from 1060 to 1063. The younger brother of Andrew I, he returned from exile in Poland and in 1048 received a third of the kingdom as a duchy, the tercia pars regni.

baginda-omar.s: Baginda Omar, Sultan Omar Riayat Shah, ruled Terengganu on the east coast of the Malay Peninsula from 1839 to 1876. One of the state's strongest rulers, he strengthened the sultan's authority over the chiefs and encouraged trade, mining and crafts such as brocade weaving.

bellerophon.s: Bellerophon was a hero of Greek myth, best known for taming the winged horse Pegasus and killing the Chimera in Lycia. Sent by King Iobates on deadly tasks, he also fought the Solymi and the Amazons, and was rewarded with a share of the kingdom.

babullah.s: Babullah was sultan of Ternate in the Maluku Islands from 1570 to 1583. After the Portuguese murdered his father, Sultan Hairun, he besieged their fort on Ternate until they surrendered it in 1575, and extended the sultanate's influence over many islands of eastern Indonesia.

bishopric-of-osel-wiek.s: The Bishopric of Ösel–Wiek was a prince-bishopric of medieval Livonia, covering the islands of Saaremaa (Ösel) and Hiiumaa and the Läänemaa (Wiek) region of western Estonia. Founded in 1228 after the crusader conquest and ruled from Haapsalu and later Kuressaare, it was a…

big-five-hawaii.s: The Big Five were five corporations that dominated the economy and politics of Hawaii in the late 19th and early 20th centuries: Castle & Cooke, Alexander & Baldwin, C. Brewer & Co., American Factors and Theo H. Davies & Co. Founded as agents for sugar plantations, they also…

bougainville-island.s: Bougainville is the largest island of the Solomon Islands chain but is politically part of Papua New Guinea. Named after the French navigator Louis-Antoine de Bougainville, it was ruled by Germany and then Australia, and saw heavy fighting in the Second World War.

bulolo.s: Bulolo is a town in Morobe Province, Papua New Guinea, in the valley of the Bulolo River. Gold was found in the area in the 1920s, and in the 1930s huge dredges were flown in piece by piece from Lae, a landmark in the history of air freight.

black-saturday-1929.s: Black Saturday was the shooting of a peaceful Mau procession by New Zealand police in Apia, Western Samoa, on 28 December 1929. About eleven Samoans were killed, among them the Mau leader Tupua Tamasese Lealofi III, who urged his followers not to retaliate.

batanaea.s: Batanaea was a region east of the Sea of Galilee and north of the Yarmuk River, in present-day southern Syria, corresponding to part of biblical Bashan. Augustus granted it to Herod the Great in the 20s BCE, and it was later ruled by Philip the Tetrarch and the last Herodian…

battle-of-philippi.s: The Battle of Philippi was fought in October 42 BCE near the city of Philippi in eastern Macedonia. The forces of the Second Triumvirate under Mark Antony and Octavian defeated the army of Brutus and Cassius, assassins of Julius Caesar, in two engagements, after which both…

bad-mergentheim.s: Bad Mergentheim is a spa town on the Tauber river in north-eastern Baden-Württemberg, Germany. From 1527 its castle was the seat of the grand masters of the Teutonic Order, which ruled the surrounding district until it passed to Württemberg in 1809.

bophuthatswana.s: Bophuthatswana was a Bantustan created by apartheid South Africa for Tswana-speaking people, declared independent in 1977 but recognised by no country other than South Africa. It consisted of several separate enclaves, with its capital at Mmabatho, and was ruled by Lucas Mangope.

battle-of-vegkop.s: The Battle of Vegkop was fought on 16 October 1836 in the present-day Free State, South Africa, between Voortrekkers under Andries Potgieter and an Ndebele army sent by Mzilikazi. About 40 Boers in a laager of wagons repelled several thousand warriors, but the Ndebele drove…

bhumibol-adulyadej.s: Bhumibol Adulyadej, also known as Rama IX, was king of Thailand from 1946 until his death in 2016, the longest reign in Thai history. Coming to the throne after the death of his brother Ananda Mahidol, he became a revered figure and an arbiter in political crises, while the…

battle-of-alange.s: The Battle of Alange was fought in 1230 near Alange, in modern Extremadura, between the army of Alfonso IX of León and the forces of Ibn Hud, ruler of Murcia and much of al-Andalus. Alfonso's victory opened the way to the Leonese capture of Mérida and Badajoz that year,…

battle-of-the-puig.s: The Battle of the Puig was fought in 1237 at El Puig, a hill north of Valencia, where Aragonese troops holding a fortress built on the orders of James I defeated an army sent by Zayyan ibn Mardanish, ruler of Valencia. The victory secured the Christian foothold near the city…

behbeit-el-hagar.s: Behbeit el-Hagar is an archaeological site in the Nile Delta of Egypt, near Samannud, the ancient Sebennytos. It holds the ruins of a great temple of Isis begun by Nectanebo II of the Thirtieth Dynasty and completed under the Ptolemies.

bormio.s: Bormio is a town in the upper Valtellina in Lombardy, northern Italy, at the foot of the Stelvio pass and known for its hot springs. As a self-governing county on the routes between Lombardy and the Tyrol, it was conquered by the Three Leagues of the Grisons in 1512 together…

battle-of-deresge.s: The Battle of Deresge was fought on 9 February 1855 in Semien, northern Ethiopia, where Kassa Hailu defeated Wube Haile Maryam, lord of Tigray and Semien. It removed the last great regional rival to Kassa, who was crowned emperor as Tewodros II at the church of Deresge Maryam…

bulgarians.s: The Bulgarians are a South Slavic people of the eastern Balkans. They formed from the union of the Turkic Bulgars of Asparuh, who crossed the Danube in 681, with the Slavs already settled in Moesia, and the conversion to Christianity under Boris I in 864 and the adoption of…

boyoma-falls.s: Boyoma Falls, formerly Stanley Falls, are a series of seven cataracts on the Lualaba, where it becomes the Congo River, stretching about 100 kilometres near Kisangani in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Named after Henry Morton Stanley, they gave their name to a station…

battle-of-komaki-and-nagakute.s: The Battle of Komaki and Nagakute was a campaign fought in 1584 in Owari province, Japan, between Toyotomi Hideyoshi and the allied forces of Tokugawa Ieyasu and Oda Nobukatsu. Ieyasu won a notable victory at Nagakute, where Hideyoshi's commanders Ikeda Tsuneoki and Mori…

basse-terre.s: Basse-Terre is the capital of the French overseas region of Guadeloupe, in the Caribbean, on the south-west coast of the island of Basse-Terre. Founded by French settlers in 1643, it was the seat of the colony's governors, while Pointe-à-Pitre became the main commercial port.

bandiagara.s: Bandiagara is a town in central Mali on the plateau above the Bandiagara Escarpment, the line of cliffs inhabited by the Dogon people and listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site. After the death of Umar Tall in 1864, his nephew Tidiani Tall made it the capital of the eastern…

bua-province.s: Bua is a province of Fiji in the west of the island of Vanua Levu. In the 19th century its chiefs were drawn into the wars and alliances of northern and eastern Fiji, and in 1867 they joined the Tongan noble Enele Maʻafu and the chiefs of Lau and Cakaudrove in forming the…

battle-of-shizugatake.s: The Battle of Shizugatake was fought in 1583 near Lake Biwa in Omi province, Japan, between Toyotomi Hideyoshi and Shibata Katsuie, rival successors to Oda Nobunaga. Hideyoshi made a rapid forced march to the battlefield and defeated Katsuie's commander Sakuma Morimasa;…

battle-of-yamazaki.s: The Battle of Yamazaki was fought in July 1582 near Yamazaki, between Kyoto and Osaka, where Toyotomi Hideyoshi defeated Akechi Mitsuhide, who had killed Oda Nobunaga at the Honnoji temple less than two weeks earlier. Mitsuhide was killed while fleeing, and Hideyoshi's swift…

brumath.s: Brumath is a town in Alsace, north-eastern France, about 17 kilometres north of Strasbourg. As Brocomagus it was the chief town of the Triboci, a Germanic people settled on the left bank of the Rhine, and under Roman rule the capital of their civitas on the road along the Rhine.

black-power-revolution.s: The Black Power Revolution was a wave of protests in Trinidad and Tobago in February–April 1970, led by students and the National Joint Action Committee, demanding economic power for Afro- and Indo-Trinidadians. Mass marches and strikes led Prime Minister Eric Williams to…

bikini-atoll.s: Bikini Atoll is a ring of coral islands in the northern Marshall Islands. In 1946 the United States moved its inhabitants to other atolls and began nuclear testing there with Operation Crossroads, followed by 23 nuclear explosions up to 1958, including the Castle Bravo…

baba-vida.s: Baba Vida is a medieval fortress on the bank of the Danube at Vidin in north-western Bulgaria, built mainly between the 10th and 14th centuries on the site of the Roman town of Bononia. It served as the residence of Ivan Sratsimir, ruler of the Tsardom of Vidin, and was later…

baltasar-maldonado.s: Baltasar Maldonado was a Spanish conquistador in the New Kingdom of Granada, in present-day Colombia. A captain in the conquest of the Muisca lands, in 1539 he led the expedition against Tundama, the ruler of Duitama, who had resisted Spanish rule.

battle-of-bonza.s: The Battle of Bonza was fought in 1539 near Duitama in present-day Boyacá, Colombia, between Spanish forces under Baltasar Maldonado, with Indian auxiliaries, and the warriors of Tundama, a Muisca ruler who had refused to submit. Tundama's army was defeated after fierce…

battle-of-the-defile.s: The Battle of the Defile was fought in 731 at the Takhtakaracha pass between Kesh and Samarkand in Central Asia. An Umayyad army under the governor of Khurasan, Junayd ibn Abd al-Rahman, marching to relieve Samarkand, was ambushed by the Turgesh under Suluk and their Sogdian…

battle-of-kharistan.s: The Battle of Kharistan was fought in December 737 in Guzgan, in present-day northern Afghanistan. The Umayyad governor of Khurasan, Asad ibn Abdallah al-Qasri, surprised the Turgesh khagan Suluk and his allies as they raided south of the Oxus and defeated them.

battle-of-geok-tepe.s: The Battle of Geok Tepe was the Russian siege and storming of the Teke Turkmen fortress of Geok Tepe, near present-day Ashgabat, by General Mikhail Skobelev in December 1880 and January 1881. After the walls were breached with a mine on 24 January 1881, thousands of defenders…

balikh-river.s: The Balikh is a river of northern Mesopotamia that rises near the Turkish–Syrian border and flows south for about 100 kilometres to join the Euphrates at Raqqa. Its valley was a corridor for trade and armies, with Harran near its upper course and the Bronze Age city of Tuttul,…

buyan-badyrgy.s: Buyan-Badyrgy was a Tuvan noble and politician who led the government of the Tuvan People's Republic in the 1920s. He favoured a moderate course that respected Buddhism and the traditional order and sought closer ties with Mongolia.

battle-of-dafei-river.s: The Battle of Dafei River was fought in 670 near Lake Kokonor in present-day Qinghai, China. A Tibetan army under the general Gar Trinring Tsendro destroyed a Tang army commanded by Xue Rengui, which had been sent to restore the Tuyuhun kingdom conquered by Tibet in 663.

bakenranef.s: Bakenranef, called Bocchoris by the Greeks, was the second and last king of the Twenty-fourth Dynasty of Egypt, ruling from Sais in the western Delta in the 720s BCE. Greek writers remembered him as a wise lawgiver who reformed contract law.

bubastis.s: Bubastis was a city in the eastern Nile Delta, at Tell Basta near modern Zagazig, and the cult centre of the cat goddess Bastet. Libyan chiefs of the Meshwesh settled there, and their descendant Shoshenq I founded the Twenty-second Dynasty, whose kings enlarged its temple.

bubastite-portal.s: The Bubastite Portal is a gateway in the temple of Amun at Karnak in Thebes, built by kings of the Twenty-second Dynasty, whose family came from Bubastis. Its walls bear a great relief of Shoshenq I smiting his enemies, with a list of more than 150 places in Palestine taken in…

battle-of-tedorigawa.s: The Battle of Tedorigawa was fought in 1577 at the Tedori River in Kaga Province, Japan, between the forces of Uesugi Kenshin and an army sent by Oda Nobunaga under Shibata Katsuie. Kenshin's troops routed the Oda army as it crossed the river.

bevagna.s: Bevagna, the ancient Mevania, is a small town in the Umbrian plain of central Italy, on the route of the Roman Via Flaminia. An Umbrian community and then a Roman municipium, it preserves a Roman mosaic of sea creatures and the remains of a theatre.

battle-of-la-ciudadela.s: The Battle of La Ciudadela was fought on 4 November 1831 near San Miguel de Tucumán in Argentina, where Juan Facundo Quiroga's Federalist army defeated the Unitarian forces of Gregorio Aráoz de Lamadrid. The victory destroyed the League of the Interior, and the interior…

battle-of-la-tablada.s: The Battle of La Tablada was fought on 22 and 23 June 1829 near Córdoba, Argentina, between the Unitarian army of José María Paz and the Federalist caudillo Juan Facundo Quiroga. Paz's disciplined troops defeated Quiroga's larger force of gaucho cavalry, securing his hold on…

battle-of-oncativo.s: The Battle of Oncativo, also called Laguna Larga, was fought on 25 February 1830 in Córdoba Province, Argentina, where José María Paz's Unitarian army again defeated Juan Facundo Quiroga. The victory let Paz install Unitarian governors in the interior provinces, which formed…

breda.s: Breda is a city in the province of North Brabant in the southern Netherlands. From 1403 it belonged to the House of Nassau, the family of William the Silent, and its castle was a seat of the princes of Orange.

battle-of-turnhout-1789.s: The Battle of Turnhout was fought on 27 October 1789 in the town of Turnhout, in the Austrian Netherlands, where the patriot army of the Brabant Revolution under Jan Andries van der Mersch defeated Austrian troops. The victory encouraged risings across the provinces, and by…

braila.s: Brăila is a city on the lower Danube in eastern Romania, in the historical region of Wallachia. Held by the Ottomans as a fortress from the mid-16th century to 1829, it was returned to Wallachia by the Treaty of Adrianople and became a free port.

bernardino-rivadavia.s: Bernardino Rivadavia was an Argentine statesman and the first President of the United Provinces of the Río de la Plata, in 1826–1827. As a minister of Buenos Aires province in the early 1820s he founded the University of Buenos Aires, reformed the Church and public finances…

bill-of-rights-1689.s: The Bill of Rights 1689 is an Act of the English Parliament that set out the terms on which William III and Mary II took the throne after the Glorious Revolution. It declared illegal the suspension of laws and taxation without Parliament's consent, forbade a standing army in…

bandung.s: Bandung is a city in the highlands of western Java, Indonesia, and the capital of West Java province. Under Dutch rule it grew into a cool hill town with planned Art Deco districts and a technical college, and was intended as a future colonial capital.

biryawaza.s: Biryawaza was a ruler in southern Syria in the 14th century BCE, known from the Amarna letters, the diplomatic correspondence of the Egyptian pharaohs. Based in the land of Upi around Damascus, he served as an Egyptian vassal and agent, opposing the expansion of the Hittites…

bunjikat.s: Bunjikat was the capital of the principality of Ustrushana in Central Asia, identified with the ruins of Kahkaha near Shahristan in northern Tajikistan, south-west of Istaravshan. Soviet excavations there uncovered the palace of the local rulers, the afshins, decorated with…

bahrain-island.s: Bahrain Island, known in medieval Arabic sources as Awal, is the largest island of the Bahrain archipelago in the Persian Gulf and the site of the capital, Manama. Fresh springs and date groves made it a centre of settlement since the Dilmun civilisation.

burgos.s: Burgos is a city in northern Spain, capital of the province of Burgos in Castile and León. Founded in 884 as a frontier fortress by Count Diego Rodríguez Porcelos, it became the capital of the County of Castile and long the chief city of the Kingdom of Castile, prospering on…

banffshire.s: Banffshire is a historic county of north-east Scotland, stretching from the Moray Firth coast at Banff and Macduff south into the Cairngorm mountains, including much of the Spey valley. It was used for local government until 1975 and is now divided between the Moray and…

burghead.s: Burghead is a village on the Moray Firth coast of north-east Scotland, built over the largest known Pictish fort. The promontory fort, defended by massive timber-laced ramparts, was occupied from about the 4th to the 10th century and was probably a major royal centre of the…

battle-of-ad-decimum.s: The Battle of Ad Decimum was fought on 13 September 533 at the tenth milestone south of Carthage, where the Byzantine general Belisarius defeated the Vandal army of King Gelimer. Gelimer's attempt to trap the invaders failed, and Belisarius entered Carthage two days later.

battle-of-tricamarum.s: The Battle of Tricamarum was fought in December 533 west of Carthage, where the Byzantine army of Belisarius defeated the Vandal king Gelimer and his brother Tzazon, who was killed. Gelimer fled to the mountains and surrendered in 534.

bhavadeva-bhatta.s: Bhavadeva Bhatta was a Brahmin scholar and minister of King Harivarman of the Varman dynasty of eastern Bengal. He wrote treatises on Vedic ritual, Mimamsa philosophy and Hindu law, among them works on rites and penances used in Bengal for centuries.

bhavabhuti.s: Bhavabhuti was a Sanskrit dramatist and poet of the 8th century, from Vidarbha, who lived at the court of King Yashovarman of Kannauj. His three surviving plays are the Mahaviracharita and Uttararamacharita, on the story of Rama, and the romantic drama Malatimadhava.

bazas.s: Bazas is a small town in the Gironde department of south-west France, south of the Garonne. As Cossium, later Civitas Vasatica, it was the chief town of the Gallic Vasates, from whose name it derives.

battle-of-palnadu.s: The Battle of Palnadu was fought around 1182 at Karempudi in the Palnadu region of Andhra Pradesh, India, between two branches of the Haihaya chiefs of Palnadu and their allies. Led on one side by the minister Nagamma and on the other by Brahma Naidu, it destroyed much of the…

bayezid-ii.s: Bayezid II was sultan of the Ottoman Empire from 1481 to 1512, the son of Mehmed II. His early reign was shaped by the rivalry of his brother Cem.

bourtzi.s: The Bourtzi is a small castle on an islet in the harbour of Nafplio in the Peloponnese, Greece, built by the Venetians in 1471 to guard the entrance to the port, which could be closed with a chain. Later held by the Ottomans and again by Venice, it was used in modern times as…

borre-mound-cemetery.s: The Borre mound cemetery, in Horten in Vestfold, Norway, is one of the largest royal burial grounds of Scandinavia, with great burial mounds of the 7th to 10th centuries. A ship burial excavated there in 1852 gave its name to the Borre style of Viking art.

blas-de-lezo.s: Blas de Lezo was a Spanish admiral from Pasajes in the Basque Country who had lost a leg, an eye and the use of an arm in earlier battles. As naval commander at Cartagena de Indias in 1741 he helped Viceroy Sebastián de Eslava repel the large British expedition of Admiral…

blasco-nunez-vela.s: Blasco Núñez Vela was the first viceroy of Peru, sent by Charles V to enforce the New Laws of 1542, which limited the encomiendas held by the conquerors. His arrival in 1544 provoked a revolt of encomenderos under Gonzalo Pizarro; the Audiencia deposed him, and he was defeated…

bolivian-national-revolution.s: The Bolivian National Revolution began in April 1952, when the Revolutionary Nationalist Movement (MNR) of Víctor Paz Estenssoro, backed by armed miners and workers, overthrew the military government. The new regime introduced universal suffrage, nationalised the large tin…

battle-of-wesenberg-1268.s: The Battle of Wesenberg was fought on 18 February 1268 near Rakvere in northern Estonia between an army of Novgorod and Pskov, led by Prince Dmitry of Pereslavl and Dovmont of Pskov, and the forces of Danish Estonia and the Livonian Order. Both sides suffered heavy losses and…

beziers.s: Béziers is a city on the River Orb in the Hérault department of Languedoc, southern France. A pre-Roman settlement that became the Roman colony of Baeterrae, it was later held by the Trencavel viscounts.

brive-la-gaillarde.s: Brive-la-Gaillarde is a town on the River Corrèze in the Limousin, central France. A market and route centre since Roman times, it grew around the collegiate church of Saint-Martin and was fortified in the Middle Ages, close to the castle of the viscounts of Turenne.

basarab-i.s: Basarab I was the first independent ruler of Wallachia, first recorded in 1324, who united the Romanian lands between the Southern Carpathians and the Danube. In November 1330 his forces ambushed and defeated King Charles I of Hungary at Posada, securing Wallachia's…

bilyar.s: Bilyar was a major city of Volga Bulgaria, in present-day Tatarstan, Russia, east of the Volga. In the 11th and 12th centuries it served as the capital, a fortified trading centre covering several square kilometres and one of the largest cities of eastern Europe.

bolghar.s: Bolghar (Bolgar) was a city on the Volga, south of modern Kazan in Tatarstan, Russia, and a capital and trading centre of Volga Bulgaria from the 10th century. After the Mongol conquest it became an important city of the Golden Horde, where coins were minted, and it flourished…

battle-of-samara-bend.s: The Battle of Samara Bend was fought in 1223 near the great bend of the Volga at Samara, Russia, when the Volga Bulgars ambushed part of the Mongol army of Subutai and Jebe returning from its victory on the Kalka River. Medieval sources report heavy Mongol losses.

bolsena.s: Bolsena is a town on the north-eastern shore of Lake Bolsena in northern Lazio, Italy. It grew from Volsinii Novi, the new town where Rome resettled the people of Etruscan Volsinii after destroying their city in 264 BCE.

brak.s: Brak was the title of the kings of Waalo, a Wolof kingdom on the lower Senegal river. The Brak was chosen by a council of electors from among the royal maternal lineages and ruled from Nder, sharing power with titled officials and royal women such as the linger, the queen…

balhaf.s: Balhaf is a small coastal settlement on the Gulf of Aden in Shabwah Governorate, southern Yemen. It was the seat of the Wahidi Sultanate of Balhaf, one of the Wahidi states under British protection in the Aden Protectorate, which joined the Federation of South Arabia in the…

babatu.s: Babatu was a leader of the Zabarma, horsemen from the Niger region who had come to northern Ghana as mercenaries in the Dagomba country and turned to slave raiding. Under his command in the 1880s and 1890s they ravaged the Grunshi lands and the Wa area.

balga-castle.s: Balga Castle is a ruined castle of the Teutonic Order on the shore of the Vistula Lagoon, in today's Kaliningrad Oblast of Russia. The Order captured the Prussian stronghold of Honeda there in 1239 and built a castle that served as an early base for the conquest of Warmia and…

bissandugu.s: Bissandugu is a town in the Kankan region of eastern Guinea that served as the capital of Samori Ture's Wassoulou Empire from the 1870s. In 1887 Samori and the French signed a treaty there that recognised the Niger as the boundary between their territories.

bauhaus.s: The Bauhaus was a German school of art, design and architecture founded by Walter Gropius at Weimar in 1919. It sought to unite crafts and fine arts and became a leading centre of modernist design, with teachers such as Paul Klee, Wassily Kandinsky and László Moholy-Nagy.

basava.s: Basava, also called Basavanna, was a 12th-century Kannada poet, philosopher and social reformer and a minister at the court of the Kalachuri ruler Bijjala II at Kalyani. He led the Virashaiva or Lingayat movement, which rejected caste distinctions and temple ritual in favour…

bilhana.s: Bilhana was an 11th-century Sanskrit poet from Kashmir who left his homeland, travelled through northern India and became court poet of the Western Chalukya king Vikramaditya VI at Kalyani. His Vikramankadevacharita, a verse biography of the king, is an important source for…

baoji.s: Baoji is a city in western Shaanxi province, China, on the Wei River at the western end of the Guanzhong plain. The area was an early homeland of the Zhou, whose ancestral plain of Zhouyuan lies within its territory, and of the State of Qin.

bingling-temple.s: Bingling Temple is a group of Buddhist cave temples in the cliffs of a canyon on the Yellow River in Yongjing County, Gansu, China, now reached by boat across the Liujiaxia reservoir. Carving began under the Western Qin, and an inscription in Cave 169 dated 420 is the earliest…

battle-of-white-wolf-mountain.s: The Battle of White Wolf Mountain was fought in 207 in present-day Liaoning between the forces of the Chinese warlord Cao Cao and the Wuhuan, who were sheltering Yuan Shao's sons Yuan Shang and Yuan Xi. After a hard march through the mountains, Cao Cao's vanguard under Zhang…

baochu-pagoda.s: The Baochu Pagoda is a slender Buddhist pagoda on Precious Stone Hill above the north shore of West Lake in Hangzhou, China. It was first built in the time of the Wuyue kingdom in the 10th century and has been rebuilt several times, most recently in 1933.

battle-of-hulao.s: The Battle of Hulao was fought in 621 at the Hulao Pass, a fortified gap west of modern Zhengzhou in Henan, during the wars that followed the fall of the Sui dynasty. The Tang prince Li Shimin, besieging Wang Shichong in Luoyang, held the pass against Dou Jiande's relieving…

battle-of-mingtiao.s: The Battle of Mingtiao is the battle in which, according to traditional Chinese history, Tang, founder of the Shang dynasty, defeated Jie, the last king of the Xia dynasty, around 1600 BCE. Jie fled and died in exile, and the event became the classic example of a virtuous…

bunkeya.s: Bunkeya is a town in Haut-Katanga province of the Democratic Republic of the Congo. In the second half of the 19th century it was the capital of Msiri's Yeke kingdom, a great trading centre for copper, ivory and slaves.

beidi-commandery.s: Beidi Commandery, the 'Northern Land', was a commandery of the Qin and Han empires on the north-western frontier of China, in eastern Gansu and Ningxia. It was created by the state of Qin after it destroyed the Yiqu Rong in the 3rd century BCE and guarded the frontier against…

book-of-wei.s: The Book of Wei (Wei shu) is the official history of the Northern Wei dynasty of China and its successor the Eastern Wei, compiled by Wei Shou and presented in 554 under the Northern Qi. Covering the Tuoba Xianbei rulers from their origins to 550, it is a major source for…

blagaj.s: Blagaj is a village near Mostar in Bosnia and Herzegovina, at the source of the Buna river below a high cliff. Above it stand the ruins of the fortress of Stjepan grad, a seat of the rulers of Hum, among them Herzog Stjepan Vukčić Kosača in the 15th century.

bakil.s: The Bakil are the largest tribal confederation of northern Yemen, spread across the highlands north and east of Sanaa, and with the Hashid one of the two great tribal blocs of the country. For centuries they supplied warriors to the Zaydi imams and to their rivals, and after…

balsa-i.s: Balša I was a nobleman of Zeta and founder of the Balšić family. After the death of the Serbian emperor Stefan Dušan in 1355 he and his sons Stracimir, Đurađ I and Balša II took control of much of Zeta, the land around Lake Skadar in present-day Montenegro and northern Albania.

bon.s: Bon is a Tibetan religious tradition that traces its teachings to the founder Tonpa Shenrab Miwoche and to the ancient kingdom of Zhangzhung in western Tibet. Early Tibetan sources use the name for priests who performed royal funerary and other rites; the organised Bon…

battle-of-haydaran.s: The Battle of Haydaran was fought in April 1052 in Ifriqiya between the army of the Zirid emir al-Mu'izz ibn Badis and the Arab Banu Hilal tribes, sent west after the Zirids broke with the Fatimids. Despite their greater numbers the Zirids were routed.

byzantine-ottoman-wars.s: The Byzantine–Ottoman wars were the conflicts between the Byzantine Empire and the rising Ottoman Turks from the late 13th century to the late 15th. The Ottomans took Byzantine Anatolia, including Bursa (1326) and Nicaea (1331), crossed into Europe in the 1350s and reduced the…

byzantine-seljuk-wars.s: The Byzantine–Seljuk wars were the conflicts between the Byzantine Empire and the Seljuk Turks, from Seljuk raids into Armenia in the mid-11th century to the end of the Sultanate of Rum. The Byzantine defeat at Manzikert in 1071 opened Anatolia to Turkish settlement, and…

byzantine-bulgarian-war-of-913-927.s: The Byzantine–Bulgarian war of 913–927 was fought between the Bulgarian Empire under Simeon I and the Byzantine Empire. Simeon sought the imperial title and the Byzantine throne, won a great victory at Achelous in 917 and dominated the Balkans, but could not take…

byzantine-conquest-of-bulgaria.s: The Byzantine conquest of Bulgaria was the series of wars from 968 to 1018 in which the Byzantine Empire destroyed the First Bulgarian Empire. John I Tzimiskes took eastern Bulgaria and its capital Preslav in 971, and Basil II, after decades of war against Tsar Samuel, won at…

bohemian-hungarian-war-1468-1478.s: The Bohemian–Hungarian War of 1468–1478 was fought between Matthias Corvinus of Hungary and George of Poděbrady, the Hussite king of Bohemia, and then his successor Vladislaus II Jagiellon. Matthias, presenting himself as a champion of the Catholic Church, conquered Moravia,…

byzantine-bulgarian-war-of-894-896.s: The Byzantine–Bulgarian war of 894–896 was fought between the Bulgarian Empire under Simeon I and the Byzantine Empire of Leo VI, after the Bulgarian market in Constantinople was moved to Thessalonica. Byzantium enlisted the Magyars, who ravaged Bulgaria, but Simeon allied…

burundian-civil-war.s: The Burundian Civil War was fought from 1993 to 2005 between the Tutsi-dominated army and Hutu rebel groups. It began after the assassination of Melchior Ndadaye, Burundi's first democratically elected Hutu president, in October 1993, and an estimated 300,000 people died.

bishops-wars.s: The Bishops' Wars were two brief conflicts in 1639 and 1640 between Charles I and the Scottish Covenanters, who rejected his imposition of bishops and a new prayer book on the Church of Scotland. The Scots defeated the English at Newburn and occupied Newcastle in 1640.

bosnian-war.s: The Bosnian War was fought from 1992 to 1995 in Bosnia and Herzegovina after its declaration of independence from Yugoslavia, among Bosniak, Bosnian Serb and Bosnian Croat forces. It saw the siege of Sarajevo, ethnic cleansing and the Srebrenica genocide of 1995.

bull-leaping.s: Bull-leaping is an acrobatic feat in which a performer vaults over a charging bull, shown above all in the art of Minoan Crete, where it is thought to have been a key ritual of the elite and perhaps of religion. Leapers, possibly both men and women, are shown grasping the…

battersea-shield.s: The Battersea Shield is the bronze facing of a vanished wooden shield, decorated in the Celtic La Tène style and now in the British Museum, which dates it to about 350–50 BCE. It was dredged from the River Thames at Battersea in London in 1857, during the building of the first…

banditaccia-necropolis.s: The Banditaccia necropolis is an Etruscan cemetery at Cerveteri, ancient Caere, in Lazio, Italy, with about 1,000 tombs over some 400 hectares dating from the 9th to the 3rd century BCE. The earliest are pits for the ashes of the dead.

bal-gangadhar-tilak.s: Bal Gangadhar Tilak, called Lokmanya, was an Indian nationalist and an early, forceful advocate of swaraj, self-rule, known for the slogan "Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it". He founded the weeklies Kesari and Mahratta and, with Lala Lajpat Rai and Bipin Chandra…

brown-v-board-of-education.s: Brown v. Board of Education was a unanimous ruling of the United States Supreme Court on 17 May 1954 that state laws establishing racial segregation in public schools violated the Fourteenth Amendment's Equal Protection Clause. The case began in Topeka, Kansas, was heard with…

butrus-al-bustani.s: Butrus al-Bustani was a writer and scholar from Mount Lebanon, a major figure of the Nahda, the Arab renaissance. Born a Maronite, he became a Protestant while working for American missionaries in Beirut and helped translate the Bible into Arabic.

beiyang-fleet.s: The Beiyang Fleet, or Northern Ocean Fleet, was one of four regional navies of late Qing China, sponsored by Li Hongzhang to guard the approaches to Beijing. Begun in 1871 and equipped mostly with warships built in Germany and Britain, among them the battleships Dingyuan and…
